Goal\n\nConduct a separate, dedicated formal security audit of the four Phase 4 advanced smart contracts. These contracts introduce higher-risk patterns (cross-chain message passing, multi-party signing, time-based scheduling) and must be audited independently from the core contracts.\n\n## 2. Context\n\nPhase 4 contracts exist in the repository as implementation baselines but are **not yet audited or deployed** to mainnet. The cross-chain bridge in particular represents the highest-risk component due to potential bridge validator compromise scenarios and cross-chain message replay.\n\nThis audit should only begin **after** A1 (core contract audit) is complete and the audit firm has full context of the protocol invariants.\n\nRelated to: [DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md — Track A, A2](../TEMP/DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md)\n\n## 3. In Scope\n\n- `contracts/CrossChainBridge.tact` — Cross-chain asset transfers between TON and EVM chains\n- `contracts/MultiSigCard.tact` — Multi-party account control (M-of-N signing)\n- `contracts/RecurringPayments.tact` — Subscription and time-based recurring payment flows\n- `contracts/LendingProtocolCoordinator.tact` — External lending protocol coordination\n\n## 4. Out of Scope\n\n- Core Phase 2 contracts — covered by A1\n- Off-chain services — covered by A4\n- Bridge validator infrastructure (external to this repository)\n\n## 5. Threat Model\n\n### CrossChainBridge.tact\n1. **Cross-chain message replay** — Identical message replayed on source or destination chain\n2. **Bridge validator compromise** — Malicious or colluding validator set approving invalid transfers\n3. **Double-spend on bridge** — Asset credited on destination before confirmed burned on source\n4. **TVL drain via oracle manipulation** — Incorrect price/amount conversion\n5. **Chain reorganization handling** — Source-chain reorg invalidating a bridged transfer\n\n### MultiSigCard.tact\n1. **Signature replay** — Reusing valid signatures from prior M-of-N approvals\n2. **Quorum manipulation** — Signer set modification without full quorum consent\n3. **Partial execution** — Partially completing a multi-sig operation leaving locked funds\n\n### RecurringPayments.tact\n1. **Time manipulation** — Exploiting block timestamp for early/repeated payment triggers\n2. **Subscription cancellation race** — Payment executed during cancellation window\n3. **Balance exhaustion griefing** — Forcing repeated failed payments to drain gas\n\n### LendingProtocolCoordinator.tact\n1. **Collateral lock bypass** — Releasing COLLATERAL_LOCK while loan is active\n2. **Oracle price manipulation** — Exploiting stale collateral price signals\n3. **Flash loan attack** — Rapidly opening/closing collateral positions\n\n## 6. Mitigations Already in Place\n\n- Contracts inherit the protocol's non-custodial guarantee (invariant I1–I7)\n- Account lock system (`COLLATERAL_LOCK`) guards lending positions\n- Documentation in `docs/` covers intended behavior\n\n## 7. Acceptance Criteria\n\n- [ ] A1 audit completed and core contracts cleared before this audit begins\n- [ ] Separate audit engagement from core contract audit\n- [ ] Cross-chain bridge receives **dedicated review** with replay and validator scenarios\n- [ ] All **Critical** findings remediated\n- [ ] All **High** findings remediated or formally accepted with rationale\n- [ ] Audit report published in `docs/security/audits/`\n- [ ] Remediation PRs merged and re-verified by auditor\n\n## 8. Purpose\n12\t\n13\tThis directory tracks every **external security engagement** performed on the TONBANKCARD protocol. It is the canonical location for:\n14\t\n15\t- Audit engagement plans (RFP-style)\n16\t- Auditor selection records\n17\t- Frozen audit packages handed over to auditors\n18\t- Audit reports as delivered by external firms\n19\t- Remediation pull requests and re-audit attestations\n20\t- Public disclosure artifacts\n21\t\n22\tInternal pre-audit reviews (such as [`audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md`](../../../audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md)) and the system-level audit ([`docs/audit/FULL_SYSTEM_AUDIT.md`](../../audit/FULL_SYSTEM_AUDIT.md)) live elsewhere — this directory is reserved for **third-party** engagements that gate mainnet deployment.\n23\t\n24\t---\n25\t\n26\t## 2. Directory Layout\n27\t\n28\t```\n29\tdocs/security/audits/\n30\t├── README.md                       — This index\n31\t├── REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md         — How findings are triaged, fixed, and verified\n32\t├── REPORT_TEMPLATE.md              — Canonical layout for incoming audit reports\n33\t└── A1-core-contracts/              — Issue #112 engagement\n34\t    ├── ENGAGEMENT.md               — Scope, deliverables, candidate firms, evaluation matrix\n35\t    └── STATUS.md                   — Live state of the engagement (firm, dates, findings)\n36\t```\n37\t\n38\tFuture engagements (A2 Phase 4 contracts, A4 off-chain pentest, etc.) are added as sibling folders named after the roadmap ID.\n39\t\n40\t---\n41\t\n42\t## 3. Engagement Index\n43\t\n44\t| ID | Scope | Roadmap | Issue | Status | Firm | Report |\n45\t|----|-------|---------|-------|--------|------|--------|\n46\t| **A1** | Core contracts (PaymentHub, MerchantPaymentHub, account-locks, nft-resolver, collateral signal) | [A1](../../../TEMP/DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md) | [#112](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/112) | Engagement preparation complete — awaiting firm selection | — | — |\n47\t| A2 | Phase 4 contracts (CrossChainBridge, MultiSigCard, RecurringPayments, LendingProtocolCoordinator) | A2 | TBD | Not started | — | — |\n48\t| A4 | Off-chain services (`api/`, `backend/`, `sdk/`) | A4 | TBD | Not started | — | — |\n49\t| A5 | Bug bounty program | A5 | TBD | Not started | — | — |\n50\t\n51\tWhen a new external engagement begins, copy `A1-core-contracts/` as a starting template, update its `ENGAGEMENT.md` for the new scope, and add a row to this table.\n52\t\n53\t---\n54\t\n55\t## 4. Gating Rules\n56\t\n57\tThe following rules are **non-negotiable** and apply to every engagement listed in §3:\n58\t\n59\t1. **No mainnet deployment** of any in-scope contract before the corresponding audit report is published and remediation is verified by the auditor.\n60\t2. **Critical findings:** zero tolerance — every Critical must be remediated and re-verified before sign-off.\n61\t3. **High findings:** remediated, or formally accepted with rationale signed off by the maintainers in `STATUS.md`.\n62\t4. **Medium findings:** remediated or documented as accepted risk in `docs/audit-notes.md`.\n63\t5. **Audit report is public** — published in this directory and linked from `docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md`.\n64\t6. **Frozen scope** — once an engagement is signed, the contract set under audit is frozen at a specific commit (see [`audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md`](../../../audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md)).\n65\t\n66\t---\n67\t\n68\t## 5. Where Auditors Should Start\n69\t\n70\tExternal auditors engaging with TONBANKCARD should read, in order:\n71\t\n72\t1. [`docs/audit/external-audit-intro.md`](../../audit/external-audit-intro.md) — protocol intent and constraints\n73\t2. [`audit/SCOPE.md`](../../../audit/SCOPE.md) — contracts in scope, focus areas\n74\t3. [`audit/INVARIANTS.md`](../../../audit/INVARIANTS.md) — formal invariants I1–I7\n75\t4. [`audit/THREAT_MODEL.md`](../../../audit/THREAT_MODEL.md) — attack vectors and mitigations\n76\t5. [`audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md`](../../../audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md) — frozen commit, compiler versions\n77\t6. [`audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md`](../../../audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md) — reproducible build\n78\t7. Gating Rules\n\nThe following rules are **non-negotiable** and apply to every engagement listed in §3:\n\n1. **No mainnet deployment** of any in-scope contract before the corresponding audit report is published and remediation is verified by the auditor.\n2. **Critical findings:** zero tolerance — every Critical must be remediated and re-verified before sign-off.\n3. **High findings:** remediated, or formally accepted with rationale signed off by the maintainers in `STATUS.md`.\n4. **Medium findings:** remediated or documented as accepted risk in `docs/audit-notes.md`.\n5. **Audit report is public** — published in this directory and linked from `docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md`.\n6. **Frozen scope** — once an engagement is signed, the contract set under audit is frozen at a specific commit (see [`audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md`](../../../audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md)).\n\n---\n\n## 5. Where Auditors Should Start\n\nExternal auditors engaging with TONBANKCARD should read, in order:\n\n1. Candidate Firms\n102\t\n103\tThree firm classes are acceptable per the roadmap and issue #112:\n104\t\n105\t1. **Top-tier general smart-contract auditors with TON experience**, e.g., Trail of Bits, OtterSec, Halborn.\n106\t2. **Layer-1-agnostic auditors with proven non-EVM track record**, e.g., CertiK, Quantstamp.\n107\t3. **TON-ecosystem specialists**, e.g., CertiK TON desk, TonGuard, scalebit (TON), Veridise TON desk.\n108\t\n109\tA non-exhaustive long list is maintained in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §\"Firm long list\".\n110\t\n111\t### 6.1 Evaluation Matrix\n112\t\n113\tEach shortlisted firm is scored on the following criteria. Numeric scores 1–5 (5 = excellent). Final score = weighted sum.\n114\t\n115\t| Criterion | Weight | Notes |\n116\t|-----------|--------|-------|\n117\t| TON / Tact / FunC depth | 25% | Prior TON engagements, in-house TON expertise, Tact language coverage |\n118\t| Methodology rigor | 20% | Manual review hours per LOC, fuzzing/property testing, formal methods readiness |\n119\t| Reputation & references | 15% | Publicly available audit reports, ecosystem feedback |\n120\t| Re-audit / remediation policy | 15% | Verified re-test included, follow-up support |\n121\t| Cost & timeline fit | 15% | Total cost, calendar window, latest available start |\n122\t| Communication & transparency | 10% | Daily-stand-up cadence, willingness to publish, NDA flexibility |\n123\t\n124\t### 6.2 Conflict-of-interest screen\n125\t\n126\tFirms must disclose any prior engagement with TONBANKCARD operators, TON Foundation grant overlap, holding of TBC token / TBC Diamonds / Series 7777/8888 NFTs, or other potential conflicts. Disqualifying conditions are recorded in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md).\n127\t\n128\t---\n129\t\n130\t## 7. Engagement Process\n131\t\n132\t```\n133\tT-0   Issue published                                       ✅\n134\tT+0   Firm long list assembled                              ⏳\n135\tT+1w  Shortlist (3 firms) + RFP sent\n136\tT+3w  Proposals received, evaluation matrix populated\n137\tT+4w  Firm selected, contract signed\n138\tT+4w  Audit kickoff:  freeze commit + package handover\n139\tT+8w  Mid-audit checkpoint (preliminary findings)\n140\tT+10w Draft report delivered\n141\tT+11w Remediation PRs opened (per REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md)\n142\tT+13w Remediation merged\n143\tT+14w Re-verification by auditor\n144\tT+14w Final report published in this directory\n145\tT+14w STATUS.md flipped to COMPLETED\n146\tT+15w Disclosure summary in CHANGELOG.md + public channels\n147\t```\n148\t\n149\tAll dates are anchored to the kickoff and tracked in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md). The remediation phase follows [`REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md`](../REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md) verbatim.\n150\t\n151\t---\n152\t\n153\t## 8. Deliverables From Auditor\n154\t\n155\tThe signed engagement must require the following deliverables (mirrored in the report template):\n156\t\n157\t1. **Audit report**, structured per [`REPORT_TEMPLATE.md`](../REPORT_TEMPLATE.md):\n158\t   - Findings categorised by severity\n159\t   - Each finding references file:line, invariant(s), and threat-model class\n160\t   - Reproduction steps for every Critical and High\n161\t   - Suggested fixes where applicable\n162\t   - Explicit attestation per invariant I1–I7\n163\t2. **Reproducible PoCs** for every Critical and High finding.\n164\t3. **Re-verification letter** signed after remediation against a specific commit hash.\n165\t4. **Right to publish** the report in this repository.\n166\t\n167\t---\n168\t\n169\t## 9. Acceptance / Gating Decision\n170\t\n171\tThe engagement is closed when:\n172\t\n173\t- All eight checkboxes in §1 are ticked.\n174\t- [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) records the gating verdict as `READY` or `READY WITH ACCEPTED RISKS`.\n175\t- [`docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md`](../../AUDIT_READINESS.md) §\"Audit completion status\" is updated.\n176\t- `CHANGELOG.md` carries a disclosure entry referencing the report.\n177\t\n178\tA verdict of `BLOCKED` keeps mainnet deployment paused per [`README.md`](../README.md) §4.\n179\t\n180\t---\n181\t\n182\t## 10. In-Scope Contracts\n\nThe audit covers exactly the contracts listed in issue #112 §3:\n\n| # | Contract | File | Language | Reason |\n|---|----------|------|----------|--------|\n| 1 | PaymentHub | `contracts/payments/PaymentHub.tact` | Tact | Core payment routing, NFT account abstraction |\n| 2 | MerchantPaymentHub | `contracts/MerchantPaymentHub.tact` | Tact | Merchant-facing payment processing |\n| 3 | Account Locks | `contracts/payments/account-locks.fc` | FunC | FRAUD_LOCK and COLLATERAL_LOCK flag logic |\n| 4 | NFT Account Resolver (FunC) | `contracts/nft-resolver/nft_account_resolver.fc` | FunC | On-chain NFT ownership resolver |\n| 5 | NFT Account Resolver (Tact) | `contracts/nft-resolver/nft_account_resolver.tact` | Tact | Tact wrapper for the resolver |\n| 6 | Public Collateral Lookup | `contracts/collateral-lookup/PublicCollateralLookup.tact` | Tact | Collateral signal read interface |\n| 7 | Collateral Signal | `contracts/CollateralSignal.tact` | Tact | Collateral signal emission |\n\nSupporting types and interfaces (`contracts/types/`, `contracts/interfaces/`) are in scope **for context only** — they are reviewed insofar as they affect the contracts above. They have already been covered by the internal per-contract audit in [`audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md`](../../../../audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md).\n\n---\n\n## 3. Out of Scope\n\nExplicitly **not** part of this engagement (per issue #112 §4):\n\n- Phase 4 contracts (`CrossChainBridge.tact`, `MultiSigCard.tact`, `RecurringPayments.tact`, `LendingProtocolCoordinator.tact`) — covered by engagement **A2**\n- Off-chain services (`api/`, `backend/`, `sdk/`) — covered by engagement **A4**\n- Governance contracts (`contracts/governance/*`) — covered in **Track E**\n- Frontend, dashboard, wallet UI\n\nExternal pre-deployed contracts (TBC jetton, NFT collections, TONCO DEX pool) are treated as trust assumptions; their audits are referenced via [`audit/SCOPE.md`](../../../../audit/SCOPE.md) §\"Out-of-Scope Components\".\n\n---\n\n## 4. Threat Model — Required Coverage\n\nThe audit must explicitly evaluate every attack class enumerated in issue #112 §5, mapped to the protocol-level threat model in [`audit/THREAT_MODEL.md`](../../../../audit/THREAT_MODEL.md):\n\n| # | Class | Where to look |\n|---|-------|---------------|\n| T1 | Re-entrancy / message ordering | `PaymentHub.tact` reentrancy guard (lines 149–150), all `receive(...)` handlers |\n| T2 | NFT ownership spoofing | `nft-resolver/*`, `MerchantPaymentHub.checkOwnership` (lines 90–96) |\n| T3 | Lock bypass | `account-locks.fc` `get_can_send` / `get_can_receive`, all fund-moving paths |\n| T4 | Admin key abuse | search for `deployer`, `admin`, `risk_authority`, `lending_adapter` — verify invariant I3 |\n| T5 | Atomicity failure | `PaymentHub.executeTransfer` (lines 196–202), debit/credit pairing |\n| T6 | Integer overflow / underflow | All `Int as uintN` casts, balance arithmetic |\n| T7 | Replay attacks | Message uniqueness, on-chain vs. off-chain replay protection |\n| T8 | Gas griefing | `receive` handler gas costs, refund paths, message storage |\n\nInvariant attestation in the final report must cover **I1–I7** as defined in [`audit/INVARIANTS.md`](../../../../audit/INVARIANTS.md).\n\n---\n\n## 5. Audit Package (Frozen Hand-off)\n\nThe protocol team will deliver the following package to the selected firm at engagement kickoff. The audited commit is frozen at the kickoff and recorded in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §\"Audited commit\".\n\n| Artifact | Location | Notes |\n|----------|----------|-------|\n| Audit intro pack | [`docs/audit/external-audit-intro.md`](../../../audit/external-audit-intro.md) | Protocol intent, trust model, intentional design constraints |\n| Scope | [`audit/SCOPE.md`](../../../../audit/SCOPE.md) | Contracts, focus areas, out-of-scope list |\n| Threat model | [`audit/THREAT_MODEL.md`](../../../../audit/THREAT_MODEL.md) | T1–T8 attack classes with mitigations |\n| Formal invariants | [`audit/INVARIANTS.md`](../../../../audit/INVARIANTS.md) | I1–I7 with contract-line mapping |\n| Freeze metadata | [`audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md`](../../../../audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md) | Compiler versions, file hashes, frozen commit |\n| Build instructions | [`audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md`](../../../../audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md) | Reproducible build & test commands |\n| Test coverage | [`audit/TEST_COVERAGE_REPORT.md`](../../../../audit/TEST_COVERAGE_REPORT.md) | Coverage breakdown per contract |\n| Internal pre-audit | [`audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md`](../../../../audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md) | Internal findings already mitigated or known |\n| Full system audit | [`docs/audit/FULL_SYSTEM_AUDIT.md`](../../../audit/FULL_SYSTEM_AUDIT.md) | System-wide context |\n| Audit readiness | [`docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md`](../../AUDIT_READINESS.md) | Entry-point navigation document |\n| Audit notes | [`docs/audit-notes.md`](../../../audit-notes.md) | Known accepted limitations |\n\nThe auditor receives **read access** to the public GitHub repository at the frozen commit, plus a direct contact channel agreed at kickoff.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Candidate Firms\n\nThree firm classes are acceptable per the roadmap and issue #112:\n\n1. **Top-tier general smart-contract auditors with TON experience**, e.g., Trail of Bits, OtterSec, Halborn.\n2. **Layer-1-agnostic auditors with proven non-EVM track record**, e.g., CertiK, Quantstamp.\n3. **TON-ecosystem specialists**, e.g., CertiK TON desk, TonGuard, scalebit (TON), Veridise TON desk.\n\nA non-exhaustive long list is maintained in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §\"Firm long list\".\n\n### 6.1 Evaluation Matrix\n\nEach shortlisted firm is scored on the following criteria. Numeric scores 1–5 (5 = excellent). Final score = weighted sum.\n\n| Criterion | Weight | Notes |\n|-----------|--------|-------|\n| TON / Tact / FunC depth | 25% | Prior TON engagements, in-house TON expertise, Tact language coverage |\n| Methodology rigor | 20% | Manual review hours per LOC, fuzzing/property testing, formal methods readiness |\n| Reputation & references | 15% | Publicly available audit reports, ecosystem feedback |\n| Re-audit / remediation policy | 15% | Verified re-test included, follow-up support |\n| Cost & timeline fit | 15% | Total cost, calendar window, latest available start |\n| Communication & transparency | 10% | Daily-stand-up cadence, willingness to publish, NDA flexibility |\n\n### 6.2 Conflict-of-interest screen\n\nFirms must disclose any prior engagement with TONBANKCARD operators, TON Foundation grant overlap, holding of TBC token / TBC Diamonds / Series 7777/8888 NFTs, or other potential conflicts. Disqualifying conditions are recorded in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md).\n\n---\n\n## 7. Engagement Process\n\n```\nT-0   Issue published                                       ✅\nT+0   Firm long list assembled                              ⏳\nT+1w  Shortlist (3 firms) + RFP sent\nT+3w  Proposals received, evaluation matrix populated\nT+4w  Firm selected, contract signed\nT+4w  Audit kickoff:  freeze commit + package handover\nT+8w  Mid-audit checkpoint (preliminary findings)\nT+10w Draft report delivered\nT+11w Remediation PRs opened (per REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md)\nT+13w Remediation merged\nT+14w Re-verification by auditor\nT+14w Final report published in this directory\nT+14w STATUS.md flipped to COMPLETED\nT+15w Disclosure summary in CHANGELOG.md + public channels\n```\n\nAll dates are anchored to the kickoff and tracked in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md). The remediation phase follows [`REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md`](../REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md) verbatim.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Deliverables From Auditor\n\nThe signed engagement must require the following deliverables (mirrored in the report template):\n\n1. **Audit report**, structured per [`REPORT_TEMPLATE.md`](../REPORT_TEMPLATE.md):\n   - Findings categorised by severity\n   - Each finding references file:line, invariant(s), and threat-model class\n   - Reproduction steps for every Critical and High\n   - Suggested fixes where applicable\n   - Explicit attestation per invariant I1–I7\n2. **Reproducible PoCs** for every Critical and High finding.\n3. **Re-verification letter** signed after remediation against a specific commit hash.\n4. **Right to publish** the report in this repository.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Acceptance / Gating Decision\n\nThe engagement is closed when:\n\n- All eight checkboxes in §1 are ticked.\n- [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) records the gating verdict as `READY` or `READY WITH ACCEPTED RISKS`.\n- [`docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md`](../../AUDIT_READINESS.md) §\"Audit completion status\" is updated.\n- `CHANGELOG.md` carries a disclosure entry referencing the report.\n\nA verdict of `BLOCKED` keeps mainnet deployment paused per [`README.md`](../README.md) §4.\n\n---\n\n## 10. Purpose\n11\t\n12\tThis document defines a single, repeatable workflow for processing findings from any external audit listed in [`README.md`](./README.md). It exists so that:\n13\t\n14\t- Every finding has a tracked GitHub issue\n15\t- Every fix has a reviewable pull request\n16\t- Auditors can re-verify fixes against a stable artifact\n17\t- Public disclosure follows a predictable timeline\n18\t\n19\tIt applies to engagements A1, A2, A4, future re-audits, and any out-of-band advisories.\n20\t\n21\t---\n22\t\n23\t## 2. Severity Classification\n24\t\n25\tThe protocol uses the severity scale already established in [`audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md`](../../../audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md) and issue #110:\n26\t\n27\t| Severity | Definition | Response Time | Mandatory Action |\n28\t|----------|------------|---------------|------------------|\n29\t| 🔴 **CRITICAL** | Threat to user funds or non-custodial guarantee | 24h triage / 7-day fix target | **Must be remediated**. Mainnet deployment blocked until re-verified. |\n30\t| 🟠 **HIGH** | Serious logic error that can lead to loss of funds or privilege escalation under plausible conditions | 72h triage / 14-day fix target | Remediated **or** formally accepted in `STATUS.md` with rationale and compensating control |\n31\t| 🟡 **MEDIUM** | Bug or deviation that produces incorrect behaviour without direct fund loss | 1-week triage / 30-day fix target | Remediated or documented as accepted risk in `docs/audit-notes.md` |\n32\t| 🟢 **LOW** | Style, documentation, or hardening issue | Best-effort | Addressed in batches; tracked but non-blocking |\n33\t| ℹ️ **INFORMATIONAL** | Notes, suggestions, design observations | Optional | Logged in `STATUS.md` if not actioned |\n34\t\n35\tMainnet deployment is gated on the rules in [`README.md`](./README.md) §4.\n36\t\n37\t---\n38\t\n39\t## 3. Workflow\n40\t\n41\t```\n42\tAuditor delivers report\n43\t        │\n44\t        ▼\n45\t1. Intake          ─►  Hash + commit report to audits/<ID>/report-vN.pdf\n46\t        │\n47\t        ▼\n48\t2. Triage          ─►  Open one GitHub issue per finding (label: audit:<ID>, severity:<level>)\n49\t        │\n50\t        ▼\n51\t3. Remediation     ─►  Branch issue-<n>-<slug>, PR linked back to the finding issue\n52\t        │\n53\t        ▼\n54\t4. Re-verification ─►  Auditor confirms fix on remediation commit hash\n55\t        │\n56\t        ▼\n57\t5. Disclosure      ─►  STATUS.md flipped to COMPLETED; AUDIT_READINESS.md updated; public note\n58\t```\n59\t\n60\tEach step is described below in detail.\n61\t\n62\t### 3.1 Intake\n63\t\n64\tWhen an audit report is received:\n65\t\n66\t1. Save the report as `docs/security/audits/<ID>/report-v<N>.pdf` (or `.md`) — keep the original filename in `STATUS.md`.\n67\t2. Record SHA-256 of the file in `STATUS.md` for tamper evidence.\n68\t3. Confirm the audited commit hash matches the freeze recorded in `audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md`. If it does not, raise this with the auditor before triage.\n69\t4. Commit the report on a branch named `audit/<ID>-report-intake`. **Do not modify the report after this commit.**\n70\t\n71\t### 3.2 Triage\n72\t\n73\tFor every finding:\n74\t\n75\t1. Open a GitHub issue titled `[audit-<ID>] <finding-id>: <short title>`.\n76\t2. Apply labels:\n77\t   - `audit:<ID>` (e.g., `audit:A1`)\n78\t   - `severity:critical` / `severity:high` / `severity:medium` / `severity:low` / `severity:informational`\n79\t   - `type:security`\n80\t3. Copy the auditor's description, evidence, and recommendation verbatim into the issue body.\n81\t4. Cross-link the issue from the corresponding row in `audits/<ID>/STATUS.md` §\"Findings ledger\".\n82\t\n83\tThe triage owner is the maintainer named in `audits/<ID>/STATUS.md` §\"Engagement parties\". Triage SLAs:\n84\t\n85\t- Critical: triage within 24 hours of intake\n86\t- High: 72 hours\n87\t- Medium / Low / Informational: 7 days\n88\t\n89\t### 3.3 Remediation\n90\t\n91\tFor every finding that will be remediated:\n92\t\n93\t1. Create a branch named `issue-<n>-<slug>` per the contributing guidelines.\n94\t2. Reproduce the finding in a test case before applying the fix. The test must fail on the audited commit.\n95\t3. Implement the fix and run the full test suite (`npx blueprint test`).\n96\t4. Open a pull request with the description fields below:\n97\t\n98\t```markdown\n99\t## Audit Finding\n100\tEngagement: <A1 / A2 / …>\n101\tFinding ID: <auditor-assigned ID>\n102\tSeverity: <Critical / High / Medium / Low / Informational>\n103\tAuditor recommendation: <one line>\n104\t\n105\t## Fix Summary\n106\t<what changed and why>\n107\t\n108\t## Verification\n109\t- [ ] Reproducing test added (link)\n110\t- [ ] Full suite passes\n111\t- [ ] Invariant tests (I1–I7) unchanged or strengthened\n112\t- [ ] No changes to public ABI without coordinator sign-off\n113\t```\n114\t\n115\t5. Request review from the maintainer named in the engagement's `STATUS.md`.\n116\t6. After merge, append the merge commit to the finding row in `STATUS.md`.\n117\t\n118\t### 3.4 Findings That Will Not Be Remediated\n119\t\n120\tWhen a finding is accepted as residual risk:\n121\t\n122\t1. Record the acceptance in `audits/<ID>/STATUS.md` §\"Accepted risks\" with:\n123\t   - Finding ID\n124\t   - Severity\n125\t   - Justification (technical + business)\n126\t   - Compensating control\n127\t   - Sign-off (maintainer GitHub handle + date)\n128\t2. Mirror the entry into `docs/audit-notes.md`.\n129\t3. Inform the auditor; request explicit acknowledgement in the re-verification letter.\n130\t\n131\tHigh-severity findings may only be accepted with maintainer + at least one independent reviewer sign-off recorded in the table.\n132\t\n133\t### 3.5 Re-verification\n134\t\n135\tAfter all remediation PRs are merged:\n136\t\n137\t1. Tag the remediation head commit (`audit-<ID>-remediation-v<N>`).\n138\t2. Provide the auditor with:\n139\t   - The tag\n140\t   - A diff against the audited commit\n141\t   - Test results\n142\t3. Receive the auditor's re-verification letter. Save it under `audits/<ID>/reverification-v<N>.pdf`.\n143\t4. Flip the engagement status in `STATUS.md` and `README.md` §3 to `COMPLETED` (or `ACCEPTED WITH RISKS` if any High items were accepted).\n144\t\n145\t### 3.6 Disclosure\n146\t\n147\tWithin 14 days of re-verification:\n148\t\n149\t1. Publish a short summary on the project's public channels referencing this directory.\n152\t4. Ensure no remediation PR is left in draft state.\n153\t\n154\t---\n155\t\n156\t## 4. Bookkeeping Templates\n157\t\n158\tThe two structured fields below are reused across every engagement's `STATUS.md`. Goal\n\nConduct a separate, dedicated formal security audit of the four Phase 4 advanced smart contracts. These contracts introduce higher-risk patterns (cross-chain message passing, multi-party signing, time-based scheduling) and must be audited independently from the core contracts.\n\n## 2. Context\n\nPhase 4 contracts exist in the repository as implementation baselines but are **not yet audited or deployed** to mainnet. The cross-chain bridge in particular represents the highest-risk component due to potential bridge validator compromise scenarios and cross-chain message replay.\n\nThis audit should only begin **after** A1 (core contract audit) is complete and the audit firm has full context of the protocol invariants.\n\nRelated to: [DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md — Track A, A2](../TEMP/DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md)\n\n## 3. In Scope\n\n- `contracts/CrossChainBridge.tact` — Cross-chain asset transfers between TON and EVM chains\n- `contracts/MultiSigCard.tact` — Multi-party account control (M-of-N signing)\n- `contracts/RecurringPayments.tact` — Subscription and time-based recurring payment flows\n- `contracts/LendingProtocolCoordinator.tact` — External lending protocol coordination\n\n## 4. Out of Scope\n\n- Core Phase 2 contracts — covered by A1\n- Off-chain services — covered by A4\n- Bridge validator infrastructure (external to this repository)\n\n## 5. Threat Model\n\n### CrossChainBridge.tact\n1. **Cross-chain message replay** — Identical message replayed on source or destination chain\n2. **Bridge validator compromise** — Malicious or colluding validator set approving invalid transfers\n3. **Double-spend on bridge** — Asset credited on destination before confirmed burned on source\n4. **TVL drain via oracle manipulation** — Incorrect price/amount conversion\n5. **Chain reorganization handling** — Source-chain reorg invalidating a bridged transfer\n\n### MultiSigCard.tact\n1. **Signature replay** — Reusing valid signatures from prior M-of-N approvals\n2. **Quorum manipulation** — Signer set modification without full quorum consent\n3. **Partial execution** — Partially completing a multi-sig operation leaving locked funds\n\n### RecurringPayments.tact\n1. **Time manipulation** — Exploiting block timestamp for early/repeated payment triggers\n2. **Subscription cancellation race** — Payment executed during cancellation window\n3. **Balance exhaustion griefing** — Forcing repeated failed payments to drain gas\n\n### LendingProtocolCoordinator.tact\n1. **Collateral lock bypass** — Releasing COLLATERAL_LOCK while loan is active\n2. **Oracle price manipulation** — Exploiting stale collateral price signals\n3. **Flash loan attack** — Rapidly opening/closing collateral positions\n\n## 6. Mitigations Already in Place\n\n- Contracts inherit the protocol's non-custodial guarantee (invariant I1–I7)\n- Account lock system (`COLLATERAL_LOCK`) guards lending positions\n- Documentation in `docs/` covers intended behavior\n\n## 7. Acceptance Criteria\n\n- [ ] A1 audit completed and core contracts cleared before this audit begins\n- [ ] Separate audit engagement from core contract audit\n- [ ] Cross-chain bridge receives **dedicated review** with replay and validator scenarios\n- [ ] All **Critical** findings remediated\n- [ ] All **High** findings remediated or formally accepted with rationale\n- [ ] Audit report published in `docs/security/audits/`\n- [ ] Remediation PRs merged and re-verified by auditor\n\n## 8. |\n62\t\n63\t**Most findings are *pre-deployment gaps*** rather than bugs in shipped code: several of the reviewed contracts carry explicitly labelled `// FOR TESTING ONLY` backdoors (`RegisterNFTOwner`, `RegisterNFTOwnerBridge`, `RegisterNFTOwnerMultiSig`, …) that allow an arbitrary sender to rewrite the ownership map used for authorisation. None of these contracts should be deployed without removing or gating those handlers. This matches the pre-existing observation in `docs/audit/FULL_SYSTEM_AUDIT.md` §10.1 (F-CRIT-1…F-CRIT-5) and extends it with new contracts that have not previously been flagged (CrossChainBridge, LendingProtocolCoordinator, MultiSigCard).\n64\t\n65\t**No new fund-draining vulnerability was discovered in the two contracts that actually handle TBC balances (`PaymentHub.tact` and `MerchantPaymentHub.tact`)** — the invariant checks I1, I2, I4, I5, I6 hold at the execution paths reviewed. Contract-by-contract findings\n70\t\n71\t### 2.1 `contracts/types/AccountState.tact`\n72\t\n73\t**Purpose:** Enum + helpers for the four-state NFT account lifecycle (ACTIVE / FROZEN / COLLATERAL_LOCKED / CLOSED). Used by `MerchantPaymentHub` and reference to `PaymentHub.tact` / `account-state.tact`.\n74\t\n75\t**Invariant mapping:** I6 (state helpers encode lock ≠ confiscation via `canReceive` allowing all non-CLOSED).\n76\t\n77\t**Findings**\n78\t\n79\t| ID | Severity | Finding |\n80\t|----|----------|---------|\n81\t| C-AS-L1 | 🟢 LOW | The enum is defined twice — here as `0/1/2/3` and in `payment-hub/account-state.tact` as `1/2/3/4` (STATE_ACTIVE=1). This is inconsistent across contracts and makes cross-contract messaging risky if the two state machines are ever wired together. **Recommendation:** collapse the two encodings into a single shared `types/AccountState.tact` and import it everywhere, or document the ABI mismatch explicitly. |\n82\t\n83\t**Standards notes**\n84\t\n85\t- The struct `AccountState { state: Int as uint8 }` is only 1 byte wide; if the number of states ever exceeds 256 (very unlikely) the `uint8` cast silently truncates. `uint8` is appropriate here — documenting the 0..3 range explicitly would help auditors.\n86\t- `canSend` correctly restricts sending to `ACTIVE` only, but downstream contracts must call it before debit — otherwise the helper is cosmetic.\n87\t\n88\t---\n89\t\n90\t### 2.2 `contracts/types/LockState.tact`\n91\t\n92\t**Purpose:** Struct describing the two independent lock flags (`fraud_locked`, `collateral_locked`) and helpers.\n93\t\n94\t**Invariant mapping:** I6 (receive always allowed; `canSendWithLocks` gates sends).\n95\t\n96\t**Findings**\n97\t\n98\t| ID | Severity | Finding |\n99\t|----|----------|---------|\n100\t| C-LS-L1 | 🟢 LOW | `defaultLockState()` is convenient but is not used consistently in consumer contracts — `MerchantPaymentHub.getLockState` calls it on miss (good), but other future callers could forget. Consider making this the only constructor and exposing it as a `trait` default. |"

None of these contracts should be deployed without removing or gating those handlers. This matches the pre-existing observation in `docs/audit/FULL_SYSTEM_AUDIT.md` §10.1 (F-CRIT-1…F-CRIT-5) and extends it with new contracts that have not previously been flagged (CrossChainBridge, LendingProtocolCoordinator, MultiSigCard).\n\n**No new fund-draining vulnerability was discovered in the two contracts that actually handle TBC balances (`PaymentHub.tact` and `MerchantPaymentHub.tact`)** — the invariant checks I1, I2, I4, I5, I6 hold at the execution paths reviewed. The remaining findings for those contracts concern defence-in-depth, NFT ownership source-of-truth, and admin role scope.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Contract-by-contract findings\n\n### 2.1 `contracts/types/AccountState.tact`\n\n**Purpose:** Enum + helpers for the four-state NFT account lifecycle (ACTIVE / FROZEN / COLLATERAL_LOCKED / CLOSED). Used by `MerchantPaymentHub` and reference to `PaymentHub.tact` / `account-state.tact`.\n\n**Invariant mapping:** I6 (state helpers encode lock ≠ confiscation via `canReceive` allowing all non-CLOSED).\n\n**Findings**\n\n| ID | Severity | Finding |\n|----|----------|---------|\n| C-AS-L1 | 🟢 LOW | The enum is defined twice — here as `0/1/2/3` and in `payment-hub/account-state.tact` as `1/2/3/4` (STATE_ACTIVE=1). This is inconsistent across contracts and makes cross-contract messaging risky if the two state machines are ever wired together. **Recommendation:** collapse the two encodings into a single shared `types/AccountState.tact` and import it everywhere, or document the ABI mismatch explicitly. |\n\n**Standards notes**\n\n- The struct `AccountState { state: Int as uint8 }` is only 1 byte wide; if the number of states ever exceeds 256 (very unlikely) the `uint8` cast silently truncates. `uint8` is appropriate here — documenting the 0..3 range explicitly would help auditors.\n- `canSend` correctly restricts sending to `ACTIVE` only, but downstream contracts must call it before debit — otherwise the helper is cosmetic.\n\n---\n\n### 2.2 `contracts/types/LockState.tact`\n\n**Purpose:** Struct describing the two independent lock flags (`fraud_locked`, `collateral_locked`) and helpers.\n\n**Invariant mapping:** I6 (receive always allowed; `canSendWithLocks` gates sends).\n\n**Findings**\n\n| ID | Severity | Finding |\n|----|----------|---------|\n| C-LS-L1 | 🟢 LOW | `defaultLockState()` is convenient but is not used consistently in consumer contracts — `MerchantPaymentHub.getLockState` calls it on miss (good), but other future callers could forget. Consider making this the only constructor and exposing it as a `trait` default. |",

U (the NFT owner)\n  AND T MUST be initiated by U\n  AND no protocol admin/operator can initiate T on behalf of U\n```\n\n**Guaranteed Properties:**\n- The NFT owner is the sole authority over the |\n\n**Evidence of Compliance:**\n- No `adminWithdraw()` function exists in any contract\n- No `emergencyDrain()` function exists\n- No `forcedTransfer()` function exists\n- Admin functions (`handle_set_paused`, `handle_flag_account`) modify flags only, never balances\n\n**Test Coverage:**\n- `tests/invariants/I1-non-custodial-ownership.spec.ts`\n- Negative: Attempt transfer from non-owner → must fail\n- Negative: Admin attempting to move user funds → must fail\n\n**Threat Model Reference:** T1 (NFT Race), T8 (Admin Key Compromise)\n\n**Audit Checklist:**\n- [ ] All fund transfer functions verify `msg.sender == current_NFT_owner`\n- [ ] Zero admin fund access functions in entire codebase\n- [ ] Backend services are read-only (no signing keys for protocol contracts)\n- [ ] No custody mechanism exists\n\n---\n\n## I2 — NFT = Account Authority\n\n**Statement:**\n> Each NFT represents exactly one account. Explicitly non-custodial (comment header: \"Cross-chain verification is EXTERNAL\").\n332\t\n333\t**Invariant mapping:** I1, I2, I3, I4.\n334\t\n335\t**Findings**\n336\t\n337\t| ID | Severity | Finding |\n338\t|----|----------|---------|\n339\t| C-CCB-C1 | 🔴 CRITICAL | `RegisterNFTOwnerBridge` (lines 399–401) is **ungated**. Any address can call this and set themselves (or anyone else) as the owner of any NFT in `self.nft_owners`. Once set, they pass `validateOwnership` and can register/cancel bridge intents for that NFT. Because this contract doesn't move funds, the direct financial impact is limited to causing external relayers to bridge TBC from the wrong address — but indexers and relayers that trust this registry are misled. **Must be removed or gated** before deployment. Same file also has an ungated `RegisterRelayer` that lets anyone whitelist themselves as an authorised relayer (see C-CCB-H1). |\n340\t| C-CCB-H1 | 🟠 HIGH | `RegisterRelayer` (lines 403–405) has **no access control**. Anyone can whitelist themselves as an authorised relayer and call `ConfirmBridgeExecution` on behalf of users. A malicious relayer cannot move funds on-chain, but they can mark *unexecuted* bridge intents as CONFIRMED with an arbitrary `external_tx_hash`, misleading off-chain systems into believing a cross-chain transfer succeeded. |\n341\t| C-CCB-H2 | 🟠 HIGH | The `intentKey` (line 377) hashes only `nft_address` and adds `intent_id`: `sha256(nft_address.asSlice()) + intent_id`. Because `intent_id` is user-supplied and the addition is plain Int addition (not a hash), an attacker can craft an `intent_id` that makes `intentKey(attacker_nft, attacker_intent) == intentKey(victim_nft, victim_intent)` (the collision requires `sha256(a) - sha256(b) == victim_intent - attacker_intent`, which is hard to search but not infeasible — 64-bit `intent_id` provides `2^64` grinding room against a 256-bit hash diff, so practically safe but theoretically unsound). **Recommendation:** use `sha256(concat(nft_address.asSlice(), intent_id_bytes))` or a TL-B-packed composite. |\n342\t| C-CCB-M1 | 🟡 MEDIUM | The authorised-relayer check (lines 226–228) treats relayer confirmations and owner confirmations identically, so a relayer can confirm an intent the owner did not initiate. Combined with C-CCB-C1/H1 this is a coordination hazard; even after gating the register functions, consider requiring the owner's prior `RegisterBridgeIntent` before any relayer confirmation is accepted (the current code does enforce `intent != null`, so this holds — but it is worth asserting in a test). |\n343\t| C-CCB-L1 | 🟢 LOW | `target_chain` is a `uint8` and validated `1..MAX_SUPPORTED_CHAIN` (currently 5). When new chains are added, all client code must be updated; consider a registry of supported chains instead of a hardcoded constant. |\n344\t\n345\t---\n346\t\n347\t### 2.16 `contracts/LendingProtocolCoordinator.tact`\n348\t\n349\t**Purpose:** Coordination layer for opt-in lending intents. Explicitly non-custodial.\n350\t\n351\t**Invariant mapping:** I1, I2, I3, I6.\n352\t\n353\t**Findings**\n354\t\n355\t| ID | Severity | Finding |\n356\t|----|----------|---------|\n357\t| C-LPC-C1 | 🔴 CRITICAL | `RegisterNFTOwner` (lines 347–350) is **ungated**. Any address can set any NFT's owner in `self.nft_owners`. Once set, they pass `validateOwnership` and can register/update/cancel lending intents for arbitrary NFTs. The contract does not move funds, so the blast radius is limited to misleading off-chain lenders (CoinRabbit). **Must be removed or gated.** Identical flavour to F-CRIT-2 / F-CRIT-4 in the system audit. |\n358\t| C-LPC-H1 | 🟠 HIGH | The file defines **two** conflicting messages: `RegisterNFTOwner` (line 347, no opcode) and `message(0x7e8764ef) RegisterNFTOwnerLending` (line 359). Only `RegisterNFTOwner` has a handler; `RegisterNFTOwnerLending` appears to be dead code. If both are ever deployed, opcode collision on `RegisterNFTOwner` with `CollateralSignal.RegisterNFTOwner` could cause cross-contract message confusion. **Recommendation:** explicitly opcode-tag `RegisterNFTOwner` (or remove the dead `RegisterNFTOwnerLending`) and add a comment explaining the test-only nature. |\n359\t| C-LPC-M1 | 🟡 MEDIUM | `UpdateLendingIntent` (line 238) does not verify the intent was previously `ACTIVE` — it happily resurrects a `CANCELLED` intent into `ACTIVE`. This may be intended (user can re-enable) but is undocumented. Document or add a state check. |\n360\t\n361\t---\n362\t\n363\t### 2.17 `contracts/MultiSigCard.tact`\n364\t\n365\t**Purpose:** Permission layer that adds required co-signatures for an NFT's payments. **Note:** The contract records APPROVED proposals but does **not** actually dispatch any payment message; the \"execution\" step is purely an event emission. Users must still sign the real payment elsewhere.\n366\t\n367\t**Invariant mapping:** I1, I2, I3, I4.\n368\t\n369\t**Findings**\n370\t\n371\t| ID | Severity | Finding |\n372\t|----|----------|---------|\n373\t| C-MSC-C1 | 🔴 CRITICAL | `RegisterNFTOwnerMultiSig` (lines 559–561) is **ungated**. Any address can claim ownership of any NFT in `self.nft_owners`, then call `ConfigureMultiSig` / `SubmitPaymentProposal` / `RemoveMultiSig` to impersonate the real owner. Because the contract itself does not move funds, the impact is confined to creating fake multi-sig proposals, but the contract's *claim* that \"NFT owner ALWAYS remains the primary authority\" is false. **Must be removed or gated.** |\n374\t| C-MSC-H1 | 🟠 HIGH | **No actual settlement.** `PaymentProposalApproved` events are emitted when threshold is reached, but there is no handler that debits the NFT's TBC balance or forwards the payment to the Payment Hub. A user who configures multi-sig on their account and believes co-signers now gate their payments will be surprised to learn that their real payments still flow through `PaymentHub.tact` with only the NFT-owner signature — the multi-sig constraint is cosmetic unless the Payment Hub is taught to consult this contract. **Recommendation:** either (a) wire PaymentHub to refuse non-multisig-approved transfers when `MultiSigCard.isMultiSigEnabled(nft) == true`, or (b) delete the contract to avoid giving users a false sense of security. |\n375\t| C-MSC-H2 | 🟠 HIGH | `approvalKey` (line 536) uses `sha256(nft_addr) + proposal_id*1000 + sha256(signer)`. Plain additions of two 256-bit hashes do not produce a collision-resistant composite; an attacker can search `signer'` such that `sha256(signer) == sha256(signer') - k` for any chosen offset. The practical impact is limited because `signer` must be a real on-chain address whose message is verified, but the mathematical weakness is still worth fixing. Use `sha256(concat(addr, id_bytes, signer))`. |\n376\t| C-MSC-M1 | 🟡 MEDIUM | `ConfigureMultiSig` takes a fixed `signer_1/2/3` plus `required_signatures: 1..3`. If the owner wants 2-of-2, they must set `signer_3 = zero address` and the `isSigner` check (line 524) must reject zero. Today `isSigner` compares the sender address to `config.signer_3` — if `signer_3 == 0` and the zero-address was ever the sender (structurally impossible today), it would pass. Not exploitable, but clean up by explicitly rejecting zero or null signer slots. |\n377\t| C-MSC-M2 | 🟡 MEDIUM | `RemoveMultiSig` clears the config but does **not** reject or auto-complete any pending proposals. Pending proposals become orphaned (status still PENDING, but `isMultiSigEnabled == false`). `ApprovePaymentProposal` would then fail with `ERROR_MS_NO_CONFIG`, so approvals cannot land — but existing approvals remain in the `approvals` map forever. Clean up on remove, or document that removing multi-sig locks out pending proposals forever. |\n378\t| C-MSC-L1 | 🟢 LOW | The same `RegisterNFTOwner…` test-only pattern appears in three separate contracts (CollateralSignal, CrossChainBridge, LendingProtocolCoordinator, MultiSigCard). Factor into a shared trait `ITestOnlyRegistrar` and delete it pre-production via a feature flag / build target. |\n379\t\n380\t---\n381\t\n382\t## 3. Cross-cutting findings\n383\t\n384\tThese are patterns that appear in multiple contracts and deserve a single architectural decision.\n385\t\n386\t| ID | Severity | Finding |\n387\t|----|----------|---------|\n388\t| X-1 | 🔴 CRITICAL | **Ungated `RegisterNFTOwner*` test backdoors.** Five contracts (`CollateralSignal`, `CrossChainBridge`, `LendingProtocolCoordinator`, `MultiSigCard`, and implicitly any future contract using the same pattern) expose a message handler that allows **any sender** to overwrite the authorisation map used for ownership checks. This is the same class of bug as F-CRIT-2…F-CRIT-4 in the existing system audit but this audit adds `CrossChainBridge`, `LendingProtocolCoordinator`, and `MultiSigCard` to the list. Recommendation: add a single CI guard that fails the build if `RegisterNFTOwner*` is present without an authority check. |\n389\t| X-2 | 🟠 HIGH | **NFT ownership source-of-truth.** Most contracts store `nft_owners: map<Address, Address>` as a local mirror of on-chain ownership, with no sync protocol back to the NFT item contract. When the NFT is transferred, these mirrors go stale and the contracts continue to grant authority to the previous owner. This directly contradicts invariant I2. A protocol-wide fix is needed: either (a) a message-based `INFTResolver` that the authority contracts consult at the moment of execution, or (b) ownership proofs (signed by the NFT item contract) attached to each authorising message. |\n390\t| X-3 | 🟠 HIGH | **Dual encodings of `AccountState`.** `types/AccountState.tact` uses `0..3`; `payment-hub/account-state.tact` uses `1..4`. `PaymentHub.tact` locally re-declares the `0..3` constants. Any cross-contract integration that transmits a state byte risks mis-interpretation. Collapse to one canonical encoding. |\n391\t| X-4 | 🟡 MEDIUM | **`get fun` misused as on-chain API.** `INFTResolver.tact` and `nft_account_resolver.tact` expose ownership lookups via `get fun`, which are off-chain only. All the on-chain authority checks therefore fall back to `nft_owners` local mirrors (see X-2). |\n392\t| X-5 | 🟡 MEDIUM | **Composite keys via addition.** `CrossChainBridge.intentKey`, `MultiSigCard.proposalKey` / `approvalKey`, and `ProposalRegistry`'s `proposal_id * 1000 + nft_id` all use non-collision-resistant composites. Any future expansion of ID ranges (e.g. >222 diamonds) can introduce silent collisions. |\n393\t| X-6 | 🟡 MEDIUM | **Storage-growth on read.** `PaymentHub.getOrCreateAccount` writes on `get fun` calls and on receive of `GetAccountStateRequest`. Any caller can inflate contract storage. Make read paths pure. |\n394\t| X-7 | 🟢 LOW | **Placeholder addresses in constants.** `ProposalRegistry.DIAMONDS_COLLECTION` and `SnapshotVerifier.DIAMONDS_COLLECTION` both hold the literal string `\"EQDiamondsCollectionAddressPlaceholder123456789\"`. The build will fail at these; replace before any audit build. |\n395\t\n396\t---\n397\t\n398\t## 4. Threat-model coverage check\n399\t\n400\tMapping of the threat classes in `audit/THREAT_MODEL.md` against the findings above:\n401\t\n402\t| Threat class | Contracts most affected | Findings |\n403\t|--------------|------------------------|----------|\n404\t| T1 — NFT transfer race | PaymentHub.tact, MerchantPaymentHub.tact | C-MPH-H1, X-2 |\n405\t| T2 — Reentrancy & callback abuse | PaymentHub.tact | C-PHT-M1 (guard is present; note semantics) |\n406\t| T3 — Ledger desynchronisation | payment-hub.fc | C-PHF-H1 (FunC hub emits but never mutates) |\n407\t| T4 — Lock bypass | payment-hub.fc | C-PHF-C2 (no lock integration) |\n408\t| T5 — Merchant payment abuse | MerchantPaymentHub.tact | C-MPH-M2 (replay protection off-chain) |\n409\t| T6 — External adapter exploits | CrossChainBridge.tact | C-CCB-H1 (self-whitelist as relayer) |\n410\t| T7 — Oracle / price manipulation | n/a (out of scope) | — |\n411\t| T8 — Admin key compromise | All `admin:` state contracts | C-MPH-C1 (admin can mint via SetAccountBalance) |\n412\t\n413\t---\n414\t\n415\t## 5. Standards compliance notes\n416\t\n417\t- **TON best practices:** bounced-message handling is present only in the FunC files (`account-locks.fc`, `nft_account_resolver.fc`, `payment-hub.fc`). Tact contracts inherit the default bounce behaviour; this is acceptable for actors that emit `SendRemainingValue` replies but should be explicitly tested.\n418\t- **Tact idioms:** use of `inline fun`, `Int as coins`, `Int as uint32`/`uint64` is consistent. Map iteration in `SnapshotVerifier.batchVerifyEligibility` relies on a hard-coded supply bound, which is the right pattern for Tact (no unbounded iteration).\n419\t- **TEP-62 / TIP-4 (NFT Standard):** `nft_account_resolver.tact` claims compliance in its comment header but does not actually invoke `get_nft_data()` on the NFT item contract. True compliance requires the message-based resolver in X-2.\n420\t- **Audit Scope (`audit/SCOPE.md`):** all contracts listed in issue #110 have been visited in this document. The following additional contracts were encountered and are either out of scope for this audit or were touched only incidentally: `RecurringPayments.tact`, `TransparencyRegistry.tact`, `PublicCollateralLookup.tact`, `governance/diamond_resolver.fc`. They should be reviewed in a follow-up audit pass.\n421\t\n422\t---\n423\t\n424\t## 6. Recommended remediation order\n425\t\n426\t1. **Before any mainnet deployment** — fix all 🔴 CRITICAL findings (C-MPH-C1, C-PHF-C1/C2, C-ASM-C1, C-PR-C1, C-SV-C1, C-CCB-C1, C-LPC-C1, C-MSC-C1) and the cross-cutting X-1.\n427\t2. **Before enabling executable governance** — fix C-PR-H1, C-PR-H2, C-SV-H1 (vote integrity) and X-2 (ownership source-of-truth).\n428\t3. **Before announcing multi-sig as a security feature** — fix C-MSC-H1 (wire PaymentHub to consult multi-sig) or remove the contract."

When new chains are added, all client code must be updated; consider a registry of supported chains instead of a hardcoded constant. |\n\n---\n\n### 2.16 `contracts/LendingProtocolCoordinator.tact`\n\n**Purpose:** Coordination layer for opt-in lending intents. Explicitly non-custodial.\n\n**Invariant mapping:** I1, I2, I3, I6.\n\n**Findings**\n\n| ID | Severity | Finding |\n|----|----------|---------|\n| C-LPC-C1 | 🔴 CRITICAL | `RegisterNFTOwner` (lines 347–350) is **ungated**. Any address can set any NFT's owner in `self.nft_owners`. Once set, they pass `validateOwnership` and can register/update/cancel lending intents for arbitrary NFTs. The contract does not move funds, so the blast radius is limited to misleading off-chain lenders (CoinRabbit). **Must be removed or gated.** Identical flavour to F-CRIT-2 / F-CRIT-4 in the system audit. |\n| C-LPC-H1 | 🟠 HIGH | The file defines **two** conflicting messages: `RegisterNFTOwner` (line 347, no opcode) and `message(0x7e8764ef) RegisterNFTOwnerLending` (line 359). Only `RegisterNFTOwner` has a handler; `RegisterNFTOwnerLending` appears to be dead code. If both are ever deployed, opcode collision on `RegisterNFTOwner` with `CollateralSignal.RegisterNFTOwner` could cause cross-contract message confusion. **Recommendation:** explicitly opcode-tag `RegisterNFTOwner` (or remove the dead `RegisterNFTOwnerLending`) and add a comment explaining the test-only nature. |\n| C-LPC-M1 | 🟡 MEDIUM | `UpdateLendingIntent` (line 238) does not verify the intent was previously `ACTIVE` — it happily resurrects a `CANCELLED` intent into `ACTIVE`. This may be intended (user can re-enable) but is undocumented. Document or add a state check. |\n\n---\n\n### 2.17 `contracts/MultiSigCard.tact`\n\n**Purpose:** Permission layer that adds required co-signatures for an NFT's payments. **Note:** The contract records APPROVED proposals but does **not** actually dispatch any payment message; the \"execution\" step is purely an event emission. Users must still sign the real payment elsewhere.\n\n**Invariant mapping:** I1, I2, I3, I4.\n\n**Findings**\n\n| ID | Severity | Finding |\n|----|----------|---------|\n| C-MSC-C1 | 🔴 CRITICAL | `RegisterNFTOwnerMultiSig` (lines 559–561) is **ungated**. Any address can claim ownership of any NFT in `self.nft_owners`, then call `ConfigureMultiSig` / `SubmitPaymentProposal` / `RemoveMultiSig` to impersonate the real owner. Because the contract itself does not move funds, the impact is confined to creating fake multi-sig proposals, but the contract's *claim* that \"NFT owner ALWAYS remains the primary authority\" is false. **Must be removed or gated.** |\n| C-MSC-H1 | 🟠 HIGH | **No actual settlement.** `PaymentProposalApproved` events are emitted when threshold is reached, but there is no handler that debits the NFT's TBC balance or forwards the payment to the Payment Hub. A user who configures multi-sig on their account and believes co-signers now gate their payments will be surprised to learn that their real payments still flow through `PaymentHub.tact` with only the NFT-owner signature — the multi-sig constraint is cosmetic unless the Payment Hub is taught to consult this contract. **Recommendation:** either (a) wire PaymentHub to refuse non-multisig-approved transfers when `MultiSigCard.isMultiSigEnabled(nft) == true`, or (b) delete the contract to avoid giving users a false sense of security. |\n| C-MSC-H2 | 🟠 HIGH | `approvalKey` (line 536) uses `sha256(nft_addr) + proposal_id*1000 + sha256(signer)`. Plain additions of two 256-bit hashes do not produce a collision-resistant composite; an attacker can search `signer'` such that `sha256(signer) == sha256(signer') - k` for any chosen offset. The practical impact is limited because `signer` must be a real on-chain address whose message is verified, but the mathematical weakness is still worth fixing. Use `sha256(concat(addr, id_bytes, signer))`. |\n| C-MSC-M1 | 🟡 MEDIUM | `ConfigureMultiSig` takes a fixed `signer_1/2/3` plus `required_signatures: 1..3`. If the owner wants 2-of-2, they must set `signer_3 = zero address` and the `isSigner` check (line 524) must reject zero. Today `isSigner` compares the sender address to `config.signer_3` — if `signer_3 == 0` and the zero-address was ever the sender (structurally impossible today), it would pass. Not exploitable, but clean up by explicitly rejecting zero or null signer slots. |\n| C-MSC-M2 | 🟡 MEDIUM | `RemoveMultiSig` clears the config but does **not** reject or auto-complete any pending proposals. Pending proposals become orphaned (status still PENDING, but `isMultiSigEnabled == false`). `ApprovePaymentProposal` would then fail with `ERROR_MS_NO_CONFIG`, so approvals cannot land — but existing approvals remain in the `approvals` map forever. Clean up on remove, or document that removing multi-sig locks out pending proposals forever. |\n| C-MSC-L1 | 🟢 LOW | The same `RegisterNFTOwner…` test-only pattern appears in three separate contracts (CollateralSignal, CrossChainBridge, LendingProtocolCoordinator, MultiSigCard). Factor into a shared trait `ITestOnlyRegistrar` and delete it pre-production via a feature flag / build target. |\n\n---\n\n## 3. Cross-cutting findings\n\nThese are patterns that appear in multiple contracts and deserve a single architectural decision.\n\n| ID | Severity | Finding |\n|----|----------|---------|\n| X-1 | 🔴 CRITICAL | **Ungated `RegisterNFTOwner*` test backdoors.** Five contracts (`CollateralSignal`, `CrossChainBridge`, `LendingProtocolCoordinator`, `MultiSigCard`, and implicitly any future contract using the same pattern) expose a message handler that allows **any sender** to overwrite the authorisation map used for ownership checks. This is the same class of bug as F-CRIT-2…F-CRIT-4 in the existing system audit but this audit adds `CrossChainBridge`, `LendingProtocolCoordinator`, and `MultiSigCard` to the list. Recommendation: add a single CI guard that fails the build if `RegisterNFTOwner*` is present without an authority check. |\n| X-2 | 🟠 HIGH | **NFT ownership source-of-truth.** Most contracts store `nft_owners: map<Address, Address>` as a local mirror of on-chain ownership, with no sync protocol back to the NFT item contract. When the NFT is transferred, these mirrors go stale and the contracts continue to grant authority to the previous owner. This directly contradicts invariant I2. A protocol-wide fix is needed: either (a) a message-based `INFTResolver` that the authority contracts consult at the moment of execution, or (b) ownership proofs (signed by the NFT item contract) attached to each authorising message. |\n| X-3 | 🟠 HIGH | **Dual encodings of `AccountState`.** `types/AccountState.tact` uses `0..3`; `payment-hub/account-state.tact` uses `1..4`. `PaymentHub.tact` locally re-declares the `0..3` constants. Any cross-contract integration that transmits a state byte risks mis-interpretation. Collapse to one canonical encoding. |\n| X-4 | 🟡 MEDIUM | **`get fun` misused as on-chain API.** `INFTResolver.tact` and `nft_account_resolver.tact` expose ownership lookups via `get fun`, which are off-chain only. All the on-chain authority checks therefore fall back to `nft_owners` local mirrors (see X-2). |\n| X-5 | 🟡 MEDIUM | **Composite keys via addition.** `CrossChainBridge.intentKey`, `MultiSigCard.proposalKey` / `approvalKey`, and `ProposalRegistry`'s `proposal_id * 1000 + nft_id` all use non-collision-resistant composites. Any future expansion of ID ranges (e.g. >222 diamonds) can introduce silent collisions. |\n| X-6 | 🟡 MEDIUM | **Storage-growth on read.** `PaymentHub.getOrCreateAccount` writes on `get fun` calls and on receive of `GetAccountStateRequest`. Any caller can inflate contract storage. Make read paths pure. |\n| X-7 | 🟢 LOW | **Placeholder addresses in constants.** `ProposalRegistry.DIAMONDS_COLLECTION` and `SnapshotVerifier.DIAMONDS_COLLECTION` both hold the literal string `\"EQDiamondsCollectionAddressPlaceholder123456789\"`. The build will fail at these; replace before any audit build. |\n\n---\n\n## 4. Threat-model coverage check\n\nMapping of the threat classes in `audit/THREAT_MODEL.md` against the findings above:\n\n| Threat class | Contracts most affected | Findings |\n|--------------|------------------------|----------|\n| T1 — NFT transfer race | PaymentHub.tact, MerchantPaymentHub.tact | C-MPH-H1, X-2 |\n| T2 — Reentrancy & callback abuse | PaymentHub.tact | C-PHT-M1 (guard is present; note semantics) |\n| T3 — Ledger desynchronisation | payment-hub.fc | C-PHF-H1 (FunC hub emits but never mutates) |\n| T4 — Lock bypass | payment-hub.fc | C-PHF-C2 (no lock integration) |\n| T5 — Merchant payment abuse | MerchantPaymentHub.tact | C-MPH-M2 (replay protection off-chain) |\n| T6 — External adapter exploits | CrossChainBridge.tact | C-CCB-H1 (self-whitelist as relayer) |\n| T7 — Oracle / price manipulation | n/a (out of scope) | — |\n| T8 — Admin key compromise | All `admin:` state contracts | C-MPH-C1 (admin can mint via SetAccountBalance) |\n\n---\n\n## 5. Standards compliance notes\n\n- **TON best practices:** bounced-message handling is present only in the FunC files (`account-locks.fc`, `nft_account_resolver.fc`, `payment-hub.fc`). Tact contracts inherit the default bounce behaviour; this is acceptable for actors that emit `SendRemainingValue` replies but should be explicitly tested.\n- **Tact idioms:** use of `inline fun`, `Int as coins`, `Int as uint32`/`uint64` is consistent. Map iteration in `SnapshotVerifier.batchVerifyEligibility` relies on a hard-coded supply bound, which is the right pattern for Tact (no unbounded iteration).\n- **TEP-62 / TIP-4 (NFT Standard):** `nft_account_resolver.tact` claims compliance in its comment header but does not actually invoke `get_nft_data()` on the NFT item contract. True compliance requires the message-based resolver in X-2.\n- **Audit Scope (`audit/SCOPE.md`):** all contracts listed in issue #110 have been visited in this document. The following additional contracts were encountered and are either out of scope for this audit or were touched only incidentally: `RecurringPayments.tact`, `TransparencyRegistry.tact`, `PublicCollateralLookup.tact`, `governance/diamond_resolver.fc`. They should be reviewed in a follow-up audit pass.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Recommended remediation order\n\n1. **Before any mainnet deployment** — fix all 🔴 CRITICAL findings (C-MPH-C1, C-PHF-C1/C2, C-ASM-C1, C-PR-C1, C-SV-C1, C-CCB-C1, C-LPC-C1, C-MSC-C1) and the cross-cutting X-1.\n2. **Before enabling executable governance** — fix C-PR-H1, C-PR-H2, C-SV-H1 (vote integrity) and X-2 (ownership source-of-truth).\n3. **Before announcing multi-sig as a security feature** — fix C-MSC-H1 (wire PaymentHub to consult multi-sig) or remove the contract.",

Any violation is a critical security finding.\n58\t\n59\t| ID | Invariant | Key Guarantee |\n60\t|----|-----------|---------------|\n61\t| **I1** | Non-Custodial Ownership | Only NFT owner can initiate fund transfers |\n62\t| **I2** | NFT = Account Authority | NFT ownership is the single source of truth for account control |\n63\t| **I3** | No Admin Fund Control | No privileged role can move user funds |\n64\t| **I4** | Atomic Transfers | All transfers are all-or-nothing; no partial state possible |\n65\t| **I5** | Ledger Conservation | Sum of all balances is preserved across all operations |\n66\t| **I6** | Lock ≠ Confiscation | Locks restrict outgoing transfers; they do not seize funds |\n67\t| **I7** | External Adapter Isolation | External providers cannot directly invoke protocol operations |\n68\t\n69\tFull formal definitions with contract-code mappings: [audit/INVARIANTS.md](../../audit/INVARIANTS.md)\n70\t\n71\t---\n72\t\n73\t## Test Coverage Summary\n74\t\n75\t| Contract | Estimated Line Coverage | Estimated Branch Coverage |\n76\t|----------|------------------------|--------------------------|\n77\t| MerchantPaymentHub.tact | ~90%+ | ~85%+ |\n78\t| PaymentHub.tact | ~85%+ | ~80%+ |\n79\t| account-locks.fc | ~85%+ | ~80%+ |\n80\t| nft_account_resolver.fc | ~80%+ | ~75%+ |\n81\t| account-state.tact | ~90%+ | ~85%+ |\n82\t\n83\tTo obtain exact figures:\n84\t\n85\t```bash\n86\tgit checkout eb5dd593248a33a5a7517ae59b840827c140906a\n87\tnpm install\n88\tnpx blueprint test --coverage\n89\t```\n90\t\n91\tSee [audit/TEST_COVERAGE_REPORT.md](../../audit/TEST_COVERAGE_REPORT.md) for full test organization.\n92\t\n93\t---\n94\t\n95\t## Critical Audit Focus Areas\n96\t\n97\t### 1. No Admin Fund Control (MUST verify)\n98\t\n99\tSearch the entire contract codebase for `withdraw`, `drain`, `emergency`, `admin_transfer`, `force_transfer`. Expected result: **zero matches** in fund-moving contexts.\n100\t\n101\tAdmin roles exist (`risk_authority`, `lending_adapter`) but are limited to setting/clearing lock flags. Atomic Balance Updates (MUST verify)\n108\t\n109\tAll balance modifications must be atomic — both debit and credit in the same transaction. Lock Enforcement (MUST verify)\n114\t\n115\tLocks prevent sending but must never seize funds. Objective\n\nProcure a **separate, dedicated formal external security audit** of the four Phase 4 advanced smart contracts (cross-chain bridge, multi-sig card, recurring payments, lending coordinator). Successfully completing this engagement is a mandatory gate before any TONBANKCARD mainnet deployment touching the in-scope contracts, and before the corresponding Phase 4 activation work in Track F (F3 — Cross-Chain Bridge Production Readiness, F4 — Recurring Payments Activation, F5 — Multi-Sig Card Activation).\n\nPer issue #113 §2, this engagement **may only begin after engagement [A1](../A1-core-contracts/ENGAGEMENT.md) is complete** — i.e., A1's audited contracts are cleared (verdict `READY` or `READY WITH ACCEPTED RISKS`) and the audit firm has full context of the protocol invariants. This ordering exists because the Phase 4 contracts are authorised through the same `nft_owners` / ownership pattern as the core contracts and inherit their trust assumptions.\n\nSuccess criteria (mirror of issue #113 acceptance criteria):\n\n- [ ] A1 audit completed and core contracts cleared before this audit begins\n- [ ] Separate audit engagement from the core contract audit (not bundled with A1)\n- [ ] Cross-chain bridge receives **dedicated review** with replay and validator scenarios\n- [ ] Audit firm engaged and scope signed\n- [ ] Frozen audit package delivered (see §5)\n- [ ] All Critical findings remediated and re-verified\n- [ ] All High findings remediated, or formally accepted with rationale in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md)\n- [ ] All Medium findings addressed (remediated or documented as accepted risk in `docs/audit-notes.md`)\n- [ ] Audit report published in this directory\n- [ ] Remediation PR(s) merged and re-verified by auditor\n- [ ] `docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md` updated with completion status\n\n---\n\n## 2. In-Scope Contracts\n\nThe audit covers exactly the four Phase 4 advanced contracts listed in issue #113 §3:\n\n| # | Contract | File | Language | Reason |\n|---|----------|------|----------|--------|\n| 1 | CrossChainBridge | `contracts/CrossChainBridge.tact` | Tact | Cross-chain asset transfers between TON and EVM chains (intent / confirm / cancel coordination) |\n| 2 | MultiSigCard | `contracts/MultiSigCard.tact` | Tact | Multi-party account control (M-of-N signing, proposal lifecycle) |\n| 3 | RecurringPayments | `contracts/RecurringPayments.tact` | Tact | Subscription and time-based recurring payment mandates |\n| 4 | LendingProtocolCoordinator | `contracts/LendingProtocolCoordinator.tact` | Tact | External lending protocol coordination (opt-in lending intents) |\n\nSupporting types and interfaces (`contracts/types/`, `contracts/interfaces/INFTResolver.tact`, `contracts/interfaces/ICollateralSignal.tact`) are in scope **for context only** — they are reviewed insofar as they affect the contracts above. They were covered by the internal per-contract audit in [`audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md`](../../../../audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md) and by engagement [A1](../A1-core-contracts/ENGAGEMENT.md).\n\nThe internal pre-audit also already raised findings for three of the four Phase 4 contracts (`C-CCB-*`, `C-LPC-*`, `C-MSC-*` and cross-cutting `X-1`/`X-2`/`X-5`). These findings — including the mitigations already applied in PR #109 (gating the test-only `RegisterNFTOwner…` handlers behind the contract deployer) — are the **starting baseline** for this engagement, not the ending state. The auditor is expected to **independently** re-evaluate each finding on the audited commit and to assess whether the remaining mitigations are sufficient. `RecurringPayments.tact` was explicitly flagged in §5 of the internal audit as not previously visited, so it requires fresh coverage.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Out of Scope\n\nExplicitly **not** part of this engagement (per issue #113 §4):\n\n- **Core Phase 2 contracts** (`PaymentHub.tact`, `MerchantPaymentHub.tact`, `account-locks.fc`, `nft-resolver/*`, `CollateralSignal.tact`, `PublicCollateralLookup.tact`) — covered by engagement [A1](../A1-core-contracts/ENGAGEMENT.md)\n- **Off-chain services** (`api/`, `backend/`, `sdk/`) — covered by engagement **A4**\n- **Bridge validator infrastructure** (off-chain relayers, ChangeNOW or other external adapters) — external to this repository\n- **Governance contracts** (`contracts/governance/*`) — covered in **Track E**\n- **Frontend, dashboard, wallet UI** — covered by Track F UX work\n- **TBC jetton master**, NFT item / collection contracts, TONCO DEX pool — treated as trust assumptions (see [`audit/SCOPE.md`](../../../../audit/SCOPE.md) §\"Out-of-Scope Components\")\n\nThe cross-chain bridge's **external** verification path (ChangeNOW / relayers) is treated as an explicit trust assumption — the audit must surface every contract-side assumption about that trust, but the external infrastructure itself is not in scope.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Threat Model — Required Coverage\n\nPer issue #113 §5, the auditor must explicitly evaluate every threat enumerated below, mapped to the protocol-level threat model in [`audit/THREAT_MODEL.md`](../../../../audit/THREAT_MODEL.md) and the invariants in [`audit/INVARIANTS.md`](../../../../audit/INVARIANTS.md).\n\n### 4.1 `CrossChainBridge.tact`\n\n| # | Threat | Where to look |\n|---|--------|---------------|\n| CCB-1 | **Cross-chain message replay** — identical message replayed on source or destination chain | `RegisterBridgeIntent` / `ConfirmBridgeExecution` (lines 159–214 / 217–266), `intentKey` (line 377) |\n| CCB-2 | **Bridge validator compromise** — malicious or colluding relayer set approving invalid transfers | `authorized_relayers` map, `isAuthorizedRelayer` (lines 366–373), `RegisterRelayer` (lines 412–415), C-CCB-H1 |\n| CCB-3 | **Double-spend on bridge** — asset credited on destination before confirmed burned on source | Status transitions `PENDING → CONFIRMED` (lines 246–256), atomicity of `confirmed_at` write |\n| CCB-4 | **TVL drain via oracle manipulation** — incorrect price / amount conversion across chains | `amount` field (informational), absence of price oracles, validity of off-chain conversion assumptions |\n| CCB-5 | **Chain reorganization handling** — source-chain reorg invalidating a bridged transfer | `external_tx_hash` provenance, absence of finality proofs, indexer responsibilities |\n| CCB-6 | **Composite-key collision** — internal pre-audit C-CCB-H2 / X-5 | `intentKey` uses `sha256(addr) + intent_id` (Int addition, not concatenation) |\n| CCB-7 | **Test-only backdoor residual risk** — C-CCB-C1 / cross-cutting X-1 | `RegisterNFTOwnerBridge` / `RegisterRelayer` deployer gating (lines 402–415) |\n\n### 4.2 `MultiSigCard.tact`\n\n| # | Threat | Where to look |\n|---|--------|---------------|\n| MSC-1 | **Signature replay** — reusing valid signatures from prior M-of-N approvals | `approvals` map keying (`approvalKey`, line 526), `ApprovePaymentProposal` idempotency (lines 327–337) |\n| MSC-2 | **Quorum manipulation** — signer set modification without full quorum consent | `ConfigureMultiSig` allows owner to overwrite signer set unilaterally (lines 199–237); `RemoveMultiSig` (lines 441–463) |\n| MSC-3 | **Partial execution** — partially completing a multi-sig operation leaving locked funds | C-MSC-H1 — proposals never settle on-chain; the contract emits events only |\n| MSC-4 | **Zero-address signer slot abuse** — internal pre-audit C-MSC-M1 | `isSigner` comparing sender to `signer_3 == zero` (lines 514–520) |\n| MSC-5 | **Orphaned pending proposals after `RemoveMultiSig`** — C-MSC-M2 | `RemoveMultiSig` does not finalise pending proposals (lines 441–463) |\n| MSC-6 | **Composite-key collision** — C-MSC-H2 / X-5 | `proposalKey` and `approvalKey` use Int addition (lines 526–529) |\n| MSC-7 | **Test-only backdoor residual risk** — C-MSC-C1 / cross-cutting X-1 | `RegisterNFTOwnerMultiSig` deployer gating (lines 555–561) |\n\n### 4.3 `RecurringPayments.tact`\n\n| # | Threat | Where to look |\n|---|--------|---------------|\n| RP-1 | **Time manipulation** — exploiting block timestamp for early / repeated payment triggers | `now()` usage in `ExecuteRecurringPayment` (lines 295–303), `MIN_PERIOD_SECONDS = 3600` (line 105) |\n| RP-2 | **Subscription cancellation race** — payment executed during the cancellation window | `CancelMandate` / `ExecuteRecurringPayment` interleavings (lines 217–263 vs. 264–339) |\n| RP-3 | **Balance exhaustion griefing** — forcing repeated failed payments to drain gas | Bouncing / refund paths, `sendResponse` with `SendRemainingValue` (lines 392–404) |\n| RP-4 | **Settlement gap** — `ExecuteRecurringPayment` only emits an event; actual fund movement happens elsewhere | Lines 264–339 — verify Payment Hub integration assumption is explicit, documented, and matches deployed behaviour |\n| RP-5 | **Mandate immutability** — header claims mandates are immutable, but `max_executions == 0` is treated as unlimited | Lines 28–38 (header), lines 308–317 (state transition logic) |\n| RP-6 | **Test-only backdoor residual risk** — cross-cutting X-1 | `RegisterNFTOwnerRecurring` deployer gating (lines 415–422) |\n\n### 4.4 `LendingProtocolCoordinator.tact`\n\n| # | Threat | Where to look |\n|---|--------|---------------|\n| LPC-1 | **Collateral lock bypass** — releasing `COLLATERAL_LOCK` while a loan is active | Verify this contract does **not** call any lock-mutation paths; cross-check against `account-locks.fc` (covered by A1) |\n| LPC-2 | **Oracle price manipulation** — exploiting stale collateral price signals | `collateral_signal_amount` is informational only; verify no contract path uses it for authorisation |\n| LPC-3 | **Flash loan attack** — rapidly opening / closing collateral positions | `UpdateLendingIntent` resurrecting a `CANCELLED` intent (lines 240–278), C-LPC-M1 |\n| LPC-4 | **Conflicting opcodes** — internal pre-audit C-LPC-H1 | `RegisterNFTOwner` (no opcode) vs. dead `message(0x7e8764ef) RegisterNFTOwnerLending` (line 359) |\n| LPC-5 | **Test-only backdoor residual risk** — C-LPC-C1 / cross-cutting X-1 | `RegisterNFTOwner` deployer gating (lines 344–351) |\n\n### 4.5 Cross-cutting\n\n| # | Threat | Coverage |\n|---|--------|----------|\n| X-1 | Ungated `RegisterNFTOwner*` handlers (mitigation: gated by deployer + write-once) | All four Phase 4 contracts |\n| X-2 | NFT ownership source-of-truth — local mirror vs. on-chain NFT item | All four Phase 4 contracts use the same mirror pattern |\n| X-5 | Composite keys via Int addition | `CrossChainBridge.intentKey`, `MultiSigCard.proposalKey` / `approvalKey` |\n\nInvariant attestation in the final report must cover **I1–I7** as defined in [`audit/INVARIANTS.md`](../../../../audit/INVARIANTS.md), with particular emphasis on:\n\n- **I1 (Non-Custodial)** — verify that none of the four contracts can move funds, despite their event-emitting flavour\n- **I2 (NFT = Account Authority)** — verify the `nft_owners` mirror does not contradict on-chain NFT ownership (X-2)\n- **I3 (No Admin Control)** — verify the deployer gating on `RegisterNFTOwner*` is the only privileged path, and that it cannot move funds\n- **I6 (Lock ≠ Confiscation)** — verify `LendingProtocolCoordinator` never mutates lock state\n- **I7 (External Adapter Isolation)** — verify `CrossChainBridge` and `LendingProtocolCoordinator` only signal to external adapters and never give them on-chain fund-moving authority\n\n---\n\n## 5.
