Candidate Firms\n\nThe same three firm classes accepted for A1 apply (per the roadmap and issue #113 §1):\n\n1. **Top-tier general smart-contract auditors with TON experience**, e.g., Trail of Bits, OtterSec, Halborn.\n2. **Layer-1-agnostic auditors with proven non-EVM track record**, e.g., CertiK, Quantstamp, Veridise.\n3. **TON-ecosystem specialists**, e.g., CertiK TON desk, TonGuard, scalebit (TON), Veridise TON desk.\n\nA non-exhaustive long list is maintained in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §\"Firm long list\".\n\nFor A2 specifically, **cross-chain bridge expertise weighs higher** than for A1 — firms with a demonstrated track record auditing bridge contracts (replay protection, validator set design, double-spend prevention) should be preferred. This is reflected in the evaluation matrix below.\n\nIf the same firm that performs A1 is contracted for A2, the engagement must still be **a separate signed scope** with separate deliverables (per issue #113 §7).\n\n### 6.1 Evaluation Matrix\n\nEach shortlisted firm is scored on the following criteria. Numeric scores 1–5 (5 = excellent). Final score = weighted sum. Compared to A1, the weights have been re-balanced to emphasise cross-chain / bridge depth.\n\n| Criterion | Weight | Notes |\n|-----------|--------|-------|\n| TON / Tact / FunC depth | 20% | Prior TON engagements, in-house TON expertise, Tact language coverage |\n| **Cross-chain bridge & multi-sig depth** | **20%** | Public bridge audit reports, replay-protection methodology, multi-sig design experience |\n| Methodology rigor | 15% | Manual review hours per LOC, fuzzing / property testing, formal methods readiness |\n| Reputation & references | 10% | Publicly available audit reports, ecosystem feedback |\n| Re-audit / remediation policy | 15% | Verified re-test included, follow-up support |\n| Cost & timeline fit | 10% | Total cost, calendar window, latest available start |\n| Communication & transparency | 10% | Daily-stand-up cadence, willingness to publish, NDA flexibility |\n\n### 6.2 Conflict-of-interest screen\n\nFirms must disclose any prior engagement with TONBANKCARD operators, TON Foundation grant overlap, holding of TBC token / TBC Diamonds / Series 7777/8888 NFTs, financial interest in ChangeNOW or any candidate bridge relayer, or other potential conflicts. Disqualifying conditions are recorded in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md).\n\nA firm that audited A1 must additionally disclose whether they reused A1 findings verbatim or re-derived them independently — the A2 audit must produce an independent assessment of any in-scope contract, even if the same team performed A1.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Engagement Process\n\n```\nT-A1  A1 engagement reaches verdict READY or READY WITH ACCEPTED RISKS  (gate)\nT-0   A2 issue published                                                ✅\nT+0   Firm long list assembled (re-using / updating A1 list)            ⏳\nT+1w  Shortlist (3 firms) + RFP sent\nT+3w  Proposals received, evaluation matrix populated\nT+4w  Firm selected, contract signed\nT+4w  Audit kickoff:  freeze commit + package handover\nT+9w  Mid-audit checkpoint (preliminary findings, with bridge focus)\nT+11w Draft report delivered (includes bridge-specific replay scenarios)\nT+12w Remediation PRs opened (per REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md)\nT+15w Remediation merged\nT+16w Re-verification by auditor\nT+16w Final report published in this directory\nT+16w STATUS.md flipped to COMPLETED\nT+17w Disclosure summary in CHANGELOG.md + public channels\n```\n\nAll dates are anchored to the A2 kickoff (`T`) and tracked in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md). `T-A1` is not under A2's control; it is the upstream completion of engagement A1 and is the hard gate for starting A2.\n\nA2 reserves one extra week of audit calendar (`T+9w` mid-audit checkpoint instead of A1's `T+8w`) to give the auditor more bandwidth for the cross-chain bridge review per issue #113 §1.\n\nThe remediation phase follows [`../REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md`](../REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md) verbatim.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Deliverables From Auditor\n\nThe signed engagement must require the following deliverables (mirrored in the report template):\n\n1. **Audit report**, structured per [`../REPORT_TEMPLATE.md`](../REPORT_TEMPLATE.md):\n   - Findings categorised by severity\n   - Each finding references file:line, invariant(s), and threat-model class (CCB-, MSC-, RP-, LPC-, X-)\n   - Reproduction steps for every Critical and High\n   - Suggested fixes where applicable\n   - Explicit attestation per invariant I1–I7\n   - **Dedicated cross-chain bridge section** covering CCB-1 (replay), CCB-2 (validator compromise), and CCB-5 (chain reorg) per issue #113 §1 / §7\n2. **Reproducible PoCs** for every Critical and High finding (on-chain test or scripted scenario).\n3. **Re-verification letter** signed after remediation against a specific commit hash.\n4. **Right to publish** the report in this repository.\n\nIf any of the in-scope contracts is recommended for **removal or non-deployment** (the internal audit's `C-MSC-H1` already raises this possibility for `MultiSigCard.tact`), the auditor's recommendation must be explicit — the protocol team will not interpret silence as approval.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Acceptance / Gating Decision\n\nThe engagement is closed when:\n\n- All eleven checkboxes in §1 are ticked.\n- [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) records the gating verdict as `READY` or `READY WITH ACCEPTED RISKS`.\n- [`docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md`](../../AUDIT_READINESS.md) §\"Audit completion status\" is updated with the A2 row populated.\n- `CHANGELOG.md` carries a disclosure entry referencing the report.\n\nA verdict of `BLOCKED` keeps **mainnet deployment of any Phase 4 contract** paused per [`../README.md`](../README.md) §4 and blocks the corresponding Track F activation work (F3 / F4 / F5).\n\n---\n\n## 10.    [solve worker-1]     "content": "# Engagement A2 — Formal Security Audit of Phase 4 Contracts\n\n**Engagement ID:** `A2`\n**Issue:** [#113 — A2 Formal Security Audit — Phase 4 Contracts](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/113)\n**Roadmap track:** A — Security & Audit\n**Status:** Engagement preparation complete — awaiting A1 sign-off and firm selection\n**Maintainer:** `@konard`\n**Last Updated:** 2026-05-16\n\n---\n\n## 1. Objective\n\nProcure a **separate, dedicated formal external security audit** of the four Phase 4 advanced smart contracts (cross-chain bridge, multi-sig card, recurring payments, lending coordinator). Successfully completing this engagement is a mandatory gate before any TONBANKCARD mainnet deployment touching the in-scope contracts, and before the corresponding Phase 4 activation work in Track F (F3 — Cross-Chain Bridge Production Readiness, F4 — Recurring Payments Activation, F5 — Multi-Sig Card Activation).\n\nPer issue #113 §2, this engagement **may only begin after engagement [A1](../A1-core-contracts/ENGAGEMENT.md) is complete** — i.e., A1's audited contracts are cleared (verdict `READY` or `READY WITH ACCEPTED RISKS`) and the audit firm has full context of the protocol invariants. This ordering exists because the Phase 4 contracts are authorised through the same `nft_owners` / ownership pattern as the core contracts and inherit their trust assumptions.\n\nSuccess criteria (mirror of issue #113 acceptance criteria):\n\n- [ ] A1 audit completed and core contracts cleared before this audit begins\n- [ ] Separate audit engagement from the core contract audit (not bundled with A1)\n- [ ] Cross-chain bridge receives **dedicated review** with replay and validator scenarios\n- [ ] Audit firm engaged and scope signed\n- [ ] Frozen audit package delivered (see §5)\n- [ ] All Critical findings remediated and re-verified\n- [ ] All High findings remediated, or formally accepted with rationale in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md)\n- [ ] All Medium findings addressed (remediated or documented as accepted risk in `docs/audit-notes.md`)\n- [ ] Audit report published in this directory\n- [ ] Remediation PR(s) merged and re-verified by auditor\n- [ ] `docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md` updated with completion status\n\n---\n\n## 2. In-Scope Contracts\n\nThe audit covers exactly the four Phase 4 advanced contracts listed in issue #113 §3:\n\n| # | Contract | File | Language | Reason |\n|---|----------|------|----------|--------|\n| 1 | CrossChainBridge | `contracts/CrossChainBridge.tact` | Tact | Cross-chain asset transfers between TON and EVM chains (intent / confirm / cancel coordination) |\n| 2 | MultiSigCard | `contracts/MultiSigCard.tact` | Tact | Multi-party account control (M-of-N signing, proposal lifecycle) |\n| 3 | RecurringPayments | `contracts/RecurringPayments.tact` | Tact | Subscription and time-based recurring payment mandates |\n| 4 | LendingProtocolCoordinator | `contracts/LendingProtocolCoordinator.tact` | Tact | External lending protocol coordination (opt-in lending intents) |\n\nSupporting types and interfaces (`contracts/types/`, `contracts/interfaces/INFTResolver.tact`, `contracts/interfaces/ICollateralSignal.tact`) are in scope **for context only** — they are reviewed insofar as they affect the contracts above. They were covered by the internal per-contract audit in [`audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md`](../../../../audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md) and by engagement [A1](../A1-core-contracts/ENGAGEMENT.md).\n\nThe internal pre-audit also already raised findings for three of the four Phase 4 contracts (`C-CCB-*`, `C-LPC-*`, `C-MSC-*` and cross-cutting `X-1`/`X-2`/`X-5`). These findings — including the mitigations already applied in PR #109 (gating the test-only `RegisterNFTOwner…` handlers behind the contract deployer) — are the **starting baseline** for this engagement, not the ending state. The auditor is expected to **independently** re-evaluate each finding on the audited commit and to assess whether the remaining mitigations are sufficient. `RecurringPayments.tact` was explicitly flagged in §5 of the internal audit as not previously visited, so it requires fresh coverage.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Out of Scope\n\nExplicitly **not** part of this engagement (per issue #113 §4):\n\n- **Core Phase 2 contracts** (`PaymentHub.tact`, `MerchantPaymentHub.tact`, `account-locks.fc`, `nft-resolver/*`, `CollateralSignal.tact`, `PublicCollateralLookup.tact`) — covered by engagement [A1](../A1-core-contracts/ENGAGEMENT.md)\n- **Off-chain services** (`api/`, `backend/`, `sdk/`) — covered by engagement **A4**\n- **Bridge validator infrastructure** (off-chain relayers, ChangeNOW or other external adapters) — external to this repository\n- **Governance contracts** (`contracts/governance/*`) — covered in **Track E**\n- **Frontend, dashboard, wallet UI** — covered by Track F UX work\n- **TBC jetton master**, NFT item / collection contracts, TONCO DEX pool — treated as trust assumptions (see [`audit/SCOPE.md`](../../../../audit/SCOPE.md) §\"Out-of-Scope Components\")\n\nThe cross-chain bridge's **external** verification path (ChangeNOW / relayers) is treated as an explicit trust assumption — the audit must surface every contract-side assumption about that trust, but the external infrastructure itself is not in scope.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Threat Model — Required Coverage\n\nPer issue #113 §5, the auditor must explicitly evaluate every threat enumerated below, mapped to the protocol-level threat model in [`audit/THREAT_MODEL.md`](../../../../audit/THREAT_MODEL.md) and the invariants in [`audit/INVARIANTS.md`](../../../../audit/INVARIANTS.md).\n\n### 4.1 `CrossChainBridge.tact`\n\n| # | Threat | Where to look |\n|---|--------|---------------|\n| CCB-1 | **Cross-chain message replay** — identical message replayed on source or destination chain | `RegisterBridgeIntent` / `ConfirmBridgeExecution` (lines 159–214 / 217–266), `intentKey` (line 377) |\n| CCB-2 | **Bridge validator compromise** — malicious or colluding relayer set approving invalid transfers | `authorized_relayers` map, `isAuthorizedRelayer` (lines 366–373), `RegisterRelayer` (lines 412–415), C-CCB-H1 |\n| CCB-3 | **Double-spend on bridge** — asset credited on destination before confirmed burned on source | Status transitions `PENDING → CONFIRMED` (lines 246–256), atomicity of `confirmed_at` write |\n| CCB-4 | **TVL drain via oracle manipulation** — incorrect price / amount conversion across chains | `amount` field (informational), absence of price oracles, validity of off-chain conversion assumptions |\n| CCB-5 | **Chain reorganization handling** — source-chain reorg invalidating a bridged transfer | `external_tx_hash` provenance, absence of finality proofs, indexer responsibilities |\n| CCB-6 | **Composite-key collision** — internal pre-audit C-CCB-H2 / X-5 | `intentKey` uses `sha256(addr) + intent_id` (Int addition, not concatenation) |\n| CCB-7 | **Test-only backdoor residual risk** — C-CCB-C1 / cross-cutting X-1 | `RegisterNFTOwnerBridge` / `RegisterRelayer` deployer gating (lines 402–415) |\n\n### 4.2 `MultiSigCard.tact`\n\n| # | Threat | Where to look |\n|---|--------|---------------|\n| MSC-1 | **Signature replay** — reusing valid signatures from prior M-of-N approvals | `approvals` map keying (`approvalKey`, line 526), `ApprovePaymentProposal` idempotency (lines 327–337) |\n| MSC-2 | **Quorum manipulation** — signer set modification without full quorum consent | `ConfigureMultiSig` allows owner to overwrite signer set unilaterally (lines 199–237); `RemoveMultiSig` (lines 441–463) |\n| MSC-3 | **Partial execution** — partially completing a multi-sig operation leaving locked funds | C-MSC-H1 — proposals never settle on-chain; the contract emits events only |\n| MSC-4 | **Zero-address signer slot abuse** — internal pre-audit C-MSC-M1 | `isSigner` comparing sender to `signer_3 == zero` (lines 514–520) |\n| MSC-5 | **Orphaned pending proposals after `RemoveMultiSig`** — C-MSC-M2 | `RemoveMultiSig` does not finalise pending proposals (lines 441–463) |\n| MSC-6 | **Composite-key collision** — C-MSC-H2 / X-5 | `proposalKey` and `approvalKey` use Int addition (lines 526–529) |\n| MSC-7 | **Test-only backdoor residual risk** — C-MSC-C1 / cross-cutting X-1 | `RegisterNFTOwnerMultiSig` deployer gating (lines 555–561) |\n\n### 4.3 `RecurringPayments.tact`\n\n| # | Threat | Where to look |\n|---|--------|---------------|\n| RP-1 | **Time manipulation** — exploiting block timestamp for early / repeated payment triggers | `now()` usage in `ExecuteRecurringPayment` (lines 295–303), `MIN_PERIOD_SECONDS = 3600` (line 105) |\n| RP-2 | **Subscription cancellation race** — payment executed during the cancellation window | `CancelMandate` / `ExecuteRecurringPayment` interleavings (lines 217–263 vs. 264–339) |\n| RP-3 | **Balance exhaustion griefing** — forcing repeated failed payments to drain gas | Bouncing / refund paths, `sendResponse` with `SendRemainingValue` (lines 392–404) |\n| RP-4 | **Settlement gap** — `ExecuteRecurringPayment` only emits an event; actual fund movement happens elsewhere | Lines 264–339 — verify Payment Hub integration assumption is explicit, documented, and matches deployed behaviour |\n| RP-5 | **Mandate immutability** — header claims mandates are immutable, but `max_executions == 0` is treated as unlimited | Lines 28–38 (header), lines 308–317 (state transition logic) |\n| RP-6 | **Test-only backdoor residual risk** — cross-cutting X-1 | `RegisterNFTOwnerRecurring` deployer gating (lines 415–422) |\n\n### 4.4 `LendingProtocolCoordinator.tact`\n\n| # | Threat | Where to look |\n|---|--------|---------------|\n| LPC-1 | **Collateral lock bypass** — releasing `COLLATERAL_LOCK` while a loan is active | Verify this contract does **not** call any lock-mutation paths; cross-check against `account-locks.fc` (covered by A1) |\n| LPC-2 | **Oracle price manipulation** — exploiting stale collateral price signals | `collateral_signal_amount` is informational only; verify no contract path uses it for authorisation |\n| LPC-3 | **Flash loan attack** — rapidly opening / closing collateral positions | `UpdateLendingIntent` resurrecting a `CANCELLED` intent (lines 240–278), C-LPC-M1 |\n| LPC-4 | **Conflicting opcodes** — internal pre-audit C-LPC-H1 | `RegisterNFTOwner` (no opcode) vs. dead `message(0x7e8764ef) RegisterNFTOwnerLending` (line 359) |\n| LPC-5 | **Test-only backdoor residual risk** — C-LPC-C1 / cross-cutting X-1 | `RegisterNFTOwner` deployer gating (lines 344–351) |\n\n### 4.5 Cross-cutting\n\n| # | Threat | Coverage |\n|---|--------|----------|\n| X-1 | Ungated `RegisterNFTOwner*` handlers (mitigation: gated by deployer + write-once) | All four Phase 4 contracts |\n| X-2 | NFT ownership source-of-truth — local mirror vs. on-chain NFT item | All four Phase 4 contracts use the same mirror pattern |\n| X-5 | Composite keys via Int addition | `CrossChainBridge.intentKey`, `MultiSigCard.proposalKey` / `approvalKey` |\n\nInvariant attestation in the final report must cover **I1–I7** as defined in [`audit/INVARIANTS.md`](../../../../audit/INVARIANTS.md), with particular emphasis on:\n\n- **I1 (Non-Custodial)** — verify that none of the four contracts can move funds, despite their event-emitting flavour\n- **I2 (NFT = Account Authority)** — verify the `nft_owners` mirror does not contradict on-chain NFT ownership (X-2)\n- **I3 (No Admin Control)** — verify the deployer gating on `RegisterNFTOwner*` is the only privileged path, and that it cannot move funds\n- **I6 (Lock ≠ Confiscation)** — verify `LendingProtocolCoordinator` never mutates lock state\n- **I7 (External Adapter Isolation)** — verify `CrossChainBridge` and `LendingProtocolCoordinator` only signal to external adapters and never give them on-chain fund-moving authority\n\n---\n\n## 5. public GitHub repository at the frozen commit, plus a direct contact channel agreed at kickoff.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Candidate Firms\n\nThe same three firm classes accepted for A1 apply (per the roadmap and issue #113 §1):\n\n1. **Top-tier general smart-contract auditors with TON experience**, e.g., Trail of Bits, OtterSec, Halborn.\n2. **Layer-1-agnostic auditors with proven non-EVM track record**, e.g., CertiK, Quantstamp, Veridise.\n3. **TON-ecosystem specialists**, e.g., CertiK TON desk, TonGuard, scalebit (TON), Veridise TON desk.\n\nA non-exhaustive long list is maintained in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §\"Firm long list\".\n\nFor A2 specifically, **cross-chain bridge expertise weighs higher** than for A1 — firms with a demonstrated track record auditing bridge contracts (replay protection, validator set design, double-spend prevention) should be preferred. This is reflected in the evaluation matrix below.\n\nIf the same firm that performs A1 is contracted for A2, the engagement must still be **a separate signed scope** with separate deliverables (per issue #113 §7).\n\n### 6.1 Evaluation Matrix\n\nEach shortlisted firm is scored on the following criteria. Numeric scores 1–5 (5 = excellent). Final score = weighted sum. Compared to A1, the weights have been re-balanced to emphasise cross-chain / bridge depth.\n\n| Criterion | Weight | Notes |\n|-----------|--------|-------|\n| TON / Tact / FunC depth | 20% | Prior TON engagements, in-house TON expertise, Tact language coverage |\n| **Cross-chain bridge & multi-sig depth** | **20%** | Public bridge audit reports, replay-protection methodology, multi-sig design experience |\n| Methodology rigor | 15% | Manual review hours per LOC, fuzzing / property testing, formal methods readiness |\n| Reputation & references | 10% | Publicly available audit reports, ecosystem feedback |\n| Re-audit / remediation policy | 15% | Verified re-test included, follow-up support |\n| Cost & timeline fit | 10% | Total cost, calendar window, latest available start |\n| Communication & transparency | 10% | Daily-stand-up cadence, willingness to publish, NDA flexibility |\n\n### 6.2 Conflict-of-interest screen\n\nFirms must disclose any prior engagement with TONBANKCARD operators, TON Foundation grant overlap, holding of TBC token / TBC Diamonds / Series 7777/8888 NFTs, financial interest in ChangeNOW or any candidate bridge relayer, or other potential conflicts. Disqualifying conditions are recorded in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md).\n\nA firm that audited A1 must additionally disclose whether they reused A1 findings verbatim or re-derived them independently — the A2 audit must produce an independent assessment of any in-scope contract, even if the same team performed A1.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Engagement Process\n\n```\nT-A1  A1 engagement reaches verdict READY or READY WITH ACCEPTED RISKS  (gate)\nT-0   A2 issue published                                                ✅\nT+0   Firm long list assembled (re-using / updating A1 list)            ⏳\nT+1w  Shortlist (3 firms) + RFP sent\nT+3w  Proposals received, evaluation matrix populated\nT+4w  Firm selected, contract signed\nT+4w  Audit kickoff:  freeze commit + package handover\nT+9w  Mid-audit checkpoint (preliminary findings, with bridge focus)\nT+11w Draft report delivered (includes bridge-specific replay scenarios)\nT+12w Remediation PRs opened (per REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md)\nT+15w Remediation merged\nT+16w Re-verification by auditor\nT+16w Final report published in this directory\nT+16w STATUS.md flipped to COMPLETED\nT+17w Disclosure summary in CHANGELOG.md + public channels\n```\n\nAll dates are anchored to the A2 kickoff (`T`) and tracked in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md). `T-A1` is not under A2's control; it is the upstream completion of engagement A1 and is the hard gate for starting A2.\n\nA2 reserves one extra week of audit calendar (`T+9w` mid-audit checkpoint instead of A1's `T+8w`) to give the auditor more bandwidth for the cross-chain bridge review per issue #113 §1.\n\nThe remediation phase follows [`../REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md`](../REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md) verbatim.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Deliverables From Auditor\n\nThe signed engagement must require the following deliverables (mirrored in the report template):\n\n1. **Audit report**, structured per [`../REPORT_TEMPLATE.md`](../REPORT_TEMPLATE.md):\n   - Findings categorised by severity\n   - Each finding references file:line, invariant(s), and threat-model class (CCB-, MSC-, RP-, LPC-, X-)\n   - Reproduction steps for every Critical and High\n   - Suggested fixes where applicable\n   - Explicit attestation per invariant I1–I7\n   - **Dedicated cross-chain bridge section** covering CCB-1 (replay), CCB-2 (validator compromise), and CCB-5 (chain reorg) per issue #113 §1 / §7\n2. **Reproducible PoCs** for every Critical and High finding (on-chain test or scripted scenario).\n3. **Re-verification letter** signed after remediation against a specific commit hash.\n4. **Right to publish** the report in this repository.\n\nIf any of the in-scope contracts is recommended for **removal or non-deployment** (the internal audit's `C-MSC-H1` already raises this possibility for `MultiSigCard.tact`), the auditor's recommendation must be explicit — the protocol team will not interpret silence as approval.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Acceptance / Gating Decision\n\nThe engagement is closed when:\n\n- All eleven checkboxes in §1 are ticked.\n- [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) records the gating verdict as `READY` or `READY WITH ACCEPTED RISKS`.\n- [`docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md`](../../AUDIT_READINESS.md) §\"Audit completion status\" is updated with the A2 row populated.\n- `CHANGELOG.md` carries a disclosure entry referencing the report.\n\nA verdict of `BLOCKED` keeps **mainnet deployment of any Phase 4 contract** paused per [`../README.md`](../README.md) §4 and blocks the corresponding Track F activation work (F3 / F4 / F5).\n\n---\n\n## 10. Purpose\n\nThis directory tracks every **external security engagement** performed on the TONBANKCARD protocol. It is the canonical location for:\n\n- Audit engagement plans (RFP-style)\n- Auditor selection records\n- Frozen audit packages handed over to auditors\n- Audit reports as delivered by external firms\n- Remediation pull requests and re-audit attestations\n- Public disclosure artifacts\n\nInternal pre-audit reviews (such as [`audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md`](../../../audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md)) and the system-level audit ([`docs/audit/FULL_SYSTEM_AUDIT.md`](../../audit/FULL_SYSTEM_AUDIT.md)) live elsewhere — this directory is reserved for **third-party** engagements that gate mainnet deployment.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Directory Layout\n\n```\ndocs/security/audits/\n├── README.md                       — This index\n├── REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md         — How findings are triaged, fixed, and verified\n├── REPORT_TEMPLATE.md              — Canonical layout for incoming audit reports\n└── A1-core-contracts/              — Issue #112 engagement\n    ├── ENGAGEMENT.md               — Scope, deliverables, candidate firms, evaluation matrix\n    └── STATUS.md                   — Live state of the engagement (firm, dates, findings)\n```\n\nFuture engagements (A2 Phase 4 contracts, A4 off-chain pentest, etc.) are added as sibling folders named after the roadmap ID.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Engagement Index\n\n| ID | Scope | Roadmap | Issue | Status | Firm | Report |\n|----|-------|---------|-------|--------|------|--------|\n| **A1** | Core contracts (PaymentHub, MerchantPaymentHub, account-locks, nft-resolver, collateral signal) | [A1](../../../TEMP/DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md) | [#112](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/112) | Engagement preparation complete — awaiting firm selection | — | — |\n| A2 | Phase 4 contracts (CrossChainBridge, MultiSigCard, RecurringPayments, LendingProtocolCoordinator) | A2 | TBD | Not started | — | — |\n| A4 | Off-chain services (`api/`, `backend/`, `sdk/`) | A4 | TBD | Not started | — | — |\n| A5 | Bug bounty program | A5 | TBD | Not started | — | — |\n\nWhen a new external engagement begins, copy `A1-core-contracts/` as a starting template, update its `ENGAGEMENT.md` for the new scope, and add a row to this table.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Gating Rules\n\nThe following rules are **non-negotiable** and apply to every engagement listed in §3:\n\n1. **No mainnet deployment** of any in-scope contract before the corresponding audit report is published and remediation is verified by the auditor.\n2. **Critical findings:** zero tolerance — every Critical must be remediated and re-verified before sign-off.\n3. **High findings:** remediated, or formally accepted with rationale signed off by the maintainers in `STATUS.md`.\n4. **Medium findings:** remediated or documented as accepted risk in `docs/audit-notes.md`.\n5. **Audit report is public** — published in this directory and linked from `docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md`.\n6. **Frozen scope** — once an engagement is signed, the contract set under audit is frozen at a specific commit (see [`audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md`](../../../audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md)).\n\n---\n\n## 5. Where Auditors Should Start\n\nExternal auditors engaging with TONBANKCARD should read, in order:\n\n1. [`docs/audit/external-audit-intro.md`](../../audit/external-audit-intro.md) — protocol intent and constraints\n2. [`audit/SCOPE.md`](../../../audit/SCOPE.md) — contracts in scope, focus areas\n3. [`audit/INVARIANTS.md`](../../../audit/INVARIANTS.md) — formal invariants I1–I7\n4. [`audit/THREAT_MODEL.md`](../../../audit/THREAT_MODEL.md) — attack vectors and mitigations\n5. [`audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md`](../../../audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md) — frozen commit, compiler versions\n6. [`audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md`](../../../audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md) — reproducible build\n7. [`audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md`](../../../audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md) — known findings from internal pre-audit\n8. Engagement-specific `ENGAGEMENT.md` in the relevant subdirectory\n\nThe [`docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md`](../AUDIT_READINESS.md) document is the navigation hub for all of the above.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Purpose\n\nThis directory tracks every **external security engagement** performed on the TONBANKCARD protocol. It is the canonical location for:\n\n- Audit engagement plans (RFP-style)\n- Auditor selection records\n- Frozen audit packages handed over to auditors\n- Audit reports as delivered by external firms\n- Remediation pull requests and re-audit attestations\n- Public disclosure artifacts\n\nInternal pre-audit reviews (such as [`audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md`](../../../audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md)) and the system-level audit ([`docs/audit/FULL_SYSTEM_AUDIT.md`](../../audit/FULL_SYSTEM_AUDIT.md)) live elsewhere — this directory is reserved for **third-party** engagements that gate mainnet deployment.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Directory Layout\n\n```\ndocs/security/audits/\n├── README.md                       — This index\n├── REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md         — How findings are triaged, fixed, and verified\n├── REPORT_TEMPLATE.md              — Canonical layout for incoming audit reports\n├── A1-core-contracts/              — Issue #112 engagement\n│   ├── ENGAGEMENT.md               — Scope, deliverables, candidate firms, evaluation matrix\n│   └── STATUS.md                   — Live state of the engagement (firm, dates, findings)\n└── A2-phase4-contracts/            — Issue #113 engagement (gated by A1 completion)\n    ├── ENGAGEMENT.md               — Phase 4 scope with dedicated cross-chain bridge review\n    └── STATUS.md                   — Live state, A1 upstream-gate tracker, threat-ID ledger\n```\n\nFuture engagements (A4 off-chain pentest, A5 bug bounty, etc.) are added as sibling folders named after the roadmap ID.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Engagement Index\n\n| ID | Scope | Roadmap | Issue | Status | Firm | Report |\n|----|-------|---------|-------|--------|------|--------|\n| **A1** | Core contracts (PaymentHub, MerchantPaymentHub, account-locks, nft-resolver, collateral signal) | [A1](../../../TEMP/DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md) | [#112](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/112) | Engagement preparation complete — awaiting firm selection | — | — |\n| A2 | Phase 4 contracts (CrossChainBridge, MultiSigCard, RecurringPayments, LendingProtocolCoordinator) | A2 | TBD | Not started | — | — |\n| A4 | Off-chain services (`api/`, `backend/`, `sdk/`) | A4 | TBD | Not started | — | — |\n| A5 | Bug bounty program | A5 | TBD | Not started | — | — |\n\nWhen a new external engagement begins, copy `A1-core-contracts/` as a starting template, update its `ENGAGEMENT.md` for the new scope, and add a row to this table.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Gating Rules\n\nThe following rules are **non-negotiable** and apply to every engagement listed in §3:\n\n1. **No mainnet deployment** of any in-scope contract before the corresponding audit report is published and remediation is verified by the auditor.\n2. **Critical findings:** zero tolerance — every Critical must be remediated and re-verified before sign-off.\n3. **High findings:** remediated, or formally accepted with rationale signed off by the maintainers in `STATUS.md`.\n4. **Medium findings:** remediated or documented as accepted risk in `docs/audit-notes.md`.\n5. **Audit report is public** — published in this directory and linked from `docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md`.\n6. **Frozen scope** — once an engagement is signed, the contract set under audit is frozen at a specific commit (see [`audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md`](../../../audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md)).\n\n---\n\n## 5. Where Auditors Should Start\n\nExternal auditors engaging with TONBANKCARD should read, in order:\n\n1. [`docs/audit/external-audit-intro.md`](../../audit/external-audit-intro.md) — protocol intent and constraints\n2. [`audit/SCOPE.md`](../../../audit/SCOPE.md) — contracts in scope, focus areas\n3. [`audit/INVARIANTS.md`](../../../audit/INVARIANTS.md) — formal invariants I1–I7\n4. [`audit/THREAT_MODEL.md`](../../../audit/THREAT_MODEL.md) — attack vectors and mitigations\n5. [`audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md`](../../../audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md) — frozen commit, compiler versions\n6. [`audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md`](../../../audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md) — reproducible build\n7. [`audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md`](../../../audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md) — known findings from internal pre-audit\n8. Engagement-specific `ENGAGEMENT.md` in the relevant subdirectory\n\nThe [`docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md`](../AUDIT_READINESS.md) document is the navigation hub for all of the above.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Purpose\n\nThis directory tracks every **external security engagement** performed on the TONBANKCARD protocol. It is the canonical location for:\n\n- Audit engagement plans (RFP-style)\n- Auditor selection records\n- Frozen audit packages handed over to auditors\n- Audit reports as delivered by external firms\n- Remediation pull requests and re-audit attestations\n- Public disclosure artifacts\n\nInternal pre-audit reviews (such as [`audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md`](../../../audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md)) and the system-level audit ([`docs/audit/FULL_SYSTEM_AUDIT.md`](../../audit/FULL_SYSTEM_AUDIT.md)) live elsewhere — this directory is reserved for **third-party** engagements that gate mainnet deployment.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Directory Layout\n\n```\ndocs/security/audits/\n├── README.md                       — This index\n├── REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md         — How findings are triaged, fixed, and verified\n├── REPORT_TEMPLATE.md              — Canonical layout for incoming audit reports\n├── A1-core-contracts/              — Issue #112 engagement\n│   ├── ENGAGEMENT.md               — Scope, deliverables, candidate firms, evaluation matrix\n│   └── STATUS.md                   — Live state of the engagement (firm, dates, findings)\n└── A2-phase4-contracts/            — Issue #113 engagement (gated by A1 completion)\n    ├── ENGAGEMENT.md               — Phase 4 scope with dedicated cross-chain bridge review\n    └── STATUS.md                   — Live state, A1 upstream-gate tracker, threat-ID ledger\n```\n\nFuture engagements (A4 off-chain pentest, A5 bug bounty, etc.) are added as sibling folders named after the roadmap ID.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Engagement Index\n\n| ID | Scope | Roadmap | Issue | Status | Firm | Report |\n|----|-------|---------|-------|--------|------|--------|\n| **A1** | Core contracts (PaymentHub, MerchantPaymentHub, account-locks, nft-resolver, collateral signal) | [A1](../../../TEMP/DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md) | [#112](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/112) | Engagement preparation complete — awaiting firm selection | — | — |\n| **A2** | Phase 4 contracts (CrossChainBridge, MultiSigCard, RecurringPayments, LendingProtocolCoordinator) | [A2](../../../TEMP/DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md) | [#113](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/113) | Engagement preparation complete — awaiting A1 completion and firm selection | — | — |\n| A4 | Off-chain services (`api/`, `backend/`, `sdk/`) | A4 | TBD | Not started | — | — |\n| A5 | Bug bounty program | A5 | TBD | Not started | — | — |\n\nWhen a new external engagement begins, copy `A1-core-contracts/` as a starting template, update its `ENGAGEMENT.md` for the new scope, and add a row to this table.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Gating Rules\n\nThe following rules are **non-negotiable** and apply to every engagement listed in §3:\n\n1. **No mainnet deployment** of any in-scope contract before the corresponding audit report is published and remediation is verified by the auditor.\n2. **Critical findings:** zero tolerance — every Critical must be remediated and re-verified before sign-off.\n3. **High findings:** remediated, or formally accepted with rationale signed off by the maintainers in `STATUS.md`.\n4. **Medium findings:** remediated or documented as accepted risk in `docs/audit-notes.md`.\n5. **Audit report is public** — published in this directory and linked from `docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md`.\n6. **Frozen scope** — once an engagement is signed, the contract set under audit is frozen at a specific commit (see [`audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md`](../../../audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md)).\n\n---\n\n## 5. Where Auditors Should Start\n\nExternal auditors engaging with TONBANKCARD should read, in order:\n\n1. [`docs/audit/external-audit-intro.md`](../../audit/external-audit-intro.md) — protocol intent and constraints\n2. [`audit/SCOPE.md`](../../../audit/SCOPE.md) — contracts in scope, focus areas\n3. [`audit/INVARIANTS.md`](../../../audit/INVARIANTS.md) — formal invariants I1–I7\n4. [`audit/THREAT_MODEL.md`](../../../audit/THREAT_MODEL.md) — attack vectors and mitigations\n5. [`audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md`](../../../audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md) — frozen commit, compiler versions\n6. [`audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md`](../../../audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md) — reproducible build\n7. [`audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md`](../../../audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md) — known findings from internal pre-audit\n8. Engagement-specific `ENGAGEMENT.md` in the relevant subdirectory\n\nThe [`docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md`](../AUDIT_READINESS.md) document is the navigation hub for all of the above.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Any violation is a critical security finding.\n58\t\n59\t| ID | Invariant | Key Guarantee |\n60\t|----|-----------|---------------|\n61\t| **I1** | Non-Custodial Ownership | Only NFT owner can initiate fund transfers |\n62\t| **I2** | NFT = Account Authority | NFT ownership is the single source of truth for account control |\n63\t| **I3** | No Admin Fund Control | No privileged role can move user funds |\n64\t| **I4** | Atomic Transfers | All transfers are all-or-nothing; no partial state possible |\n65\t| **I5** | Ledger Conservation | Sum of all balances is preserved across all operations |\n66\t| **I6** | Lock ≠ Confiscation | Locks restrict outgoing transfers; they do not seize funds |\n67\t| **I7** | External Adapter Isolation | External providers cannot directly invoke protocol operations |\n68\t\n69\tFull formal definitions with contract-code mappings: [audit/INVARIANTS.md](../../audit/INVARIANTS.md)\n70\t\n71\t---\n72\t\n73\t## Test Coverage Summary\n74\t\n75\t| Contract | Estimated Line Coverage | Estimated Branch Coverage |\n76\t|----------|------------------------|--------------------------|\n77\t| MerchantPaymentHub.tact | ~90%+ | ~85%+ |\n78\t| PaymentHub.tact | ~85%+ | ~80%+ |\n79\t| account-locks.fc | ~85%+ | ~80%+ |\n80\t| nft_account_resolver.fc | ~80%+ | ~75%+ |\n81\t| account-state.tact | ~90%+ | ~85%+ |\n82\t\n83\tTo obtain exact figures:\n84\t\n85\t```bash\n86\tgit checkout eb5dd593248a33a5a7517ae59b840827c140906a\n87\tnpm install\n88\tnpx blueprint test --coverage\n89\t```\n90\t\n91\tSee [audit/TEST_COVERAGE_REPORT.md](../../audit/TEST_COVERAGE_REPORT.md) for full test organization.\n92\t\n93\t---\n94\t\n95\t## Critical Audit Focus Areas\n96\t\n97\t### 1. No Admin Fund Control (MUST verify)\n98\t\n99\tSearch the entire contract codebase for `withdraw`, `drain`, `emergency`, `admin_transfer`, `force_transfer`. Expected result: **zero matches** in fund-moving contexts.\n100\t\n101\tAdmin roles exist (`risk_authority`, `lending_adapter`) but are limited to setting/clearing lock flags. They cannot move funds.\n102\t\n103\t### 2. NFT Ownership Enforcement (MUST verify)\n104\t\n105\tEvery fund-moving operation must verify the caller is the current on-chain NFT owner. No cached ownership. No secondary authorization paths.\n106\t\n107\t### 3. Atomic Balance Updates (MUST verify)\n108\t\n109\tAll balance modifications must be atomic — both debit and credit in the same transaction. Reentrancy protection must be verified at:\n110\t- `PaymentHub.tact` lines 149–150 (reentrancy guard)\n111\t- `PaymentHub.tact` lines 196–202 (`executeTransfer`)\n112\t\n113\t### 4. Lock Enforcement (MUST verify)\n114\t\n115\tLocks prevent sending but must never seize funds. Verify:\n116\t- `account-locks.fc` `can_receive()` always returns 1\n117\t- Lock operations do not modify balances\n118\t- FRAUD_LOCK and COLLATERAL_LOCK both correctly gate `can_send()`\n119\t\n120\t### 5. No Upgrade Paths (MUST verify)\n121\t\n122\tContracts are immutable. No upgradeable proxy patterns. No `setAdmin()` paths that could change invariants.\n123\t\n124\t---\n125\t\n126\t## Known Limitations (Auditor Notice)\n127\t\n128\t| Limitation | Severity | Description |\n129\t|------------|----------|-------------|\n130\t| Invoice replay (off-chain only) | MEDIUM | Contract does not enforce invoice uniqueness on-chain; handled off-chain |\n131\t| DAO unlock not implemented | LOW | FROZEN → ACTIVE transition requires future DAO governance |\n132\t| Lending unlock not implemented | LOW | COLLATERAL_LOCKED → ACTIVE requires Lending Adapter (not yet deployed) |\n133\t| NFT ownership integration (partial) | MEDIUM | Some contracts rely on calling contract for ownership check |\n134\t| Single admin key (temporary) | HIGH | Admin key is single-key pending multi-sig migration (Q1 2026) |\n135\t\n136\tThese are documented accepted risks. Any violation is a critical security finding.\n\n| ID | Invariant | Key Guarantee |\n|----|-----------|---------------|\n| **I1** | Non-Custodial Ownership | Only NFT owner can initiate fund transfers |\n| **I2** | NFT = Account Authority | NFT ownership is the single source of truth for account control |\n| **I3** | No Admin Fund Control | No privileged role can move user funds |\n| **I4** | Atomic Transfers | All transfers are all-or-nothing; no partial state possible |\n| **I5** | Ledger Conservation | Sum of all balances is preserved across all operations |\n| **I6** | Lock ≠ Confiscation | Locks restrict outgoing transfers; they do not seize funds |\n| **I7** | External Adapter Isolation | External providers cannot directly invoke protocol operations |\n\nFull formal definitions with contract-code mappings: [audit/INVARIANTS.md](../../audit/INVARIANTS.md)\n\n---\n\n## Test Coverage Summary\n\n| Contract | Estimated Line Coverage | Estimated Branch Coverage |\n|----------|------------------------|--------------------------|\n| MerchantPaymentHub.tact | ~90%+ | ~85%+ |\n| PaymentHub.tact | ~85%+ | ~80%+ |\n| account-locks.fc | ~85%+ | ~80%+ |\n| nft_account_resolver.fc | ~80%+ | ~75%+ |\n| account-state.tact | ~90%+ | ~85%+ |\n\nTo obtain exact figures:\n\n```bash\ngit checkout eb5dd593248a33a5a7517ae59b840827c140906a\nnpm install\nnpx blueprint test --coverage\n```\n\nSee [audit/TEST_COVERAGE_REPORT.md](../../audit/TEST_COVERAGE_REPORT.md) for full test organization.\n\n---\n\n## Critical Audit Focus Areas\n\n### 1. No Admin Fund Control (MUST verify)\n\nSearch the entire contract codebase for `withdraw`, `drain`, `emergency`, `admin_transfer`, `force_transfer`. Expected result: **zero matches** in fund-moving contexts.\n\nAdmin roles exist (`risk_authority`, `lending_adapter`) but are limited to setting/clearing lock flags. They cannot move funds.\n\n### 2. NFT Ownership Enforcement (MUST verify)\n\nEvery fund-moving operation must verify the caller is the current on-chain NFT owner. No cached ownership. No secondary authorization paths.\n\n### 3. Atomic Balance Updates (MUST verify)\n\nAll balance modifications must be atomic — both debit and credit in the same transaction. Reentrancy protection must be verified at:\n- `PaymentHub.tact` lines 149–150 (reentrancy guard)\n- `PaymentHub.tact` lines 196–202 (`executeTransfer`)\n\n### 4. Lock Enforcement (MUST verify)\n\nLocks prevent sending but must never seize funds. Verify:\n- `account-locks.fc` `can_receive()` always returns 1\n- Lock operations do not modify balances\n- FRAUD_LOCK and COLLATERAL_LOCK both correctly gate `can_send()`\n\n### 5. No Upgrade Paths (MUST verify)\n\nContracts are immutable. No upgradeable proxy patterns. No `setAdmin()` paths that could change invariants.\n\n---\n\n## Known Limitations (Auditor Notice)\n\n| Limitation | Severity | Description |\n|------------|----------|-------------|\n| Invoice replay (off-chain only) | MEDIUM | Contract does not enforce invoice uniqueness on-chain; handled off-chain |\n| DAO unlock not implemented | LOW | FROZEN → ACTIVE transition requires future DAO governance |\n| Lending unlock not implemented | LOW | COLLATERAL_LOCKED → ACTIVE requires Lending Adapter (not yet deployed) |\n| NFT ownership integration (partial) | MEDIUM | Some contracts rely on calling contract for ownership check |\n| Single admin key (temporary) | HIGH | Admin key is single-key pending multi-sig migration (Q1 2026) |\n\nThese are documented accepted risks. Full details in [docs/audit-notes.md](../audit-notes.md).\n\n---\n\n## Auditor Engagement Process\n\n### Access\n\n- Repository: `https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol`\n- Audit freeze commit: `eb5dd593248a33a5a7517ae59b840827c140906a`\n- Build instructions: [audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md](../../audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md)\n- Contact for questions: via GitHub issues tagged `audit`\n\n### Scope Confirmation\n\nBefore beginning, auditors must confirm:\n- Which contracts are in scope (see [audit/SCOPE.md](../../audit/SCOPE.md))\n- Which compiler versions to use (see [audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md](../../audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md))\n- Which invariants to verify (see [audit/INVARIANTS.md](../../audit/INVARIANTS.md))\n\n### Expected Deliverables\n\n| Deliverable | Description |\n|-------------|-------------|\n| Audit Report | Findings categorized by severity (Critical, High, Medium, Low, Informational) |\n| Finding References | Each finding references specific invariant(s) and contract line(s) |\n| Reproduction Steps | Each finding includes steps to reproduce |\n| Suggested Fixes | Where applicable |\n| Invariant Attestation | Statement on whether each of I1–I7 holds |\n\nThe end-to-end engagement workflow (intake → triage → remediation → re-verification → disclosure) is canonicalised in [docs/security/audits/REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md](./audits/REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md). It serves as a navigation guide for external auditors and internal reviewers approaching the protocol for the first time.\n\nFor the complete frozen audit package (used by external auditors), see the [`audit/`](../../audit/) directory.\n\n---\n\n## Audit Package Location\n\nThe pre-audit package is located at:\n\n```\naudit/\n├── SCOPE.md              — Audit boundaries, focus areas, and contract inventory\n├── THREAT_MODEL.md       — Threat classes, attack vectors, and mitigations\n├── INVARIANTS.md         — Formal invariants with contract-code mapping\n├── FREEZE_METADATA.md    — Git hash, compiler versions, file checksums\n├── BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md — How to reproduce builds and run tests\n└── TEST_COVERAGE_REPORT.md — Coverage data and test organization\n```\n\n**Freeze status:** The audit package was frozen at commit `4027b9d` (2025-12-29). No contract logic changes are permitted to the frozen set. See [audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md](../../audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md).\n\n---\n\n## Contracts Under Audit\n\nFull details in [audit/SCOPE.md](../../audit/SCOPE.md). Summary:\n\n| Contract | File | Priority | Lines | Primary Concern |\n|----------|------|----------|-------|-----------------|\n| MerchantPaymentHub | `contracts/MerchantPaymentHub.tact` | Critical | 287 | Payment settlement, ownership, locks |\n| PaymentHub | `contracts/payments/PaymentHub.tact` | Critical | 355 | Internal transfers, atomicity |\n| NFT Account Resolver | `contracts/nft-resolver/nft_account_resolver.fc` | Critical | 149 | Ownership resolution |\n| NFT Account Resolver | `contracts/nft-resolver/nft_account_resolver.tact` | Critical | 121 | Ownership resolution (Tact wrapper) |\n| Account State Machine | `contracts/payment-hub/account-state.tact` | Critical | 285 | State management, balance integrity |\n| Account Locks | `contracts/payments/account-locks.fc` | High | 269 | Lock authorization, lock semantics |\n\n**Total lines under audit:** 1,466 (critical) + 269 (high) = **1,735 lines**\n\n---\n\n## Protocol Invariants\n\nSeven formal invariants define the protocol's security guarantees. Any violation is a critical security finding.\n\n| ID | Invariant | Key Guarantee |\n|----|-----------|---------------|\n| **I1** | Non-Custodial Ownership | Only NFT owner can initiate fund transfers |\n| **I2** | NFT = Account Authority | NFT ownership is the single source of truth for account control |\n| **I3** | No Admin Fund Control | No privileged role can move user funds |\n| **I4** | Atomic Transfers | All transfers are all-or-nothing; no partial state possible |\n| **I5** | Ledger Conservation | Sum of all balances is preserved across all operations |\n| **I6** | Lock ≠ Confiscation | Locks restrict outgoing transfers; they do not seize funds |\n| **I7** | External Adapter Isolation | External providers cannot directly invoke protocol operations |\n\nFull formal definitions with contract-code mappings: [audit/INVARIANTS.md](../../audit/INVARIANTS.md)\n\n---\n\n## Test Coverage Summary\n\n| Contract | Estimated Line Coverage | Estimated Branch Coverage |\n|----------|------------------------|--------------------------|\n| MerchantPaymentHub.tact | ~90%+ | ~85%+ |\n| PaymentHub.tact | ~85%+ | ~80%+ |\n| account-locks.fc | ~85%+ | ~80%+ |\n| nft_account_resolver.fc | ~80%+ | ~75%+ |\n| account-state.tact | ~90%+ | ~85%+ |\n\nTo obtain exact figures:\n\n```bash\ngit checkout eb5dd593248a33a5a7517ae59b840827c140906a\nnpm install\nnpx blueprint test --coverage\n```\n\nSee [audit/TEST_COVERAGE_REPORT.md](../../audit/TEST_COVERAGE_REPORT.md) for full test organization.\n\n---\n\n## Critical Audit Focus Areas\n\n### 1. No Admin Fund Control (MUST verify)\n\nSearch the entire contract codebase for `withdraw`, `drain`, `emergency`, `admin_transfer`, `force_transfer`. Expected result: **zero matches** in fund-moving contexts.\n\nAdmin roles exist (`risk_authority`, `lending_adapter`) but are limited to setting/clearing lock flags. They cannot move funds.\n\n### 2. NFT Ownership Enforcement (MUST verify)\n\nEvery fund-moving operation must verify the caller is the current on-chain NFT owner. No cached ownership. No secondary authorization paths.\n\n### 3. Atomic Balance Updates (MUST verify)\n\nAll balance modifications must be atomic — both debit and credit in the same transaction. Reentrancy protection must be verified at:\n- `PaymentHub.tact` lines 149–150 (reentrancy guard)\n- `PaymentHub.tact` lines 196–202 (`executeTransfer`)\n\n### 4. Lock Enforcement (MUST verify)\n\nLocks prevent sending but must never seize funds. Verify:\n- `account-locks.fc` `can_receive()` always returns 1\n- Lock operations do not modify balances\n- FRAUD_LOCK and COLLATERAL_LOCK both correctly gate `can_send()`\n\n### 5. No Upgrade Paths (MUST verify)\n\nContracts are immutable. No upgradeable proxy patterns. No `setAdmin()` paths that could change invariants.\n\n---\n\n## Known Limitations (Auditor Notice)\n\n| Limitation | Severity | Description |\n|------------|----------|-------------|\n| Invoice replay (off-chain only) | MEDIUM | Contract does not enforce invoice uniqueness on-chain; handled off-chain |\n| DAO unlock not implemented | LOW | FROZEN → ACTIVE transition requires future DAO governance |\n| Lending unlock not implemented | LOW | COLLATERAL_LOCKED → ACTIVE requires Lending Adapter (not yet deployed) |\n| NFT ownership integration (partial) | MEDIUM | Some contracts rely on calling contract for ownership check |\n| Single admin key (temporary) | HIGH | Admin key is single-key pending multi-sig migration (Q1 2026) |\n\nThese are documented accepted risks. Full details in [docs/audit-notes.md](../audit-notes.md).\n\n---\n\n## Auditor Engagement Process\n\n### Access\n\n- Repository: `https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol`\n- Audit freeze commit: `eb5dd593248a33a5a7517ae59b840827c140906a`\n- Build instructions: [audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md](../../audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md)\n- Contact for questions: via GitHub issues tagged `audit`\n\n### Scope Confirmation\n\nBefore beginning, auditors must confirm:\n- Which contracts are in scope (see [audit/SCOPE.md](../../audit/SCOPE.md))\n- Which compiler versions to use (see [audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md](../../audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md))\n- Which invariants to verify (see [audit/INVARIANTS.md](../../audit/INVARIANTS.md))\n\n### Expected Deliverables\n\n| Deliverable | Description |\n|-------------|-------------|\n| Audit Report | Findings categorized by severity (Critical, High, Medium, Low, Informational) |\n| Finding References | Each finding references specific invariant(s) and contract line(s) |\n| Reproduction Steps | Each finding includes steps to reproduce |\n| Suggested Fixes | Where applicable |\n| Invariant Attestation | Statement on whether each of I1–I7 holds |\n\nThe end-to-end engagement workflow (intake → triage → remediation → re-verification → disclosure) is canonicalised in [docs/security/audits/REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md](./audits/REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md). It serves as a navigation guide for external auditors and internal reviewers approaching the protocol for the first time.\n\nFor the complete frozen audit package (used by external auditors), see the [`audit/`](../../audit/) directory.\n\n---\n\n## Audit Package Location\n\nThe pre-audit package is located at:\n\n```\naudit/\n├── SCOPE.md              — Audit boundaries, focus areas, and contract inventory\n├── THREAT_MODEL.md       — Threat classes, attack vectors, and mitigations\n├── INVARIANTS.md         — Formal invariants with contract-code mapping\n├── FREEZE_METADATA.md    — Git hash, compiler versions, file checksums\n├── BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md — How to reproduce builds and run tests\n└── TEST_COVERAGE_REPORT.md — Coverage data and test organization\n```\n\n**Freeze status:** The audit package was frozen at commit `4027b9d` (2025-12-29). Summary:\n\n| Contract | File | Priority | Lines | Primary Concern |\n|----------|------|----------|-------|-----------------|\n| MerchantPaymentHub | `contracts/MerchantPaymentHub.tact` | Critical | 287 | Payment settlement, ownership, locks |\n| PaymentHub | `contracts/payments/PaymentHub.tact` | Critical | 355 | Internal transfers, atomicity |\n| NFT Account Resolver | `contracts/nft-resolver/nft_account_resolver.fc` | Critical | 149 | Ownership resolution |\n| NFT Account Resolver | `contracts/nft-resolver/nft_account_resolver.tact` | Critical | 121 | Ownership resolution (Tact wrapper) |\n| Account State Machine | `contracts/payment-hub/account-state.tact` | Critical | 285 | State management, balance integrity |\n| Account Locks | `contracts/payments/account-locks.fc` | High | 269 | Lock authorization, lock semantics |\n\n**Total lines under audit:** 1,466 (critical) + 269 (high) = **1,735 lines**\n\n---\n\n## Protocol Invariants\n\nSeven formal invariants define the protocol's security guarantees. Any violation is a critical security finding.\n\n| ID | Invariant | Key Guarantee |\n|----|-----------|---------------|\n| **I1** | Non-Custodial Ownership | Only NFT owner can initiate fund transfers |\n| **I2** | NFT = Account Authority | NFT ownership is the single source of truth for account control |\n| **I3** | No Admin Fund Control | No privileged role can move user funds |\n| **I4** | Atomic Transfers | All transfers are all-or-nothing; no partial state possible |\n| **I5** | Ledger Conservation | Sum of all balances is preserved across all operations |\n| **I6** | Lock ≠ Confiscation | Locks restrict outgoing transfers; they do not seize funds |\n| **I7** | External Adapter Isolation | External providers cannot directly invoke protocol operations |\n\nFull formal definitions with contract-code mappings: [audit/INVARIANTS.md](../../audit/INVARIANTS.md)\n\n---\n\n## Test Coverage Summary\n\n| Contract | Estimated Line Coverage | Estimated Branch Coverage |\n|----------|------------------------|--------------------------|\n| MerchantPaymentHub.tact | ~90%+ | ~85%+ |\n| PaymentHub.tact | ~85%+ | ~80%+ |\n| account-locks.fc | ~85%+ | ~80%+ |\n| nft_account_resolver.fc | ~80%+ | ~75%+ |\n| account-state.tact | ~90%+ | ~85%+ |\n\nTo obtain exact figures:\n\n```bash\ngit checkout eb5dd593248a33a5a7517ae59b840827c140906a\nnpm install\nnpx blueprint test --coverage\n```\n\nSee [audit/TEST_COVERAGE_REPORT.md](../../audit/TEST_COVERAGE_REPORT.md) for full test organization.\n\n---\n\n## Critical Audit Focus Areas\n\n### 1. No Admin Fund Control (MUST verify)\n\nSearch the entire contract codebase for `withdraw`, `drain`, `emergency`, `admin_transfer`, `force_transfer`. Expected result: **zero matches** in fund-moving contexts.\n\nAdmin roles exist (`risk_authority`, `lending_adapter`) but are limited to setting/clearing lock flags. They cannot move funds.\n\n### 2. NFT Ownership Enforcement (MUST verify)\n\nEvery fund-moving operation must verify the caller is the current on-chain NFT owner. No cached ownership. No secondary authorization paths.\n\n### 3. Atomic Balance Updates (MUST verify)\n\nAll balance modifications must be atomic — both debit and credit in the same transaction. Reentrancy protection must be verified at:\n- `PaymentHub.tact` lines 149–150 (reentrancy guard)\n- `PaymentHub.tact` lines 196–202 (`executeTransfer`)\n\n### 4. Lock Enforcement (MUST verify)\n\nLocks prevent sending but must never seize funds. Verify:\n- `account-locks.fc` `can_receive()` always returns 1\n- Lock operations do not modify balances\n- FRAUD_LOCK and COLLATERAL_LOCK both correctly gate `can_send()`\n\n### 5. No Upgrade Paths (MUST verify)\n\nContracts are immutable. No upgradeable proxy patterns. No `setAdmin()` paths that could change invariants.\n\n---\n\n## Known Limitations (Auditor Notice)\n\n| Limitation | Severity | Description |\n|------------|----------|-------------|\n| Invoice replay (off-chain only) | MEDIUM | Contract does not enforce invoice uniqueness on-chain; handled off-chain |\n| DAO unlock not implemented | LOW | FROZEN → ACTIVE transition requires future DAO governance |\n| Lending unlock not implemented | LOW | COLLATERAL_LOCKED → ACTIVE requires Lending Adapter (not yet deployed) |\n| NFT ownership integration (partial) | MEDIUM | Some contracts rely on calling contract for ownership check |\n| Single admin key (temporary) | HIGH | Admin key is single-key pending multi-sig migration (Q1 2026) |\n\nThese are documented accepted risks. Full details in [docs/audit-notes.md](../audit-notes.md).\n\n---\n\n## Auditor Engagement Process\n\n### Access\n\n- Repository: `https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol`\n- Audit freeze commit: `eb5dd593248a33a5a7517ae59b840827c140906a`\n- Build instructions: [audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md](../../audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md)\n- Contact for questions: via GitHub issues tagged `audit`\n\n### Scope Confirmation\n\nBefore beginning, auditors must confirm:\n- Which contracts are in scope (see [audit/SCOPE.md](../../audit/SCOPE.md))\n- Which compiler versions to use (see [audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md](../../audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md))\n- Which invariants to verify (see [audit/INVARIANTS.md](../../audit/INVARIANTS.md))\n\n### Expected Deliverables\n\n| Deliverable | Description |\n|-------------|-------------|\n| Audit Report | Findings categorized by severity (Critical, High, Medium, Low, Informational) |\n| Finding References | Each finding references specific invariant(s) and contract line(s) |\n| Reproduction Steps | Each finding includes steps to reproduce |\n| Suggested Fixes | Where applicable |\n| Invariant Attestation | Statement on whether each of I1–I7 holds |\n\nThe end-to-end engagement workflow (intake → triage → remediation → re-verification → disclosure) is canonicalised in [docs/security/audits/REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md](./audits/REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md). At minimum, produce property-based tests integrated into CI for the two highest-risk invariants: I4 (atomic transfers) and I7 (lock enforcement).\n\n## 2. Context\n\nThe protocol defines seven correctness invariants in `docs/invariants.md`. These invariants are currently verified by manual code review and functional tests. Formal verification (TLA+, Lean 4) or machine-checked property tests would provide a higher assurance level and are required before the protocol can claim production-grade security.\n\nThis task can be pursued in parallel with Track B but should be completed before DAO governance activation (E1).\n\nRelated to: [DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md — Track A, A3](../TEMP/DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md)\n\n## 3. In Scope\n\nAll seven protocol invariants from `docs/invariants.md`:\n\n| ID | Invariant |\n|----|-----------|\n| I1 | **Non-Custodial**: Only the NFT owner can initiate transfers |\n| I2 | **NFT Authority**: NFT ownership is the sole account authority |\n| I3 | **No Admin Control**: The deployer cannot move user funds |\n| I4 | **Atomic Transfers**: All fund operations are all-or-nothing |\n| I5 | **Ledger Conservation**: No fees for internal TBC transfers |\n| I6 | **State Integrity**: Account state transitions follow valid state machine rules |\n| I7 | **Lock Enforcement**: Locked accounts cannot initiate sends |\n\n**Minimum deliverable**: Property-based tests for I4 and I7 integrated into CI.\n**Stretch goal**: TLA+ or Lean 4 formal proofs for I1, I3, I4, I7.\n\n## 4. Out of Scope\n\n- Formal verification of Phase 4 contract-specific logic (bridge replay, multi-sig quorum)\n- Economic invariants (fee structure, DEX pricing)\n- Off-chain service correctness\n\n## 5. Functional Requirements\n\n1. For each invariant, produce at minimum:\n   - A clear, formal statement of the invariant (predicate form)\n   - Property-based test cases that attempt to violate the invariant\n   - CI integration so violations are caught automatically\n\n2. For I4 (atomicity) and I7 (lock enforcement):\n   - Adversarial test scenarios in `tests/adversarial/`\n   - Tests cover: message reordering, partial execution, lock bypass attempts\n\n3. For TLA+/Lean 4 formal proofs (stretch):\n   - Model covers the state machine defined in `docs/invariants.md`\n   - Proofs checked by TLC (TLA+) or Lean 4 type checker\n   - Proof artifacts stored in `docs/formal-verification/`\n\n4. For Acton/Tolk-based testing:\n   - Evaluate Acton through D6 before adopting it as required tooling\n   - If D6 approves adoption, use Acton fuzz or mutation testing only for Tolk prototypes or migrated contract modules\n   - Keep the current Tact/FunC test path authoritative until a migration decision is accepted\n\n## 6. Non-Functional Requirements\n\n- Property tests must complete in < 60 seconds per invariant in CI\n- Formal proofs must be reproducible in a clean environment\n- All test tooling must be documented in `CONTRIBUTING.md`\n\n## 7. Security Requirements\n\n- Adversarial test cases must include: replay attacks, race conditions, double-spend attempts\n- Property tests must use randomized inputs (not just happy-path values)\n- False positives in property tests are unacceptable — each failure must represent a real violation\n\n## 8. Acceptance Criteria\n\n- [ ] Formal predicate statement written for each of I1–I7\n- [ ] Property-based test suite created in `tests/invariants/` covering I1–I7\n- [ ] Adversarial tests for I4 and I7 in `tests/adversarial/`\n- [ ] All property tests passing in CI (`npm test` in root)\n- [ ] (Stretch) TLA+ or Lean 4 proofs for I1, I3, I4, I7 stored in `docs/formal-verification/`\n- [ ] Documentation updated in `docs/invariants.md` with proof status per invariant\n\n## 9.    [solve worker-1]         "content": "1\t# TONBANKCARD Protocol — Formal Invariants & Guarantees\n2\t\n3\t**Document Type:** Security Foundation\n4\t**Status:** Formal Specification\n5\t**Issue Reference:** [#18 - Issue 4.1 Formal Invariants & Protocol Guarantees](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/18)\n6\t**Last Updated:** 2025-12-27\n7\t\n8\t---\n9\t\n10\t## Purpose\n11\t\n12\tThis document defines the **core invariants and guarantees** of the TONBANKCARD protocol. These invariants are non-negotiable rules that must always hold true across all smart contracts, adapters, and future extensions.\n13\t\n14\tThese invariants form the basis for:\n15\t- Security audits\n16\t- Formal verification\n17\t- Governance decisions\n18\t- Ecosystem integrations\n19\t\n20\t**Any violation of these invariants represents a critical security vulnerability.**\n21\t\n22\t---\n23\t\n24\t## Core Protocol Invariants\n25\t\n26\t### I1 — Non-Custodial Ownership\n27\t\n28\t**Statement:**\n29\t> At no point may the protocol take custody of user funds, move funds without explicit user-initiated transactions, or override NFT ownership.\n30\t\n31\t**Formal Definition:**\n32\t```\n33\t∀ transaction T, ∀ user U:\n34\t  IF T transfers funds from U's account\n35\t  THEN T MUST be signed by U (the NFT owner)\n36\t  AND T MUST be initiated by U\n37\t  AND no protocol admin/operator can initiate T on behalf of U\n38\t```\n39\t\n40\t**Guaranteed Properties:**\n41\t- The owner of the NFT account is the sole authority over the associated on-chain balance\n42\t- No smart contract can move funds without the NFT owner's explicit signature\n43\t- No backend service can initiate fund transfers\n44\t- No external adapter can trigger fund movement\n45\t\n46\t**Implementation Requirements:**\n47\t1. All transfer functions MUST verify `msg.sender == NFT_owner`\n48\t2. No admin override functions are permitted\n49\t3. No proxy delegation to third parties for fund movement\n50\t4. Backend services are read-only\n51\t\n52\t**Contract Mapping:**\n53\t- `PaymentHub.tact`: Verifies ownership in `TransferInternalRequest` handler (line 164)\n54\t- `MerchantPaymentHub.tact`: Validates payer ownership before settlement (lines 90-96)\n55\t- `account-locks.fc`: Lock mechanisms do not move funds, only restrict operations\n56\t\n57\t**Test Coverage:**\n58\t- `tests/invariants/I1-non-custodial-ownership.spec.ts`\n59\t- Negative test: Attempt transfer from non-owner account\n60\t- Negative test: Admin attempting to move user funds\n61\t\n62\t---\n63\t\n64\t### I2 — NFT = Account Authority\n65\t\n66\t**Statement:**\n67\t> Each NFT represents exactly one account. Account control is transferred only via NFT transfer. No secondary ownership mechanisms are allowed.\n68\t\n69\t**Formal Definition:**\n70\t```\n71\t∀ NFT n, ∀ account a:\n72\t  account_authority(a) = NFT_owner(n)\n73\t  AND ∀ time t1, t2 where t2 > t1:\n74\t    IF NFT_owner(n, t1) ≠ NFT_owner(n, t2)\n75\t    THEN account_authority(a, t2) = NFT_owner(n, t2)\n76\t```\n77\t\n78\t**Guaranteed Properties:**\n79\t- NFT ownership is the single source of truth for account authority\n80\t- Account control transfers atomically with NFT ownership transfer\n81\t- No separate \"authorized users\" or \"delegates\" with fund control\n82\t- No multi-signature override without multi-sig NFT ownership\n83\t\n84\t**Implementation Requirements:**\n85\t1. Always query current NFT owner on-chain before operations\n86\t2. No cached ownership records for fund control decisions\n87\t3. NFT transfer automatically updates account authority\n88\t4. No separate authorization layer\n89\t\n90\t**Contract Mapping:**\n91\t- `PaymentHub.tact`: Uses `owner` field from `AccountState` (line 36)\n92\t- `MerchantPaymentHub.tact`: Stores and validates NFT owners (lines 42, 90-96)\n93\t- `nft_account_resolver.fc`: Resolves NFT ownership as authority source (lines 61-69)\n94\t\n95\t**Test Coverage:**\n96\t- `tests/invariants/I2-nft-account-authority.spec.ts`\n97\t- Test: NFT transfer updates account authority\n98\t- Negative test: Previous owner cannot transact after NFT transfer\n99\t\n100\t---\n101\t\n102\t### I3 — No Admin Fund Control\n103\t\n104\t**Statement:**\n105\t> The protocol must not contain admin withdrawals, emergency drains, privileged fund movement, or hidden upgrade paths.\n106\t\n107\t**Formal Definition:**\n108\t```\n109\t∀ role R in [admin, operator, risk_authority, lending_adapter]:\n110\t  ∀ account A:\n111\t    R CANNOT initiate fund transfer from A\n112\t    R CANNOT withdraw from A\n113\t    R CANNOT modify balance(A) except through user-initiated transfers\n114\t    R CANNOT upgrade contracts to bypass these restrictions\n115\t    R CAN transfer the admin role to another address only via the two-phase timelock\n116\t```\n117\t\n118\t**Guaranteed Properties:**\n119\t- No role other than the NFT owner can initiate fund transfers\n120\t- Admin roles (admin, risk authority, lending adapter) can only set flags/states\n121\t- No emergency withdrawal functions exist\n122\t- No upgradeable proxies that could bypass these rules\n123\t- Development/testing admin functions MUST be removed before production\n124\t- Admin role is transferable but ONLY via two-phase timelock (7-day delay)\n125\t- Admin role transfer does NOT affect user fund ownership or balances\n126\t\n127\t**Implementation Requirements:**\n128\t1. Admin roles limited to non-financial operations:\n129\t   - Admin: Whitelist NFT collections, initialize accounts (testing only)\n130\t   - Risk authority: Set/clear fraud locks only\n131\t   - Lending adapter: Set/clear collateral locks only\n132\t2. No `onlyAdmin` functions that move funds\n133\t3. No upgradeable proxy patterns\n134\t4. All contracts are immutable after deployment\n135\t\n136\t**Admin Transfer Mechanism (Issue #96):**\n137\t\n138\tTo prevent single-point-of-failure from the deployer key and allow migration to DAO/multisig, the `admin` role supports two-phase transferable ownership with a 7-day timelock:\n139\t\n140\t1. **Phase 1 — Propose** (`ProposeAdminTransfer` / `MerchantProposeAdminTransfer`):\n141\t   - Only the current admin can call this\n142\t   - Records the proposed new admin and a timestamp = `now() + 7 days`\n143\t   - Does NOT change admin immediately\n144\t2. **Phase 2 — Execute** (`ExecuteAdminTransfer` / `MerchantExecuteAdminTransfer`):\n145\t   - Only the proposed new admin can call this\n146\t   - Can only execute after the 7-day timelock has elapsed\n147\t   - Commits the admin change; clears the pending proposal\n148\t3. **Cancel** (`CancelAdminTransfer` / `MerchantCancelAdminTransfer`):\n149\t   - Only the current admin can cancel a pending proposal before it executes\n150\t\n151\tThe same two-phase timelock pattern applies to `risk_authority` and `lending_adapter` roles in `account-locks.fc` (op codes `0x4001`–`0x4013`).\n152\t\n153\t**Contract Mapping:**\n154\t- `PaymentHub.tact`: `admin` field replaces `deployer`; admin transfer via `ProposeAdminTransfer`/`ExecuteAdminTransfer`/`CancelAdminTransfer`\n155\t- `MerchantPaymentHub.tact`: Same pattern via `MerchantProposeAdminTransfer`/`MerchantExecuteAdminTransfer`/`MerchantCancelAdminTransfer`\n156\t- `account-locks.fc`: `risk_authority` and `lending_adapter` transferable via `op::propose_risk_authority` / `op::execute_risk_authority` / `op::cancel_risk_authority` and equivalents for `lending_adapter`\n157\t\n158\t**Test Coverage:**\n159\t- `tests/invariants/I3-no-admin-fund-control.spec.ts`\n160\t  - Negative test: Admin cannot withdraw user funds\n161\t  - Negative test: Risk authority cannot move funds\n162\t  - Negative test: Deployer cannot drain account balances\n163\t  - Positive test: Admin can propose a transfer\n164\t  - Negative test: Execution before timelock expiry is rejected\n165\t  - Positive test: Execution after timelock succeeds; user funds unchanged\n166\t  - Negative test: New admin cannot move user funds (I3 preserved post-transfer)\n167\t  - Positive test: Admin can cancel a pending transfer\n168\t- `tests/admin-transfer/PaymentHub-admin-transfer.spec.ts` — comprehensive admin transfer tests\n169\t- `tests/admin-transfer/MerchantPaymentHub-admin-transfer.spec.ts` — comprehensive admin transfer tests\n170\t\n171\t---\n172\t\n173\t### I4 — Atomic Transfers\n174\t\n175\t**Statement:**\n176\t> All internal transfers must be atomic, fully settled or reverted, and free from intermediate states.\n177\t\n178\t**Formal Definition:**\n179\t```\n180\t∀ transfer T from account A to account B with amount X:\n181\t  EITHER:\n182\t    (balance(A) = balance(A)_before - X) AND\n183\t    (balance(B) = balance(B)_before + X) AND\n184\t    (T.status = SUCCESS)\n185\t  OR:\n186\t    (balance(A) = balance(A)_before) AND\n187\t    (balance(B) = balance(B)_before) AND\n188\t    (T.status = REVERTED)\n189\t```\n190\t\n191\t**Guaranteed Properties:**\n192\t- A transfer either completes fully or does not occur at all\n193\t- No partial balance updates\n194\t- No intermediate states where funds are \"in flight\"\n195\t- Reentrancy protection ensures atomicity\n196\t\n197\t**Implementation Requirements:**\n198\t1. Use transaction revert on any validation failure\n199\t2. Update both sender and receiver balances in same transaction\n200\t3. Implement reentrancy guards\n201\t4. No asynchronous balance updates\n202\t\n203\t**Contract Mapping:**\n204\t- `PaymentHub.tact`: Atomic balance update (lines 196-202), reentrancy guard (lines 121, 149-150)\n205\t- `MerchantPaymentHub.tact`: Atomic debit/credit (lines 134-135)\n206\t\n207\t**Test Coverage:**\n208\t- `tests/invariants/I4-atomic-transfers.spec.ts`\n209\t- Test: Successful transfer updates both balances atomically\n210\t- Test: Failed transfer leaves both balances unchanged\n211\t- Test: Reentrancy attempt is blocked\n212\t\n213\t---\n214\t\n215\t### I5 — Ledger Conservation\n216\t\n217\t**Statement:**\n218\t> Internal ledger operations must satisfy: Σ(balances before) = Σ(balances after), except for protocol-defined fees (if any) or explicitly defined mint/burn logic.\n219\t\n220\t**Formal Definition:**\n221\t```\n222\t∀ transaction T:\n223\t  Σ(all_balances_after(T)) = Σ(all_balances_before(T)) - fees(T) - burns(T) + mints(T)\n224\t\n225\tWHERE:\n226\t  fees(T) = 0 for internal TBC transfers (zero-fee guarantee)\n227\t  burns(T) = 0 (no burn mechanism in current protocol)\n228\t  mints(T) = 0 (no mint mechanism in payment hub)\n229\t```\n230\t\n231\t**Guaranteed Properties:**\n232\t- Total TBC in the system is conserved during transfers\n233\t- No funds can be created or destroyed during transfers\n234\t- Internal transfers have zero fees\n235\t- Balance sum is an invariant across all operations\n236\t\n237\t**Implementation Requirements:**\n238\t1. Every debit MUST have a corresponding credit of equal amount\n239\t2. No rounding errors or precision loss\n240\t3. No hidden fees deducted from transfers\n241\t4. Explicit tracking of any future fee mechanisms\n242\t\n243\t**Contract Mapping:**\n244\t- `PaymentHub.tact`: Direct balance arithmetic (lines 197-198)\n245\t- `MerchantPaymentHub.tact`: Symmetric debit/credit (lines 178-187)\n246\t\n247\t**Test Coverage:**\n248\t- `tests/invariants/I5-ledger-conservation.spec.ts`\n249\t- Test: Sum of balances unchanged after transfer\n250\t- Test: Multiple concurrent transfers preserve total supply\n251\t- Test: Self-transfer does not create/destroy funds\n252\t\n253\t---\n254\t\n255\t### I6 — Lock ≠ Confiscation\n256\t\n257\t**Statement:**\n258\t> Account locks prevent outgoing transfers, do NOT seize or move funds, and are reversible.\n259\t\n260\t**Formal Definition:**\n261\t```\n262\t∀ account A, ∀ lock L in [FRAUD_LOCK, COLLATERAL_LOCK]:\n263\t  IF is_locked(A, L) THEN:\n264\t    can_send(A) = FALSE\n265\t    can_receive(A) = TRUE\n266\t    balance(A) = unchanged\n267\t    owner(A) = unchanged\n268\t    ∃ authorized_role R: R can clear_lock(A, L)\n269\t```\n270\t\n271\t**Guaranteed Properties:**\n272\t- Locks restrict actions, not ownership\n273\t- Locked accounts can still receive funds\n274\t- Locks do not transfer or freeze funds to protocol custody\n275\t- All locks are reversible by appropriate authority\n276\t- Lock operations emit auditable events\n277\t\n278\t**Implementation Requirements:**\n279\t1. Lock operations MUST NOT modify account balances\n280\t2. Receiving operations MUST remain functional when locked\n281\t3. Lock state is stored separately from balance/ownership\n282\t4. Lock/unlock operations emit events for transparency\n283\t\n284\t**Contract Mapping:**\n285\t- `account-locks.fc`: Lock operations don't touch balances (lines 100-110, 160-217)\n286\t- `account-locks.fc`: `can_receive()` always returns true (lines 94-98)\n287\t- `MerchantPaymentHub.tact`: Checks locks before send, not receive (lines 116-119)\n288\t\n289\t**Test Coverage:**\n290\t- `tests/invariants/I6-lock-not-confiscation.spec.ts`\n291\t- Test: Fraud lock prevents sending, allows receiving\n292\t- Test: Collateral lock prevents sending, allows receiving\n293\t- Test: Lock does not change balance\n294\t- Test: Lock can be reversed by authorized party\n295\t- Negative test: Lock cannot seize funds\n296\t\n297\t---\n298\t\n299\t### I7 — External Adapter Isolation\n300\t\n301\t**Statement:**\n302\t> External providers cannot trigger transfers, cannot bypass protocol rules, and can only interact through explicit user actions.\n303\t\n304\t**Formal Definition:**\n305\t```\n306\t∀ external_adapter E in [ChangeNOW, NOWPayments, CoinRabbit, TONCO]:\n307\t  ∀ protocol_operation O:\n308\t    E CANNOT directly invoke O\n309\t    E CANNOT bypass validation rules of O\n310\t    IF E participates in O THEN:\n311\t      O MUST be initiated by user U\n312\t      O MUST follow all invariants I1-I6\n313\t```\n314\t\n315\t**Guaranteed Properties:**\n316\t- External providers have no direct smart contract access\n317\t- All external interactions are mediated by user wallets\n318\t- Backend APIs orchestrate but don't execute transfers\n319\t- External adapters are read-only from protocol perspective\n320\t\n321\t**Implementation Requirements:**\n322\t1. No external adapter addresses in smart contract authorization\n323\t2. Backend services orchestrate user-signed transactions only\n324\t3. External adapters interact with user wallets, not protocol contracts\n325\t4. DEX interactions are user-initiated swaps\n326\t\n327\t**Contract Mapping:**\n328\t- `account-locks.fc`: Only `risk_authority` and `lending_adapter` have special roles, and they cannot move funds\n329\t- No external adapter addresses in Payment Hub contracts\n330\t- All transfers require NFT owner signature\n331\t\n332\t**Test Coverage:**\n333\t- `tests/invariants/I7-external-adapter-isolation.spec.ts`\n334\t- Test: External services cannot initiate transfers\n335\t- Test: All transfers require valid user signature\n336\t- Architectural review: No external adapter privileged access\n337\t\n338\t---\n339\t\n340\t## Invariant Violation Response\n341\t\n342\tIf any invariant is violated (detected through testing, audit, or production monitoring):\n343\t\n344\t1. **CRITICAL SEVERITY**: All invariant violations are critical\n345\t2. **IMMEDIATE HALT**: Affected operations must be stopped\n346\t3. **INCIDENT RESPONSE**: Follow security incident protocol\n347\t4. **ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS**: Full investigation required\n348\t5. **FIX VERIFICATION**: Must demonstrate invariant restoration\n349\t6. **AUDIT REVIEW**: Security audit
