   [solve worker-1]       "content": "# TONBANKCARD Protocol — Formal Invariants & Guarantees\n\n**Document Type:** Security Foundation\n**Status:** Formal Specification\n**Issue Reference:** [#18 - Issue 4.1 Formal Invariants & Protocol Guarantees](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/18)\n**Last Updated:** 2025-12-27\n\n---\n\n## Purpose\n\nThis document defines the **core invariants and guarantees** of the TONBANKCARD protocol. These invariants are non-negotiable rules that must always hold true across all smart contracts, adapters, and future extensions.\n\nThese invariants form the basis for:\n- Security audits\n- Formal verification\n- Governance decisions\n- Ecosystem integrations\n\n**Any violation of these invariants represents a critical security vulnerability.**\n\n---\n\n## Core Protocol Invariants\n\n### I1 — Non-Custodial Ownership\n\n**Statement:**\n> At no point may the protocol take custody of user funds, move funds without explicit user-initiated transactions, or override NFT ownership.\n\n**Formal Definition:**\n```\n∀ transaction T, ∀ user U:\n  IF T transfers funds from U's account\n  THEN T MUST be signed by U (the NFT owner)\n  AND T MUST be initiated by U\n  AND no protocol admin/operator can initiate T on behalf of U\n```\n\n**Guaranteed Properties:**\n- The owner of the NFT account is the sole authority over the associated on-chain balance\n- No smart contract can move funds without the NFT owner's explicit signature\n- No backend service can initiate fund transfers\n- No external adapter can trigger fund movement\n\n**Implementation Requirements:**\n1. All transfer functions MUST verify `msg.sender == NFT_owner`\n2. No admin override functions are permitted\n3. No proxy delegation to third parties for fund movement\n4. Backend services are read-only\n\n**Contract Mapping:**\n- `PaymentHub.tact`: Verifies ownership in `TransferInternalRequest` handler (line 164)\n- `MerchantPaymentHub.tact`: Validates payer ownership before settlement (lines 90-96)\n- `account-locks.fc`: Lock mechanisms do not move funds, only restrict operations\n\n**Test Coverage:**\n- `tests/invariants/I1-non-custodial-ownership.spec.ts`\n- Negative test: Attempt transfer from non-owner account\n- Negative test: Admin attempting to move user funds\n\n---\n\n### I2 — NFT = Account Authority\n\n**Statement:**\n> Each NFT represents exactly one account. Account control is transferred only via NFT transfer. No secondary ownership mechanisms are allowed.\n\n**Formal Definition:**\n```\n∀ NFT n, ∀ account a:\n  account_authority(a) = NFT_owner(n)\n  AND ∀ time t1, t2 where t2 > t1:\n    IF NFT_owner(n, t1) ≠ NFT_owner(n, t2)\n    THEN account_authority(a, t2) = NFT_owner(n, t2)\n```\n\n**Guaranteed Properties:**\n- NFT ownership is the single source of truth for account authority\n- Account control transfers atomically with NFT ownership transfer\n- No separate \"authorized users\" or \"delegates\" with fund control\n- No multi-signature override without multi-sig NFT ownership\n\n**Implementation Requirements:**\n1. Always query current NFT owner on-chain before operations\n2. No cached ownership records for fund control decisions\n3. NFT transfer automatically updates account authority\n4. No separate authorization layer\n\n**Contract Mapping:**\n- `PaymentHub.tact`: Uses `owner` field from `AccountState` (line 36)\n- `MerchantPaymentHub.tact`: Stores and validates NFT owners (lines 42, 90-96)\n- `nft_account_resolver.fc`: Resolves NFT ownership as authority source (lines 61-69)\n\n**Test Coverage:**\n- `tests/invariants/I2-nft-account-authority.spec.ts`\n- Test: NFT transfer updates account authority\n- Negative test: Previous owner cannot transact after NFT transfer\n\n---\n\n### I3 — No Admin Fund Control\n\n**Statement:**\n> The protocol must not contain admin withdrawals, emergency drains, privileged fund movement, or hidden upgrade paths.\n\n**Formal Definition:**\n```\n∀ role R in [admin, operator, risk_authority, lending_adapter]:\n  ∀ account A:\n    R CANNOT initiate fund transfer from A\n    R CANNOT withdraw from A\n    R CANNOT modify balance(A) except through user-initiated transfers\n    R CANNOT upgrade contracts to bypass these restrictions\n    R CAN transfer the admin role to another address only via the two-phase timelock\n```\n\n**Guaranteed Properties:**\n- No role other than the NFT owner can initiate fund transfers\n- Admin roles (admin, risk authority, lending adapter) can only set flags/states\n- No emergency withdrawal functions exist\n- No upgradeable proxies that could bypass these rules\n- Development/testing admin functions MUST be removed before production\n- Admin role is transferable but ONLY via two-phase timelock (7-day delay)\n- Admin role transfer does NOT affect user fund ownership or balances\n\n**Implementation Requirements:**\n1. Admin roles limited to non-financial operations:\n   - Admin: Whitelist NFT collections, initialize accounts (testing only)\n   - Risk authority: Set/clear fraud locks only\n   - Lending adapter: Set/clear collateral locks only\n2. No `onlyAdmin` functions that move funds\n3. No upgradeable proxy patterns\n4. All contracts are immutable after deployment\n\n**Admin Transfer Mechanism (Issue #96):**\n\nTo prevent single-point-of-failure from the deployer key and allow migration to DAO/multisig, the `admin` role supports two-phase transferable ownership with a 7-day timelock:\n\n1. **Phase 1 — Propose** (`ProposeAdminTransfer` / `MerchantProposeAdminTransfer`):\n   - Only the current admin can call this\n   - Records the proposed new admin and a timestamp = `now() + 7 days`\n   - Does NOT change admin immediately\n2. **Phase 2 — Execute** (`ExecuteAdminTransfer` / `MerchantExecuteAdminTransfer`):\n   - Only the proposed new admin can call this\n   - Can only execute after the 7-day timelock has elapsed\n   - Commits the admin change; clears the pending proposal\n3. **Cancel** (`CancelAdminTransfer` / `MerchantCancelAdminTransfer`):\n   - Only the current admin can cancel a pending proposal before it executes\n\nThe same two-phase timelock pattern applies to `risk_authority` and `lending_adapter` roles in `account-locks.fc` (op codes `0x4001`–`0x4013`).\n\n**Contract Mapping:**\n- `PaymentHub.tact`: `admin` field replaces `deployer`; admin transfer via `ProposeAdminTransfer`/`ExecuteAdminTransfer`/`CancelAdminTransfer`\n- `MerchantPaymentHub.tact`: Same pattern via `MerchantProposeAdminTransfer`/`MerchantExecuteAdminTransfer`/`MerchantCancelAdminTransfer`\n- `account-locks.fc`: `risk_authority` and `lending_adapter` transferable via `op::propose_risk_authority` / `op::execute_risk_authority` / `op::cancel_risk_authority` and equivalents for `lending_adapter`\n\n**Test Coverage:**\n- `tests/invariants/I3-no-admin-fund-control.spec.ts`\n  - Negative test: Admin cannot withdraw user funds\n  - Negative test: Risk authority cannot move funds\n  - Negative test: Deployer cannot drain account balances\n  - Positive test: Admin can propose a transfer\n  - Negative test: Execution before timelock expiry is rejected\n  - Positive test: Execution after timelock succeeds; user funds unchanged\n  - Negative test: New admin cannot move user funds (I3 preserved post-transfer)\n  - Positive test: Admin can cancel a pending transfer\n- `tests/admin-transfer/PaymentHub-admin-transfer.spec.ts` — comprehensive admin transfer tests\n- `tests/admin-transfer/MerchantPaymentHub-admin-transfer.spec.ts` — comprehensive admin transfer tests\n\n---\n\n### I4 — Atomic Transfers\n\n**Statement:**\n> All internal transfers must be atomic, fully settled or reverted, and free from intermediate states.\n\n**Formal Definition:**\n```\n∀ transfer T from account A to account B with amount X:\n  EITHER:\n    (balance(A) = balance(A)_before - X) AND\n    (balance(B) = balance(B)_before + X) AND\n    (T.status = SUCCESS)\n  OR:\n    (balance(A) = balance(A)_before) AND\n    (balance(B) = balance(B)_before) AND\n    (T.status = REVERTED)\n```\n\n**Guaranteed Properties:**\n- A transfer either completes fully or does not occur at all\n- No partial balance updates\n- No intermediate states where funds are \"in flight\"\n- Reentrancy protection ensures atomicity\n\n**Implementation Requirements:**\n1. Use transaction revert on any validation failure\n2. Update both sender and receiver balances in same transaction\n3. Implement reentrancy guards\n4. No asynchronous balance updates\n\n**Contract Mapping:**\n- `PaymentHub.tact`: Atomic balance update (lines 196-202), reentrancy guard (lines 121, 149-150)\n- `MerchantPaymentHub.tact`: Atomic debit/credit (lines 134-135)\n\n**Test Coverage:**\n- `tests/invariants/I4-atomic-transfers.spec.ts`\n- Test: Successful transfer updates both balances atomically\n- Test: Failed transfer leaves both balances unchanged\n- Test: Reentrancy attempt is blocked\n\n---\n\n### I5 — Ledger Conservation\n\n**Statement:**\n> Internal ledger operations must satisfy: Σ(balances before) = Σ(balances after), except for protocol-defined fees (if any) or explicitly defined mint/burn logic.\n\n**Formal Definition:**\n```\n∀ transaction T:\n  Σ(all_balances_after(T)) = Σ(all_balances_before(T)) - fees(T) - burns(T) + mints(T)\n\nWHERE:\n  fees(T) = 0 for internal TBC transfers (zero-fee guarantee)\n  burns(T) = 0 (no burn mechanism in current protocol)\n  mints(T) = 0 (no mint mechanism in payment hub)\n```\n\n**Guaranteed Properties:**\n- Total TBC in the system is conserved during transfers\n- No funds can be created or destroyed during transfers\n- Internal transfers have zero fees\n- Balance sum is an invariant across all operations\n\n**Implementation Requirements:**\n1. Every debit MUST have a corresponding credit of equal amount\n2. No rounding errors or precision loss\n3. No hidden fees deducted from transfers\n4. Explicit tracking of any future fee mechanisms\n\n**Contract Mapping:**\n- `PaymentHub.tact`: Direct balance arithmetic (lines 197-198)\n- `MerchantPaymentHub.tact`: Symmetric debit/credit (lines 178-187)\n\n**Test Coverage:**\n- `tests/invariants/I5-ledger-conservation.spec.ts`\n- Test: Sum of balances unchanged after transfer\n- Test: Multiple concurrent transfers preserve total supply\n- Test: Self-transfer does not create/destroy funds\n\n---\n\n### I6 — Lock ≠ Confiscation\n\n**Statement:**\n> Account locks prevent outgoing transfers, do NOT seize or move funds, and are reversible.\n\n**Formal Definition:**\n```\n∀ account A, ∀ lock L in [FRAUD_LOCK, COLLATERAL_LOCK]:\n  IF is_locked(A, L) THEN:\n    can_send(A) = FALSE\n    can_receive(A) = TRUE\n    balance(A) = unchanged\n    owner(A) = unchanged\n    ∃ authorized_role R: R can clear_lock(A, L)\n```\n\n**Guaranteed Properties:**\n- Locks restrict actions, not ownership\n- Locked accounts can still receive funds\n- Locks do not transfer or freeze funds to protocol custody\n- All locks are reversible by appropriate authority\n- Lock operations emit auditable events\n\n**Implementation Requirements:**\n1. Lock operations MUST NOT modify account balances\n2. Receiving operations MUST remain functional when locked\n3. Lock state is stored separately from balance/ownership\n4. Lock/unlock operations emit events for transparency\n\n**Contract Mapping:**\n- `account-locks.fc`: Lock operations don't touch balances (lines 100-110, 160-217)\n- `account-locks.fc`: `can_receive()` always returns true (lines 94-98)\n- `MerchantPaymentHub.tact`: Checks locks before send, not receive (lines 116-119)\n\n**Test Coverage:**\n- `tests/invariants/I6-lock-not-confiscation.spec.ts`\n- Test: Fraud lock prevents sending, allows receiving\n- Test: Collateral lock prevents sending, allows receiving\n- Test: Lock does not change balance\n- Test: Lock can be reversed by authorized party\n- Negative test: Lock cannot seize funds\n\n---\n\n### I7 — External Adapter Isolation\n\n**Statement:**\n> External providers cannot trigger transfers, cannot bypass protocol rules, and can only interact through explicit user actions.\n\n**Formal Definition:**\n```\n∀ external_adapter E in [ChangeNOW, NOWPayments, CoinRabbit, TONCO]:\n  ∀ protocol_operation O:\n    E CANNOT directly invoke O\n    E CANNOT bypass validation rules of O\n    IF E participates in O THEN:\n      O MUST be initiated by user U\n      O MUST follow all invariants I1-I6\n```\n\n**Guaranteed Properties:**\n- External providers have no direct smart contract access\n- All external interactions are mediated by user wallets\n- Backend APIs orchestrate but don't execute transfers\n- External adapters are read-only from protocol perspective\n\n**Implementation Requirements:**\n1. No external adapter addresses in smart contract authorization\n2. Backend services orchestrate user-signed transactions only\n3. External adapters interact with user wallets, not protocol contracts\n4. DEX interactions are user-initiated swaps\n\n**Contract Mapping:**\n- `account-locks.fc`: Only `risk_authority` and `lending_adapter` have special roles, and they cannot move funds\n- No external adapter addresses in Payment Hub contracts\n- All transfers require NFT owner signature\n\n**Test Coverage:**\n- `tests/invariants/I7-external-adapter-isolation.spec.ts`\n- Test: External services cannot initiate transfers\n- Test: All transfers require valid user signature\n- Architectural review: No external adapter privileged access\n\n---\n\n## Invariant Violation Response\n\nIf any invariant is violated (detected through testing, audit, or production monitoring):\n\n1. **CRITICAL SEVERITY**: All invariant violations are critical\n2. **IMMEDIATE HALT**: Affected operations must be stopped\n3. **INCIDENT RESPONSE**: Follow security incident protocol\n4. **ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS**: Full investigation required\n5. **FIX VERIFICATION**: Must demonstrate invariant restoration\n6. **AUDIT REVIEW**: Security audit of fix before deployment\n\n---\n\n## Audit Checklist\n\nFor auditors reviewing the TONBANKCARD protocol:\n\n### I1 — Non-Custodial Ownership\n- [ ] All fund transfers verify NFT ownership\n- [ ] No admin override for fund movement\n- [ ] Backend services are read-only\n- [ ] No custody mechanisms exist\n\n### I2 — NFT = Account Authority\n- [ ] NFT ownership is queried on-chain for each operation\n- [ ] No cached ownership for authorization\n- [ ] No secondary authorization mechanisms\n- [ ] Account control transfers with NFT\n\n### I3 — No Admin Fund Control\n- [ ] No admin withdrawal functions\n- [ ] Admin roles limited to non-financial operations\n- [ ] No upgradeable proxies\n- [ ] Test-only admin functions documented for removal\n\n### I4 — Atomic Transfers\n- [ ] Balance updates are atomic\n- [ ] Reentrancy protection implemented\n- [ ] No intermediate states\n- [ ] Failed transfers fully revert\n\n### I5 — Ledger Conservation\n- [ ] Every debit has equal credit\n- [ ] No hidden fees\n- [ ] Total balance sum is preserved\n- [ ] No rounding errors\n\n### I6 — Lock ≠ Confiscation\n- [ ] Locks don't modify balances\n- [ ] Locked accounts can receive\n- [ ] Locks are reversible\n- [ ] Lock events are emitted\n\n### I7 — External Adapter Isolation\n- [ ] No external adapter direct contract access\n- [ ] All operations user-initiated\n- [ ] No bypass mechanisms\n- [ ] Backend is orchestration-only\n\n---\n\n## Invariant-to-Contract Mapping\n\n| Invariant | PaymentHub.tact | MerchantPaymentHub.tact | account-locks.fc Invariant Changes\nThese invariants are **foundational** to the protocol. Any future Issue, PR, or governance proposal that violates them must:\n\n1. **Explicitly declare the violation** in the Issue/PR description\n2. **Undergo protocol-level review** by security team\n3. **Receive explicit governance approval** (future DAO mechanism)\n4. **Update this document** with the new invariant definition\n5. **Pass full audit** before deployment\n\n### Acceptable Changes\nChanges that **do not** violate invariants and are acceptable without governance:\n- Additional validation rules (more restrictive)\n- New lock types (following I6 pattern)\n- Performance optimizations (preserving semantics)\n- Additional getter functions (read-only)\n- Event additions (non-state-changing)\n\n### Prohibited Changes\nChanges that **always** violate invariants and are prohibited:\n- Admin fund withdrawal mechanisms\n- Custody of user funds\n- Non-atomic transfers\n- Hidden fees or balance manipulation\n- NFT ownership bypass mechanisms\n- Irreversible confiscation locks\n\n---\n\n## References\n\n- **Architecture**: [docs/architecture.md](./architecture.md)\n- **Payment Hub**: [contracts/payments/README.md](../contracts/payments/README.md)\n- **Account Locks**: [contracts/payments/ACCOUNT_LOCKS.md](../contracts/payments/ACCOUNT_LOCKS.md)\n- **Contributing**: [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md)\n- **Issue #18**: [Formal Invariants & Protocol Guarantees](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/18)\n\n---\n\n## Document Maintenance\n\n**Responsibility**: Protocol Security Team\n**Review Frequency**: Before each major release\n**Update Triggers**:\n- New smart contract deployment\n- Protocol architecture changes\n- Security audit findings\n- Governance decisions\n\n**Version History**:\n- v1.0 (2025-12-27): Initial formal specification (Issue #18)\n\n---\n\n**Built on TON. [Name]', ...)`\n- Test cases: `it('Should [expected behavior] when [attack scenario]', ...)`\n\n### Assertion Patterns\n\n```typescript\n// Attack should FAIL (mitigation works)\nawait expect(maliciousTransaction).toRevertWith('error::unauthorized');\n\n// Attack should be DETECTED\nconst events = result.events;\nexpect(events).toContainEventMatching({ type: 'SecurityAlert' });\n\n// Invariant should HOLD\nconst balanceSum = await getAllBalances();\nconst totalSupply = await getTotalSupply();\nexpect(balanceSum).toEqual(totalSupply);  // Invariant I5\n```\n\n---\n\n## Test File Specifications\n\nThe following sections provide detailed specifications for each test file. These can be implemented by developers or used as acceptance criteria for test-driven development.\n\n---\n\n## File: `nft-race-conditions.spec.ts`\n\n### Test Suite: T1 - NFT Transfer Race Conditions\n\n#### Test 1: Front-Running Attack\n```\nSCENARIO: Attacker observes pending transfer and buys NFT before execution\n\nSETUP:\n1. Alice owns NFT #7777001 with 1000 TBC balance\n2. Alice initiates transfer: 500 TBC from NFT #7777001 to NFT #8888001\n3. Before execution, Bob purchases NFT #7777001 from marketplace\n4. The flag\n * is exposed to property tests so they can construct adversarial scenarios.\n */\nexport class ProtocolModel {\n    private readonly accounts = new Map<Address, Account>();\n    private _admin: Address;\n    private _riskAuthority: Address;\n    private _lendingAdapter: Address;\n    private _reentrancyLocked = false;\n\n    constructor(params: {\n        admin: Address;\n        riskAuthority?: Address;\n        lendingAdapter?: Address;\n    }) {\n        this._admin = params.admin;\n        this._riskAuthority = params.riskAuthority ?? params.admin;\n        this._lendingAdapter = params.lendingAdapter ?? params.admin;\n    }\n\n    get admin(): Address {\n        return this._admin;\n    }\n\n    get riskAuthority(): Address {\n        return this._riskAuthority;\n    }\n\n    get lendingAdapter(): Address {\n        return this._lendingAdapter;\n    }\n\n    get reentrancyLocked(): boolean {\n        return this._reentrancyLocked;\n    }\n\n    snapshot(): ProtocolSnapshot {\n        const copy = new Map<Address, Account>();\n        for (const [k, v] of this.accounts) {\n            copy.set(k, { ...v });\n        }\n        return {\n            accounts: copy,\n            admin: this._admin,\n            riskAuthority: this._riskAuthority,\n            lendingAdapter: this._lendingAdapter,\n            reentrancyLocked: this._reentrancyLocked,\n        };\n    }\n\n    getAccount(nft: Address): Readonly<Account> | undefined {\n        const acc = this.accounts.get(nft);\n        return acc ? { ...acc } : undefined;\n    }\n\n    balanceOf(nft: Address): bigint {\n        return this.accounts.get(nft)?.balance ?? 0n;\n    }\n\n    totalSupply(): bigint {\n        let sum = 0n;\n        for (const acc of this.accounts.values()) {\n            sum += acc.balance;\n        }\n        return sum;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Admin-only: register an account record. Models I1 (owner-only), I4 (atomic),\n     * I5 (conservation), I6 (lock prevents sending), I7 (no privileged path).\n     */\n    transfer(\n        caller: Caller,\n        fromNft: Address,\n        toNft: Address,\n        amount: bigint,\n    ): TxResult {\n        if (this._reentrancyLocked) {\n            return { status: 'REVERTED', error: 'REENTRANCY' };\n        }\n        this._reentrancyLocked = true;\n        try {\n            return this.transferUnchecked(caller, fromNft, toNft, amount);\n        } finally {\n            this._reentrancyLocked = false;\n        }\n    }\n\n    private transferUnchecked(\n        caller: Caller,\n        fromNft: Address,\n        toNft: Address,\n        amount: bigint,\n    ): TxResult {\n        const from = this.accounts.get(fromNft);\n        const to = this.accounts.get(toNft);\n\n        if (!from) return { status: 'REVERTED', error: 'NO_FROM_ACCOUNT' };\n        if (!to) return { status: 'REVERTED', error: 'NO_TO_ACCOUNT' };\n        if (amount < 0n) return { status: 'REVERTED', error: 'NEGATIVE_AMOUNT' };\n\n        // I1: only the NFT owner can initiate a transfer. Admin / risk_authority /\n        // lending_adapter / external_adapter must all be rejected.\n        if (caller.role !== 'user' || caller.address !== from.owner) {\n            return { status: 'REVERTED', error: 'NOT_OWNER' };\n        }\n\n        if (from.state !== AccountState.ACTIVE) {\n            return { status: 'REVERTED', error: 'FROM_NOT_ACTIVE' };\n        }\n        if (to.state === AccountState.CLOSED) {\n            return { status: 'REVERTED', error: 'TO_CLOSED' };\n        }\n\n        // I6/I7: locks prevent sending but never receiving.\n        if (from.fraudLocked) {\n            return { status: 'REVERTED', error: 'FRAUD_LOCKED' };\n        }\n        if (from.collateralLocked) {\n            return { status: 'REVERTED', error: 'COLLATERAL_LOCKED' };\n        }\n\n        if (from.balance < amount) {\n            return { status: 'REVERTED', error: 'INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE' };\n        }\n\n        // Self-transfer is a no-op (matches PaymentHub.tact behaviour).\n        if (fromNft === toNft) {\n            return { status: 'SUCCESS' };\n        }\n\n        // I4: atomic — both updates in the same transition or none.\n        from.balance -= amount;\n        to.balance += amount;\n        return { status: 'SUCCESS' };\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * NFT transfer changes account authority. 'fast-check';\nimport { ProtocolModel, AccountState, Caller } from '../model/protocol-model';\nimport {\n    ADMIN,\n    RISK_AUTHORITY,\n    LENDING_ADAPTER,\n    EXTERNAL_ADAPTER,\n    USER_POOL,\n    NFT_POOL,\n    amountArb,\n} from './arbitraries';\nimport {\n    ADMIN_CALLER,\n    buildModel,\n    snapshotBalances,\n} from './helpers';\n\ndescribe('I1 — Non-Custodial Ownership (property)', () => {\n    it('no non-owner caller can debit any account', () => {\n        fc.assert(\n            fc.property(\n                fc.array(\n                    fc.record({\n                          ...s,\n                            state: AccountState.ACTIVE,\n                        })),\n                    );\n                    const from = model.getAccount(fromNft);\n                    if (!from || !model.getAccount(toNft)) return;\n\n                    // Build a non-owner caller deterministically from callerIdx.\n                    const candidates: Caller[] = [\n                        { address: ADMIN, role: 'admin' },\n                        { address: RISK_AUTHORITY, role: 'risk_authority' },\n                        { address: LENDING_ADAPTER, role: 'lending_adapter' },\n                        {\n                            address: EXTERNAL_ADAPTER,\n                            role: 'external_adapter',\n                        },\n                        // a user that is provably not the owner\n                        {\n                            address:\n                                USER_POOL.find((u) => u !== from.owner) ??\n                                USER_POOL[0],\n                            role: 'user',\n                        },\n                    ];\n                    const caller = candidates[callerIdx];\n                    if (\n                        caller.role === 'user' &&\n                        caller.address === from.owner\n                    ) {\n amount);\n                    const after = snapshotBalances(model);\n\n                    expect(res.status).toBe('REVERTED');\n                    expect(after).toEqual(before);\n                },\n            ),\n            { numRuns: 200 },\n        );\n    });\n\n    it('only the current NFT owner can authorize a debit', () => {\n        fc.assert(\n            fc.property(\n    [solve worker-1]         "content": "1\t# TONBANKCARD Protocol — Formal Invariants & Guarantees\n2\t\n3\t**Document Type:** Security Foundation\n4\t**Status:** Formal Specification\n5\t**Issue Reference:** [#18 - Issue 4.1 Formal Invariants & Protocol Guarantees](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/18)\n6\t**Last Updated:** 2025-12-27\n7\t\n8\t---\n9\t\n10\t## Purpose\n11\t\n12\tThis document defines the **core invariants and guarantees** of the TONBANKCARD protocol. These invariants are non-negotiable rules that must always hold true across all smart contracts, adapters, and future extensions.\n13\t\n14\tThese invariants form the basis for:\n15\t- Security audits\n16\t- Formal verification\n17\t- Governance decisions\n18\t- Ecosystem integrations\n19\t\n20\t**Any violation of these invariants represents a critical security vulnerability.**\n21\t\n22\t---\n23\t\n24\t## Core Protocol Invariants\n25\t\n26\t### I1 — Non-Custodial Ownership\n27\t\n28\t**Statement:**\n29\t> At no point may the protocol take custody of user funds, move funds without explicit user-initiated transactions, or override NFT ownership.\n30\t\n31\t**Formal Definition:**\n32\t```\n33\t∀ transaction T, ∀ user U:\n34\t  IF T transfers funds from U's account\n35\t  THEN T MUST be signed by U (the NFT owner)\n36\t  AND T MUST be initiated by U\n37\t  AND no protocol admin/operator can initiate T on behalf of U\n38\t```\n39\t\n40\t**Guaranteed Properties:**\n41\t- The owner of the NFT account is the sole authority over the associated on-chain balance\n42\t- No smart contract can move funds without the NFT owner's explicit signature\n43\t- No backend service can initiate fund transfers\n44\t- No external adapter can trigger fund movement\n45\t\n46\t**Implementation Requirements:**\n47\t1. All transfer functions MUST verify `msg.sender == NFT_owner`\n48\t2. No admin override functions are permitted\n49\t3. No proxy delegation to third parties for fund movement\n50\t4. Backend services are read-only\n51\t\n52\t**Contract Mapping:**\n53\t- `PaymentHub.tact`: Verifies ownership in `TransferInternalRequest` handler (line 164)\n54\t- `MerchantPaymentHub.tact`: Validates payer ownership before settlement (lines 90-96)\n55\t- `account-locks.fc`: Lock mechanisms do not move funds, only restrict operations\n56\t\n57\t**Test Coverage:**\n58\t- `tests/invariants/I1-non-custodial-ownership.spec.ts`\n59\t- Negative test: Attempt transfer from non-owner account\n60\t- Negative test: Admin attempting to move user funds\n61\t\n62\t---\n63\t\n64\t### I2 — NFT = Account Authority\n65\t\n66\t**Statement:**\n67\t> Each NFT represents exactly one account. Account control is transferred only via NFT transfer. No secondary ownership mechanisms are allowed.\n68\t\n69\t**Formal Definition:**\n70\t```\n71\t∀ NFT n, ∀ account a:\n72\t  account_authority(a) = NFT_owner(n)\n73\t  AND ∀ time t1, t2 where t2 > t1:\n74\t    IF NFT_owner(n, t1) ≠ NFT_owner(n, t2)\n75\t    THEN account_authority(a, t2) = NFT_owner(n, t2)\n76\t```\n77\t\n78\t**Guaranteed Properties:**\n79\t- NFT ownership is the single source of truth for account authority\n80\t- Account control transfers atomically with NFT ownership transfer\n81\t- No separate \"authorized users\" or \"delegates\" with fund control\n82\t- No multi-signature override without multi-sig NFT ownership\n83\t\n84\t**Implementation Requirements:**\n85\t1. Always query current NFT owner on-chain before operations\n86\t2. No cached ownership records for fund control decisions\n87\t3. NFT transfer automatically updates account authority\n88\t4. No separate authorization layer\n89\t\n90\t**Contract Mapping:**\n91\t- `PaymentHub.tact`: Uses `owner` field from `AccountState` (line 36)\n92\t- `MerchantPaymentHub.tact`: Stores and validates NFT owners (lines 42, 90-96)\n93\t- `nft_account_resolver.fc`: Resolves NFT ownership as authority source (lines 61-69)\n94\t\n95\t**Test Coverage:**\n96\t- `tests/invariants/I2-nft-account-authority.spec.ts`\n97\t- Test: NFT transfer updates account authority\n98\t- Negative test: Previous owner cannot transact after NFT transfer\n99\t\n100\t---\n101\t\n102\t### I3 — No Admin Fund Control\n103\t\n104\t**Statement:**\n105\t> The protocol must not contain admin withdrawals, emergency drains, privileged fund movement, or hidden upgrade paths.\n106\t\n107\t**Formal Definition:**\n108\t```\n109\t∀ role R in [admin, operator, risk_authority, lending_adapter]:\n110\t  ∀ account A:\n111\t    R CANNOT initiate fund transfer from A\n112\t    R CANNOT withdraw from A\n113\t    R CANNOT modify balance(A) except through user-initiated transfers\n114\t    R CANNOT upgrade contracts to bypass these restrictions\n115\t    R CAN transfer the admin role to another address only via the two-phase timelock\n116\t```\n117\t\n118\t**Guaranteed Properties:**\n119\t- No role other than the NFT owner can initiate fund transfers\n120\t- Admin roles (admin, risk authority, lending adapter) can only set flags/states\n121\t- No emergency withdrawal functions exist\n122\t- No upgradeable proxies that could bypass these rules\n123\t- Development/testing admin functions MUST be removed before production\n124\t- Admin role is transferable but ONLY via two-phase timelock (7-day delay)\n125\t- Admin role transfer does NOT affect user fund ownership or balances\n126\t\n127\t**Implementation Requirements:**\n128\t1. Admin roles limited to non-financial operations:\n129\t   - Admin: Whitelist NFT collections, initialize accounts (testing only)\n130\t   - Risk authority: Set/clear fraud locks only\n131\t   - Lending adapter: Set/clear collateral locks only\n132\t2. No `onlyAdmin` functions that move funds\n133\t3. No upgradeable proxy patterns\n134\t4. All contracts are immutable after deployment\n135\t\n136\t**Admin Transfer Mechanism (Issue #96):**\n137\t\n138\tTo prevent single-point-of-failure from the deployer key and allow migration to DAO/multisig, the `admin` role supports two-phase transferable ownership with a 7-day timelock:\n139\t\n140\t1. **Phase 1 — Propose** (`ProposeAdminTransfer` / `MerchantProposeAdminTransfer`):\n141\t   - Only the current admin can call this\n142\t   - Records the proposed new admin and a timestamp = `now() + 7 days`\n143\t   - Does NOT change admin immediately\n144\t2. **Phase 2 — Execute** (`ExecuteAdminTransfer` / `MerchantExecuteAdminTransfer`):\n145\t   - Only the proposed new admin can call this\n146\t   - Can only execute after the 7-day timelock has elapsed\n147\t   - Commits the admin change; clears the pending proposal\n148\t3. **Cancel** (`CancelAdminTransfer` / `MerchantCancelAdminTransfer`):\n149\t   - Only the current admin can cancel a pending proposal before it executes\n150\t\n151\tThe same two-phase timelock pattern applies to `risk_authority` and `lending_adapter` roles in `account-locks.fc` (op codes `0x4001`–`0x4013`).\n152\t\n153\t**Contract Mapping:**\n154\t- `PaymentHub.tact`: `admin` field replaces `deployer`; admin transfer via `ProposeAdminTransfer`/`ExecuteAdminTransfer`/`CancelAdminTransfer`\n155\t- `MerchantPaymentHub.tact`: Same pattern via `MerchantProposeAdminTransfer`/`MerchantExecuteAdminTransfer`/`MerchantCancelAdminTransfer`\n156\t- `account-locks.fc`: `risk_authority` and `lending_adapter` transferable via `op::propose_risk_authority` / `op::execute_risk_authority` / `op::cancel_risk_authority` and equivalents for `lending_adapter`\n157\t\n158\t**Test Coverage:**\n159\t- `tests/invariants/I3-no-admin-fund-control.spec.ts`\n160\t  - Negative test: Admin cannot withdraw user funds\n161\t  - Negative test: Risk authority cannot move funds\n162\t  - Negative test: Deployer cannot drain account balances\n163\t  - Positive test: Admin can propose a transfer\n164\t  - Negative test: Execution before timelock expiry is rejected\n165\t  - Positive test: Execution after timelock succeeds; user funds unchanged\n166\t  - Negative test: New admin cannot move user funds (I3 preserved post-transfer)\n167\t  - Positive test: Admin can cancel a pending transfer\n168\t- `tests/admin-transfer/PaymentHub-admin-transfer.spec.ts` — comprehensive admin transfer tests\n169\t- `tests/admin-transfer/MerchantPaymentHub-admin-transfer.spec.ts` — comprehensive admin transfer tests\n170\t\n171\t---\n172\t\n173\t### I4 — Atomic Transfers\n174\t\n175\t**Statement:**\n176\t> All internal transfers must be atomic, fully settled or reverted, and free from intermediate states.\n177\t\n178\t**Formal Definition:**\n179\t```\n180\t∀ transfer T from account A to account B with amount X:\n181\t  EITHER:\n182\t    (balance(A) = balance(A)_before - X) AND\n183\t    (balance(B) = balance(B)_before + X) AND\n184\t    (T.status = SUCCESS)\n185\t  OR:\n186\t    (balance(A) = balance(A)_before) AND\n187\t    (balance(B) = balance(B)_before) AND\n188\t    (T.status = REVERTED)\n189\t```\n190\t\n191\t**Guaranteed Properties:**\n192\t- A transfer either completes fully or does not occur at all\n193\t- No partial balance updates\n194\t- No intermediate states where funds are \"in flight\"\n195\t- Reentrancy protection ensures atomicity\n196\t\n197\t**Implementation Requirements:**\n198\t1. Use transaction revert on any validation failure\n199\t2. Update both sender and receiver balances in same transaction\n200\t3. Implement reentrancy guards\n201\t4. No asynchronous balance updates\n202\t\n203\t**Contract Mapping:**\n204\t- `PaymentHub.tact`: Atomic balance update (lines 196-202), reentrancy guard (lines 121, 149-150)\n205\t- `MerchantPaymentHub.tact`: Atomic debit/credit (lines 134-135)\n206\t\n207\t**Test Coverage:**\n208\t- `tests/invariants/I4-atomic-transfers.spec.ts`\n209\t- Test: Successful transfer updates both balances atomically\n210\t- Test: Failed transfer leaves both balances unchanged\n211\t- Test: Reentrancy attempt is blocked\n212\t\n213\t---\n214\t\n215\t### I5 — Ledger Conservation\n216\t\n217\t**Statement:**\n218\t> Internal ledger operations must satisfy: Σ(balances before) = Σ(balances after), except for protocol-defined fees (if any) or explicitly defined mint/burn logic.\n219\t\n220\t**Formal Definition:**\n221\t```\n222\t∀ transaction T:\n223\t  Σ(all_balances_after(T)) = Σ(all_balances_before(T)) - fees(T) - burns(T) + mints(T)\n224\t\n225\tWHERE:\n226\t  fees(T) = 0 for internal TBC transfers (zero-fee guarantee)\n227\t  burns(T) = 0 (no burn mechanism in current protocol)\n228\t  mints(T) = 0 (no mint mechanism in payment hub)\n229\t```\n230\t\n231\t**Guaranteed Properties:**\n232\t- Total TBC in the system is conserved during transfers\n233\t- No funds can be created or destroyed during transfers\n234\t- Internal transfers have zero fees\n235\t- Balance sum is an invariant across all operations\n236\t\n237\t**Implementation Requirements:**\n238\t1. Every debit MUST have a corresponding credit of equal amount\n239\t2. No rounding errors or precision loss\n240\t3. No hidden fees deducted from transfers\n241\t4. Explicit tracking of any future fee mechanisms\n242\t\n243\t**Contract Mapping:**\n244\t- `PaymentHub.tact`: Direct balance arithmetic (lines 197-198)\n245\t- `MerchantPaymentHub.tact`: Symmetric debit/credit (lines 178-187)\n246\t\n247\t**Test Coverage:**\n248\t- `tests/invariants/I5-ledger-conservation.spec.ts`\n249\t- Test: Sum of balances unchanged after transfer\n250\t- Test: Multiple concurrent transfers preserve total supply\n251\t- Test: Self-transfer does not create/destroy funds\n252\t\n253\t---\n254\t\n255\t### I6 — Lock ≠ Confiscation\n256\t\n257\t**Statement:**\n258\t> Account locks prevent outgoing transfers, do NOT seize or move funds, and are reversible.\n259\t\n260\t**Formal Definition:**\n261\t```\n262\t∀ account A, ∀ lock L in [FRAUD_LOCK, COLLATERAL_LOCK]:\n263\t  IF is_locked(A, L) THEN:\n264\t    can_send(A) = FALSE\n265\t    can_receive(A) = TRUE\n266\t    balance(A) = unchanged\n267\t    owner(A) = unchanged\n268\t    ∃ authorized_role R: R can clear_lock(A, L)\n269\t```\n270\t\n271\t**Guaranteed Properties:**\n272\t- Locks restrict actions, not ownership\n273\t- Locked accounts can still receive funds\n274\t- Locks do not transfer or freeze funds to protocol custody\n275\t- All locks are reversible by appropriate authority\n276\t- Lock operations emit auditable events\n277\t\n278\t**Implementation Requirements:**\n279\t1. Lock operations MUST NOT modify account balances\n280\t2. Receiving operations MUST remain functional when locked\n281\t3. Lock state is stored separately from balance/ownership\n282\t4. Lock/unlock operations emit events for transparency\n283\t\n284\t**Contract Mapping:**\n285\t- `account-locks.fc`: Lock operations don't touch balances (lines 100-110, 160-217)\n286\t- `account-locks.fc`: `can_receive()` always returns true (lines 94-98)\n287\t- `MerchantPaymentHub.tact`: Checks locks before send, not receive (lines 116-119)\n288\t\n289\t**Test Coverage:**\n290\t- `tests/invariants/I6-lock-not-confiscation.spec.ts`\n291\t- Test: Fraud lock prevents sending, allows receiving\n292\t- Test: Collateral lock prevents sending, allows receiving\n293\t- Test: Lock does not change balance\n294\t- Test: Lock can be reversed by authorized party\n295\t- Negative test: Lock cannot seize funds\n296\t\n297\t---\n298\t\n299\t### I7 — External Adapter Isolation\n300\t\n301\t**Statement:**\n302\t> External providers cannot trigger transfers, cannot bypass protocol rules, and can only interact through explicit user actions.\n303\t\n304\t**Formal Definition:**\n305\t```\n306\t∀ external_adapter E in [ChangeNOW, NOWPayments, CoinRabbit, TONCO]:\n307\t  ∀ protocol_operation O:\n308\t    E CANNOT directly invoke O\n309\t    E CANNOT bypass validation rules of O\n310\t    IF E participates in O THEN:\n311\t      O MUST be initiated by user U\n312\t      O MUST follow all invariants I1-I6\n313\t```\n314\t\n315\t**Guaranteed Properties:**\n316\t- External providers have no direct smart contract access\n317\t- All external interactions are mediated by user wallets\n318\t- Backend APIs orchestrate but don't execute transfers\n319\t- External adapters are read-only from protocol perspective\n320\t\n321\t**Implementation Requirements:**\n322\t1. No external adapter addresses in smart contract authorization\n323\t2. Backend services orchestrate user-signed transactions only\n324\t3. External adapters interact with user wallets, not protocol contracts\n325\t4. DEX interactions are user-initiated swaps\n326\t\n327\t**Contract Mapping:**\n328\t- `account-locks.fc`: Only `risk_authority` and `lending_adapter` have special roles, and they cannot move funds\n329\t- No external adapter addresses in Payment Hub contracts\n330\t- All transfers require NFT owner signature\n331\t\n332\t**Test Coverage:**\n333\t- `tests/invariants/I7-external-adapter-isolation.spec.ts`\n334\t- Test: External services cannot initiate transfers\n335\t- Test: All transfers require valid user signature\n336\t- Architectural review: No external adapter privileged access\n337\t\n338\t---\n339\t\n340\t## Invariant Violation Response\n341\t\n342\tIf any invariant is violated (detected through testing, audit, or production monitoring):\n343\t\n344\t1. **CRITICAL SEVERITY**: All invariant violations are critical\n345\t2. **IMMEDIATE HALT**: Affected operations must be stopped\n346\t3. **INCIDENT RESPONSE**: Follow security incident protocol\n347\t4. **ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS**: Full investigation required\n348\t5. **FIX VERIFICATION**: Must demonstrate invariant restoration\n349\t6. **AUDIT REVIEW**: Security audit of fix before deployment\n350\t\n351\t---\n352\t\n353\t## Audit Checklist\n354\t\n355\tFor auditors reviewing the TONBANKCARD protocol:\n356\t\n357\t### I1 — Non-Custodial Ownership\n358\t- [ ] All fund transfers verify NFT ownership\n359\t- [ ] No admin override for fund movement\n360\t- [ ] Backend services are read-only\n361\t- [ ] No custody mechanisms exist\n362\t\n363\t### I2 — NFT = Account Authority\n364\t- [ ] NFT ownership is queried on-chain for each operation\n365\t- [ ] No cached ownership for authorization\n366\t- [ ] No secondary authorization mechanisms\n367\t- [ ] Account control transfers with NFT\n368\t\n369\t### I3 — No Admin Fund Control\n370\t- [ ] No admin withdrawal functions\n371\t- [ ] Admin roles limited to non-financial operations\n372\t- [ ] No upgradeable proxies\n373\t- [ ] Test-only admin functions documented for removal\n374\t\n375\t### I4 — Atomic Transfers\n376\t- [ ] Balance updates are atomic\n377\t- [ ] Reentrancy protection implemented\n378\t- [ ] No intermediate states\n379\t- [ ] Failed transfers fully revert\n380\t\n381\t### I5 — Ledger Conservation\n382\t- [ ] Every debit has equal credit\n383\t- [ ] No hidden fees\n384\t- [ ] Total balance sum is preserved\n385\t- [ ] No rounding errors\n386\t\n387\t### I6 — Lock ≠ Confiscation\n388\t- [ ] Locks don't modify balances\n389\t- [ ] Locked accounts can receive\n390\t- [ ] Locks are reversible\n391\t- [ ] Lock events are emitted\n392\t\n393\t### I7 — External Adapter Isolation\n394\t- [ ] No external adapter direct contract access\n395\t- [ ] All operations user-initiated\n396\t- [ ] No bypass mechanisms\n397\t- [ ] Backend is orchestration-only\n398\t\n399\t---\n400\t\n401\t## Invariant-to-Contract Mapping\n402\t\n403\t| Invariant | protocol. Any future Issue, PR, or governance proposal that violates them must:\n437\t\n438\t1. **Explicitly declare the violation** in the Issue/PR description\n439\t2. **Undergo protocol-level review** by security team\n440\t3. **Receive explicit governance approval** (future DAO mechanism)\n441\t4. **Update this document** with the new invariant definition\n442\t5. **Pass full audit** before deployment\n443\t\n444\t### Acceptable Changes\n445\tChanges that **do not** violate invariants and are acceptable without governance:\n446\t- Additional validation rules (more restrictive)\n447\t- New lock types (following I6 pattern)\n448\t- Performance optimizations (preserving semantics)\n449\t- Additional getter functions (read-only)\n450\t- Event additions (non-state-changing)\n451\t\n452\t### Prohibited Changes\n453\tChanges that **always** violate invariants and are prohibited:\n454\t- Admin fund withdrawal mechanisms\n455\t- Custody of user funds\n456\t- Non-atomic transfers\n457\t- Hidden fees or balance manipulation\n458\t- NFT ownership bypass mechanisms\n459\t- Irreversible confiscation locks\n460\t\n461\t---\n462\t\n463\t##    [solve worker-1]       "content": "# TONBANKCARD Protocol — Formal Invariants & Guarantees\n\n**Document Type:** Security Foundation\n**Status:** Formal Specification\n**Issue Reference:** [#18 - Issue 4.1 Formal Invariants & Protocol Guarantees](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/18)\n**Last Updated:** 2025-12-27\n\n---\n\n## Purpose\n\nThis document defines the **core invariants and guarantees** of the TONBANKCARD protocol. These invariants are non-negotiable rules that must always hold true across all smart contracts, adapters, and future extensions.\n\nThese invariants form the basis for:\n- Security audits\n- Formal verification\n- Governance decisions\n- Ecosystem integrations\n\n**Any violation of these invariants represents a critical security vulnerability.**\n\n---\n\n## Core Protocol Invariants\n\n### I1 — Non-Custodial Ownership\n\n**Statement:**\n> At no point may the protocol take custody of user funds, move funds without explicit user-initiated transactions, or override NFT ownership.\n\n**Formal Definition:**\n```\n∀ transaction T, ∀ user U:\n  IF T transfers funds from U's account\n  THEN T MUST be signed by U (the NFT owner)\n  AND T MUST be initiated by U\n  AND no protocol admin/operator can initiate T on behalf of U\n```\n\n**Guaranteed Properties:**\n- The owner of the NFT account is the sole authority over the associated on-chain balance\n- No smart contract can move funds without the NFT owner's explicit signature\n- No backend service can initiate fund transfers\n- No external adapter can trigger fund movement\n\n**Implementation Requirements:**\n1. All transfer functions MUST verify `msg.sender == NFT_owner`\n2. No admin override functions are permitted\n3. No proxy delegation to third parties for fund movement\n4. Backend services are read-only\n\n**Contract Mapping:**\n- `PaymentHub.tact`: Verifies ownership in `TransferInternalRequest` handler (line 164)\n- `MerchantPaymentHub.tact`: Validates payer ownership before settlement (lines 90-96)\n- `account-locks.fc`: Lock mechanisms do not move funds, only restrict operations\n\n**Test Coverage:**\n- `tests/invariants/I1-non-custodial-ownership.spec.ts`\n- Negative test: Attempt transfer from non-owner account\n- Negative test: Admin attempting to move user funds\n\n---\n\n### I2 — NFT = Account Authority\n\n**Statement:**\n> Each NFT represents exactly one account. Account control is transferred only via NFT transfer. No secondary ownership mechanisms are allowed.\n\n**Formal Definition:**\n```\n∀ NFT n, ∀ account a:\n  account_authority(a) = NFT_owner(n)\n  AND ∀ time t1, t2 where t2 > t1:\n    IF NFT_owner(n, t1) ≠ NFT_owner(n, t2)\n    THEN account_authority(a, t2) = NFT_owner(n, t2)\n```\n\n**Guaranteed Properties:**\n- NFT ownership is the single source of truth for account authority\n- Account control transfers atomically with NFT ownership transfer\n- No separate \"authorized users\" or \"delegates\" with fund control\n- No multi-signature override without multi-sig NFT ownership\n\n**Implementation Requirements:**\n1. Always query current NFT owner on-chain before operations\n2. No cached ownership records for fund control decisions\n3. NFT transfer automatically updates account authority\n4. No separate authorization layer\n\n**Contract Mapping:**\n- `PaymentHub.tact`: Uses `owner` field from `AccountState` (line 36)\n- `MerchantPaymentHub.tact`: Stores and validates NFT owners (lines 42, 90-96)\n- `nft_account_resolver.fc`: Resolves NFT ownership as authority source (lines 61-69)\n\n**Test Coverage:**\n- `tests/invariants/I2-nft-account-authority.spec.ts`\n- Test: NFT transfer updates account authority\n- Negative test: Previous owner cannot transact after NFT transfer\n\n---\n\n### I3 — No Admin Fund Control\n\n**Statement:**\n> The protocol must not contain admin withdrawals, emergency drains, privileged fund movement, or hidden upgrade paths.\n\n**Formal Definition:**\n```\n∀ role R in [admin, operator, risk_authority, lending_adapter]:\n  ∀ account A:\n    R CANNOT initiate fund transfer from A\n    R CANNOT withdraw from A\n    R CANNOT modify balance(A) except through user-initiated transfers\n    R CANNOT upgrade contracts to bypass these restrictions\n    R CAN transfer the admin role to another address only via the two-phase timelock\n```\n\n**Guaranteed Properties:**\n- No role other than the NFT owner can initiate fund transfers\n- Admin roles (admin, risk authority, lending adapter) can only set flags/states\n- No emergency withdrawal functions exist\n- No upgradeable proxies that could bypass these rules\n- Development/testing admin functions MUST be removed before production\n- Admin role is transferable but ONLY via two-phase timelock (7-day delay)\n- Admin role transfer does NOT affect user fund ownership or balances\n\n**Implementation Requirements:**\n1. Admin roles limited to non-financial operations:\n   - Admin: Whitelist NFT collections, initialize accounts (testing only)\n   - Risk authority: Set/clear fraud locks only\n   - Lending adapter: Set/clear collateral locks only\n2. No `onlyAdmin` functions that move funds\n3. No upgradeable proxy patterns\n4. All contracts are immutable after deployment\n\n**Admin Transfer Mechanism (Issue #96):**\n\nTo prevent single-point-of-failure from the deployer key and allow migration to DAO/multisig, the `admin` role supports two-phase transferable ownership with a 7-day timelock:\n\n1. **Phase 1 — Propose** (`ProposeAdminTransfer` / `MerchantProposeAdminTransfer`):\n   - Only the current admin can call this\n   - Records the proposed new admin and a timestamp = `now() + 7 days`\n   - Does NOT change admin immediately\n2. **Phase 2 — Execute** (`ExecuteAdminTransfer` / `MerchantExecuteAdminTransfer`):\n   - Only the proposed new admin can call this\n   - Can only execute after the 7-day timelock has elapsed\n   - Commits the admin change; clears the pending proposal\n3. **Cancel** (`CancelAdminTransfer` / `MerchantCancelAdminTransfer`):\n   - Only the current admin can cancel a pending proposal before it executes\n\nThe same two-phase timelock pattern applies to `risk_authority` and `lending_adapter` roles in `account-locks.fc` (op codes `0x4001`–`0x4013`).\n\n**Contract Mapping:**\n- `PaymentHub.tact`: `admin` field replaces `deployer`; admin transfer via `ProposeAdminTransfer`/`ExecuteAdminTransfer`/`CancelAdminTransfer`\n- `MerchantPaymentHub.tact`: Same pattern via `MerchantProposeAdminTransfer`/`MerchantExecuteAdminTransfer`/`MerchantCancelAdminTransfer`\n- `account-locks.fc`: `risk_authority` and `lending_adapter` transferable via `op::propose_risk_authority` / `op::execute_risk_authority` / `op::cancel_risk_authority` and equivalents for `lending_adapter`\n\n**Test Coverage:**\n- `tests/invariants/I3-no-admin-fund-control.spec.ts`\n  - Negative test: Admin cannot withdraw user funds\n  - Negative test: Risk authority cannot move funds\n  - Negative test: Deployer cannot drain account balances\n  - Positive test: Admin can propose a transfer\n  - Negative test: Execution before timelock expiry is rejected\n  - Positive test: Execution after timelock succeeds; user funds unchanged\n  - Negative test: New admin cannot move user funds (I3 preserved post-transfer)\n  - Positive test: Admin can cancel a pending transfer\n- `tests/admin-transfer/PaymentHub-admin-transfer.spec.ts` — comprehensive admin transfer tests\n- `tests/admin-transfer/MerchantPaymentHub-admin-transfer.spec.ts` — comprehensive admin transfer tests\n\n---\n\n### I4 — Atomic Transfers\n\n**Statement:**\n> All internal transfers must be atomic, fully settled or reverted, and free from intermediate states.\n\n**Formal Definition:**\n```\n∀ transfer T from account A to account B with amount X:\n  EITHER:\n    (balance(A) = balance(A)_before - X) AND\n    (balance(B) = balance(B)_before + X) AND\n    (T.status = SUCCESS)\n  OR:\n    (balance(A) = balance(A)_before) AND\n    (balance(B) = balance(B)_before) AND\n    (T.status = REVERTED)\n```\n\n**Guaranteed Properties:**\n- A transfer either completes fully or does not occur at all\n- No partial balance updates\n- No intermediate states where funds are \"in flight\"\n- Reentrancy protection ensures atomicity\n\n**Implementation Requirements:**\n1. Use transaction revert on any validation failure\n2. Update both sender and receiver balances in same transaction\n3. Implement reentrancy guards\n4. No asynchronous balance updates\n\n**Contract Mapping:**\n- `PaymentHub.tact`: Atomic balance update (lines 196-202), reentrancy guard (lines 121, 149-150)\n- `MerchantPaymentHub.tact`: Atomic debit/credit (lines 134-135)\n\n**Test Coverage:**\n- `tests/invariants/I4-atomic-transfers.spec.ts`\n- Test: Successful transfer updates both balances atomically\n- Test: Failed transfer leaves both balances unchanged\n- Test: Reentrancy attempt is blocked\n\n---\n\n### I5 — Ledger Conservation\n\n**Statement:**\n> Internal ledger operations must satisfy: Σ(balances before) = Σ(balances after), except for protocol-defined fees (if any) or explicitly defined mint/burn logic.\n\n**Formal Definition:**\n```\n∀ transaction T:\n  Σ(all_balances_after(T)) = Σ(all_balances_before(T)) - fees(T) - burns(T) + mints(T)\n\nWHERE:\n  fees(T) = 0 for internal TBC transfers (zero-fee guarantee)\n  burns(T) = 0 (no burn mechanism in current protocol)\n  mints(T) = 0 (no mint mechanism in payment hub)\n```\n\n**Guaranteed Properties:**\n- Total TBC in the system is conserved during transfers\n- No funds can be created or destroyed during transfers\n- Internal transfers have zero fees\n- Balance sum is an invariant across all operations\n\n**Implementation Requirements:**\n1. Every debit MUST have a corresponding credit of equal amount\n2. No rounding errors or precision loss\n3. No hidden fees deducted from transfers\n4. Explicit tracking of any future fee mechanisms\n\n**Contract Mapping:**\n- `PaymentHub.tact`: Direct balance arithmetic (lines 197-198)\n- `MerchantPaymentHub.tact`: Symmetric debit/credit (lines 178-187)\n\n**Test Coverage:**\n- `tests/invariants/I5-ledger-conservation.spec.ts`\n- Test: Sum of balances unchanged after transfer\n- Test: Multiple concurrent transfers preserve total supply\n- Test: Self-transfer does not create/destroy funds\n\n---\n\n### I6 — Lock ≠ Confiscation\n\n**Statement:**\n> Account locks prevent outgoing transfers, do NOT seize or move funds, and are reversible.\n\n**Formal Definition:**\n```\n∀ account A, ∀ lock L in [FRAUD_LOCK, COLLATERAL_LOCK]:\n  IF is_locked(A, L) THEN:\n    can_send(A) = FALSE\n    can_receive(A) = TRUE\n    balance(A) = unchanged\n    owner(A) = unchanged\n    ∃ authorized_role R: R can clear_lock(A, L)\n```\n\n**Guaranteed Properties:**\n- Locks restrict actions, not ownership\n- Locked accounts can still receive funds\n- Locks do not transfer or freeze funds to protocol custody\n- All locks are reversible by appropriate authority\n- Lock operations emit auditable events\n\n**Implementation Requirements:**\n1. Lock operations MUST NOT modify account balances\n2. Receiving operations MUST remain functional when locked\n3. Lock state is stored separately from balance/ownership\n4. Lock/unlock operations emit events for transparency\n\n**Contract Mapping:**\n- `account-locks.fc`: Lock operations don't touch balances (lines 100-110, 160-217)\n- `account-locks.fc`: `can_receive()` always returns true (lines 94-98)\n- `MerchantPaymentHub.tact`: Checks locks before send, not receive (lines 116-119)\n\n**Test Coverage:**\n- `tests/invariants/I6-lock-not-confiscation.spec.ts`\n- Test: Fraud lock prevents sending, allows receiving\n- Test: Collateral lock prevents sending, allows receiving\n- Test: Lock does not change balance\n- Test: Lock can be reversed by authorized party\n- Negative test: Lock cannot seize funds\n\n---\n\n### I7 — External Adapter Isolation\n\n**Statement:**\n> External providers cannot trigger transfers, cannot bypass protocol rules, and can only interact through explicit user actions.\n\n**Formal Definition:**\n```\n∀ external_adapter E in [ChangeNOW, NOWPayments, CoinRabbit, TONCO]:\n  ∀ protocol_operation O:\n    E CANNOT directly invoke O\n    E CANNOT bypass validation rules of O\n    IF E participates in O THEN:\n      O MUST be initiated by user U\n      O MUST follow all invariants I1-I6\n```\n\n**Guaranteed Properties:**\n- External providers have no direct smart contract access\n- All external interactions are mediated by user wallets\n- Backend APIs orchestrate but don't execute transfers\n- External adapters are read-only from protocol perspective\n\n**Implementation Requirements:**\n1. No external adapter addresses in smart contract authorization\n2. Backend services orchestrate user-signed transactions only\n3. External adapters interact with user wallets, not protocol contracts\n4. DEX interactions are user-initiated swaps\n\n**Contract Mapping:**\n- `account-locks.fc`: Only `risk_authority` and `lending_adapter` have special roles, and they cannot move funds\n- No external adapter addresses in Payment Hub contracts\n- All transfers require NFT owner signature\n\n**Test Coverage:**\n- `tests/invariants/I7-external-adapter-isolation.spec.ts`\n- Test: External services cannot initiate transfers\n- Test: All transfers require valid user signature\n- Architectural review: No external adapter privileged access\n\n---\n\n## Invariant Violation Response\n\nIf any invariant is violated (detected through testing, audit, or production monitoring):\n\n1. **CRITICAL SEVERITY**: All invariant violations are critical\n2. **IMMEDIATE HALT**: Affected operations must be stopped\n3. **INCIDENT RESPONSE**: Follow security incident protocol\n4. **ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS**: Full investigation required\n5. **FIX VERIFICATION**: Must demonstrate invariant restoration\n6. **AUDIT REVIEW**: Security audit of fix before deployment\n\n---\n\n## Audit Checklist\n\nFor auditors reviewing the TONBANKCARD protocol:\n\n### I1 — Non-Custodial Ownership\n- [ ] All fund transfers verify NFT ownership\n- [ ] No admin override for fund movement\n- [ ] Backend services are read-only\n- [ ] No custody mechanisms exist\n\n### I2 — NFT = Account Authority\n- [ ] NFT ownership is queried on-chain for each operation\n- [ ] No cached ownership for authorization\n- [ ] No secondary authorization mechanisms\n- [ ] Account control transfers with NFT\n\n### I3 — No Admin Fund Control\n- [ ] No admin withdrawal functions\n- [ ] Admin roles limited to non-financial operations\n- [ ] No upgradeable proxies\n- [ ] Test-only admin functions documented for removal\n\n### I4 — Atomic Transfers\n- [ ] Balance updates are atomic\n- [ ] Reentrancy protection implemented\n- [ ] No intermediate states\n- [ ] Failed transfers fully revert\n\n### I5 — Ledger Conservation\n- [ ] Every debit has equal credit\n- [ ] No hidden fees\n- [ ] Total balance sum is preserved\n- [ ] No rounding errors\n\n### I6 — Lock ≠ Confiscation\n- [ ] Locks don't modify balances\n- [ ] Locked accounts can receive\n- [ ] Locks are reversible\n- [ ] Lock events are emitted\n\n### I7 — External Adapter Isolation\n- [ ] No external adapter direct contract access\n- [ ] All operations user-initiated\n- [ ] No bypass mechanisms\n- [ ] Backend is orchestration-only\n\n---\n\n## Invariant-to-Contract Mapping\n\n| Invariant | PaymentHub.tact | MerchantPaymentHub.tact | account-locks.fc `tests/invariants/I2-nft-account-authority.spec.ts`\n- `tests/invariants/I3-no-admin-fund-control.spec.ts`\n- `tests/invariants/I4-atomic-transfers.spec.ts`\n- Violations)\nEach invariant test file includes negative test cases that attempt to violate the invariant and verify the violation is prevented.\n\n---\n\n## Governance & Protocol Evolution\n\n### Invariant Changes\nThese invariants are **foundational** to the protocol. Any future Issue, PR, or governance proposal that violates them must:\n\n1. **Explicitly declare the violation** in the Issue/PR description\n2. **Undergo protocol-level review** by security team\n3. **Receive explicit governance approval** (future DAO mechanism)\n4. **Update this document** with the new invariant definition\n5. **Pass full audit** before deployment\n\n### Acceptable Changes\nChanges that **do not** violate invariants and are acceptable without governance:\n- Additional validation rules (more restrictive)\n- New lock types (following I6 pattern)\n- Performance optimizations (preserving semantics)\n- Additional getter functions (read-only)\n- Event additions (non-state-changing)\n\n### Prohibited Changes\nChanges that **always** violate invariants and are prohibited:\n- Admin fund withdrawal mechanisms\n- Custody of user funds\n- Non-atomic transfers\n- Hidden fees or balance manipulation\n- NFT ownership bypass mechanisms\n- Irreversible confiscation locks\n\n---\n\n## References\n\n- **Architecture**: [docs/architecture.md](./architecture.md)\n- **Payment Hub**: [contracts/payments/README.md](../contracts/payments/README.md)\n- **Account Locks**: [contracts/payments/ACCOUNT_LOCKS.md](../contracts/payments/ACCOUNT_LOCKS.md)\n- **Contributing**: [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md)\n- **Issue #18**: [Formal Invariants & Protocol Guarantees](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/18)\n\n---\n\n## Document Maintenance\n\n**Responsibility**: Protocol Security Team\n**Review Frequency**: Before each major release\n**Update Triggers**:\n- New smart contract deployment\n- Protocol architecture changes\n- Security audit findings\n- Governance decisions\n\n**Version History**:\n- v1.0 (2025-12-27): Initial formal specification (Issue #18)\n\n---\n\n**Built on TON. The companion configuration `Protocol.cfg` instantiates\n\\* small constants (NFTs, Owners) so TLC can finish in seconds.\n\\*\n\\* See `docs/formal-verification/README.md` for usage.\n\nEXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets, TLC\n\nCONSTANTS\n    NFTs,         \\* finite set of NFT account identifiers\n    Owners,       \\* finite set of possible NFT owners (subset of all addresses)\n    AdminAddr,    \\* the single admin address\n    RiskAuthAddr, \\* risk authority address\n    LendingAddr,  \\* lending adapter address\n    Amounts       \\* finite set of allowed transfer amounts (e.g. {0, 1, 2, 3})\n\nVARIABLES\n    balance,    \\* [NFT -> Nat]\n    owner,      \\* [NFT -> Owners]\n    fraud,      \\* [NFT -> BOOLEAN]\n    collat      \\* [NFT -> BOOLEAN]\n\nvars == << balance, owner, fraud, collat >>\n\n\\* Initial state: all balances start at 0 except the seed allocation, and no\n\\* account is locked.    [solve worker-1]     "originalFile": "# TONBANKCARD Protocol — Formal Invariants & Guarantees\n\n**Document Type:** Security Foundation\n**Status:** Formal Specification\n**Issue Reference:** [#18 - Issue 4.1 Formal Invariants & Protocol Guarantees](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/18)\n**Last Updated:** 2025-12-27\n\n---\n\n## Purpose\n\nThis document defines the **core invariants and guarantees** of the TONBANKCARD protocol. These invariants are non-negotiable rules that must always hold true across all smart contracts, adapters, and future extensions.\n\nThese invariants form the basis for:\n- Security audits\n- Formal verification\n- Governance decisions\n- Ecosystem integrations\n\n**Any violation of these invariants represents a critical security vulnerability.**\n\n---\n\n## Core Protocol Invariants\n\n### I1 — Non-Custodial Ownership\n\n**Statement:**\n> At no point may the protocol take custody of user funds, move funds without explicit user-initiated transactions, or override NFT ownership.\n\n**Formal Definition:**\n```\n∀ transaction T, ∀ user U:\n  IF T transfers funds from U's account\n  THEN T MUST be signed by U (the NFT owner)\n  AND T MUST be initiated by U\n  AND no protocol admin/operator can initiate T on behalf of U\n```\n\n**Guaranteed Properties:**\n- The owner of the NFT account is the sole authority over the associated on-chain balance\n- No smart contract can move funds without the NFT owner's explicit signature\n- No backend service can initiate fund transfers\n- No external adapter can trigger fund movement\n\n**Implementation Requirements:**\n1. All transfer functions MUST verify `msg.sender == NFT_owner`\n2. No admin override functions are permitted\n3. No proxy delegation to third parties for fund movement\n4. Backend services are read-only\n\n**Contract Mapping:**\n- `PaymentHub.tact`: Verifies ownership in `TransferInternalRequest` handler (line 164)\n- `MerchantPaymentHub.tact`: Validates payer ownership before settlement (lines 90-96)\n- `account-locks.fc`: Lock mechanisms do not move funds, only restrict operations\n\n**Test Coverage:**\n- `tests/invariants/I1-non-custodial-ownership.spec.ts`\n- Negative test: Attempt transfer from non-owner account\n- Negative test: Admin attempting to move user funds\n\n---\n\n### I2 — NFT = Account Authority\n\n**Statement:**\n> Each NFT represents exactly one account. Account control is transferred only via NFT transfer. No secondary ownership mechanisms are allowed.\n\n**Formal Definition:**\n```\n∀ NFT n, ∀ account a:\n  account_authority(a) = NFT_owner(n)\n  AND ∀ time t1, t2 where t2 > t1:\n    IF NFT_owner(n, t1) ≠ NFT_owner(n, t2)\n    THEN account_authority(a, t2) = NFT_owner(n, t2)\n```\n\n**Guaranteed Properties:**\n- NFT ownership is the single source of truth for account authority\n- Account control transfers atomically with NFT ownership transfer\n- No separate \"authorized users\" or \"delegates\" with fund control\n- No multi-signature override without multi-sig NFT ownership\n\n**Implementation Requirements:**\n1. Always query current NFT owner on-chain before operations\n2. No cached ownership records for fund control decisions\n3. NFT transfer automatically updates account authority\n4. No separate authorization layer\n\n**Contract Mapping:**\n- `PaymentHub.tact`: Uses `owner` field from `AccountState` (line 36)\n- `MerchantPaymentHub.tact`: Stores and validates NFT owners (lines 42, 90-96)\n- `nft_account_resolver.fc`: Resolves NFT ownership as authority source (lines 61-69)\n\n**Test Coverage:**\n- `tests/invariants/I2-nft-account-authority.spec.ts`\n- Test: NFT transfer updates account authority\n- Negative test: Previous owner cannot transact after NFT transfer\n\n---\n\n### I3 — No Admin Fund Control\n\n**Statement:**\n> The protocol must not contain admin withdrawals, emergency drains, privileged fund movement, or hidden upgrade paths.\n\n**Formal Definition:**\n```\n∀ role R in [admin, operator, risk_authority, lending_adapter]:\n  ∀ account A:\n    R CANNOT initiate fund transfer from A\n    R CANNOT withdraw from A\n    R CANNOT modify balance(A) except through user-initiated transfers\n    R CANNOT upgrade contracts to bypass these restrictions\n    R CAN transfer the admin role to another address only via the two-phase timelock\n```\n\n**Guaranteed Properties:**\n- No role other than the NFT owner can initiate fund transfers\n- Admin roles (admin, risk authority, lending adapter) can only set flags/states\n- No emergency withdrawal functions exist\n- No upgradeable proxies that could bypass these rules\n- Development/testing admin functions MUST be removed before production\n- Admin role is transferable but ONLY via two-phase timelock (7-day delay)\n- Admin role transfer does NOT affect user fund ownership or balances\n\n**Implementation Requirements:**\n1. Admin roles limited to non-financial operations:\n   - Admin: Whitelist NFT collections, initialize accounts (testing only)\n   - Risk authority: Set/clear fraud locks only\n   - Lending adapter: Set/clear collateral locks only\n2. No `onlyAdmin` functions that move funds\n3. No upgradeable proxy patterns\n4. All contracts are immutable after deployment\n\n**Admin Transfer Mechanism (Issue #96):**\n\nTo prevent single-point-of-failure from the deployer key and allow migration to DAO/multisig, the `admin` role supports two-phase transferable ownership with a 7-day timelock:\n\n1. **Phase 1 — Propose** (`ProposeAdminTransfer` / `MerchantProposeAdminTransfer`):\n   - Only the current admin can call this\n   - Records the proposed new admin and a timestamp = `now() + 7 days`\n   - Does NOT change admin immediately\n2. **Phase 2 — Execute** (`ExecuteAdminTransfer` / `MerchantExecuteAdminTransfer`):\n   - Only the proposed new admin can call this\n   - Can only execute after the 7-day timelock has elapsed\n   - Commits the admin change; clears the pending proposal\n3. **Cancel** (`CancelAdminTransfer` / `MerchantCancelAdminTransfer`):\n   - Only the current admin can cancel a pending proposal before it executes\n\nThe same two-phase timelock pattern applies to `risk_authority` and `lending_adapter` roles in `account-locks.fc` (op codes `0x4001`–`0x4013`).\n\n**Contract Mapping:**\n- `PaymentHub.tact`: `admin` field replaces `deployer`; admin transfer via `ProposeAdminTransfer`/`ExecuteAdminTransfer`/`CancelAdminTransfer`\n- `MerchantPaymentHub.tact`: Same pattern via `MerchantProposeAdminTransfer`/`MerchantExecuteAdminTransfer`/`MerchantCancelAdminTransfer`\n- `account-locks.fc`: `risk_authority` and `lending_adapter` transferable via `op::propose_risk_authority` / `op::execute_risk_authority` / `op::cancel_risk_authority` and equivalents for `lending_adapter`\n\n**Test Coverage:**\n- `tests/invariants/I3-no-admin-fund-control.spec.ts`\n  - Negative test: Admin cannot withdraw user funds\n  - Negative test: Risk authority cannot move funds\n  - Negative test: Deployer cannot drain account balances\n  - Positive test: Admin can propose a transfer\n  - Negative test: Execution before timelock expiry is rejected\n  - Positive test: Execution after timelock succeeds; user funds unchanged\n  - Negative test: New admin cannot move user funds (I3 preserved post-transfer)\n  - Positive test: Admin can cancel a pending transfer\n- `tests/admin-transfer/PaymentHub-admin-transfer.spec.ts` — comprehensive admin transfer tests\n- `tests/admin-transfer/MerchantPaymentHub-admin-transfer.spec.ts` — comprehensive admin transfer tests\n\n---\n\n### I4 — Atomic Transfers\n\n**Statement:**\n> All internal transfers must be atomic, fully settled or reverted, and free from intermediate states.\n\n**Formal Definition:**\n```\n∀ transfer T from account A to account B with amount X:\n  EITHER:\n    (balance(A) = balance(A)_before - X) AND\n    (balance(B) = balance(B)_before + X) AND\n    (T.status = SUCCESS)\n  OR:\n    (balance(A) = balance(A)_before) AND\n    (balance(B) = balance(B)_before) AND\n    (T.status = REVERTED)\n```\n\n**Guaranteed Properties:**\n- A transfer either completes fully or does not occur at all\n- No partial balance updates\n- No intermediate states where funds are \"in flight\"\n- Reentrancy protection ensures atomicity\n\n**Implementation Requirements:**\n1. Use transaction revert on any validation failure\n2. Update both sender and receiver balances in same transaction\n3. Implement reentrancy guards\n4. No asynchronous balance updates\n\n**Contract Mapping:**\n- `PaymentHub.tact`: Atomic balance update (lines 196-202), reentrancy guard (lines 121, 149-150)\n- `MerchantPaymentHub.tact`: Atomic debit/credit (lines 134-135)\n\n**Test Coverage:**\n- `tests/invariants/I4-atomic-transfers.spec.ts`\n- Test: Successful transfer updates both balances atomically\n- Test: Failed transfer leaves both balances unchanged\n- Test: Reentrancy attempt is blocked\n\n---\n\n### I5 — Ledger Conservation\n\n**Statement:**\n> Internal ledger operations must satisfy: Σ(balances before) = Σ(balances after), except for protocol-defined fees (if any) or explicitly defined mint/burn logic.\n\n**Formal Definition:**\n```\n∀ transaction T:\n  Σ(all_balances_after(T)) = Σ(all_balances_before(T)) - fees(T) - burns(T) + mints(T)\n\nWHERE:\n  fees(T) = 0 for internal TBC transfers (zero-fee guarantee)\n  burns(T) = 0 (no burn mechanism in current protocol)\n  mints(T) = 0 (no mint mechanism in payment hub)\n```\n\n**Guaranteed Properties:**\n- Total TBC in the system is conserved during transfers\n- No funds can be created or destroyed during transfers\n- Internal transfers have zero fees\n- Balance sum is an invariant across all operations\n\n**Implementation Requirements:**\n1. Every debit MUST have a corresponding credit of equal amount\n2. No rounding errors or precision loss\n3. No hidden fees deducted from transfers\n4. Explicit tracking of any future fee mechanisms\n\n**Contract Mapping:**\n- `PaymentHub.tact`: Direct balance arithmetic (lines 197-198)\n- `MerchantPaymentHub.tact`: Symmetric debit/credit (lines 178-187)\n\n**Test Coverage:**\n- `tests/invariants/I5-ledger-conservation.spec.ts`\n- Test: Sum of balances unchanged after transfer\n- Test: Multiple concurrent transfers preserve total supply\n- Test: Self-transfer does not create/destroy funds\n\n---\n\n### I6 — Lock ≠ Confiscation\n\n**Statement:**\n> Account locks prevent outgoing transfers, do NOT seize or move funds, and are reversible.\n\n**Formal Definition:**\n```\n∀ account A, ∀ lock L in [FRAUD_LOCK, COLLATERAL_LOCK]:\n  IF is_locked(A, L) THEN:\n    can_send(A) = FALSE\n    can_receive(A) = TRUE\n    balance(A) = unchanged\n    owner(A) = unchanged\n    ∃ authorized_role R: R can clear_lock(A, L)\n```\n\n**Guaranteed Properties:**\n- Locks restrict actions, not ownership\n- Locked accounts can still receive funds\n- Locks do not transfer or freeze funds to protocol custody\n- All locks are reversible by appropriate authority\n- Lock operations emit auditable events\n\n**Implementation Requirements:**\n1. Lock operations MUST NOT modify account balances\n2. Receiving operations MUST remain functional when locked\n3. Lock state is stored separately from balance/ownership\n4. Lock/unlock operations emit events for transparency\n\n**Contract Mapping:**\n- `account-locks.fc`: Lock operations don't touch balances (lines 100-110, 160-217)\n- `account-locks.fc`: `can_receive()` always returns true (lines 94-98)\n- `MerchantPaymentHub.tact`: Checks locks before send, not receive (lines 116-119)\n\n**Test Coverage:**\n- `tests/invariants/I6-lock-not-confiscation.spec.ts`\n- Test: Fraud lock prevents sending, allows receiving\n- Test: Collateral lock prevents sending, allows receiving\n- Test: Lock does not change balance\n- Test: Lock can be reversed by authorized party\n- Negative test: Lock cannot seize funds\n\n---\n\n### I7 — External Adapter Isolation\n\n**Statement:**\n> External providers cannot trigger transfers, cannot bypass protocol rules, and can only interact through explicit user actions.\n\n**Formal Definition:**\n```\n∀ external_adapter E in [ChangeNOW, NOWPayments, CoinRabbit, TONCO]:\n  ∀ protocol_operation O:\n    E CANNOT directly invoke O\n    E CANNOT bypass validation rules of O\n    IF E participates in O THEN:\n      O MUST be initiated by user U\n      O MUST follow all invariants I1-I6\n```\n\n**Guaranteed Properties:**\n- External providers have no direct smart contract access\n- All external interactions are mediated by user wallets\n- Backend APIs orchestrate but don't execute transfers\n- External adapters are read-only from protocol perspective\n\n**Implementation Requirements:**\n1. No external adapter addresses in smart contract authorization\n2. Backend services orchestrate user-signed transactions only\n3. External adapters interact with user wallets, not protocol contracts\n4. DEX interactions are user-initiated swaps\n\n**Contract Mapping:**\n- `account-locks.fc`: Only `risk_authority` and `lending_adapter` have special roles, and they cannot move funds\n- No external adapter addresses in Payment Hub contracts\n- All transfers require NFT owner signature\n\n**Test Coverage:**\n- `tests/invariants/I7-external-adapter-isolation.spec.ts`\n- Test: External services cannot initiate transfers\n- Test: All transfers require valid user signature\n- Architectural review: No external adapter privileged access\n\n---\n\n## Invariant Violation Response\n\nIf any invariant is violated (detected through testing, audit, or production monitoring):\n\n1. **CRITICAL SEVERITY**: All invariant violations are critical\n2. **IMMEDIATE HALT**: Affected operations must be stopped\n3. **INCIDENT RESPONSE**: Follow security incident protocol\n4. **ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS**: Full investigation required\n5. **FIX VERIFICATION**: Must demonstrate invariant restoration\n6. **AUDIT REVIEW**: Security audit of fix before deployment\n\n---\n\n## Audit Checklist\n\nFor auditors reviewing the TONBANKCARD protocol:\n\n### I1 — Non-Custodial Ownership\n- [ ] All fund transfers verify NFT ownership\n- [ ] No admin override for fund movement\n- [ ] Backend services are read-only\n- [ ] No custody mechanisms exist\n\n### I2 — NFT = Account Authority\n- [ ] NFT ownership is queried on-chain for each operation\n- [ ] No cached ownership for authorization\n- [ ] No secondary authorization mechanisms\n- [ ] Account control transfers with NFT\n\n### I3 — No Admin Fund Control\n- [ ] No admin withdrawal functions\n- [ ] Admin roles limited to non-financial operations\n- [ ] No upgradeable proxies\n- [ ] Test-only admin functions documented for removal\n\n### I4 — Atomic Transfers\n- [ ] Balance updates are atomic\n- [ ] Reentrancy protection implemented\n- [ ] No intermediate states\n- [ ] Failed transfers fully revert\n\n### I5 — Ledger Conservation\n- [ ] Every debit has equal credit\n- [ ] No hidden fees\n- [ ] Total balance sum is preserved\n- [ ] No rounding errors\n\n### I6 — Lock ≠ Confiscation\n- [ ] Locks don't modify balances\n- [ ] Locked accounts can receive\n- [ ] Locks are reversible\n- [ ] Lock events are emitted\n\n### I7 — External Adapter Isolation\n- [ ] No external adapter direct contract access\n- [ ] All operations user-initiated\n- [ ] No bypass mechanisms\n- [ ] Backend is orchestration-only\n\n---\n\n## Invariant-to-Contract Mapping\n\n| Invariant | PaymentHub.tact | MerchantPaymentHub.tact | account-locks.fc Invariant Changes\nThese invariants are **foundational** to the protocol. Any future Issue, PR, or governance proposal that violates them must:\n\n1. **Explicitly declare the violation** in the Issue/PR description\n2. **Undergo protocol-level review** by security team\n3. **Receive explicit governance approval** (future DAO mechanism)\n4. **Update this document** with the new invariant definition\n5. **Pass full audit** before deployment\n\n### Acceptable Changes\nChanges that **do not** violate invariants and are acceptable without governance:\n- Additional validation rules (more restrictive)\n- New lock types (following I6 pattern)\n- Performance optimizations (preserving semantics)\n- Additional getter functions (read-only)\n- Event additions (non-state-changing)\n\n### Prohibited Changes\nChanges that **always** violate invariants and are prohibited:\n- Admin fund withdrawal mechanisms\n- Custody of user funds\n- Non-atomic transfers\n- Hidden fees or balance manipulation\n- NFT ownership bypass mechanisms\n- Irreversible confiscation locks\n\n---\n\n## References\n\n- **Architecture**: [docs/architecture.md](./architecture.md)\n- **Payment Hub**: [contracts/payments/README.md](../contracts/payments/README.md)\n- **Account Locks**: [contracts/payments/ACCOUNT_LOCKS.md](../contracts/payments/ACCOUNT_LOCKS.md)\n- **Contributing**: [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md)\n- **Issue #18**: [Formal Invariants & Protocol Guarantees](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/18)\n\n---\n\n## Document Maintenance\n\n**Responsibility**: Protocol Security Team\n**Review Frequency**: Before each major release\n**Update Triggers**:\n- New smart contract deployment\n- Protocol architecture changes\n- Security audit findings\n- Governance decisions\n\n**Version History**:\n- v1.0 (2025-12-27): Initial formal specification (Issue #18)\n\n---\n\n**Built on TON.
