   [solve worker-1]     "content": "# A4 — Penetration Test Plan\n\n**Engagement ID:** `A4`\n**Issue:** [#115](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/115)\n**Plan:** [`ENGAGEMENT.md`](./ENGAGEMENT.md)\n**OWASP coverage:** [`OWASP_CHECKLIST.md`](./OWASP_CHECKLIST.md)\n**Status tracker:** [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md)\n**Last Updated:** 2026-05-16\n\n---\n\n## 1. Test Environment\n\n### 1.1 Targets\n\nThe pentester exercises three packages, each at the audited commit recorded in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §\"Audited commit\":\n\n| Package | Version | Surface tested |\n|---------|---------|----------------|\n| `@tonbankcard/merchant-api` | 1.0.0 | HTTP REST endpoints + Express middleware stack |\n| `@tonbankcard/payment-indexer` | 1.0.0 | HTTP read endpoints + ingestion pipeline + database |\n| `@tonbankcard/merchant-sdk` | 1.0.0 | npm package, published bundle, browser widget |\n\n### 1.2 Staging environment\n\nThe protocol team provides a representative **staging environment** at engagement kickoff. The environment is shaped to match the production deployment topology so OWASP Top 10 findings are reproducible against the same surface the production launch will expose.\n\n| Component | Staging configuration | Notes |\n|-----------|----------------------|-------|\n| Merchant API | `https://staging-api.<staging-host>` | Same Helmet / CORS / rate-limit configuration as production; backed by isolated Postgres + Redis |\n| Indexer | `https://staging-indexer.<staging-host>` (internal-only by default) | Backed by SQLite (default) and a parallel Postgres for the integrity tests in §3.2.4 |\n| TON network | Testnet (`https://testnet.toncenter.com/api/v2/...`) | Throwaway TON HTTP API key; no production TBC issuance |\n| SDK consumer harness | `https://staging-merchant.<staging-host>` | Plain HTML page embedding `@tonbankcard/merchant-sdk` against staging API; isolated CSP for the widget tests in §3.3 |\n| Webhook receiver | `https://staging-webhook.<staging-host>` | Logging-only sink the pentester controls; used for §3.3 webhook tests |\n| TON wallet | Tonkeeper / MyTonWallet on testnet | Pentester-controlled funded testnet wallet |\n\nThe staging environment is provisioned **after D4 hardening lands**. Production secrets are never present; throwaway API keys are issued for the pentester with the same scope model as production. The staging URL set is recorded in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §3.\n\nThe pentester is granted:\n\n- Two API keys per scope (`invoices:read`, `invoices:write`) under two distinct merchant tenants A and B, to support cross-tenant IDOR tests (§3.1.2).\n- Direct network access to the indexer (the production-deployment hardening guidance is that the indexer is internal-only; the staging environment exposes it externally only to enable IDX-2 testing per [`OWASP_CHECKLIST.md`](./OWASP_CHECKLIST.md) §A01.5).\n- A snapshot of `npm-audit` baselines for all three packages at the audited commit, recorded in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §9.\n\n### 1.3 Out-of-environment items\n\nThe pentester does **not** receive:\n\n- Production secrets, production API keys, or production database credentials.\n- Operator-controlled cloud infrastructure access (Kubernetes, managed Postgres, Redis cluster).\n- Source access to third-party payment gateways (ChangeNOW, NOWPayments, CoinRabbit) — these are out of scope per [`ENGAGEMENT.md`](./ENGAGEMENT.md) §3.\n\nIf a test requires access not listed in §1.2, the pentester opens a Q-entry in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §11 rather than improvising.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Tooling Baseline\n\nThe following baseline tooling is expected; the pentester may add equivalents.\n\n| Class | Tools |\n|-------|-------|\n| HTTP intercept / fuzz | Burp Suite Professional, OWASP ZAP, mitmproxy |\n| Request scripting | `curl`, [`httpie`](https://httpie.io/), Postman, Node `fetch` |\n| Webhook capture & replay | [`smee.io`](https://smee.io/), [`ngrok`](https://ngrok.com/), custom Node listener |\n| SQL injection | `sqlmap`, manual payload sets |\n| Dependency audit | `npm audit`, `npm ls --all`, `osv-scanner`, `socket.dev` reports |\n| SDK bundle inspection | `npm pack`, `tar -xvf`, `source-map-explorer`, `esbuild --analyze` |\n| TLS posture | `testssl.sh`, `nmap --script ssl-enum-ciphers` |\n| Network surface | `nmap`, `masscan` (rate-limited, staging only) |\n| Browser exploit harness | Headless Chromium via Playwright; manual Firefox + Chromium DevTools |\n| Timing analysis | Node scripts driving `process.hrtime.bigint()`, `wrk2`, custom statistical helpers |\n\nAll tooling outputs that feed a finding are archived in the engagement bundle (see §4).\n\n---\n\n## 3. Per-Component Test Cases\n\nThe threat IDs cited below are defined in [`ENGAGEMENT.md`](./ENGAGEMENT.md) §4 and mirrored in the OWASP coverage rows of [`OWASP_CHECKLIST.md`](./OWASP_CHECKLIST.md).\n\n### 3.1 Merchant API (`api/`)\n\n#### 3.1.1 Authentication & authorisation\n\n| # | Case | Maps to | Expected behaviour |\n|---|------|---------|--------------------|\n| 3.1.1.1 | Send each mutating route with no `Authorization` header | API-1, A01.1 | `401 Unauthorized`; no side effects |\n| 3.1.1.2 | Send each mutating route with `Authorization: Bearer invalid` | API-1, A01.1, A07.1 | `401 Unauthorized`; logged under §3.1.6.2 |\n| 3.1.1.3 | Issue an `invoices:read` key and call every `invoices:write` route | API-1, A01.2 | `403 Forbidden`; no state change |\n| 3.1.1.4 | Issue an `invoices:write` key from tenant A and access tenant B's invoice via `GET /invoices/:id` | API-2, A01.3 | `404 Not Found`; response body identical to a non-existent ID |\n| 3.1.1.5 | Enumerate invoice IDs starting from a captured ID ±1, ±10, ±100 | API-2, A01.4 | All return `404`; IDs derived from CSPRNG and cannot be guessed |\n| 3.1.1.6 | Sample 1000 valid + 1000 near-valid API-key checks; compare response latency distributions | A07.2 | Distributions statistically indistinguishable (Mann-Whitney U `p > 0.05`) |\n| 3.1.1.7 | Revoke an API key; immediately reuse it for ≤60 s | A07.3 | First request after revocation propagation returns `401` |\n| 3.1.1.8 | Send `OPTIONS`, `HEAD`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE` against `GET`-only routes | A01.7 | `405 Method Not Allowed` |\n\n#### 3.1.2 IDOR & enumeration\n\n| # | Case | Maps to | Expected behaviour |\n|---|------|---------|--------------------|\n| 3.1.2.1 | Iterate `GET /invoices/:id` with adjacent IDs derived from a captured invoice | API-2, A01.4 | `404` for all; no `403` that leaks existence |\n| 3.1.2.2 | Submit `GET /invoices/:id` with the same ID using tenant A and tenant B credentials | API-2, A01.3 | Tenant A sees `200` with full body; tenant B sees `404` with empty body |\n| 3.1.2.3 | Reuse tenant A's idempotency key under tenant B for `POST /invoices` | API-8, A04.3 | Returns a fresh invoice scoped to tenant B; tenant A's invoice is unaffected |\n| 3.1.2.4 | List invoices via paginated route; confirm cursor includes tenant binding | API-2, A01.3 | Cursor is opaque and tenant-bound; rewriting the cursor across tenants returns `404` |\n\n#### 3.1.3 Input validation & injection\n\n| # | Case | Maps to | Expected behaviour |\n|---|------|---------|--------------------|\n| 3.1.3.1 | Fuzz every Postgres-backed query path with classical SQLi payloads (`' OR 1=1 --`, UNION SELECT, time-based delays via `pg_sleep`) using `sqlmap` against the staging API | API-6, A03.1 | All queries are parameterised; `sqlmap` reports no injection vectors |\n| 3.1.3.2 | Submit oversized JSON body (>1 MB), deeply nested JSON (>32 levels) | A03.5 | Express body limit enforced; `413 Payload Too Large` or `400 Bad Request`; no panic |\n| 3.1.3.3 | Submit invoice with `metadata = {\"x\": \"<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>\"}`; retrieve and inspect | API-9, A03.7 | `sanitizeMetadata` strips active content; round-tripped value is safe to render |\n| 3.1.3.4 | Submit invoice with `amount` of `-1`, `0`, `Infinity`, `1e308`, `\"100\"` (string), `null`, `0.000001` | API-6 (validation) | Validator rejects with `400 Bad Request` per [`api/src/utils/validation.ts`](../../../../api/src/utils/validation.ts); no Postgres-side coercion |\n| 3.1.3.5 | Submit invoice with NFT collateral address outside the documented whitelist | Validation | Validator rejects with `400 Bad Request` and an actionable error code |\n| 3.1.3.6 | Submit invoice with `returnUrl = javascript:alert(1)` or `data:text/html,…` | A03.8 | Validator rejects (non-`https:` scheme) |\n| 3.1.3.7 | Search for `child_process` / `execSync` use sites in the in-scope files | A03.4 | None should accept user-controlled arguments |\n| 3.1.3.8 | Submit Redis-stored idempotency record key built from raw user input | A03.3 | Idempotency key is hashed/normalised before being used as a Redis key; no `EVAL` site accepts user-controlled script |\n\n#### 3.1.4 Rate limiting & DoS\n\n| # | Case | Maps to | Expected behaviour |\n|---|------|---------|--------------------|\n| 3.1.4.1 | Send `RATE_LIMIT_MAX + 1` invoice-creation requests from a single IP within the window | API-5, A04.4 | First `RATE_LIMIT_MAX` succeed (or are gracefully throttled), then `429 Too Many Requests` with `Retry-After` header |\n| 3.1.4.2 | Spoof `X-Forwarded-For`, `X-Real-IP`, `CF-Connecting-IP`, `True-Client-IP` from a single source IP | API-5 | Limiter uses the operator-trusted proxy chain only; spoofed headers do not bypass the limit |\n| 3.1.4.3 | Rotate API keys across one IP, sending one request per key | API-5 | Limiter enforces a per-IP cap independent of per-key cap |\n| 3.1.4.4 | Stop Redis on staging mid-test; continue sending requests | A04.7 | Limiter degrades per documented fail-open / fail-closed policy; behaviour matches [`docs/merchant-api-security.md`](../../../merchant-api-security.md) and is recorded in the report regardless of which mode is in effect |\n| 3.1.4.5 | Submit clock-skewed requests (system clock ±10 min) | API-5, A04.4 | Limiter resists; no window jumping |\n\n#### 3.1.5 CORS & security headers\n\n| # | Case | Maps to | Expected behaviour |\n|---|------|---------|--------------------|\n| 3.1.5.1 | Preflight `OPTIONS` from an off-list origin with `credentials: include` | API-4, A05.1 | No `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` echoed; browser blocks the actual request |\n| 3.1.5.2 | Preflight `OPTIONS` from an allow-listed origin | API-4 | `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` echoes the request origin verbatim (no `*` with credentials) |\n| 3.1.5.3 | Inspect response headers on every route | A05.2 | `Content-Security-Policy`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY` (or CSP `frame-ancestors`), `Strict-Transport-Security` present and not overridden |\n| 3.1.5.4 | Inspect for `x-powered-by` and library version banners | A05.4 | Absent |\n| 3.1.5.5 | Trigger malformed JSON, oversized body, missing content-type | A05.3 | Error response body does not include stack traces, file paths, or library versions |\n\n#### 3.1.6 Logging & observability\n\n| # | Case | Maps to | Expected behaviour |\n|---|------|---------|--------------------|\n| 3.1.6.1 | Run the API with `LOG_LEVEL=debug`; perform a webhook send and an API-key validation | OFF-2, A09.1 | `TON_API_KEY`, `Authorization`, `X-Tonbankcard-Signature`, DB password redacted as `***` (or equivalent) at every log site |\n| 3.1.6.2 | Trigger `401`, `403`, `404` on representative routes | A09.2 | Each emits a structured log line with `request_id`, route, outcome — but **without** the offending credential value |\n| 3.1.6.3 | Perform a complete invoice lifecycle (create → pay → webhook deliver → cancel) | A09.3 | Each state transition produces an audit-trail entry with `request_id`, `merchant_id`, `route`, `outcome` |\n| 3.1.6.4 | Trigger an unhandled exception (e.g., kill Postgres mid-request) | A09.2, A05.3 | Server returns generic error; full stack trace appears only in server logs, never in HTTP response |\n\n#### 3.1.7 Path & file safety\n\n| # | Case | Maps to | Expected behaviour |\n|---|------|---------|--------------------|\n| 3.1.7.1 | Request `/` (default route), `/static/...`, `/.env`, `/package.json`, `/.git/HEAD` | API-7 | All return `404`; no static-file middleware is mounted; default-deny posture |\n| 3.1.7.2 | Path-traversal probes (`..%2F..%2Fetc%2Fpasswd`) on any path parameter | API-7 | All return `404` or `400`; no file-system access from user input |\n\n### 3.2 Indexer (`backend/indexer/`)\n\n#### 3.2.1 Exposure & authentication\n\n| # | Case | Maps to | Expected behaviour |\n|---|------|---------|--------------------|\n| 3.2.1.1 | From a host outside the operator's network, attempt `GET /health` | IDX-2, A01.5 | Either reachable and benign (no secrets in response), or correctly blocked at the network layer; document either outcome |\n| 3.2.1.2 | From a host outside the operator's network, attempt account-history endpoints | IDX-2, A01.5 | Sensitive data must not be reachable from public internet without an auth boundary; a reachable + unauthenticated endpoint that leaks payment metadata is a High |\n| 3.2.1.3 | Run `nmap` against the staging host | A05.8 | Only documented ports reachable |\n\n#### 3.2.2 Replay & deduplication\n\n| # | Case | Maps to | Expected behaviour |\n|---|------|---------|--------------------|\n| 3.2.2.1 | Replay a captured TON block / message into the ingestion pipeline | IDX-1, IDX-3, A04.6 | Payment events dedupe on `(tx_hash, lt)`; no double-credit |\n| 3.2.2.2 | Submit conflicting block updates (same `(tx_hash, lt)`, different amount) | IDX-1 | Indexer trusts the on-chain message and refuses the conflicting record; emit a structured warning |\n| 3.2.2.3 | Re-run pagination from PR #107 against a tenant other than the cursor's origin | IDX-8, A01.3 | Cursor is account-bound; rewrite attempt returns no foreign data |\n\n#### 3.2.3 SQL injection on the indexer\n\n| # | Case | Maps to | Expected behaviour |\n|---|------|---------|--------------------|\n| 3.2.3.1 | Fuzz `accountAddress` parameter with SQLi payloads | IDX-7, A03.2 | Parameterised; no injection |\n| 3.2.3.2 | Fuzz pagination cursor (post PR #107) | IDX-7, IDX-8, A03.2 | Cursor is opaque; injection payloads rejected at parse time |\n| 3.2.3.3 | Switch staging indexer to Postgres mode; repeat 3.2.3.1 + 3.2.3.2 | IDX-7 | Both SQLite and Postgres paths use parameterised statements |\n\n#### 3.2.4 Database integrity\n\n| # | Case | Maps to | Expected behaviour |\n|---|------|---------|--------------------|\n| 3.2.4.1 | Run every migration in [`backend/indexer/scripts/migrate.js`](../../../../backend/indexer/scripts/) forward, then roll back | A08.5 | Deterministic, transactional, rollbackable |\n| 3.2.4.2 | Snapshot the SQLite file before and after a representative day of ingestion | IDX-1, A04.6 | Hashes of payment-event rows match `(tx_hash, lt)` derivations from the source messages |\n| 3.2.4.3 | Direct DB write of a fake payment record; restart the indexer | IDX-1 | Inconsistency surfaced by ingestion-time integrity check (or documented as residual trust on the operator) |\n\n#### 3.2.5 Outbound calls & SSRF\n\n| # | Case | Maps to | Expected behaviour |\n|---|------|---------|--------------------|\n| 3.2.5.1 | Attempt to swap the TON HTTP API endpoint via request input or environment edge case | IDX-4, A10.1 | Endpoint is read once at boot from env and pinned for the process lifetime |\n| 3.2.5.2 | Point staging indexer at a malicious TON HTTP API; verify response signature checks | IDX-4 | Indexer treats upstream data as untrusted; reject malformed messages |\n| 3.2.5.3 | Submit ingestion retry storm by failing the upstream | A04.7 | Indexer applies the PR #108 retry/backoff policy; no unbounded loops |\n\n#### 3.2.6 Logging on the indexer\n\n| # | Case | Maps to | Expected behaviour |\n|---|------|---------|--------------------|\n| 3.2.6.1 | Start indexer with `LOG_LEVEL=debug`; ingest several blocks | IDX-6, OFF-2, A09.1 | `TON_API_KEY`, DB DSN password, webhook secret redacted at every log site |\n| 3.2.6.2 | Trigger an upstream fetch failure | IDX-6, A09.2 | Error logged with category and retry counter; no secret material in payload |\n\n### 3.3 SDK (`sdk/`)\n\nThe SDK is the public-facing artefact published to npm; the test cases below cover **supply chain**, **browser-runtime safety**, and **non-custody verification**. Section 3.3.2 implements the webhook replay test cases that [`OWASP_CHECKLIST.md`](./OWASP_CHECKLIST.md) §A02.2 cross-references; the webhook signer lives on the API side, but the verifier reference implementation ships in the SDK and is tested here end-to-end.\n\n#### 3.3.1 Supply-chain & dependency hygiene\n\n| # | Case | Maps to | Expected behaviour |\n|---|------|---------|--------------------|\n| 3.3.1.1 | `npm audit --omit=dev --json` in a clean `sdk/` checkout | SDK-1, A06.1 | Zero High / Critical (acceptance bar); output archived as `npm-audit-sdk-v0.json` |\n| 3.3.1.2 | `npm audit --json` (incl. devDependencies) | SDK-1, A06.2 | Dev-only High/Critical flagged but not blocking; any dev dep that touches the published bundle is escalated |\n| 3.3.1.3 | Inspect every direct dependency in `sdk/package.json` for pinning style | SDK-2, A06.3 | `^` / `>=` on production deps are findings; recommend exact pinning. The known `>=` on `@ton/core`/`@ton/ton` is captured as **SDK-2-seed** in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) |\n| 3.3.1.4 | `npm ls --all` against `sdk/`; flag deprecated, unmaintained (>2y), single-maintainer prod deps | SDK-1, A06.4 | Each flagged dep documented with risk note |\n| 3.3.1.5 | Re-run `npm ci` in clean checkout; compare lock-file digest | A08.1 | Digest matches the value recorded in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §9 at engagement freeze |\n| 3.3.1.6 | Modify `package-lock.json` to point at a yanked / typosquat version | A08.1 | `npm ci` rejects via integrity check |\n| 3.3.1.7 | Reproducible build per [`sdk/VERIFICATION.md`](../../../../sdk/VERIFICATION.md) | A08.2 | Rebuilt `dist/` matches the published npm tarball byte-for-byte (or the documented allowed diff) |\n| 3.3.1.8 | Inspect published bundle (`dist/index.js`, `dist/index.mjs`) for `mock.ts` artefacts | SDK-7, A08.3 | No mock symbols in the production entry; `mock` exports only via the `mock` subpath |\n| 3.3.1.9 | License surface scan (`license-checker --production --json`) | A06.6 | No GPL / AGPL contamination |\n\n#### 3.3.2 Webhook replay test cases\n\nThe post-D4 webhook scheme is HMAC-SHA256 with `X-Tonbankcard-Signature`, `X-Tonbankcard-Timestamp`, and a monotonic nonce. The pentester captures a legitimate webhook against the staging webhook receiver (§1.2), then runs the following replays.\n\n| # | Case | Maps to | Expected behaviour |\n|---|------|---------|--------------------|\n| 3.3.2.1 | Resend the captured webhook verbatim 5 s after delivery (within the documented validity window) | API-3, A02.2 | Verifier rejects due to nonce-store collision |\n| 3.3.2.2 | Resend the captured webhook 10 min after delivery (outside the validity window) | API-3, A02.2 | Verifier rejects due to timestamp outside acceptable skew |\n| 3.3.2.3 | Resend with `X-Tonbankcard-Timestamp` rewritten to current time, signature unchanged | API-3, A02.3 | Verifier rejects: timestamp is part of the HMAC input; signature no longer matches |\n| 3.3.2.4 | Resend with `X-Tonbankcard-Timestamp` and signature recomputed using a previously-rotated secret | API-3, A02.4 | Verifier rejects when the old secret is outside the documented overlap window; accepts within the overlap window |\n| 3.3.2.5 | Flip a single bit in the payload, leaving signature + timestamp intact | A02.3 | Verifier rejects (signature mismatch) |\n| 3.3.2.6 | Strip the nonce header; replay with valid timestamp + signature | API-3, A02.1 | Verifier rejects (mandatory header missing) |\n| 3.3.2.7 | Send 10 000 webhooks with distinct nonces; measure nonce-store growth | A04.4 | Nonce store applies the documented TTL; no unbounded memory growth |\n| 3.3.2.8 | Send a webhook whose signed envelope claims a `merchant_id` other than the bound merchant | A02.1, API-2 | Verifier rejects (envelope mismatch); event not credited |\n| 3.3.2.9 | Send two webhooks for the same payment event with different signatures (e.g., signing-secret straddle) | API-3 | Verifier accepts at most one; duplicate handling is idempotent |\n\nThe verifier reference is the canonical implementation in the SDK and the documented snippet in [`docs/merchant-api-security.md`](../../../merchant-api-security.md) §6. Findings here are recorded both against `API-3` and against the SDK code paths that consume the verifier.\n\n#### 3.3.3 Browser-runtime safety (widget)\n\n| # | Case | Maps to | Expected behaviour |\n|---|------|---------|--------------------|\n| 3.3.3.1 | Mount `PaymentWidget` with `description = '<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>'` | SDK-3, A03.6 | No script execution; value rendered as text via DOM API (no `innerHTML` of untrusted strings) |\n| 3.3.3.2 | Mount with `orderId = '\"><script>alert(1)</script>'`, `returnUrl = 'javascript:alert(1)'` | SDK-3, A03.6, A03.8 | Validator refuses non-`https:` `returnUrl`; `orderId` is text-escaped wherever rendered |\n| 3.3.3.3 | Embed the widget in an attacker-controlled iframe with `sandbox=\"allow-scripts\"` only | SDK-5 | Widget renders a visible framing-warning per documented clickjacking guidance; integrators are told to set `X-Frame-Options`/`frame-ancestors` |\n| 3.3.3.4 | Drive widget interactions via Playwright; record network requests | SDK-4 | No `Authorization` header outbound from the browser; no API-key echo into `onError` callbacks |\n| 3.3.3.5 | Trigger SDK error paths (invalid invoice ID, network failure, declined wallet response) | SDK-4 | `onError` callback receives a sanitised error object; no secret material, no raw HTTP response |\n| 3.3.3.6 | Inspect generated TON Connect deep links | SDK-6 | Parameters are on-chain-verifiable only (NFT address, amount, comment); no off-chain trust marker |\n| 3.3.3.7 | Inspect published `.d.ts` files against the documented public contract | SDK-8 | Types match documentation; no `any` leakage on security-sensitive surfaces |\n\n#### 3.3.4 Non-custody verification\n\n| # | Case | Maps to | Expected behaviour |\n|---|------|---------|--------------------|\n| 3.3.4.1 | Static review of all SDK source files for references to private keys, mnemonics, seed phrases, or signing APIs | OFF-1, A04.1 | None present |\n| 3.3.4.2 | Static review of `api/` and `backend/indexer/` for the same | OFF-1, A04.1 | None present |\n| 3.3.4.3 | Confirm the SDK does not ship a wallet implementation in its dependency tree | OFF-1 | No `@ton/crypto`-style private-key handling in production deps |\n\n### 3.4 Cross-cutting\n\n| # | Case | Maps to | Expected behaviour |\n|---|------|---------|--------------------|\n| 3.4.1 | TLS posture sweep with `testssl.sh` against staging API + indexer hosts | API-10, A02.7 | TLS 1.2+ only; HSTS present; no broken ciphers |\n| 3.4.2 | Confirm default-config startup of `api/` with no `STORAGE_BACKEND` set | A05.6 | Fails to start (or warns loudly); never silently selects `InMemoryStorage` for a production-shaped deployment |\n| 3.4.3 | Confirm default-config startup of `backend/indexer/` with no DB DSN set | A05.5, A05.6 | Same default-deny posture |\n| 3.4.4 | Alerting baseline review | A09.6 | Documented signals: spike in 401s, webhook signature failures, indexer fetch errors. Missing alerting on Critical signals is a Medium |\n| 3.4.5 | Telemetry / observability privacy review | OFF-4, A09.5 | No PII, no wallet addresses, no merchant metadata sent to third-party observability services without explicit opt-in |\n\n---\n\n## 4. PoC Expectations\n\nEvery Critical and High finding is delivered with a **reproducible PoC** that runs against the staging environment. Acceptable forms:\n\n| Form | When to use | What to include |\n|------|-------------|-----------------|\n| `curl` script | Single-request or short-sequence HTTP exploits | Shebang, env-var inputs, no embedded secrets, expected response captured as a comment |\n| Postman collection (`v2.1`) | Multi-step HTTP flows | Variables for `STAGING_API_URL`, `MERCHANT_A_KEY`, `MERCHANT_B_KEY`; pre-request scripts for any setup |\n| Node script (`node ≥20`) | Webhook replay, timing analysis, supply-chain probes | `package.json` declaring exact deps; no network calls outside the staging environment |\n| Playwright spec | Browser-runtime widget tests | Headless Chromium; baseline screenshots; deterministic seeds |\n| `npm ci` + `npm audit` archive | Dependency-tree findings | `npm-audit-<pkg>-v0.json` plus a one-line invocation `README.md` |\n\nPoC bundles are delivered as a tarball named `A4-poc-bundle-v<N>.tar.gz` and SHA-256-recorded in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §9.\n\nOut-of-bounds PoCs (e.g., attacks against TON mainnet, attacks against any third-party gateway, attacks against operator infrastructure) are **not** acceptable and must be replaced with staging-bound equivalents.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Reporting Cadence\n\n| Milestone | Cadence | Deliverable |\n|-----------|---------|-------------|\n| Daily, working days | 17:00 UTC | Short Slack / email update — endpoints touched, working hypotheses, blockers |\n| Mid-pentest (T+6w) | One scheduled checkpoint | OWASP coverage walk-through; pentester populates `pass / fail / pending` against every row of [`OWASP_CHECKLIST.md`](./OWASP_CHECKLIST.md) §3 |\n| Critical / High discovery | Immediate (≤24 h) | Out-of-band notification per [`../REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md`](../REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md); placeholder finding ID reserved |\n| Draft report (T+8w) | One deliverable | Full report draft per [`../REPORT_TEMPLATE.md`](../REPORT_TEMPLATE.md) adapted to off-chain pentest |\n| Re-test (T+12w) | One deliverable | Signed re-test letter against the remediation commit |\n\nThe protocol team mirrors every status change into [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) within one working day.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Purpose\n\nThis directory tracks every **external security engagement** performed on the TONBANKCARD protocol. It is the canonical location for:\n\n- Audit engagement plans (RFP-style)\n- Auditor selection records\n- Frozen audit packages handed over to auditors\n- Audit reports as delivered by external firms\n- Remediation pull requests and re-audit attestations\n- Public disclosure artifacts\n\nInternal pre-audit reviews (such as [`audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md`](../../../audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md)) and the system-level audit ([`docs/audit/FULL_SYSTEM_AUDIT.md`](../../audit/FULL_SYSTEM_AUDIT.md)) live elsewhere — this directory is reserved for **third-party** engagements that gate mainnet deployment.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Directory Layout\n\n```\ndocs/security/audits/\n├── README.md                       — This index\n├── REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md         — How findings are triaged, fixed, and verified\n├── REPORT_TEMPLATE.md              — Canonical layout for incoming audit reports\n├── A1-core-contracts/              — Issue #112 engagement\n│   ├── ENGAGEMENT.md               — Scope, deliverables, candidate firms, evaluation matrix\n│   └── STATUS.md                   — Live state of the engagement (firm, dates, findings)\n└── A2-phase4-contracts/            — Issue #113 engagement (gated by A1 completion)\n    ├── ENGAGEMENT.md               — Phase 4 scope with dedicated cross-chain bridge review\n    └── STATUS.md                   — Live state, A1 upstream-gate tracker, threat-ID ledger\n```\n\nFuture engagements (A4 off-chain pentest, A5 bug bounty, etc.) are added as sibling folders named after the roadmap ID.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Engagement Index\n\n| ID | Scope | Roadmap | Issue | Status | Firm | Report |\n|----|-------|---------|-------|--------|------|--------|\n| **A1** | Core contracts (PaymentHub, MerchantPaymentHub, account-locks, nft-resolver, collateral signal) | [A1](../../../TEMP/DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md) | [#112](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/112) | Engagement preparation complete — awaiting firm selection | — | — |\n| **A2** | Phase 4 contracts (CrossChainBridge, MultiSigCard, RecurringPayments, LendingProtocolCoordinator) | [A2](../../../TEMP/DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md) | [#113](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/113) | Engagement preparation complete — awaiting A1 completion and firm selection | — | — |\n| A4 | Off-chain services (`api/`, `backend/`, `sdk/`) | A4 | TBD | Not started | — | — |\n| A5 | Bug bounty program | A5 | TBD | Not started | — | — |\n\nWhen a new external engagement begins, copy `A1-core-contracts/` as a starting template, update its `ENGAGEMENT.md` for the new scope, and add a row to this table.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Gating Rules\n\nThe following rules are **non-negotiable** and apply to every engagement listed in §3:\n\n1. **No mainnet deployment** of any in-scope contract before the corresponding audit report is published and remediation is verified by the auditor.\n2. **Critical findings:** zero tolerance — every Critical must be remediated and re-verified before sign-off.\n3. **High findings:** remediated, or formally accepted with rationale signed off by the maintainers in `STATUS.md`.\n4. **Medium findings:** remediated or documented as accepted risk in `docs/audit-notes.md`.\n5. **Audit report is public** — published in this directory and linked from `docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md`.\n6. **Frozen scope** — once an engagement is signed, the contract set under audit is frozen at a specific commit (see [`audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md`](../../../audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md)).\n\n---\n\n## 5. Where Auditors Should Start\n\nExternal auditors engaging with TONBANKCARD should read, in order:\n\n1. [`docs/audit/external-audit-intro.md`](../../audit/external-audit-intro.md) — protocol intent and constraints\n2. [`audit/SCOPE.md`](../../../audit/SCOPE.md) — contracts in scope, focus areas\n3. [`audit/INVARIANTS.md`](../../../audit/INVARIANTS.md) — formal invariants I1–I7\n4. [`audit/THREAT_MODEL.md`](../../../audit/THREAT_MODEL.md) — attack vectors and mitigations\n5. [`audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md`](../../../audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md) — frozen commit, compiler versions\n6. [`audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md`](../../../audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md) — reproducible build\n7. [`audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md`](../../../audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md) — known findings from internal pre-audit\n8. Engagement-specific `ENGAGEMENT.md` in the relevant subdirectory\n\nThe [`docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md`](../AUDIT_READINESS.md) document is the navigation hub for all of the above.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Purpose\n\nThis directory tracks every **external security engagement** performed on the TONBANKCARD protocol. It is the canonical location for:\n\n- Audit engagement plans (RFP-style)\n- Auditor selection records\n- Frozen audit packages handed over to auditors\n- Audit reports as delivered by external firms\n- Remediation pull requests and re-audit attestations\n- Public disclosure artifacts\n\nInternal pre-audit reviews (such as [`audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md`](../../../audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md)) and the system-level audit ([`docs/audit/FULL_SYSTEM_AUDIT.md`](../../audit/FULL_SYSTEM_AUDIT.md)) live elsewhere — this directory is reserved for **third-party** engagements that gate mainnet deployment.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Directory Layout\n\n```\ndocs/security/audits/\n├── README.md                       — This index\n├── REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md         — How findings are triaged, fixed, and verified\n├── REPORT_TEMPLATE.md              — Canonical layout for incoming audit reports\n├── A1-core-contracts/              — Issue #112 engagement\n│   ├── ENGAGEMENT.md               — Scope, deliverables, candidate firms, evaluation matrix\n│   └── STATUS.md                   — Live state of the engagement (firm, dates, findings)\n└── A2-phase4-contracts/            — Issue #113 engagement (gated by A1 completion)\n    ├── ENGAGEMENT.md               — Phase 4 scope with dedicated cross-chain bridge review\n    └── STATUS.md                   — Live state, A1 upstream-gate tracker, threat-ID ledger\n```\n\nFuture engagements (A4 off-chain pentest, A5 bug bounty, etc.) are added as sibling folders named after the roadmap ID.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Engagement Index\n\n| ID | Scope | Roadmap | Issue | Status | Firm | Report |\n|----|-------|---------|-------|--------|------|--------|\n| **A1** | Core contracts (PaymentHub, MerchantPaymentHub, account-locks, nft-resolver, collateral signal) | [A1](../../../TEMP/DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md) | [#112](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/112) | Engagement preparation complete — awaiting firm selection | — | — |\n| **A2** | Phase 4 contracts (CrossChainBridge, MultiSigCard, RecurringPayments, LendingProtocolCoordinator) | [A2](../../../TEMP/DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md) | [#113](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/113) | Engagement preparation complete — awaiting A1 completion and firm selection | — | — |\n| A4 | Off-chain services (`api/`, `backend/`, `sdk/`) | A4 | TBD | Not started | — | — |\n| A5 | Bug bounty program | A5 | TBD | Not started | — | — |\n\nWhen a new external engagement begins, copy `A1-core-contracts/` as a starting template, update its `ENGAGEMENT.md` for the new scope, and add a row to this table.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Gating Rules\n\nThe following rules are **non-negotiable** and apply to every engagement listed in §3:\n\n1. **No mainnet deployment** of any in-scope contract before the corresponding audit report is published and remediation is verified by the auditor.\n2. **Critical findings:** zero tolerance — every Critical must be remediated and re-verified before sign-off.\n3. **High findings:** remediated, or formally accepted with rationale signed off by the maintainers in `STATUS.md`.\n4. **Medium findings:** remediated or documented as accepted risk in `docs/audit-notes.md`.\n5. **Audit report is public** — published in this directory and linked from `docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md`.\n6. **Frozen scope** — once an engagement is signed, the contract set under audit is frozen at a specific commit (see [`audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md`](../../../audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md)).\n\n---\n\n## 5. Where Auditors Should Start\n\nExternal auditors engaging with TONBANKCARD should read, in order:\n\n1. [`docs/audit/external-audit-intro.md`](../../audit/external-audit-intro.md) — protocol intent and constraints\n2. [`audit/SCOPE.md`](../../../audit/SCOPE.md) — contracts in scope, focus areas\n3. [`audit/INVARIANTS.md`](../../../audit/INVARIANTS.md) — formal invariants I1–I7\n4. [`audit/THREAT_MODEL.md`](../../../audit/THREAT_MODEL.md) — attack vectors and mitigations\n5. [`audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md`](../../../audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md) — frozen commit, compiler versions\n6. [`audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md`](../../../audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md) — reproducible build\n7. [`audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md`](../../../audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md) — known findings from internal pre-audit\n8. Engagement-specific `ENGAGEMENT.md` in the relevant subdirectory\n\nThe [`docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md`](../AUDIT_READINESS.md) document is the navigation hub for all of the above.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Purpose\n\nThis directory tracks every **external security engagement** performed on the TONBANKCARD protocol. It is the canonical location for:\n\n- Audit engagement plans (RFP-style)\n- Auditor selection records\n- Frozen audit packages handed over to auditors\n- Audit reports as delivered by external firms\n- Remediation pull requests and re-audit attestations\n- Public disclosure artifacts\n\nInternal pre-audit reviews (such as [`audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md`](../../../audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md)) and the system-level audit ([`docs/audit/FULL_SYSTEM_AUDIT.md`](../../audit/FULL_SYSTEM_AUDIT.md)) live elsewhere — this directory is reserved for **third-party** engagements that gate mainnet deployment.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Directory Layout\n\n```\ndocs/security/audits/\n├── README.md                       — This index\n├── REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md         — How findings are triaged, fixed, and verified\n├── REPORT_TEMPLATE.md              — Canonical layout for incoming audit reports\n├── A1-core-contracts/              — Issue #112 engagement\n│   ├── ENGAGEMENT.md               — Scope, deliverables, candidate firms, evaluation matrix\n│   └── STATUS.md                   — Live state of the engagement (firm, dates, findings)\n├── A2-phase4-contracts/            — Issue #113 engagement (gated by A1 completion)\n│   ├── ENGAGEMENT.md               — Phase 4 scope with dedicated cross-chain bridge review\n│   └── STATUS.md                   — Live state, A1 upstream-gate tracker, threat-ID ledger\n└── A4-offchain-services/           — Issue #115 engagement (off-chain pentest)\n    ├── ENGAGEMENT.md               — api/ + backend/indexer/ + sdk/ pentest scope, OWASP-driven\n    ├── STATUS.md                   — Live state, D4/D5 upstream-gate tracker, OWASP coverage\n    ├── OWASP_CHECKLIST.md          — OWASP Top 10:2021 category-by-category required tests\n    └── PENTEST_PLAN.md             — Detailed per-component test cases, PoC expectations\n```\n\nFuture engagements (A5 bug bounty, etc.) are added as sibling folders named after the roadmap ID.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Engagement Index\n\n| ID | Scope | Roadmap | Issue | Status | Firm | Report |\n|----|-------|---------|-------|--------|------|--------|\n| **A1** | Core contracts (PaymentHub, MerchantPaymentHub, account-locks, nft-resolver, collateral signal) | [A1](../../../TEMP/DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md) | [#112](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/112) | Engagement preparation complete — awaiting firm selection | — | — |\n| **A2** | Phase 4 contracts (CrossChainBridge, MultiSigCard, RecurringPayments, LendingProtocolCoordinator) | [A2](../../../TEMP/DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md) | [#113](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/113) | Engagement preparation complete — awaiting A1 completion and firm selection | — | — |\n| A4 | Off-chain services (`api/`, `backend/`, `sdk/`) | A4 | TBD | Not started | — | — |\n| A5 | Bug bounty program | A5 | TBD | Not started | — | — |\n\nWhen a new external engagement begins, copy `A1-core-contracts/` as a starting template, update its `ENGAGEMENT.md` for the new scope, and add a row to this table.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Gating Rules\n\nThe following rules are **non-negotiable** and apply to every engagement listed in §3:\n\n1. **No mainnet deployment** of any in-scope contract before the corresponding audit report is published and remediation is verified by the auditor.\n2. **Critical findings:** zero tolerance — every Critical must be remediated and re-verified before sign-off.\n3. **High findings:** remediated, or formally accepted with rationale signed off by the maintainers in `STATUS.md`.\n4. **Medium findings:** remediated or documented as accepted risk in `docs/audit-notes.md`.\n5. **Audit report is public** — published in this directory and linked from `docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md`.\n6. **Frozen scope** — once an engagement is signed, the contract set under audit is frozen at a specific commit (see [`audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md`](../../../audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md)).\n\n---\n\n## 5. Where Auditors Should Start\n\nExternal auditors engaging with TONBANKCARD should read, in order:\n\n1. [`docs/audit/external-audit-intro.md`](../../audit/external-audit-intro.md) — protocol intent and constraints\n2. [`audit/SCOPE.md`](../../../audit/SCOPE.md) — contracts in scope, focus areas\n3. [`audit/INVARIANTS.md`](../../../audit/INVARIANTS.md) — formal invariants I1–I7\n4. [`audit/THREAT_MODEL.md`](../../../audit/THREAT_MODEL.md) — attack vectors and mitigations\n5. [`audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md`](../../../audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md) — frozen commit, compiler versions\n6. [`audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md`](../../../audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md) — reproducible build\n7. [`audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md`](../../../audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md) — known findings from internal pre-audit\n8. Engagement-specific `ENGAGEMENT.md` in the relevant subdirectory\n\nThe [`docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md`](../AUDIT_READINESS.md) document is the navigation hub for all of the above.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Any violation is a critical security finding.\n58\t\n59\t| ID | Invariant | Key Guarantee |\n60\t|----|-----------|---------------|\n61\t| **I1** | Non-Custodial Ownership | Only NFT owner can initiate fund transfers |\n62\t| **I2** | NFT = Account Authority | NFT ownership is the single source of truth for account control |\n63\t| **I3** | No Admin Fund Control | No privileged role can move user funds |\n64\t| **I4** | Atomic Transfers | All transfers are all-or-nothing; no partial state possible |\n65\t| **I5** | Ledger Conservation | Sum of all balances is preserved across all operations |\n66\t| **I6** | Lock ≠ Confiscation | Locks restrict outgoing transfers; they do not seize funds |\n67\t| **I7** | External Adapter Isolation | External providers cannot directly invoke protocol operations |\n68\t\n69\tFull formal definitions with contract-code mappings: [audit/INVARIANTS.md](../../audit/INVARIANTS.md)\n70\t\n71\t---\n72\t\n73\t## Test Coverage Summary\n74\t\n75\t| Contract | Estimated Line Coverage | Estimated Branch Coverage |\n76\t|----------|------------------------|--------------------------|\n77\t| MerchantPaymentHub.tact | ~90%+ | ~85%+ |\n78\t| PaymentHub.tact | ~85%+ | ~80%+ |\n79\t| account-locks.fc | ~85%+ | ~80%+ |\n80\t| nft_account_resolver.fc | ~80%+ | ~75%+ |\n81\t| account-state.tact | ~90%+ | ~85%+ |\n82\t\n83\tTo obtain exact figures:\n84\t\n85\t```bash\n86\tgit checkout eb5dd593248a33a5a7517ae59b840827c140906a\n87\tnpm install\n88\tnpx blueprint test --coverage\n89\t```\n90\t\n91\tSee [audit/TEST_COVERAGE_REPORT.md](../../audit/TEST_COVERAGE_REPORT.md) for full test organization.\n92\t\n93\t---\n94\t\n95\t## Critical Audit Focus Areas\n96\t\n97\t### 1. No Admin Fund Control (MUST verify)\n98\t\n99\tSearch the entire contract codebase for `withdraw`, `drain`, `emergency`, `admin_transfer`, `force_transfer`. Expected result: **zero matches** in fund-moving contexts.\n100\t\n101\tAdmin roles exist (`risk_authority`, `lending_adapter`) but are limited to setting/clearing lock flags. They cannot move funds.\n102\t\n103\t### 2. NFT Ownership Enforcement (MUST verify)\n104\t\n105\tEvery fund-moving operation must verify the caller is the current on-chain NFT owner. No cached ownership. No secondary authorization paths.\n106\t\n107\t### 3. Atomic Balance Updates (MUST verify)\n108\t\n109\tAll balance modifications must be atomic — both debit and credit in the same transaction. Reentrancy protection must be verified at:\n110\t- `PaymentHub.tact` lines 149–150 (reentrancy guard)\n111\t- `PaymentHub.tact` lines 196–202 (`executeTransfer`)\n112\t\n113\t### 4. Lock Enforcement (MUST verify)\n114\t\n115\tLocks prevent sending but must never seize funds. Verify:\n116\t- `account-locks.fc` `can_receive()` always returns 1\n117\t- Lock operations do not modify balances\n118\t- FRAUD_LOCK and COLLATERAL_LOCK both correctly gate `can_send()`\n119\t\n120\t### 5. No Upgrade Paths (MUST verify)\n121\t\n122\tContracts are immutable. No upgradeable proxy patterns. No `setAdmin()` paths that could change invariants.\n123\t\n124\t---\n125\t\n126\t## Known Limitations (Auditor Notice)\n127\t\n128\t| Limitation | Severity | Description |\n129\t|------------|----------|-------------|\n130\t| Invoice replay (off-chain only) | MEDIUM | Contract does not enforce invoice uniqueness on-chain; handled off-chain |\n131\t| DAO unlock not implemented | LOW | FROZEN → ACTIVE transition requires future DAO governance |\n132\t| Lending unlock not implemented | LOW | COLLATERAL_LOCKED → ACTIVE requires Lending Adapter (not yet deployed) |\n133\t| NFT ownership integration (partial) | MEDIUM | Some contracts rely on calling contract for ownership check |\n134\t| Single admin key (temporary) | HIGH | Admin key is single-key pending multi-sig migration (Q1 2026) |\n135\t\n136\tThese are documented accepted risks. It serves as a navigation guide for external auditors and internal reviewers approaching the protocol for the first time.\n\nFor the complete frozen audit package (used by external auditors), see the [`audit/`](../../audit/) directory.\n\n---\n\n## Audit Package Location\n\nThe pre-audit package is located at:\n\n```\naudit/\n├── SCOPE.md              — Audit boundaries, focus areas, and contract inventory\n├── THREAT_MODEL.md       — Threat classes, attack vectors, and mitigations\n├── INVARIANTS.md         — Formal invariants with contract-code mapping\n├── FREEZE_METADATA.md    — Git hash, compiler versions, file checksums\n├── BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md — How to reproduce builds and run tests\n└── TEST_COVERAGE_REPORT.md — Coverage data and test organization\n```\n\n**Freeze status:** The audit package was frozen at commit `4027b9d` (2025-12-29). Summary:\n\n| Contract | File | Priority | Lines | Primary Concern |\n|----------|------|----------|-------|-----------------|\n| MerchantPaymentHub | `contracts/MerchantPaymentHub.tact` | Critical | 287 | Payment settlement, ownership, locks |\n| PaymentHub | `contracts/payments/PaymentHub.tact` | Critical | 355 | Internal transfers, atomicity |\n| NFT Account Resolver | `contracts/nft-resolver/nft_account_resolver.fc` | Critical | 149 | Ownership resolution |\n| NFT Account Resolver | `contracts/nft-resolver/nft_account_resolver.tact` | Critical | 121 | Ownership resolution (Tact wrapper) |\n| Account State Machine | `contracts/payment-hub/account-state.tact` | Critical | 285 | State management, balance integrity |\n| Account Locks | `contracts/payments/account-locks.fc` | High | 269 | Lock authorization, lock semantics |\n\n**Total lines under audit:** 1,466 (critical) + 269 (high) = **1,735 lines**\n\n---\n\n## Protocol Invariants\n\nSeven formal invariants define the protocol's security guarantees. Any violation is a critical security finding.\n\n| ID | Invariant | Key Guarantee |\n|----|-----------|---------------|\n| **I1** | Non-Custodial Ownership | Only NFT owner can initiate fund transfers |\n| **I2** | NFT = Account Authority | NFT ownership is the single source of truth for account control |\n| **I3** | No Admin Fund Control | No privileged role can move user funds |\n| **I4** | Atomic Transfers | All transfers are all-or-nothing; no partial state possible |\n| **I5** | Ledger Conservation | Sum of all balances is preserved across all operations |\n| **I6** | Lock ≠ Confiscation | Locks restrict outgoing transfers; they do not seize funds |\n| **I7** | External Adapter Isolation | External providers cannot directly invoke protocol operations |\n\nFull formal definitions with contract-code mappings: [audit/INVARIANTS.md](../../audit/INVARIANTS.md)\n\n---\n\n## Test Coverage Summary\n\n| Contract | Estimated Line Coverage | Estimated Branch Coverage |\n|----------|------------------------|--------------------------|\n| MerchantPaymentHub.tact | ~90%+ | ~85%+ |\n| PaymentHub.tact | ~85%+ | ~80%+ |\n| account-locks.fc | ~85%+ | ~80%+ |\n| nft_account_resolver.fc | ~80%+ | ~75%+ |\n| account-state.tact | ~90%+ | ~85%+ |\n\nTo obtain exact figures:\n\n```bash\ngit checkout eb5dd593248a33a5a7517ae59b840827c140906a\nnpm install\nnpx blueprint test --coverage\n```\n\nSee [audit/TEST_COVERAGE_REPORT.md](../../audit/TEST_COVERAGE_REPORT.md) for full test organization.\n\n---\n\n## Critical Audit Focus Areas\n\n### 1. No Admin Fund Control (MUST verify)\n\nSearch the entire contract codebase for `withdraw`, `drain`, `emergency`, `admin_transfer`, `force_transfer`. Expected result: **zero matches** in fund-moving contexts.\n\nAdmin roles exist (`risk_authority`, `lending_adapter`) but are limited to setting/clearing lock flags. They cannot move funds.\n\n### 2. NFT Ownership Enforcement (MUST verify)\n\nEvery fund-moving operation must verify the caller is the current on-chain NFT owner. No cached ownership. No secondary authorization paths.\n\n### 3. Atomic Balance Updates (MUST verify)\n\nAll balance modifications must be atomic — both debit and credit in the same transaction. Reentrancy protection must be verified at:\n- `PaymentHub.tact` lines 149–150 (reentrancy guard)\n- `PaymentHub.tact` lines 196–202 (`executeTransfer`)\n\n### 4. Lock Enforcement (MUST verify)\n\nLocks prevent sending but must never seize funds. Verify:\n- `account-locks.fc` `can_receive()` always returns 1\n- Lock operations do not modify balances\n- FRAUD_LOCK and COLLATERAL_LOCK both correctly gate `can_send()`\n\n### 5. No Upgrade Paths (MUST verify)\n\nContracts are immutable. No upgradeable proxy patterns. No `setAdmin()` paths that could change invariants.\n\n---\n\n## Known Limitations (Auditor Notice)\n\n| Limitation | Severity | Description |\n|------------|----------|-------------|\n| Invoice replay (off-chain only) | MEDIUM | Contract does not enforce invoice uniqueness on-chain; handled off-chain |\n| DAO unlock not implemented | LOW | FROZEN → ACTIVE transition requires future DAO governance |\n| Lending unlock not implemented | LOW | COLLATERAL_LOCKED → ACTIVE requires Lending Adapter (not yet deployed) |\n| NFT ownership integration (partial) | MEDIUM | Some contracts rely on calling contract for ownership check |\n| Single admin key (temporary) | HIGH | Admin key is single-key pending multi-sig migration (Q1 2026) |\n\nThese are documented accepted risks. Full details in [docs/audit-notes.md](../audit-notes.md).\n\n---\n\n## Auditor Engagement Process\n\n### Access\n\n- Repository: `https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol`\n- Audit freeze commit: `eb5dd593248a33a5a7517ae59b840827c140906a`\n- Build instructions: [audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md](../../audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md)\n- Contact for questions: via GitHub issues tagged `audit`\n\n### Scope Confirmation\n\nBefore beginning, auditors must confirm:\n- Which contracts are in scope (see [audit/SCOPE.md](../../audit/SCOPE.md))\n- Which compiler versions to use (see [audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md](../../audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md))\n- Which invariants to verify (see [audit/INVARIANTS.md](../../audit/INVARIANTS.md))\n\n### Expected Deliverables\n\n| Deliverable | Description |\n|-------------|-------------|\n| Audit Report | Findings categorized by severity (Critical, High, Medium, Low, Informational) |\n| Finding References | Each finding references specific invariant(s) and contract line(s) |\n| Reproduction Steps | Each finding includes steps to reproduce |\n| Suggested Fixes | Where applicable |\n| Invariant Attestation | Statement on whether each of I1–I7 holds |\n\nThe end-to-end engagement workflow (intake → triage → remediation → re-verification → disclosure) is canonicalised in [docs/security/audits/REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md](./audits/REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md). Summary:\n\n| Contract | File | Priority | Lines | Primary Concern |\n|----------|------|----------|-------|-----------------|\n| MerchantPaymentHub | `contracts/MerchantPaymentHub.tact` | Critical | 287 | Payment settlement, ownership, locks |\n| PaymentHub | `contracts/payments/PaymentHub.tact` | Critical | 355 | Internal transfers, atomicity |\n| NFT Account Resolver | `contracts/nft-resolver/nft_account_resolver.fc` | Critical | 149 | Ownership resolution |\n| NFT Account Resolver | `contracts/nft-resolver/nft_account_resolver.tact` | Critical | 121 | Ownership resolution (Tact wrapper) |\n| Account State Machine | `contracts/payment-hub/account-state.tact` | Critical | 285 | State management, balance integrity |\n| Account Locks | `contracts/payments/account-locks.fc` | High | 269 | Lock authorization, lock semantics |\n\n**Total lines under audit:** 1,466 (critical) + 269 (high) = **1,735 lines**\n\n---\n\n## Protocol Invariants\n\nSeven formal invariants define the protocol's security guarantees. Any violation is a critical security finding.\n\n| ID | Invariant | Key Guarantee |\n|----|-----------|---------------|\n| **I1** | Non-Custodial Ownership | Only NFT owner can initiate fund transfers |\n| **I2** | NFT = Account Authority | NFT ownership is the single source of truth for account control |\n| **I3** | No Admin Fund Control | No privileged role can move user funds |\n| **I4** | Atomic Transfers | All transfers are all-or-nothing; no partial state possible |\n| **I5** | Ledger Conservation | Sum of all balances is preserved across all operations |\n| **I6** | Lock ≠ Confiscation | Locks restrict outgoing transfers; they do not seize funds |\n| **I7** | External Adapter Isolation | External providers cannot directly invoke protocol operations |\n\nFull formal definitions with contract-code mappings: [audit/INVARIANTS.md](../../audit/INVARIANTS.md)\n\n---\n\n## Test Coverage Summary\n\n| Contract | Estimated Line Coverage | Estimated Branch Coverage |\n|----------|------------------------|--------------------------|\n| MerchantPaymentHub.tact | ~90%+ | ~85%+ |\n| PaymentHub.tact | ~85%+ | ~80%+ |\n| account-locks.fc | ~85%+ | ~80%+ |\n| nft_account_resolver.fc | ~80%+ | ~75%+ |\n| account-state.tact | ~90%+ | ~85%+ |\n\nTo obtain exact figures:\n\n```bash\ngit checkout eb5dd593248a33a5a7517ae59b840827c140906a\nnpm install\nnpx blueprint test --coverage\n```\n\nSee [audit/TEST_COVERAGE_REPORT.md](../../audit/TEST_COVERAGE_REPORT.md) for full test organization.\n\n---\n\n## Critical Audit Focus Areas\n\n### 1. No Admin Fund Control (MUST verify)\n\nSearch the entire contract codebase for `withdraw`, `drain`, `emergency`, `admin_transfer`, `force_transfer`. Expected result: **zero matches** in fund-moving contexts.\n\nAdmin roles exist (`risk_authority`, `lending_adapter`) but are limited to setting/clearing lock flags. They cannot move funds.\n\n### 2. NFT Ownership Enforcement (MUST verify)\n\nEvery fund-moving operation must verify the caller is the current on-chain NFT owner. No cached ownership. No secondary authorization paths.\n\n### 3. Atomic Balance Updates (MUST verify)\n\nAll balance modifications must be atomic — both debit and credit in the same transaction. Reentrancy protection must be verified at:\n- `PaymentHub.tact` lines 149–150 (reentrancy guard)\n- `PaymentHub.tact` lines 196–202 (`executeTransfer`)\n\n### 4. Lock Enforcement (MUST verify)\n\nLocks prevent sending but must never seize funds. Verify:\n- `account-locks.fc` `can_receive()` always returns 1\n- Lock operations do not modify balances\n- FRAUD_LOCK and COLLATERAL_LOCK both correctly gate `can_send()`\n\n### 5. No Upgrade Paths (MUST verify)\n\nContracts are immutable. No upgradeable proxy patterns. No `setAdmin()` paths that could change invariants.\n\n---\n\n## Known Limitations (Auditor Notice)\n\n| Limitation | Severity | Description |\n|------------|----------|-------------|\n| Invoice replay (off-chain only) | MEDIUM | Contract does not enforce invoice uniqueness on-chain; handled off-chain |\n| DAO unlock not implemented | LOW | FROZEN → ACTIVE transition requires future DAO governance |\n| Lending unlock not implemented | LOW | COLLATERAL_LOCKED → ACTIVE requires Lending Adapter (not yet deployed) |\n| NFT ownership integration (partial) | MEDIUM | Some contracts rely on calling contract for ownership check |\n| Single admin key (temporary) | HIGH | Admin key is single-key pending multi-sig migration (Q1 2026) |\n\nThese are documented accepted risks. Full details in [docs/audit-notes.md](../audit-notes.md).\n\n---\n\n## Auditor Engagement Process\n\n### Access\n\n- Repository: `https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol`\n- Audit freeze commit: `eb5dd593248a33a5a7517ae59b840827c140906a`\n- Build instructions: [audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md](../../audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md)\n- Contact for questions: via GitHub issues tagged `audit`\n\n### Scope Confirmation\n\nBefore beginning, auditors must confirm:\n- Which contracts are in scope (see [audit/SCOPE.md](../../audit/SCOPE.md))\n- Which compiler versions to use (see [audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md](../../audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md))\n- Which invariants to verify (see [audit/INVARIANTS.md](../../audit/INVARIANTS.md))\n\n### Expected Deliverables\n\n| Deliverable | Description |\n|-------------|-------------|\n| Audit Report | Findings categorized by severity (Critical, High, Medium, Low, Informational) |\n| Finding References | Each finding references specific invariant(s) and contract line(s) |\n| Reproduction Steps | Each finding includes steps to reproduce |\n| Suggested Fixes | Where applicable |\n| Invariant Attestation | Statement on whether each of I1–I7 holds |\n\nThe end-to-end engagement workflow (intake → triage → remediation → re-verification → disclosure) is canonicalised in [docs/security/audits/REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md](./audits/REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md).    [solve worker-1] - `backend/indexer/` — `@tonbankcard/payment-indexer` v1.0.0 (blockchain event ingestion, SQLite/Postgres integrity, indexer API)

   [solve worker-1] - **Upstream gate** на D4 (rate-limit + HMAC-SHA256 вебхуки + API-key auth) и D5 (`npm audit` в CI) — engagement стартует только после слияния D4.

A formal bug bounty program extends this by providing financial incentives for researchers, a standardized submission process, and public transparency about the scope and rewards.\n\nThis should be launched **after** A1 and A2 audits are complete and known issues have been remediated — to avoid rewarding researchers for findings the team is already aware of.\n\nRelated to: [DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md — Track A, A5](../TEMP/DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md)\n\n## 3. Out of Scope\n\n- Theoretical vulnerabilities without a proof-of-concept\n- Issues in third-party dependencies (ChangeNOW, NOWPayments, CoinRabbit) — report to those vendors\n- Social engineering attacks against team members\n- Physical security\n- Denial of service via flooding (unless causing fund loss)\n\n## 5. Program terms must include:\n   - 90-day fix window for critical/high before public disclosure\n   - Researcher is prohibited from exploiting vulnerabilities in production\n   - Good faith testing on testnet only\n\n4. Response SLA:\n   - Initial triage: 3 business days\n   - Severity classification: 7 business days\n   - Payment: within 30 days of fix deployment\n\n## 6. Non-Functional Requirements\n\n- Program page must be publicly accessible and link from `SECURITY.md`\n- All submissions handled via the bounty platform (not email) for transparency\n- Public statistics: number of reports, resolved, paid — updated quarterly\n\n## 7. Security Requirements\n\n- Audits A1 and A2 must be complete before program launch to avoid paying for known issues\n- Program must explicitly prohibit live mainnet exploitation (testnet testing only)\n- Researcher submissions must not include private keys or wallet credentials\n\n## 8. [Reporting Channels](#1-reporting-channels)\n13\t2. [Encryption Requirements](#2-encryption-requirements)\n14\t3. [Scope](#3-scope)\n15\t4. [Response Timeline](#4-response-timeline)\n16\t5. [Disclosure Policy](#5-disclosure-policy)\n17\t6. [Safe Harbor Statement](#6-safe-harbor-statement)\n18\t\n19\t---\n20\t\n21\t## Supported Versions\n22\t\n23\t| Version | Status | Security Support |\n24\t|---------|--------|-----------------|\n25\t| v1.0.x | Active | Supported |\n26\t\n27\tEarlier versions and pre-release deployments are not covered by this policy.\n28\t\n29\t---\n30\t\n31\t## 1. Reporting Channels\n32\t\n33\t**DO NOT** disclose security vulnerabilities publicly. Public disclosure before a patch is available puts all users at risk.\n34\t\n35\tThe preferred channel is GitHub's private security advisory feature:\n36\t\n37\t1. Go to the [Security tab](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/security) of this repository\n38\t2. Click **\"Report a vulnerability\"**\n39\t3. Provide a detailed description of the issue\n40\t\n41\tIf you are unable to use GitHub's private advisory feature, report via email:\n42\t\n43\t- **Email:** security@tonbankcard.com\n44\t- **Subject line format:** `[SECURITY] <brief description>`\n45\t- Include a detailed description of the issue, reproduction steps, and potential impact\n46\t\n47\tIf you do not receive an acknowledgement within 72 hours, send a follow-up referencing your original report.\n48\t\n49\t### What to Include\n50\t\n51\tA useful vulnerability report includes:\n52\t\n53\t- Description of the vulnerability and its potential impact\n54\t- Steps to reproduce the issue\n55\t- Affected contract(s) or component(s)\n56\t- Proof of concept or test case, if available\n57\t- Suggested severity (Critical, High, Medium, Low)\n58\t\n59\t---\n60\t\n61\t## 2. Encryption Requirements\n62\t\n63\tFor sensitive vulnerability reports, encrypted submission is strongly preferred.\n64\t\n65\t- **PGP:** Encrypt your report to the TONBANKCARD security team PGP key (key details to be published at `security@tonbankcard.com` upon request)\n66\t- **Plain email** is accepted for low-severity or non-sensitive reports\n67\t- Do not include full exploit code or credential material in unencrypted email\n68\t\n69\tEncryption key details will be provided upon initial contact if not yet published.\n70\t\n71\t---\n72\t\n73\t## 3. Scope\n74\t\n75\t### In Scope\n76\t\n77\tThe following components are in scope for vulnerability reports:\n78\t\n79\t- **Smart contracts:** `PaymentHub`, `MerchantNFT`, and related on-chain contracts in this repository (`contracts/`)\n80\t- **Backend API:** REST endpoints handling invoice creation, settlement verification, and merchant registry (`api/`)\n81\t- **Merchant SDK:** JavaScript/TypeScript SDK published under `@tonbankcard/sdk` (`sdk/`)\n82\t- **Authentication and access control logic:** Key management, role-based access, admin operations\n83\t- **Protocol-level logic:** Settlement finality, reorg handling, invariant violations\n84\t\n85\t### Priority Focus Areas\n86\t\n87\tThe most security-critical areas of this protocol:\n88\t\n89\t- **Fund safety:** any path that could result in unauthorized fund movement\n90\t- **NFT ownership enforcement:** any bypass of the ownership check\n91\t- **Lock bypass:** any path to transfer from a locked account\n92\t- **Admin key misuse:** any undocumented admin capability\n93\t\n94\t### Out of Scope\n95\t\n96\tThe following are not in scope:\n97\t\n98\t- Already-deployed and frozen external contracts (TBC Token Jetton, NFT Collections, TBC Diamonds, TONCO DEX) — these are immutable and separately governed\n99\t- Third-party services (ChangeNOW, NOWPayments, CoinRabbit, TONCO) — report vulnerabilities directly to those providers\n100\t- Vulnerabilities in third-party dependencies unless directly exploitable through TONBANKCARD code\n101\t- TON blockchain infrastructure, validator nodes, or core protocol\n102\t- Reports requiring physical access to infrastructure\n103\t- Social engineering attacks against team members or users\n104\t- Denial-of-service attacks without demonstrated exploit impact\n105\t- Issues in test environments or non-production deployments with no production impact\n106\t- Theoretical vulnerabilities with no demonstrated impact\n107\t\n108\t---\n109\t\n110\t## 4. [Reporting Channels](#1-reporting-channels)\n2. [Encryption Requirements](#2-encryption-requirements)\n3. [Scope](#3-scope)\n4. [Response Timeline](#4-response-timeline)\n5. [Disclosure Policy](#5-disclosure-policy)\n6. [Safe Harbor Statement](#6-safe-harbor-statement)\n\n---\n\n## Supported Versions\n\n| Version | Status | Security Support |\n|---------|--------|-----------------|\n| v1.0.x | Active | Supported |\n\nEarlier versions and pre-release deployments are not covered by this policy.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Reporting Channels\n\n**DO NOT** disclose security vulnerabilities publicly. Public disclosure before a patch is available puts all users at risk.\n\nThe preferred channel is GitHub's private security advisory feature:\n\n1. Go to the [Security tab](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/security) of this repository\n2. Click **\"Report a vulnerability\"**\n3. Provide a detailed description of the issue\n\nIf you are unable to use GitHub's private advisory feature, report via email:\n\n- **Email:** security@tonbankcard.com\n- **Subject line format:** `[SECURITY] <brief description>`\n- Include a detailed description of the issue, reproduction steps, and potential impact\n\nIf you do not receive an acknowledgement within 72 hours, send a follow-up referencing your original report.\n\n### What to Include\n\nA useful vulnerability report includes:\n\n- Description of the vulnerability and its potential impact\n- Steps to reproduce the issue\n- Affected contract(s) or component(s)\n- Proof of concept or test case, if available\n- Suggested severity (Critical, High, Medium, Low)\n\n---\n\n## 2. Encryption Requirements\n\nFor sensitive vulnerability reports, encrypted submission is strongly preferred.\n\n- **PGP:** Encrypt your report to the TONBANKCARD security team PGP key (key details to be published at `security@tonbankcard.com` upon request)\n- **Plain email** is accepted for low-severity or non-sensitive reports\n- Do not include full exploit code or credential material in unencrypted email\n\nEncryption key details will be provided upon initial contact if not yet published.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Scope\n\n### In Scope\n\nThe following components are in scope for vulnerability reports:\n\n- **Smart contracts:** `PaymentHub`, `MerchantNFT`, and related on-chain contracts in this repository (`contracts/`)\n- **Backend API:** REST endpoints handling invoice creation, settlement verification, and merchant registry (`api/`)\n- **Merchant SDK:** JavaScript/TypeScript SDK published under `@tonbankcard/sdk` (`sdk/`)\n- **Authentication and access control logic:** Key management, role-based access, admin operations\n- **Protocol-level logic:** Settlement finality, reorg handling, invariant violations\n\n### Priority Focus Areas\n\nThe most security-critical areas of this protocol:\n\n- **Fund safety:** any path that could result in unauthorized fund movement\n- **NFT ownership enforcement:** any bypass of the ownership check\n- **Lock bypass:** any path to transfer from a locked account\n- **Admin key misuse:** any undocumented admin capability\n\n### Out of Scope\n\nThe following are not in scope:\n\n- Already-deployed and frozen external contracts (TBC Token Jetton, NFT Collections, TBC Diamonds, TONCO DEX) — these are immutable and separately governed\n- Third-party services (ChangeNOW, NOWPayments, CoinRabbit, TONCO) — report vulnerabilities directly to those providers\n- Vulnerabilities in third-party dependencies unless directly exploitable through TONBANKCARD code\n- TON blockchain infrastructure, validator nodes, or core protocol\n- Reports requiring physical access to infrastructure\n- Social engineering attacks against team members or users\n- Denial-of-service attacks without demonstrated exploit impact\n- Issues in test environments or non-production deployments with no production impact\n- Theoretical vulnerabilities with no demonstrated impact\n\n---\n\n## 4. Response Timeline\n\n| Milestone | Target |\n|-----------|--------|\n| Acknowledgement of receipt | Within 72 hours |\n| Initial severity assessment | Within 7 days |\n| Status update to reporter | Every 14 days until resolved |\n| Patch for critical severity | Within 30 days |\n| Patch for high severity | Within 60 days |\n| Patch for medium/low severity | Within 90 days |\n\n### Fix Timeline by Severity\n\n| Severity | Target Fix Timeline |\n|----------|---------------------|\n| Critical | Within 72 hours for containment; patch within 30 days |\n| High | Within 60 days |\n| Medium | Within 90 days |\n| Low | Next planned release |\n\nThese are target timelines. Complex issues involving on-chain contracts may require additional time due to audit and deployment constraints. Reporters will be kept informed of any delays.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Disclosure Policy\n\nTONBANKCARD follows a **coordinated disclosure** model:\n\n1. Reporter submits vulnerability via the channel in Section 1\n2. TONBANKCARD acknowledges receipt and opens a private investigation\n3. TONBANKCARD and reporter agree on a disclosure timeline (default: 90 days from acknowledgement)\n4. A patch or mitigation is developed and deployed\n5. Reporter is given a preview of the disclosure and credited (if desired)\n6. A public disclosure is issued after the fix is available\n\n**Early disclosure may occur** if:\n\n- The vulnerability is already being actively exploited\n- A partial fix is available that significantly reduces risk\n\n**Extension of the 90-day timeline** may be requested by either party in writing. Extensions are granted on a case-by-case basis.\n\nIf TONBANKCARD does not respond within the timelines defined in Section 4, reporters may proceed with disclosure at their discretion, having acted in good faith.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Safe Harbor Statement\n\nTONBANKCARD supports responsible security research. If you report a vulnerability in good faith and in accordance with this policy, we will not pursue legal action against you for that research.\n\nGood faith research means:\n\n- You do not access, modify, or exfiltrate data beyond what is necessary to demonstrate the vulnerability\n- You do not disrupt service availability or degrade performance for other users\n- You do not use social engineering techniques against team members or users\n- You report the issue to us before public disclosure\n- You allow reasonable time for a fix before disclosing publicly\n\nThis safe harbor applies to research conducted under these terms. It does not extend to:\n\n- Exploitation of vulnerabilities for personal gain\n- Access to or exfiltration of user data\n- Any activity that violates applicable law\n\nThis statement is not legal advice and does not constitute a legal agreement. Researchers are responsible for understanding and complying with all applicable laws.\n\n---\n\n## Non-Custodial Architecture\n\nTONBANKCARD is a **non-custodial protocol**. The architecture enforces that:\n\n- No admin or operator can move user funds\n- No emergency mechanism exists that transfers or seizes funds\n- Account locks restrict outgoing transfers but do not confiscate balances\n\nFor more on the security model, see [docs/security/SECURITY.md](docs/security/SECURITY.md).\n\n---\n\n## Security Documentation\n\nFor the full security framework, see:\n\n- [docs/security/SECURITY.md](docs/security/SECURITY.md) — Security documentation index and unified framework\n- [docs/security/THREAT_MODEL.md](docs/security/THREAT_MODEL.md) — Threat model and security architecture\n- [docs/security/KEY_MANAGEMENT.md](docs/security/KEY_MANAGEMENT.md) — Key management and operational security\n- [docs/security/INCIDENT_RESPONSE.md](docs/security/INCIDENT_RESPONSE.md) — Incident response procedures\n- [docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md](docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md) — Audit readiness status\n\n---\n\n**Security Contact:** security@tonbankcard.com\n",

Objective\n13\t\n14\tCommission an **independent third-party penetration test** of the TONBANKCARD off-chain services — the Merchant API (`api/`), the Payment Status Indexer (`backend/indexer/`), and the Merchant SDK (`sdk/`) — focusing on OWASP Top 10, authentication weaknesses, data integrity, replay protection, and supply-chain risks.\n15\t\n16\tPer issue #115 §2, this engagement **should be conducted after Track D rate-limiting and webhook hardening (D4) lands**, so that the test exercises the production-grade hardened surface rather than the reference scaffolding currently in the repository. Engagements A1 (core contracts) and A2 (Phase 4 contracts) cover the on-chain surface and are out of scope here; this engagement is the matching off-chain counterpart and is a mandatory gate before mainnet exposure of the merchant-facing services.\n17\t\n18\tSuccess criteria (mirror of issue #115 acceptance criteria):\n19\t\n20\t- [ ] Pentest scope agreed with the security team and tested against a representative staging environment\n21\t- [ ] D4 rate-limiting, API-key authentication, and HMAC-SHA256 webhook signature work landed in the audited commit (or the residual gap is documented as a known limitation)\n22\t- [ ] All Critical findings remediated before any production launch\n23\t- [ ] All High findings remediated or formally accepted in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md)\n24\t- [ ] OWASP Top 10 checklist (see [`OWASP_CHECKLIST.md`](./OWASP_CHECKLIST.md)) completed for `api/`\n25\t- [ ] `npm audit` reports zero High / Critical vulnerabilities in the `sdk/` dependency tree at the audited commit\n26\t- [ ] Webhook signature verification confirmed resistant to replay attacks\n27\t- [ ] Pentest report published in this directory (`docs/security/audits/A4-offchain-services/`)\n28\t- [ ] Remediation PR(s) merged and re-tested by the pentester\n29\t- [ ] [`docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md`](../../AUDIT_READINESS.md) updated with the completion status\n30\t\n31\t---\n32\t\n33\t## 2.
