Out of Scope\n83\t\n84\tExplicitly **not** part of this engagement (per issue #115 §4):\n85\t\n86\t- **Smart contracts** (`contracts/`) — covered by engagements [A1](../A1-core-contracts/ENGAGEMENT.md) and [A2](../A2-phase4-contracts/ENGAGEMENT.md)\n87\t- **Formal verification** of invariants I1–I7 — covered by [A3](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/pull/146)\n88\t- **Third-party payment gateways** (ChangeNOW, NOWPayments, CoinRabbit) — security is the responsibility of those providers; their security claims are recorded as trust assumptions only\n89\t- **Private key storage** — the system must not store private keys off-chain at all; verifying that no such storage exists is a **correctness check**, not a pentest target\n90\t- **Wallet UI / mobile / dashboard** (`wallet-ui/`, `mobile/`, `dashboard/`) — separate review tracks (Track F UX)\n91\t- **Bug bounty operational tooling** — covered by [A5](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/) (separate engagement)\n92\t- **Underlying cloud infrastructure** (Kubernetes nodes, managed Postgres, Redis) — operator responsibility, exercised only insofar as it affects the application surface\n93\t\n94\tExternal pre-deployed components (TBC jetton, TON public HTTP API, indexer's upstream `@ton/ton` client) are treated as trust assumptions; their security is referenced from [`audit/SCOPE.md`](../../../../audit/SCOPE.md) §\"Out-of-Scope Components\".\n95\t\n96\t---\n97\t\n98\t## 4. Threat Model — Required Coverage\n99\t\n100\tThe pentester must explicitly evaluate every threat enumerated below, mapped to the protocol-level threat model in [`docs/security/THREAT_MODEL.md`](../../THREAT_MODEL.md) and the off-chain security guidance in [`docs/merchant-api-security.md`](../../../merchant-api-security.md). Each row maps a threat to file/line evidence so the auditor can begin work without a discovery phase.\n101\t\n102\tThe detailed test plan that operationalises this table is [`PENTEST_PLAN.md`](./PENTEST_PLAN.md); the OWASP Top 10 surface is recorded in [`OWASP_CHECKLIST.md`](./OWASP_CHECKLIST.md).\n103\t\n104\t### 4.1 Merchant API (`api/`)\n105\t\n106\t| # | Threat | Where to look |\n107\t|---|--------|---------------|\n108\t| API-1 | **Unauthenticated invoice manipulation** — creating, listing, or cancelling invoices without a valid API key | `apiKeyService.requireScope` callers in [`api/src/routes/invoiceRoutes.ts`](../../../../api/src/routes/invoiceRoutes.ts); confirm every mutating endpoint checks scope before doing work |\n109\t| API-2 | **IDOR (Insecure Direct Object Reference)** — accessing another merchant's invoices by guessing the 32-char invoice ID | [`api/src/services/InvoiceService.ts`](../../../../api/src/services/InvoiceService.ts) `getInvoice` / `getInvoiceStatus`; verify ownership is enforced on every read |\n110\t| API-3 | **Webhook replay** — replaying old webhook events to credit payments twice (post-D4 the HMAC-SHA256 signature scheme must include a monotonic nonce + timestamp window) | Webhook generator & verifier hand-off; replay-window test must fail (see [`PENTEST_PLAN.md`](./PENTEST_PLAN.md) §3.3) |\n111\t| API-4 | **CORS misconfiguration** — cross-origin requests from arbitrary domains carrying API-key credentials | Confirm PR #109 mitigation (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin` allow-list) is in effect; no `*` with credentials |\n112\t| API-5 | **Rate-limit bypass** — flooding invoice creation to exhaust quota or cause DoS by spoofing `X-Forwarded-For` / `CF-Connecting-IP` | `getClientIp` extraction logic (Redis-backed limiter from PR #104); confirm proxy trust is bounded |\n113\t| API-6 | **SQL injection** — malformed inputs reaching `PostgresStorage` queries | [`api/src/storage/PostgresStorage.ts`](../../../../api/src/storage/PostgresStorage.ts); verify all queries are parameterised, no string concatenation |\n114\t| API-7 | **Path traversal** — accessing files outside intended directories via static-asset / log endpoints (none today; ensure none are introduced) | Express `static` middleware audit; default-deny posture |\n115\t| API-8 | **Idempotency-key abuse** — predicting or colliding idempotency keys to steal another merchant's pending invoice | [`api/src/utils/helpers.ts`](../../../../api/src/utils/helpers.ts) `generateIdempotencyKey`; entropy and storage scoping |\n116\t| API-9 | **Metadata injection / XSS via API response** — merchant-supplied metadata rendered unsanitised by downstream UIs | `sanitizeMetadata` in [`api/src/utils/helpers.ts`](../../../../api/src/utils/helpers.ts); confirm canonical sanitisation |\n117\t| API-10 | **TLS / transport stripping** — downgrade attacks on the API endpoint | Deployment defaults; HSTS posture per [`docs/merchant-api-security.md`](../../../merchant-api-security.md) §9 |\n118\t\n119\t### 4.2 Indexer (`backend/indexer/`)\n120\t\n121\t| # | Threat | Where to look |\n122\t|---|--------|---------------|\n123\t| IDX-1 | **Data-integrity tampering** — injecting fraudulent payment records into the local cache via a malicious upstream | [`backend/indexer/src/parsers/`](../../../../backend/indexer/src/parsers/), `IndexerService.ingestBlock`; verify on-chain hash provenance is preserved |\n124\t| IDX-2 | **Unauthenticated API exposure** — indexer internal endpoints reachable from the public internet without an auth boundary | `/health`, `/payment/:id` in [`backend/indexer/src/api/routes.ts`](../../../../backend/indexer/src/api/routes.ts); confirm deployment binds to internal interface or fronts with auth |\n125\t| IDX-3 | **Replay attack** — processing the same blockchain event twice (double-credit) | Event de-duplication keys in `db/database.ts`; idempotency over `(tx_hash, lt)` |\n126\t| IDX-4 | **TON HTTP API trust** — accepting tampered data from a malicious or compromised TON HTTP API endpoint | Indexer's TON client configuration; verify response signature checks where the protocol allows, and document residual trust |\n127\t| IDX-5 | **Rate-limit / DoS** — flooding the indexer's read API to starve legitimate merchants | `RateLimiterRedis` configuration in [`server.ts`](../../../../backend/indexer/src/api/server.ts); confirm production tuning, not memory-only fallback |\n128\t| IDX-6 | **Log / config secret exposure** — TON API key, DB credentials leaking via verbose error responses or structured logs | Pino redaction config; confirm `tonApiKey: '***'` redaction holds for all log sites |\n129\t| IDX-7 | **SQL injection** — same class as API-6, applied to the indexer's SQLite/PostgreSQL queries | `db/database.ts` query construction |\n130\t| IDX-8 | **Account-history pagination abuse** — keyset pagination from PR #107 must not leak entries across accounts or skip events | Re-verify cursors include account binding |\n131\t\n132\t### 4.3 SDK (`sdk/`)\n133\t\n134\t| # | Threat | Where to look |\n135\t|---|--------|---------------|\n136\t| SDK-1 | **Supply-chain compromise** — malicious or yanked transitive dependency reaching consumers | `sdk/package.json`, `sdk/package-lock.json`; `npm audit` baseline at the audited commit |\n137\t| SDK-2 | **Dependency pinning drift** — `^` / `>=` ranges allowing post-publication upgrades that ship unaudited code | Verify lock-file integrity; recommend exact-pinning or `npm shrinkwrap` |\n138\t| SDK-3 | **XSS in payment widget** — user-controlled inputs (description, orderId, returnUrl) rendered unsafely in the widget DOM | [`sdk/src/widget/PaymentWidget.ts`](../../../../sdk/src/widget/PaymentWidget.ts) `mount` / `render`; confirm DOM API usage (no `innerHTML` with untrusted strings) |\n139\t| SDK-4 | **Sensitive-data leakage** — API keys or merchant secrets exposed via browser DevTools, `console.log`, or error callbacks | SDK's `onError` callback contract; verify no credential echo in error payloads |\n140\t| SDK-5 | **Clickjacking** — embedding the widget in a malicious framing context to harvest deep-link clicks | Widget framing policy — `X-Frame-Options` guidance for merchant integrators, `sandbox` attributes when iframed |\n141\t| SDK-6 | **Deep-link tampering** — TON Connect deep links altered between SDK generation and wallet handoff | Confirm deep links carry on-chain-verifiable parameters only (NFT address, amount, comment); no off-chain trust |\n142\t| SDK-7 | **Mock-vs-real flow confusion** — `sdk/src/mock.ts` accidentally shipped in production bundles, masking real settlement failures | Bundling configuration in [`sdk/package.json`](../../../../sdk/package.json) `tsup` setup; tree-shaking guards |\n143\t| SDK-8 | **Type-confusion attacks via published `.d.ts`** — relaxed types allowing unsafe merchant code paths | Published types in `dist/index.d.ts`; verify they match documented contract |\n144\t\n145\t### 4.4 Cross-cutting\n146\t\n147\t| # | Threat | Coverage |\n148\t|---|--------|----------|\n149\t| OFF-1 | **Non-custody verification** — none of the off-chain components stores private keys, signs transactions, or moves funds | Verified across `api/`, `backend/indexer/`, `sdk/`; cross-check against documented guarantees in [`docs/merchant-api-security.md`](../../../merchant-api-security.md) §2 |\n150\t| OFF-2 | **Secret management** — environment variables (`TON_API_KEY`, DB credentials, webhook signing secret) never logged, never sent to the client | All three packages |\n151\t| OFF-3 | **Defaults are secure** — out-of-the-box configuration (no overrides) is safe to deploy to a production-shaped environment | All three packages |\n152\t| OFF-4 | **Telemetry & observability privacy** — no PII or transaction-tying identifiers exported to third-party observability services without explicit opt-in | Pino logger configurations, SDK callback wiring |\n153\t| OFF-5 | **OWASP Top 10:2021** — every A0x category explicitly visited for `api/` | See [`OWASP_CHECKLIST.md`](./OWASP_CHECKLIST.md) |\n154\t\n155\tInvariant attestation in the final report must confirm that **I1 (Non-Custodial)** and **I3 (No Admin Fund Control)** remain intact end-to-end through the off-chain surface — i.e., no off-chain bug should allow a privileged operator to move user funds. Full invariant definitions: [`audit/INVARIANTS.md`](../../../../audit/INVARIANTS.md).\n156\t\n157\t---\n158\t\n159\t## 5. Candidate Firms\n188\t\n189\tThree firm classes are acceptable per the roadmap and issue #115:\n190\t\n191\t1. **Application-security pentest specialists with cryptocurrency / fintech experience**, e.g., NCC Group, Cure53, Doyensec, Trail of Bits (apps-security desk).\n192\t2. **Web3-native pentest teams with web-app coverage**, e.g., Halborn (apps division), OtterSec (web-app desk), Sigma Prime (apps-side), Quarkslab.\n193\t3. **TON / non-EVM ecosystem specialists with apps-security capability**, e.g., CertiK (TON desk apps-side), TonGuard, scalebit (TON), Veridise (apps-side).\n194\t\n195\tA non-exhaustive long list is maintained in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §\"Firm long list\".\n196\t\n197\tFor A4 specifically, **web-app pentest depth and supply-chain experience** weigh higher than for A1/A2 — firms with a demonstrated track record running OWASP-driven engagements, plus npm / JavaScript ecosystem supply-chain reviews, should be preferred. This is reflected in the evaluation matrix below.\n198\t\n199\tA firm that performed A1 or A2 may also bid for A4 only on a **separately signed scope** — code-level smart-contract expertise is not the same as app-layer pentest expertise, and bundling discourages cross-checking.\n200\t\n201\t### 6.1 Evaluation Matrix\n202\t\n203\tEach shortlisted firm is scored on the following criteria. Numeric scores 1–5 (5 = excellent). Final score = weighted sum. Compared to A1/A2, weights are re-balanced to emphasise application-security depth and supply-chain coverage over Tact/FunC depth.\n204\t\n205\t| Criterion | Weight | Notes |\n206\t|-----------|--------|-------|\n207\t| **Web-app / API pentest depth** | **25%** | OWASP engagements run per year, OSCP / OSWE / GWAPT credentials on team |\n208\t| **Supply-chain / npm review experience** | **15%** | Prior public engagements on JavaScript dependency trees, SBOM review |\n209\t| Crypto / fintech context | 15% | Familiarity with merchant-payments flows, webhook design, replay-protection idioms |\n210\t| Methodology rigor | 15% | Documented testing methodology, manual review hours per endpoint, fuzzing tools |\n211\t| Reputation & references | 10% | Publicly available pentest reports, ecosystem feedback |\n212\t| Re-test / remediation policy | 10% | Verified re-test included after remediation, follow-up support |\n213\t| Cost & timeline fit | 5% | Total cost, calendar window, latest available start |\n214\t| Communication & transparency | 5% | Daily stand-up cadence, willingness to publish, NDA flexibility |\n215\t\n216\t### 6.2 Conflict-of-interest screen\n217\t\n218\tFirms must disclose any prior engagement with TONBANKCARD operators, TON Foundation grant overlap, holding of TBC token / TBC Diamonds / Series 7777/8888 NFTs, financial interest in any candidate webhook-delivery / observability vendor used by the protocol, or other potential conflicts. Disqualifying conditions are recorded in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md).\n219\t\n220\tA firm that audited A1 or A2 must additionally disclose whether A4 findings were re-derived independently or carry over from the smart-contract engagement; the A4 report must produce an independent assessment of the off-chain surface regardless of overlap.\n221\t\n222\t---\n223\t\n224\t## 7. Engagement Process\n225\t\n226\t```\n227\tT-D4  D4 rate-limiting + webhook + API-key hardening merged              (gate)\n228\tT-D5  D5 npm-audit-in-CI merged                                          (recommended gate)\n229\tT-0   A4 issue published                                                 ✅\n230\tT+0   Firm long list assembled                                           ⏳\n231\tT+1w  Shortlist (3 firms) + RFP sent\n232\tT+3w  Proposals received, evaluation matrix populated\n233\tT+4w  Firm selected, contract signed\n234\tT+4w  Pentest kickoff: freeze commit + package handover + staging access\n235\tT+6w  Mid-pentest checkpoint (preliminary findings, OWASP coverage walk-through)\n236\tT+8w  Draft report delivered\n237\tT+9w  Remediation PRs opened (per REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md)\n238\tT+11w Remediation merged\n239\tT+12w Re-testing by pentester against remediation commit\n240\tT+12w Final report published in this directory\n241\tT+12w STATUS.md flipped to COMPLETED\n242\tT+13w Disclosure summary in CHANGELOG.md + public channels\n243\t```\n244\t\n245\tAll dates are anchored to the A4 kickoff (`T`) and tracked in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md). `T-D4` and `T-D5` are not under A4's control; they are upstream completion gates for the hardening work that A4 is designed to validate.\n246\t\n247\tA4 is intentionally shorter than A1/A2 (12 weeks total versus 14–16) because the off-chain surface is smaller in lines-of-code and the scope is well-bounded by the three packages. The mid-pentest checkpoint at T+6w explicitly walks through the OWASP Top 10 coverage matrix from [`OWASP_CHECKLIST.md`](./OWASP_CHECKLIST.md) so any uncovered class is escalated early.\n248\t\n249\tThe remediation phase follows [`../REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md`](../REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md) verbatim.\n250\t\n251\t---\n252\t\n253\t## 8. Deliverables From Pentester\n254\t\n255\tThe signed engagement must require the following deliverables (mirrored in the report template):\n256\t\n257\t1. **Pentest report**, structured per [`../REPORT_TEMPLATE.md`](../REPORT_TEMPLATE.md), adapted for an off-chain pentest:\n258\t   - Findings categorised by severity (Critical / High / Medium / Low / Informational)\n259\t   - Each finding references file:line (or HTTP method + path), threat-model class (API-, IDX-, SDK-, OFF-), and OWASP Top 10 category where applicable\n260\t   - Reproduction steps for every Critical and High (HTTP request capture or scripted PoC)\n261\t   - Suggested fixes where applicable\n262\t   - **OWASP Top 10:2021 coverage table** — every A01–A10 category marked as Tested / Not applicable / Out of scope with rationale; the table must mirror [`OWASP_CHECKLIST.md`](./OWASP_CHECKLIST.md)\n263\t   - Explicit attestation that **I1** and **I3** invariants remain intact through the off-chain surface\n264\t   - **Supply-chain section** for `sdk/`: dependency tree summary, `npm audit` output at the audited commit, pinning recommendations\n265\t   - **Webhook replay analysis**: explicit confirmation that the post-D4 HMAC-SHA256 + nonce / timestamp window scheme cannot be replayed within the documented validity window\n266\t2. **Reproducible PoCs** for every Critical and High finding — provided as curl scripts, Postman collections, or short Node scripts. PoCs must run against the staging environment without modification.\n267\t3. **Re-test letter** signed after remediation against a specific commit hash, confirming whether each finding is Fixed / Mitigated / Accepted / Unresolved.\n268\t4. **Right to publish** the report in this repository (full report, or summary + redacted appendix if any sensitive infrastructure details require omission — the decision is documented in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §\"Disclosure decisions\").\n269\t\n270\tIf any component is recommended for **redesign or removal** (e.g., the reference-only in-memory adapters in `api/src/storage/InMemoryStorage.ts`), the pentester's recommendation must be explicit — the protocol team will not interpret silence as approval.\n271\t\n272\t---\n273\t\n274\t## 9. Acceptance / Gating Decision\n275\t\n276\tThe engagement is closed when:\n277\t\n278\t- All ten checkboxes in §1 are ticked.\n279\t- [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) records the gating verdict as `READY` or `READY WITH ACCEPTED RISKS`.\n280\t- [`docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md`](../../AUDIT_READINESS.md) §\"Audit completion status\" is updated with the A4 row populated.\n281\t- `CHANGELOG.md` carries a disclosure entry referencing the report.\n282\t\n283\tA verdict of `BLOCKED` keeps **production deployment of the merchant-facing off-chain surface** paused per [`../README.md`](../README.md) §4 and blocks the related Track B (production deployment) and Track C (developer-experience launches) work from going public-facing.\n284\t\n285\t---\n286\t\n287\t## 10.    [solve worker-1]       "content": "# Engagement A4 — Penetration Test of Off-Chain Services\n\n**Engagement ID:** `A4`\n**Issue:** [#115 — A4 Penetration Testing — Off-Chain Services](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/115)\n**Roadmap track:** A — Security & Audit\n**Status:** Engagement preparation complete — awaiting D4 hardening and firm selection\n**Maintainer:** `@konard`\n**Last Updated:** 2026-05-16\n\n---\n\n## 1. Objective\n\nCommission an **independent third-party penetration test** of the TONBANKCARD off-chain services — the Merchant API (`api/`), the Payment Status Indexer (`backend/indexer/`), and the Merchant SDK (`sdk/`) — focusing on OWASP Top 10, authentication weaknesses, data integrity, replay protection, and supply-chain risks.\n\nPer issue #115 §2, this engagement **should be conducted after Track D rate-limiting and webhook hardening (D4) lands**, so that the test exercises the production-grade hardened surface rather than the reference scaffolding currently in the repository. Engagements A1 (core contracts) and A2 (Phase 4 contracts) cover the on-chain surface and are out of scope here; this engagement is the matching off-chain counterpart and is a mandatory gate before mainnet exposure of the merchant-facing services.\n\nSuccess criteria (mirror of issue #115 acceptance criteria):\n\n- [ ] Pentest scope agreed with the security team and tested against a representative staging environment\n- [ ] D4 rate-limiting, API-key authentication, and HMAC-SHA256 webhook signature work landed in the audited commit (or the residual gap is documented as a known limitation)\n- [ ] All Critical findings remediated before any production launch\n- [ ] All High findings remediated or formally accepted in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md)\n- [ ] OWASP Top 10 checklist (see [`OWASP_CHECKLIST.md`](./OWASP_CHECKLIST.md)) completed for `api/`\n- [ ] `npm audit` reports zero High / Critical vulnerabilities in the `sdk/` dependency tree at the audited commit\n- [ ] Webhook signature verification confirmed resistant to replay attacks\n- [ ] Pentest report published in this directory (`docs/security/audits/A4-offchain-services/`)\n- [ ] Remediation PR(s) merged and re-tested by the pentester\n- [ ] [`docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md`](../../AUDIT_READINESS.md) updated with the completion status\n\n---\n\n## 2. Out of Scope\n\nExplicitly **not** part of this engagement (per issue #115 §4):\n\n- **Smart contracts** (`contracts/`) — covered by engagements [A1](../A1-core-contracts/ENGAGEMENT.md) and [A2](../A2-phase4-contracts/ENGAGEMENT.md)\n- **Formal verification** of invariants I1–I7 — covered by [A3](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/pull/146)\n- **Third-party payment gateways** (ChangeNOW, NOWPayments, CoinRabbit) — security is the responsibility of those providers; their security claims are recorded as trust assumptions only\n- **Private key storage** — the system must not store private keys off-chain at all; verifying that no such storage exists is a **correctness check**, not a pentest target\n- **Wallet UI / mobile / dashboard** (`wallet-ui/`, `mobile/`, `dashboard/`) — separate review tracks (Track F UX)\n- **Bug bounty operational tooling** — covered by [A5](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/) (separate engagement)\n- **Underlying cloud infrastructure** (Kubernetes nodes, managed Postgres, Redis) — operator responsibility, exercised only insofar as it affects the application surface\n\nExternal pre-deployed components (TBC jetton, TON public HTTP API, indexer's upstream `@ton/ton` client) are treated as trust assumptions; their security is referenced from [`audit/SCOPE.md`](../../../../audit/SCOPE.md) §\"Out-of-Scope Components\".\n\n---\n\n## 4. Threat Model — Required Coverage\n\nThe pentester must explicitly evaluate every threat enumerated below, mapped to the protocol-level threat model in [`docs/security/THREAT_MODEL.md`](../../THREAT_MODEL.md) and the off-chain security guidance in [`docs/merchant-api-security.md`](../../../merchant-api-security.md). Each row maps a threat to file/line evidence so the auditor can begin work without a discovery phase.\n\nThe detailed test plan that operationalises this table is [`PENTEST_PLAN.md`](./PENTEST_PLAN.md); the OWASP Top 10 surface is recorded in [`OWASP_CHECKLIST.md`](./OWASP_CHECKLIST.md).\n\n### 4.1 Merchant API (`api/`)\n\n| # | Threat | Where to look |\n|---|--------|---------------|\n| API-1 | **Unauthenticated invoice manipulation** — creating, listing, or cancelling invoices without a valid API key | `apiKeyService.requireScope` callers in [`api/src/routes/invoiceRoutes.ts`](../../../../api/src/routes/invoiceRoutes.ts); confirm every mutating endpoint checks scope before doing work |\n| API-2 | **IDOR (Insecure Direct Object Reference)** — accessing another merchant's invoices by guessing the 32-char invoice ID | [`api/src/services/InvoiceService.ts`](../../../../api/src/services/InvoiceService.ts) `getInvoice` / `getInvoiceStatus`; verify ownership is enforced on every read |\n| API-3 | **Webhook replay** — replaying old webhook events to credit payments twice (post-D4 the HMAC-SHA256 signature scheme must include a monotonic nonce + timestamp window) | Webhook generator & verifier hand-off; replay-window test must fail (see [`PENTEST_PLAN.md`](./PENTEST_PLAN.md) §3.3) |\n| API-4 | **CORS misconfiguration** — cross-origin requests from arbitrary domains carrying API-key credentials | Confirm PR #109 mitigation (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin` allow-list) is in effect; no `*` with credentials |\n| API-5 | **Rate-limit bypass** — flooding invoice creation to exhaust quota or cause DoS by spoofing `X-Forwarded-For` / `CF-Connecting-IP` | `getClientIp` extraction logic (Redis-backed limiter from PR #104); confirm proxy trust is bounded |\n| API-6 | **SQL injection** — malformed inputs reaching `PostgresStorage` queries | [`api/src/storage/PostgresStorage.ts`](../../../../api/src/storage/PostgresStorage.ts); verify all queries are parameterised, no string concatenation |\n| API-7 | **Path traversal** — accessing files outside intended directories via static-asset / log endpoints (none today; ensure none are introduced) | Express `static` middleware audit; default-deny posture |\n| API-8 | **Idempotency-key abuse** — predicting or colliding idempotency keys to steal another merchant's pending invoice | [`api/src/utils/helpers.ts`](../../../../api/src/utils/helpers.ts) `generateIdempotencyKey`; entropy and storage scoping |\n| API-9 | **Metadata injection / XSS via API response** — merchant-supplied metadata rendered unsanitised by downstream UIs | `sanitizeMetadata` in [`api/src/utils/helpers.ts`](../../../../api/src/utils/helpers.ts); confirm canonical sanitisation |\n| API-10 | **TLS / transport stripping** — downgrade attacks on the API endpoint | Deployment defaults; HSTS posture per [`docs/merchant-api-security.md`](../../../merchant-api-security.md) §9 |\n\n### 4.2 Indexer (`backend/indexer/`)\n\n| # | Threat | Where to look |\n|---|--------|---------------|\n| IDX-1 | **Data-integrity tampering** — injecting fraudulent payment records into the local cache via a malicious upstream | [`backend/indexer/src/parsers/`](../../../../backend/indexer/src/parsers/), `IndexerService.ingestBlock`; verify on-chain hash provenance is preserved |\n| IDX-2 | **Unauthenticated API exposure** — indexer internal endpoints reachable from the public internet without an auth boundary | `/health`, `/payment/:id` in [`backend/indexer/src/api/routes.ts`](../../../../backend/indexer/src/api/routes.ts); confirm deployment binds to internal interface or fronts with auth |\n| IDX-3 | **Replay attack** — processing the same blockchain event twice (double-credit) | Event de-duplication keys in `db/database.ts`; idempotency over `(tx_hash, lt)` |\n| IDX-4 | **TON HTTP API trust** — accepting tampered data from a malicious or compromised TON HTTP API endpoint | Indexer's TON client configuration; verify response signature checks where the protocol allows, and document residual trust |\n| IDX-5 | **Rate-limit / DoS** — flooding the indexer's read API to starve legitimate merchants | `RateLimiterRedis` configuration in [`server.ts`](../../../../backend/indexer/src/api/server.ts); confirm production tuning, not memory-only fallback |\n| IDX-6 | **Log / config secret exposure** — TON API key, DB credentials leaking via verbose error responses or structured logs | Pino redaction config; confirm `tonApiKey: '***'` redaction holds for all log sites |\n| IDX-7 | **SQL injection** — same class as API-6, applied to the indexer's SQLite/PostgreSQL queries | `db/database.ts` query construction |\n| IDX-8 | **Account-history pagination abuse** — keyset pagination from PR #107 must not leak entries across accounts or skip events | Re-verify cursors include account binding |\n\n### 4.3 SDK (`sdk/`)\n\n| # | Threat | Where to look |\n|---|--------|---------------|\n| SDK-1 | **Supply-chain compromise** — malicious or yanked transitive dependency reaching consumers | `sdk/package.json`, `sdk/package-lock.json`; `npm audit` baseline at the audited commit |\n| SDK-2 | **Dependency pinning drift** — `^` / `>=` ranges allowing post-publication upgrades that ship unaudited code | Verify lock-file integrity; recommend exact-pinning or `npm shrinkwrap` |\n| SDK-3 | **XSS in payment widget** — user-controlled inputs (description, orderId, returnUrl) rendered unsafely in the widget DOM | [`sdk/src/widget/PaymentWidget.ts`](../../../../sdk/src/widget/PaymentWidget.ts) `mount` / `render`; confirm DOM API usage (no `innerHTML` with untrusted strings) |\n| SDK-4 | **Sensitive-data leakage** — API keys or merchant secrets exposed via browser DevTools, `console.log`, or error callbacks | SDK's `onError` callback contract; verify no credential echo in error payloads |\n| SDK-5 | **Clickjacking** — embedding the widget in a malicious framing context to harvest deep-link clicks | Widget framing policy — `X-Frame-Options` guidance for merchant integrators, `sandbox` attributes when iframed |\n| SDK-6 | **Deep-link tampering** — TON Connect deep links altered between SDK generation and wallet handoff | Confirm deep links carry on-chain-verifiable parameters only (NFT address, amount, comment); no off-chain trust |\n| SDK-7 | **Mock-vs-real flow confusion** — `sdk/src/mock.ts` accidentally shipped in production bundles, masking real settlement failures | Bundling configuration in [`sdk/package.json`](../../../../sdk/package.json) `tsup` setup; tree-shaking guards |\n| SDK-8 | **Type-confusion attacks via published `.d.ts`** — relaxed types allowing unsafe merchant code paths | Published types in `dist/index.d.ts`; verify they match documented contract |\n\n### 4.4 Cross-cutting\n\n| # | Threat | Coverage |\n|---|--------|----------|\n| OFF-1 | **Non-custody verification** — none of the off-chain components stores private keys, signs transactions, or moves funds | Verified across `api/`, `backend/indexer/`, `sdk/`; cross-check against documented guarantees in [`docs/merchant-api-security.md`](../../../merchant-api-security.md) §2 |\n| OFF-2 | **Secret management** — environment variables (`TON_API_KEY`, DB credentials, webhook signing secret) never logged, never sent to the client | All three packages |\n| OFF-3 | **Defaults are secure** — out-of-the-box configuration (no overrides) is safe to deploy to a production-shaped environment | All three packages |\n| OFF-4 | **Telemetry & observability privacy** — no PII or transaction-tying identifiers exported to third-party observability services without explicit opt-in | Pino logger configurations, SDK callback wiring |\n| OFF-5 | **OWASP Top 10:2021** — every A0x category explicitly visited for `api/` | See [`OWASP_CHECKLIST.md`](./OWASP_CHECKLIST.md) |\n\nInvariant attestation in the final report must confirm that **I1 (Non-Custodial)** and **I3 (No Admin Fund Control)** remain intact end-to-end through the off-chain surface — i.e., no off-chain bug should allow a privileged operator to move user funds. Full invariant definitions: [`audit/INVARIANTS.md`](../../../../audit/INVARIANTS.md).\n\n---\n\n## 5. representative **staging environment** (URL, isolated TON testnet endpoint, throwaway API keys with the same scopes the production service issues, an SDK consumer harness). Production-only secrets are never shared with the pentester.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Candidate Firms\n\nThree firm classes are acceptable per the roadmap and issue #115:\n\n1. **Application-security pentest specialists with cryptocurrency / fintech experience**, e.g., NCC Group, Cure53, Doyensec, Trail of Bits (apps-security desk).\n2. **Web3-native pentest teams with web-app coverage**, e.g., Halborn (apps division), OtterSec (web-app desk), Sigma Prime (apps-side), Quarkslab.\n3. **TON / non-EVM ecosystem specialists with apps-security capability**, e.g., CertiK (TON desk apps-side), TonGuard, scalebit (TON), Veridise (apps-side).\n\nA non-exhaustive long list is maintained in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §\"Firm long list\".\n\nFor A4 specifically, **web-app pentest depth and supply-chain experience** weigh higher than for A1/A2 — firms with a demonstrated track record running OWASP-driven engagements, plus npm / JavaScript ecosystem supply-chain reviews, should be preferred. This is reflected in the evaluation matrix below.\n\nA firm that performed A1 or A2 may also bid for A4 only on a **separately signed scope** — code-level smart-contract expertise is not the same as app-layer pentest expertise, and bundling discourages cross-checking.\n\n### 6.1 Evaluation Matrix\n\nEach shortlisted firm is scored on the following criteria. Numeric scores 1–5 (5 = excellent). Final score = weighted sum. Compared to A1/A2, weights are re-balanced to emphasise application-security depth and supply-chain coverage over Tact/FunC depth.\n\n| Criterion | Weight | Notes |\n|-----------|--------|-------|\n| **Web-app / API pentest depth** | **25%** | OWASP engagements run per year, OSCP / OSWE / GWAPT credentials on team |\n| **Supply-chain / npm review experience** | **15%** | Prior public engagements on JavaScript dependency trees, SBOM review |\n| Crypto / fintech context | 15% | Familiarity with merchant-payments flows, webhook design, replay-protection idioms |\n| Methodology rigor | 15% | Documented testing methodology, manual review hours per endpoint, fuzzing tools |\n| Reputation & references | 10% | Publicly available pentest reports, ecosystem feedback |\n| Re-test / remediation policy | 10% | Verified re-test included after remediation, follow-up support |\n| Cost & timeline fit | 5% | Total cost, calendar window, latest available start |\n| Communication & transparency | 5% | Daily stand-up cadence, willingness to publish, NDA flexibility |\n\n### 6.2 Conflict-of-interest screen\n\nFirms must disclose any prior engagement with TONBANKCARD operators, TON Foundation grant overlap, holding of TBC token / TBC Diamonds / Series 7777/8888 NFTs, financial interest in any candidate webhook-delivery / observability vendor used by the protocol, or other potential conflicts. Disqualifying conditions are recorded in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md).\n\nA firm that audited A1 or A2 must additionally disclose whether A4 findings were re-derived independently or carry over from the smart-contract engagement; the A4 report must produce an independent assessment of the off-chain surface regardless of overlap.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Engagement Process\n\n```\nT-D4  D4 rate-limiting + webhook + API-key hardening merged              (gate)\nT-D5  D5 npm-audit-in-CI merged                                          (recommended gate)\nT-0   A4 issue published                                                 ✅\nT+0   Firm long list assembled                                           ⏳\nT+1w  Shortlist (3 firms) + RFP sent\nT+3w  Proposals received, evaluation matrix populated\nT+4w  Firm selected, contract signed\nT+4w  Pentest kickoff: freeze commit + package handover + staging access\nT+6w  Mid-pentest checkpoint (preliminary findings, OWASP coverage walk-through)\nT+8w  Draft report delivered\nT+9w  Remediation PRs opened (per REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md)\nT+11w Remediation merged\nT+12w Re-testing by pentester against remediation commit\nT+12w Final report published in this directory\nT+12w STATUS.md flipped to COMPLETED\nT+13w Disclosure summary in CHANGELOG.md + public channels\n```\n\nAll dates are anchored to the A4 kickoff (`T`) and tracked in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md). `T-D4` and `T-D5` are not under A4's control; they are upstream completion gates for the hardening work that A4 is designed to validate.\n\nA4 is intentionally shorter than A1/A2 (12 weeks total versus 14–16) because the off-chain surface is smaller in lines-of-code and the scope is well-bounded by the three packages. The mid-pentest checkpoint at T+6w explicitly walks through the OWASP Top 10 coverage matrix from [`OWASP_CHECKLIST.md`](./OWASP_CHECKLIST.md) so any uncovered class is escalated early.\n\nThe remediation phase follows [`../REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md`](../REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md) verbatim.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Deliverables From Pentester\n\nThe signed engagement must require the following deliverables (mirrored in the report template):\n\n1. **Pentest report**, structured per [`../REPORT_TEMPLATE.md`](../REPORT_TEMPLATE.md), adapted for an off-chain pentest:\n   - Findings categorised by severity (Critical / High / Medium / Low / Informational)\n   - Each finding references file:line (or HTTP method + path), threat-model class (API-, IDX-, SDK-, OFF-), and OWASP Top 10 category where applicable\n   - Reproduction steps for every Critical and High (HTTP request capture or scripted PoC)\n   - Suggested fixes where applicable\n   - **OWASP Top 10:2021 coverage table** — every A01–A10 category marked as Tested / Not applicable / Out of scope with rationale; the table must mirror [`OWASP_CHECKLIST.md`](./OWASP_CHECKLIST.md)\n   - Explicit attestation that **I1** and **I3** invariants remain intact through the off-chain surface\n   - **Supply-chain section** for `sdk/`: dependency tree summary, `npm audit` output at the audited commit, pinning recommendations\n   - **Webhook replay analysis**: explicit confirmation that the post-D4 HMAC-SHA256 + nonce / timestamp window scheme cannot be replayed within the documented validity window\n2. **Reproducible PoCs** for every Critical and High finding — provided as curl scripts, Postman collections, or short Node scripts. PoCs must run against the staging environment without modification.\n3. **Re-test letter** signed after remediation against a specific commit hash, confirming whether each finding is Fixed / Mitigated / Accepted / Unresolved.\n4. **Right to publish** the report in this repository (full report, or summary + redacted appendix if any sensitive infrastructure details require omission — the decision is documented in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §\"Disclosure decisions\").\n\nIf any component is recommended for **redesign or removal** (e.g., the reference-only in-memory adapters in `api/src/storage/InMemoryStorage.ts`), the pentester's recommendation must be explicit — the protocol team will not interpret silence as approval.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Acceptance / Gating Decision\n\nThe engagement is closed when:\n\n- All ten checkboxes in §1 are ticked.\n- [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) records the gating verdict as `READY` or `READY WITH ACCEPTED RISKS`.\n- [`docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md`](../../AUDIT_READINESS.md) §\"Audit completion status\" is updated with the A4 row populated.\n- `CHANGELOG.md` carries a disclosure entry referencing the report.\n\nA verdict of `BLOCKED` keeps **production deployment of the merchant-facing off-chain surface** paused per [`../README.md`](../README.md) §4 and blocks the related Track B (production deployment) and Track C (developer-experience launches) work from going public-facing.\n\n---\n\n## 10. Any violation is a critical security finding.\n58\t\n59\t| ID | Invariant | Key Guarantee |\n60\t|----|-----------|---------------|\n61\t| **I1** | Non-Custodial Ownership | Only NFT owner can initiate fund transfers |\n62\t| **I2** | NFT = Account Authority | NFT ownership is the single source of truth for account control |\n63\t| **I3** | No Admin Fund Control | No privileged role can move user funds |\n64\t| **I4** | Atomic Transfers | All transfers are all-or-nothing; no partial state possible |\n65\t| **I5** | Ledger Conservation | Sum of all balances is preserved across all operations |\n66\t| **I6** | Lock ≠ Confiscation | Locks restrict outgoing transfers; they do not seize funds |\n67\t| **I7** | External Adapter Isolation | External providers cannot directly invoke protocol operations |\n68\t\n69\tFull formal definitions with contract-code mappings: [audit/INVARIANTS.md](../../audit/INVARIANTS.md)\n70\t\n71\t---\n72\t\n73\t## Test Coverage Summary\n74\t\n75\t| Contract | Estimated Line Coverage | Estimated Branch Coverage |\n76\t|----------|------------------------|--------------------------|\n77\t| MerchantPaymentHub.tact | ~90%+ | ~85%+ |\n78\t| PaymentHub.tact | ~85%+ | ~80%+ |\n79\t| account-locks.fc | ~85%+ | ~80%+ |\n80\t| nft_account_resolver.fc | ~80%+ | ~75%+ |\n81\t| account-state.tact | ~90%+ | ~85%+ |\n82\t\n83\tTo obtain exact figures:\n84\t\n85\t```bash\n86\tgit checkout eb5dd593248a33a5a7517ae59b840827c140906a\n87\tnpm install\n88\tnpx blueprint test --coverage\n89\t```\n90\t\n91\tSee [audit/TEST_COVERAGE_REPORT.md](../../audit/TEST_COVERAGE_REPORT.md) for full test organization.\n92\t\n93\t---\n94\t\n95\t## Critical Audit Focus Areas\n96\t\n97\t### 1. No Admin Fund Control (MUST verify)\n98\t\n99\tSearch the entire contract codebase for `withdraw`, `drain`, `emergency`, `admin_transfer`, `force_transfer`. Atomic Balance Updates (MUST verify)\n108\t\n109\tAll balance modifications must be atomic — both debit and credit in the same transaction. Lock Enforcement (MUST verify)\n114\t\n115\tLocks prevent sending but must never seize funds. Objective\n\nProcure a **formal external security audit** of the Phase 2 core smart contracts by a TON-specialist firm. Successfully completing this engagement is a mandatory gate before any TONBANKCARD mainnet deployment touching the in-scope contracts.\n\nSuccess criteria (mirror of issue #112 acceptance criteria):\n\n- [ ] Audit firm engaged and scope signed\n- [ ] Frozen audit package delivered (see §5)\n- [ ] All Critical findings remediated and re-verified\n- [ ] All High findings remediated, or formally accepted with rationale in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md)\n- [ ] All Medium findings addressed (remediated or documented as accepted risk in `docs/audit-notes.md`)\n- [ ] Audit report published in this directory\n- [ ] Remediation PR(s) merged and re-verified by auditor\n- [ ] `docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md` updated with completion status\n\n---\n\n## 2. In-Scope Contracts\n\nThe audit covers exactly the contracts listed in issue #112 §3:\n\n| # | Contract | File | Language | Reason |\n|---|----------|------|----------|--------|\n| 1 | PaymentHub | `contracts/payments/PaymentHub.tact` | Tact | Core payment routing, NFT account abstraction |\n| 2 | MerchantPaymentHub | `contracts/MerchantPaymentHub.tact` | Tact | Merchant-facing payment processing |\n| 3 | Account Locks | `contracts/payments/account-locks.fc` | FunC | FRAUD_LOCK and COLLATERAL_LOCK flag logic |\n| 4 | NFT Account Resolver (FunC) | `contracts/nft-resolver/nft_account_resolver.fc` | FunC | On-chain NFT ownership resolver |\n| 5 | NFT Account Resolver (Tact) | `contracts/nft-resolver/nft_account_resolver.tact` | Tact | Tact wrapper for the resolver |\n| 6 | Public Collateral Lookup | `contracts/collateral-lookup/PublicCollateralLookup.tact` | Tact | Collateral signal read interface |\n| 7 | Collateral Signal | `contracts/CollateralSignal.tact` | Tact | Collateral signal emission |\n\nSupporting types and interfaces (`contracts/types/`, `contracts/interfaces/`) are in scope **for context only** — they are reviewed insofar as they affect the contracts above. They have already been covered by the internal per-contract audit in [`audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md`](../../../../audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md).\n\n---\n\n## 3. Out of Scope\n\nExplicitly **not** part of this engagement (per issue #112 §4):\n\n- Phase 4 contracts (`CrossChainBridge.tact`, `MultiSigCard.tact`, `RecurringPayments.tact`, `LendingProtocolCoordinator.tact`) — covered by engagement **A2**\n- Off-chain services (`api/`, `backend/`, `sdk/`) — covered by engagement **A4**\n- Governance contracts (`contracts/governance/*`) — covered in **Track E**\n- Frontend, dashboard, wallet UI\n\nExternal pre-deployed contracts (TBC jetton, NFT collections, TONCO DEX pool) are treated as trust assumptions; their audits are referenced via [`audit/SCOPE.md`](../../../../audit/SCOPE.md) §\"Out-of-Scope Components\".\n\n---\n\n## 4. Threat Model — Required Coverage\n\nThe audit must explicitly evaluate every attack class enumerated in issue #112 §5, mapped to the protocol-level threat model in [`audit/THREAT_MODEL.md`](../../../../audit/THREAT_MODEL.md):\n\n| # | Class | Where to look |\n|---|-------|---------------|\n| T1 | Re-entrancy / message ordering | `PaymentHub.tact` reentrancy guard (lines 149–150), all `receive(...)` handlers |\n| T2 | NFT ownership spoofing | `nft-resolver/*`, `MerchantPaymentHub.checkOwnership` (lines 90–96) |\n| T3 | Lock bypass | `account-locks.fc` `get_can_send` / `get_can_receive`, all fund-moving paths |\n| T4 | Admin key abuse | search for `deployer`, `admin`, `risk_authority`, `lending_adapter` — verify invariant I3 |\n| T5 | Atomicity failure | `PaymentHub.executeTransfer` (lines 196–202), debit/credit pairing |\n| T6 | Integer overflow / underflow | All `Int as uintN` casts, balance arithmetic |\n| T7 | Replay attacks | Message uniqueness, on-chain vs. off-chain replay protection |\n| T8 | Gas griefing | `receive` handler gas costs, refund paths, message storage |\n\nInvariant attestation in the final report must cover **I1–I7** as defined in [`audit/INVARIANTS.md`](../../../../audit/INVARIANTS.md).\n\n---\n\n## 5. Audit Package (Frozen Hand-off)\n\nThe protocol team will deliver the following package to the selected firm at engagement kickoff. Purpose\n11\t\n12\tThis document defines a single, repeatable workflow for processing findings from any external audit listed in [`README.md`](./README.md). It exists so that:\n13\t\n14\t- Every finding has a tracked GitHub issue\n15\t- Every fix has a reviewable pull request\n16\t- Auditors can re-verify fixes against a stable artifact\n17\t- Public disclosure follows a predictable timeline\n18\t\n19\tIt applies to engagements A1, A2, A4, future re-audits, and any out-of-band advisories.\n20\t\n21\t---\n22\t\n23\t## 2. Severity Classification\n24\t\n25\tThe protocol uses the severity scale already established in [`audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md`](../../../audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md) and issue #110:\n26\t\n27\t| Severity | Definition | Response Time | Mandatory Action |\n28\t|----------|------------|---------------|------------------|\n29\t| 🔴 **CRITICAL** | Threat to user funds or non-custodial guarantee | 24h triage / 7-day fix target | **Must be remediated**. Mainnet deployment blocked until re-verified. |\n30\t| 🟠 **HIGH** | Serious logic error that can lead to loss of funds or privilege escalation under plausible conditions | 72h triage / 14-day fix target | Remediated **or** formally accepted in `STATUS.md` with rationale and compensating control |\n31\t| 🟡 **MEDIUM** | Bug or deviation that produces incorrect behaviour without direct fund loss | 1-week triage / 30-day fix target | Remediated or documented as accepted risk in `docs/audit-notes.md` |\n32\t| 🟢 **LOW** | Style, documentation, or hardening issue | Best-effort | Addressed in batches; tracked but non-blocking |\n33\t| ℹ️ **INFORMATIONAL** | Notes, suggestions, design observations | Optional | Logged in `STATUS.md` if not actioned |\n34\t\n35\tMainnet deployment is gated on the rules in [`README.md`](./README.md) §4.\n36\t\n37\t---\n38\t\n39\t## 3. Workflow\n40\t\n41\t```\n42\tAuditor delivers report\n43\t        │\n44\t        ▼\n45\t1. Intake          ─►  Hash + commit report to audits/<ID>/report-vN.pdf\n46\t        │\n47\t        ▼\n48\t2. Triage          ─►  Open one GitHub issue per finding (label: audit:<ID>, severity:<level>)\n49\t        │\n50\t        ▼\n51\t3. Remediation     ─►  Branch issue-<n>-<slug>, PR linked back to the finding issue\n52\t        │\n53\t        ▼\n54\t4. Re-verification ─►  Auditor confirms fix on remediation commit hash\n55\t        │\n56\t        ▼\n57\t5. Disclosure      ─►  STATUS.md flipped to COMPLETED; AUDIT_READINESS.md updated; public note\n58\t```\n59\t\n60\tEach step is described below in detail.\n61\t\n62\t### 3.1 Intake\n63\t\n64\tWhen an audit report is received:\n65\t\n66\t1. Save the report as `docs/security/audits/<ID>/report-v<N>.pdf` (or `.md`) — keep the original filename in `STATUS.md`.\n67\t2. Record SHA-256 of the file in `STATUS.md` for tamper evidence.\n68\t3. Confirm the audited commit hash matches the freeze recorded in `audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md`. If it does not, raise this with the auditor before triage.\n69\t4. Commit the report on a branch named `audit/<ID>-report-intake`. **Do not modify the report after this commit.**\n70\t\n71\t### 3.2 Triage\n72\t\n73\tFor every finding:\n74\t\n75\t1. Open a GitHub issue titled `[audit-<ID>] <finding-id>: <short title>`.\n76\t2. Apply labels:\n77\t   - `audit:<ID>` (e.g., `audit:A1`)\n78\t   - `severity:critical` / `severity:high` / `severity:medium` / `severity:low` / `severity:informational`\n79\t   - `type:security`\n80\t3. Copy the auditor's description, evidence, and recommendation verbatim into the issue body.\n81\t4. Cross-link the issue from the corresponding row in `audits/<ID>/STATUS.md` §\"Findings ledger\".\n82\t\n83\tThe triage owner is the maintainer named in `audits/<ID>/STATUS.md` §\"Engagement parties\". Triage SLAs:\n84\t\n85\t- Critical: triage within 24 hours of intake\n86\t- High: 72 hours\n87\t- Medium / Low / Informational: 7 days\n88\t\n89\t### 3.3 Remediation\n90\t\n91\tFor every finding that will be remediated:\n92\t\n93\t1. Create a branch named `issue-<n>-<slug>` per the contributing guidelines.\n94\t2. Reproduce the finding in a test case before applying the fix. The test must fail on the audited commit.\n95\t3. Implement the fix and run the full test suite (`npx blueprint test`).\n96\t4. Open a pull request with the description fields below:\n97\t\n98\t```markdown\n99\t## Audit Finding\n100\tEngagement: <A1 / A2 / …>\n101\tFinding ID: <auditor-assigned ID>\n102\tSeverity: <Critical / High / Medium / Low / Informational>\n103\tAuditor recommendation: <one line>\n104\t\n105\t## Fix Summary\n106\t<what changed and why>\n107\t\n108\t## Verification\n109\t- [ ] Reproducing test added (link)\n110\t- [ ] Full suite passes\n111\t- [ ] Invariant tests (I1–I7) unchanged or strengthened\n112\t- [ ] No changes to public ABI without coordinator sign-off\n113\t```\n114\t\n115\t5. Request review from the maintainer named in the engagement's `STATUS.md`.\n116\t6. After merge, append the merge commit to the finding row in `STATUS.md`.\n117\t\n118\t### 3.4 Findings That Will Not Be Remediated\n119\t\n120\tWhen a finding is accepted as residual risk:\n121\t\n122\t1. Record the acceptance in `audits/<ID>/STATUS.md` §\"Accepted risks\" with:\n123\t   - Finding ID\n124\t   - Severity\n125\t   - Justification (technical + business)\n126\t   - Compensating control\n127\t   - Sign-off (maintainer GitHub handle + date)\n128\t2. Mirror the entry into `docs/audit-notes.md`.\n129\t3. Inform the auditor; request explicit acknowledgement in the re-verification letter.\n130\t\n131\tHigh-severity findings may only be accepted with maintainer + at least one independent reviewer sign-off recorded in the table.\n132\t\n133\t### 3.5 Re-verification\n134\t\n135\tAfter all remediation PRs are merged:\n136\t\n137\t1. Tag the remediation head commit (`audit-<ID>-remediation-v<N>`).\n138\t2. Provide the auditor with:\n139\t   - The tag\n140\t   - A diff against the audited commit\n141\t   - Test results\n142\t3. Receive the auditor's re-verification letter. Save it under `audits/<ID>/reverification-v<N>.pdf`.\n143\t4. Flip the engagement status in `STATUS.md` and `README.md` §3 to `COMPLETED` (or `ACCEPTED WITH RISKS` if any High items were accepted).\n144\t\n145\t### 3.6 Disclosure\n146\t\n147\tWithin 14 days of re-verification:\n148\t\n149\t1. Update `docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md` §\"Audit completion status\" with a one-line summary and a link to the report.\n150\t2. Add an entry to `CHANGELOG.md` under the next release.\n151\t3. Publish a short summary on the project's public channels referencing this directory.\n152\t4. Ensure no remediation PR is left in draft state.\n153\t\n154\t---\n155\t\n156\t## 4. Bookkeeping Templates\n157\t\n158\tThe two structured fields below are reused across every engagement's `STATUS.md`. Copy them as-is and fill in.\n159\t\n160\t### 4.1 Findings ledger row\n161\t\n162\t```markdown\n163\t| <finding-id> | <severity> | <one-line title> | <github-issue> | <pr> | <status> | <notes> |\n164\t```\n165\t\n166\t`<status>` values: `triage`, `in-progress`, `merged`, `re-verified`, `accepted`, `wont-fix-with-rationale`.\n167\t\n168\t### 4.2 Accepted-risk row\n169\t\n170\t```markdown\n171\t| <finding-id> | <severity> | <rationale> | <compensating-control> | <sign-off> | <date> |\n172\t```\n173\t\n174\t---\n175\t\n176\t## 5. Communication Channels\n177\t\n178\t- **Auditor ↔ Maintainers:** private channel agreed at engagement kickoff (recorded in `STATUS.md`).\n179\t- **Internal triage:** GitHub issues labelled `audit:<ID>`.\n180\t- **Public communication:** delayed until §3.6 disclosure, except for already-public information already disclosed by the auditor.\n181\t\n182\tOut-of-band advisories (responsible-disclosure reports outside an engagement) follow the same workflow starting from §3.2, with §3.1 replaced by saving the advisory to `docs/security/audits/_advisories/<date>-<short>.md`.\n183\t\n184\t---\n185\t\n186\t## 6. Open a pull request with the description fields below:\n\n```markdown\n## Audit Finding\nEngagement: <A1 / A2 / …>\nFinding ID: <auditor-assigned ID>\nSeverity: <Critical / High / Medium / Low / Informational>\nAuditor recommendation: <one line>\n\n## Fix Summary\n<what changed and why>\n\n## Verification\n- [ ] Reproducing test added (link)\n- [ ] Full suite passes\n- [ ] Invariant tests (I1–I7) unchanged or strengthened\n- [ ] No changes to public ABI without coordinator sign-off\n```\n\n5. Request review from the maintainer named in the engagement's `STATUS.md`.\n6. After merge, append the merge commit to the finding row in `STATUS.md`.\n\n### 3.4 Findings That Will Not Be Remediated\n\nWhen a finding is accepted as residual risk:\n\n1. Record the acceptance in `audits/<ID>/STATUS.md` §\"Accepted risks\" with:\n   - Finding ID\n   - Severity\n   - Justification (technical + business)\n   - Compensating control\n   - Sign-off (maintainer GitHub handle + date)\n2. Mirror the entry into `docs/audit-notes.md`.\n3. Inform the auditor; request explicit acknowledgement in the re-verification letter.\n\nHigh-severity findings may only be accepted with maintainer + at least one independent reviewer sign-off recorded in the table.\n\n### 3.5 Re-verification\n\nAfter all remediation PRs are merged:\n\n1. Tag the remediation head commit (`audit-<ID>-remediation-v<N>`).\n2. Provide the auditor with:\n   - The tag\n   - A diff against the audited commit\n   - Test results\n3. Receive the auditor's re-verification letter. Save it under `audits/<ID>/reverification-v<N>.pdf`.\n4. Flip the engagement status in `STATUS.md` and `README.md` §3 to `COMPLETED` (or `ACCEPTED WITH RISKS` if any High items were accepted).\n\n### 3.6 Disclosure\n\nWithin 14 days of re-verification:\n\n1. Update `docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md` §\"Audit completion status\" with a one-line summary and a link to the report.\n2. Add an entry to `CHANGELOG.md` under the next release.\n3. Publish a short summary on the project's public channels referencing this directory.\n4. Ensure no remediation PR is left in draft state.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Bookkeeping Templates\n\nThe two structured fields below are reused across every engagement's `STATUS.md`. Copy them as-is and fill in.\n\n### 4.1 Findings ledger row\n\n```markdown\n| <finding-id> | <severity> | <one-line title> | <github-issue> | <pr> | <status> | <notes> |\n```\n\n`<status>` values: `triage`, `in-progress`, `merged`, `re-verified`, `accepted`, `wont-fix-with-rationale`.\n\n### 4.2 Accepted-risk row\n\n```markdown\n| <finding-id> | <severity> | <rationale> | <compensating-control> | <sign-off> | <date> |\n```\n\n---\n\n## 5. Communication Channels\n\n- **Auditor ↔ Maintainers:** private channel agreed at engagement kickoff (recorded in `STATUS.md`).\n- **Internal triage:** GitHub issues labelled `audit:<ID>`.\n- **Public communication:** delayed until §3.6 disclosure, except for already-public information already disclosed by the auditor.\n\nOut-of-band advisories (responsible-disclosure reports outside an engagement) follow the same workflow starting from §3.2, with §3.1 replaced by saving the advisory to `docs/security/audits/_advisories/<date>-<short>.md`.\n\n---\n\n## 6.    [solve worker-1]       "content": "---\nname: \"[A5] Bug Bounty Program\"\nabout: Set up a public bug bounty program (Immunefi or HackenProof) for the protocol\nlabels: type:security\ntrack: A\npriority: medium\n---\n\n## 1. Goal\n\nLaunch a public bug bounty program on Immunefi or HackenProof to enable the security research community to responsibly disclose vulnerabilities in the protocol. This provides continuous security coverage beyond point-in-time audits.\n\n## 2. Context\n\nThe protocol already has a responsible disclosure framework in `SECURITY.md`. A formal bug bounty program extends this by providing financial incentives for researchers, a standardized submission process, and public transparency about the scope and rewards.\n\nThis should be launched **after** A1 and A2 audits are complete and known issues have been remediated — to avoid rewarding researchers for findings the team is already aware of.\n\nRelated to: [DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md — Track A, A5](../TEMP/DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md)\n\n## 3. In Scope\n\n### Bounty Scope\n**Highest Severity (smart contracts)**:\n- `contracts/payments/PaymentHub.tact`\n- `contracts/MerchantPaymentHub.tact`\n- `contracts/payments/account-locks.fc`\n- `contracts/nft-resolver/`\n- `contracts/CrossChainBridge.tact` (after A2 audit)\n- `contracts/MultiSigCard.tact` (after A2 audit)\n\n**Medium Severity (off-chain services)**:\n- `api/` (Merchant API)\n- `backend/indexer/`\n- `sdk/` (npm package, client-side widget)\n\n**Lower Severity (frontend)**:\n- `wallet-ui/`\n- `dashboard/`\n\n## 4. Out of Scope\n\n- Theoretical vulnerabilities without a proof-of-concept\n- Issues in third-party dependencies (ChangeNOW, NOWPayments, CoinRabbit) — report to those vendors\n- Social engineering attacks against team members\n- Physical security\n- Denial of service via flooding (unless causing fund loss)\n\n## 5. Functional Requirements\n\n1. Select a bug bounty platform: Immunefi (preferred for DeFi) or HackenProof\n2. Define reward tiers:\n\n| Severity | Smart Contract | Off-Chain Service |\n|----------|---------------|-------------------|\n| Critical | $10,000+ | $5,000 |\n| High | $5,000 | $2,500 |\n| Medium | $1,000 | $500 |\n| Low | $100 | $100 |\n\n3. Program terms must include:\n   - 90-day fix window for critical/high before public disclosure\n   - Researcher is prohibited from exploiting vulnerabilities in production\n   - Good faith testing on testnet only\n\n4. Response SLA:\n   - Initial triage: 3 business days\n   - Severity classification: 7 business days\n   - Payment: within 30 days of fix deployment\n\n## 6. Non-Functional Requirements\n\n- Program page must be publicly accessible and link from `SECURITY.md`\n- All submissions handled via the bounty platform (not email) for transparency\n- Public statistics: number of reports, resolved, paid — updated quarterly\n\n## 7. Security Requirements\n\n- Audits A1 and A2 must be complete before program launch to avoid paying for known issues\n- Program must explicitly prohibit live mainnet exploitation (testnet testing only)\n- Researcher submissions must not include private keys or wallet credentials\n\n## 8. Acceptance Criteria\n\n- [ ] A1 and A2 audits completed (prerequisite)\n- [ ] Bug bounty platform account created and verified\n- [ ] Program brief published on platform with full scope and reward tiers\n- [ ] `SECURITY.md` updated with link to bug bounty program page\n- [ ] First quarterly transparency report published (including bounty program statistics)\n- [ ] At least one dry-run internal submission tested through the process\n\n## 9. References\n\n- [SECURITY.md](../SECURITY.md)\n- [Threat Model](../docs/security/THREAT_MODEL.md)\n- Immunefi: https://immunefi.com\n- HackenProof: https://hackenproof.com\n- Issue A1: [A1-formal-security-audit-core-contracts.md](./A1-formal-security-audit-core-contracts.md)\n- Issue A2: [A2-formal-security-audit-phase4-contracts.md](./A2-formal-security-audit-phase4-contracts.md)\n",
