   [solve worker-1]           "content": "# A5 Bug Bounty — Severity Rubric\n\n**Document Type:** Severity Classification Rubric\n**Engagement:** [A5](./ENGAGEMENT.md) · [Issue #116](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/116)\n**Status:** Active (applies on program launch)\n**Last Updated:** 2026-05-16\n\n---\n\n## 1. Purpose\n\nThis rubric tells researchers (and the triage team) how a submission is classified into one of `Critical / High / Medium / Low / Informational` for reward purposes. It bridges:\n\n- the protocol-internal severity scale already used by audit findings ([`../REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md`](../REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md) §2),\n- the protocol's seven formal invariants `I1`–`I7` ([`audit/INVARIANTS.md`](../../../../audit/INVARIANTS.md)),\n- the Immunefi Vulnerability Severity Classification System v2.3 (https://immunefi.com/immunefi-vulnerability-severity-classification-system-v2-3/).\n\nA researcher's proposed severity is taken as input. Final classification is made by the triage owner recorded in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §1.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Rubric\n\n### 2.1 🔴 Critical\n\nA vulnerability that **directly** violates one of `I1` (Non-Custodial), `I2` (NFT = Account Authority), `I3` (No Admin Fund Control), `I4` (Atomic Transfers), `I5` (Ledger Conservation), or causes catastrophic loss of merchant funds at scale.\n\nHallmarks:\n\n- Direct theft of user funds without prior interaction or social engineering.\n- Permanent freezing of user funds in `PaymentHub` / `MerchantPaymentHub` accounts (cannot be unlocked by NFT owner).\n- Mint / burn of unbacked balance state in the on-chain ledger (`I5` Ledger Conservation break).\n- Any admin / operator / external-adapter path that moves user funds without the on-chain NFT owner's signature (`I3` break).\n- Full compromise of the npm package supply chain that ships executable code to widget consumers.\n- Compromise of the indexer that allows fabricating confirmed-payment status for unsettled invoices at scale.\n\nReward bands (per [`PROGRAM_BRIEF.md`](./PROGRAM_BRIEF.md) §2.1):\n\n- **Smart contract:** $10,000+ (open-ended; uplift requires sign-off per [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §10)\n- **Off-chain:** $5,000\n- **Frontend:** escalated to off-chain or smart-contract per impact\n\nWorked examples (illustrative; not exhaustive):\n\n- A `MerchantPaymentHub` message handler accepts a payer that is not the current NFT owner and routes funds to attacker-controlled address → `I1` + `I2` break, Critical.\n- An `account-locks.fc` path mutates balance during lock change → `I6` (Lock ≠ Confiscation) + `I5` (Ledger Conservation) break, Critical.\n- A bridge or lending adapter (post-A2) invokes `executeTransfer` directly without going through the protocol's authorisation path → `I7` (External Adapter Isolation) break, Critical.\n- An npm post-install script in a transitive `sdk/` dependency overrides the published widget bundle → supply-chain Critical.\n\n### 2.2 🟠 High\n\nA vulnerability that violates `I6` (Lock ≠ Confiscation), `I7` (External Adapter Isolation), enables privilege escalation, or makes a Critical-class break feasible under realistic preconditions.\n\nHallmarks:\n\n- Cross-merchant IDOR on `api/` invoice endpoints that exposes settlement data without authorisation.\n- Webhook replay that allows double-credit of a payment in a merchant's bookkeeping (post-D4, replay must be infeasible — any working replay PoC against the post-D4 surface is High at minimum).\n- Bypass of `risk_authority` scoping — e.g., an attacker can set `FRAUD_LOCK` without authority key but cannot drain (so not Critical) yet can deny service.\n- API-key derivation that lets an attacker mint valid keys for arbitrary merchants.\n- Auth bypass on indexer admin endpoints (if any are added in the future).\n\nReward bands:\n\n- **Smart contract:** $5,000\n- **Off-chain:** $2,500\n- **Frontend:** escalated to off-chain per impact\n\nWorked examples:\n\n- `account-locks.fc` allows `lending_adapter` to clear `FRAUD_LOCK` set by `risk_authority` → privilege escalation, High.\n- Idempotency-key prediction in `api/src/utils/helpers.ts` lets a researcher overwrite another merchant's pending invoice → High.\n- Widget DOM renders `description` field with `innerHTML` allowing reflected XSS on the merchant-controlled domain → High.\n\n### 2.3 🟡 Medium\n\nA bug or deviation that produces incorrect behaviour without direct fund loss or invariant violation.\n\nHallmarks:\n\n- Indexer mis-categorises a payment as `pending` indefinitely under a specific edge case.\n- Rate-limit bypass that exhausts a single merchant's quota but does not affect others.\n- Information leak that exposes non-sensitive operational data (e.g., internal queue lengths).\n- Frontend wallet UI rendering bug that hides a balance under specific theme + locale combinations.\n\nReward bands:\n\n- **Smart contract:** $1,000\n- **Off-chain:** $500\n- **Frontend:** $500\n\nWorked examples:\n\n- `backend/indexer/` keyset pagination cursor encoding leaks an internal row identifier (no cross-account leak) → Medium.\n- Merchant API returns 500 on a malformed but parseable input that should be 400 (denial of service of a single endpoint, recoverable) → Medium.\n- Dashboard misrenders a settled payment as pending under a particular locale → Medium.\n\n### 2.4 🟢 Low\n\nStyle, hardening, or low-impact defensive issue. Pays a flat tier per [`PROGRAM_BRIEF.md`](./PROGRAM_BRIEF.md) §2.1.\n\nHallmarks:\n\n- Missing security header on a non-credentialed endpoint.\n- Dependency-pinning suggestion not amounting to an exploitable supply-chain risk.\n- Wallet-UI accessibility issue with a security read (e.g., focus state hidden in dark theme).\n\nReward bands:\n\n- **Smart contract:** $100\n- **Off-chain:** $100\n- **Frontend:** $100\n\n### 2.5 ℹ️ Informational\n\nNotes, suggestions, or design observations without security impact. Not eligible for reward but credited in the quarterly transparency report.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Decision Process\n\nFor every submission:\n\n1. **Identify affected invariants.** Map the vulnerability to `I1`–`I7` using [`audit/INVARIANTS.md`](../../../../audit/INVARIANTS.md). A direct break of `I1`, `I2`, `I3`, `I4`, or `I5` floors the severity at **Critical**.\n2. **Map to threat class.** Use the protocol threat model [`audit/THREAT_MODEL.md`](../../../../audit/THREAT_MODEL.md) (T1–T8) to anchor the attacker model.\n3. **Identify the attacker capability and preconditions.** A vulnerability that requires the attacker to control a privileged role is typically downgraded one band; a vulnerability that requires only an unprivileged researcher is at its full band.\n4. **Apply the Immunefi rubric.** Cross-check the candidate severity against the Immunefi v2.3 scale; pick the higher of the two assessments.\n5. **Record the decision in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §6** with the finding ID, the invariant(s) referenced, the threat class(es), and the rationale.\n\nWhen the team and the researcher disagree on severity, the team's decision is final but is **always** accompanied by a written rationale recorded in the finding row.\n\n### 3.1 Floors and Ceilings\n\n| Condition | Floor |\n|-----------|-------|\n| Direct break of `I1` Non-Custodial or `I3` No Admin Fund Control | Critical |\n| Direct break of `I4` Atomic Transfers or `I5` Ledger Conservation | Critical |\n| Break of `I6` Lock ≠ Confiscation or `I7` External Adapter Isolation | High |\n| Cross-merchant IDOR with PII or settlement-state leak | High |\n| Webhook replay against post-D4 HMAC-SHA256 surface | High |\n\n| Condition | Ceiling |\n|-----------|---------|\n| Theoretical issue with no working PoC | Out of scope (no reward) — per [`PROGRAM_BRIEF.md`](./PROGRAM_BRIEF.md) §3.4 |\n| Self-XSS or attack requiring full prior browser control | Low (only if a defensive note remains useful) |\n| Volumetric DoS without invariant violation | Out of scope |\n| Vulnerability in third-party service (ChangeNOW, NOWPayments, CoinRabbit, TONCO, TON HTTP API) | Out of scope |\n\n---\n\n## 4.    [solve worker-1]     "content": "# A5 Bug Bounty — Severity Rubric\n\n**Document Type:** Severity Classification Rubric\n**Engagement:** [A5](./ENGAGEMENT.md) · [Issue #116](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/116)\n**Status:** Active (applies on program launch)\n**Last Updated:** 2026-05-16\n\n---\n\n## 1. Purpose\n\nThis rubric tells researchers (and the triage team) how a submission is classified into one of `Critical / High / Medium / Low / Informational` for reward purposes. It bridges:\n\n- the protocol-internal severity scale already used by audit findings ([`../REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md`](../REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md) §2),\n- the protocol's seven formal invariants `I1`–`I7` ([`audit/INVARIANTS.md`](../../../../audit/INVARIANTS.md)),\n- the Immunefi Vulnerability Severity Classification System v2.3 (https://immunefi.com/immunefi-vulnerability-severity-classification-system-v2-3/).\n\nA researcher's proposed severity is taken as input. Final classification is made by the triage owner recorded in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §1.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Rubric\n\n### 2.1 🔴 Critical\n\nA vulnerability that **directly** violates one of `I1` (Non-Custodial), `I2` (NFT = Account Authority), `I3` (No Admin Fund Control), `I4` (Atomic Transfers), `I5` (Ledger Conservation), or causes catastrophic loss of merchant funds at scale.\n\nHallmarks:\n\n- Direct theft of user funds without prior interaction or social engineering.\n- Permanent freezing of user funds in `PaymentHub` / `MerchantPaymentHub` accounts (cannot be unlocked by NFT owner).\n- Mint / burn of unbacked balance state in the on-chain ledger (`I5` Ledger Conservation break).\n- Any admin / operator / external-adapter path that moves user funds without the on-chain NFT owner's signature (`I3` break).\n- Full compromise of the npm package supply chain that ships executable code to widget consumers.\n- Compromise of the indexer that allows fabricating confirmed-payment status for unsettled invoices at scale.\n\nReward bands (per [`PROGRAM_BRIEF.md`](./PROGRAM_BRIEF.md) §2.1):\n\n- **Smart contract:** $10,000+ (open-ended; uplift requires sign-off per [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §10)\n- **Off-chain:** $5,000\n- **Frontend:** escalated to off-chain or smart-contract per impact\n\nWorked examples (illustrative; not exhaustive):\n\n- A `MerchantPaymentHub` message handler accepts a payer that is not the current NFT owner and routes funds to attacker-controlled address → `I1` + `I2` break, Critical.\n- An `account-locks.fc` path mutates balance during lock change → `I6` (Lock ≠ Confiscation) + `I5` (Ledger Conservation) break, Critical.\n- A bridge or lending adapter (post-A2) invokes `executeTransfer` directly without going through the protocol's authorisation path → `I7` (External Adapter Isolation) break, Critical.\n- An npm post-install script in a transitive `sdk/` dependency overrides the published widget bundle → supply-chain Critical.\n\n### 2.2 🟠 High\n\nA vulnerability that violates `I6` (Lock ≠ Confiscation), `I7` (External Adapter Isolation), enables privilege escalation, or makes a Critical-class break feasible under realistic preconditions.\n\nHallmarks:\n\n- Cross-merchant IDOR on `api/` invoice endpoints that exposes settlement data without authorisation.\n- Webhook replay that allows double-credit of a payment in a merchant's bookkeeping (post-D4, replay must be infeasible — any working replay PoC against the post-D4 surface is High at minimum).\n- Bypass of `risk_authority` scoping — e.g., an attacker can set `FRAUD_LOCK` without authority key but cannot drain (so not Critical) yet can deny service.\n- API-key derivation that lets an attacker mint valid keys for arbitrary merchants.\n- Auth bypass on indexer admin endpoints (if any are added in the future).\n\nReward bands:\n\n- **Smart contract:** $5,000\n- **Off-chain:** $2,500\n- **Frontend:** escalated to off-chain per impact\n\nWorked examples:\n\n- `account-locks.fc` allows `lending_adapter` to clear `FRAUD_LOCK` set by `risk_authority` → privilege escalation, High.\n- Idempotency-key prediction in `api/src/utils/helpers.ts` lets a researcher overwrite another merchant's pending invoice → High.\n- Widget DOM renders `description` field with `innerHTML` allowing reflected XSS on the merchant-controlled domain → High.\n\n### 2.3 🟡 Medium\n\nA bug or deviation that produces incorrect behaviour without direct fund loss or invariant violation.\n\nHallmarks:\n\n- Indexer mis-categorises a payment as `pending` indefinitely under a specific edge case.\n- Rate-limit bypass that exhausts a single merchant's quota but does not affect others.\n- Information leak that exposes non-sensitive operational data (e.g., internal queue lengths).\n- Frontend wallet UI rendering bug that hides a balance under specific theme + locale combinations.\n\nReward bands:\n\n- **Smart contract:** $1,000\n- **Off-chain:** $500\n- **Frontend:** $500\n\nWorked examples:\n\n- `backend/indexer/` keyset pagination cursor encoding leaks an internal row identifier (no cross-account leak) → Medium.\n- Merchant API returns 500 on a malformed but parseable input that should be 400 (denial of service of a single endpoint, recoverable) → Medium.\n- Dashboard misrenders a settled payment as pending under a particular locale → Medium.\n\n### 2.4 🟢 Low\n\nStyle, hardening, or low-impact defensive issue. Pays a flat tier per [`PROGRAM_BRIEF.md`](./PROGRAM_BRIEF.md) §2.1.\n\nHallmarks:\n\n- Missing security header on a non-credentialed endpoint.\n- Dependency-pinning suggestion not amounting to an exploitable supply-chain risk.\n- Wallet-UI accessibility issue with a security read (e.g., focus state hidden in dark theme).\n\nReward bands:\n\n- **Smart contract:** $100\n- **Off-chain:** $100\n- **Frontend:** $100\n\n### 2.5 ℹ️ Informational\n\nNotes, suggestions, or design observations without security impact. Not eligible for reward but credited in the quarterly transparency report.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Purpose\n\nThis template is the canonical source for the quarterly public transparency report mandated by [`PROGRAM_BRIEF.md`](./PROGRAM_BRIEF.md) §8 and acceptance criterion #5 of [Issue #116](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/116). A new report is produced every calendar quarter while the program is active, stored at `docs/security/audits/A5-bug-bounty/reports/YYYY-Qn.md`, and linked from the root [`SECURITY.md`](../../../../SECURITY.md) and the program page on the chosen platform.\n\nHow to use:\n\n1. Replace every `<…>` placeholder with the actual value from [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §6 (findings ledger) and §7 (SLA tracker).\n3. Remove §10 (Internal Editor Notes) before publishing.\n4. Open a PR titled `docs(security): A5 quarterly report <YYYY-Qn>` and request review from the maintainers listed in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §1.\n\nIf a figure cannot be disclosed in the public report (e.g., undisclosed Critical finding still within the 90-day fix window), record `redacted (see §<n>)` and add a short rationale in §9.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Executive Summary\n\nOne to three sentences covering:\n\n- whether the program operated normally during the window,\n- the number of confirmed valid findings paid out,\n- the total payout in USDC,\n- any notable trend (e.g., spike in `sdk/` submissions following a release).\n\nExample:\n\n> \"Between <YYYY-MM-DD> and <YYYY-MM-DD>, the A5 bug bounty program received `<n>` submissions, of which `<k>` were valid and resulted in a total payout of `<X>` USDC. No Critical findings were confirmed during the window. All SLAs were met.\"\n\n---\n\n## 4. Submission Counters\n\nNumbers are sourced from [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §6 (findings ledger) for the reporting window only.\n\n| Metric | Count |\n|--------|-------|\n| Submissions received | `<n>` |\n| Out-of-scope | `<n>` |\n| Duplicate | `<n>` |\n| Confirmed valid — Critical | `<n>` |\n| Confirmed valid — High | `<n>` |\n| Confirmed valid — Medium | `<n>` |\n| Confirmed valid — Low | `<n>` |\n| Informational (credited only) | `<n>` |\n| Withdrawn / closed by researcher | `<n>` |\n| **Total confirmed valid (Critical + High + Medium + Low)** | `<n>` |\n\nNotes:\n\n- \"Confirmed valid\" means triage assigned a non-Informational severity per [`SEVERITY_RUBRIC.md`](./SEVERITY_RUBRIC.md). Disagreements with the researcher about severity are resolved by the team per [`SEVERITY_RUBRIC.md`](./SEVERITY_RUBRIC.md) §3 and reflected in this count.\n- A submission that was valid but unpaid because of policy (e.g., self-XSS or third-party vendor scope per [`PROGRAM_BRIEF.md`](./PROGRAM_BRIEF.md) §3.4) is counted under \"Out-of-scope\" with a footnote.\n\n---\n\n## 5.    [solve worker-1]           "content": "# A5 Bug Bounty — Dry-Run Plan\n\n**Document Type:** Internal Dry-Run / Soft-Launch Plan\n**Engagement:** [A5](./ENGAGEMENT.md) · [Issue #116](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/116)\n**Status:** Active (executed before public launch)\n**Last Updated:** 2026-05-16\n\n---\n\n## 1. Purpose\n\nThe dry-run validates the **submission, triage, payout, and disclosure pipeline** before the program goes public. It satisfies acceptance criterion #6 of [Issue #116](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/116): *\"Dry-run submission tested through the platform.\"*\n\nThe dry-run is an **end-to-end rehearsal**, not a real bug report. Its goal is to exercise every SLA clock, every reporting field, every payout-disbursement step, and every public-disclosure artifact at least once on real infrastructure, with no public exposure of the program.\n\nThe dry-run must complete with no `Critical` or `High` open issues against itself, and the platform program page must remain in `private` / `unlisted` mode throughout (per [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §3 checklist row \"Dry-run executed\").\n\n---\n\n## 2. Preconditions\n\nThe dry-run cannot start until **all** of the following are true. The check is recorded in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §3.\n\n| Precondition | Source of truth | Required state |\n|--------------|-----------------|----------------|\n| A1 audit closed | [`audits/A1-core-contracts/STATUS.md`](../A1-core-contracts/STATUS.md) | `Gating Decision: pass` |\n| A2 audit closed | [`audits/A2-external-adapters/STATUS.md`](../A2-external-adapters/STATUS.md) | `Gating Decision: pass` |\n| Platform vendor selected | [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §4 | `decided` |\n| Platform account created (private) | [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §3 | `done` |\n| [`PROGRAM_BRIEF.md`](./PROGRAM_BRIEF.md) uploaded to platform draft | [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §9 | `done` (with SHA-256) |\n| [`SEVERITY_RUBRIC.md`](./SEVERITY_RUBRIC.md) referenced in platform brief | [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §9 | `done` |\n| Triage owner assigned (24/7 escalation contact) | [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §1 | `name + paging method` |\n| Payout treasury funded with at least 1× Critical (smart contract) reward | [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §11 | `funded` |\n| KYC / sanctions screening flow tested with at least one mock researcher identity | [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §11 | `tested` |\n| Webhook receiver for platform → internal ticket system online | [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §3 | `online` |\n| `reports/` directory exists with [`QUARTERLY_REPORT_TEMPLATE.md`](./QUARTERLY_REPORT_TEMPLATE.md) committed | this repo | `done` |\n\nIf any row is not `done`, the dry-run is **blocked** and a row is added to [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §12 (open questions) describing the blocker.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Roles for the Rehearsal\n\nThe dry-run is staffed exclusively by internal participants. No external researcher is involved.\n\n| Role | Responsibility | Performed by |\n|------|----------------|--------------|\n| Synthetic researcher | Files the rehearsal report on the platform under a dedicated test account; never uses a real-world handle | Security maintainer (rotates per quarter) |\n| Triage owner | Receives the platform notification, acknowledges within the §5.3 SLA, classifies severity | Triage owner of record ([`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §1) |\n| Reviewer | Validates the proposed severity, signs off on payout amount | Second maintainer |\n| Treasury | Disburses the rehearsal payout to a wallet controlled by the security team | Treasury operator ([`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §1) |\n| Observer | Records timing, evidence, and findings against the rehearsal itself | Engineering manager |\n\nThe synthetic researcher and the triage owner **must** be different people, so the SLA clock and the platform notification path are exercised end-to-end.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Scenarios\n\nFour scenarios are required for a passing dry-run. Each scenario exercises a different code path. All four can run in parallel on the platform after the first acknowledgement clock is verified.\n\n### 4.1 Scenario S1 — Valid Critical (smart contract)\n\n- **Synthetic finding:** a pre-staged invariant break in a private test branch (never merged) that maps to `I5` Ledger Conservation. The PoC is a transaction trace on local sandbox; no testnet deployment.\n- **Expected severity:** 🔴 Critical (smart contract).\n- **Expected payout band:** $10,000 baseline, no uplift.\n- **Validates:** Critical acknowledgement SLA, Critical severity floor in [`SEVERITY_RUBRIC.md`](./SEVERITY_RUBRIC.md) §3.1, treasury disbursement of the largest baseline reward, coordinated-disclosure window calculation.\n\n### 4.2 Scenario S2 — Valid High (off-chain)\n\n- **Synthetic finding:** a fabricated cross-merchant IDOR PoC against a staging copy of `api/` that exposes one merchant's invoice list to another merchant's API key.\n- **Expected severity:** 🟠 High (off-chain).\n- **Expected payout band:** $2,500.\n- **Validates:** off-chain severity classification, post-D4 webhook-replay reasoning if applicable, payout in non-Critical band.\n\n### 4.3 Scenario S3 — Duplicate\n\n- **Synthetic finding:** the same `I5` PoC from S1 filed by the synthetic researcher under a second platform account, after S1 has been triaged but before it is publicly disclosed.\n- **Expected outcome:** marked `Duplicate` per [`PROGRAM_BRIEF.md`](./PROGRAM_BRIEF.md) §5.5; not eligible for payout; counted under §4 of [`QUARTERLY_REPORT_TEMPLATE.md`](./QUARTERLY_REPORT_TEMPLATE.md) \"Duplicate\".\n- **Validates:** duplicate-detection policy, researcher-facing communication template, counter reconciliation in the quarterly report.\n\n### 4.4 Scenario S4 — Out-of-scope\n\n- **Synthetic finding:** a volumetric DoS against the public health endpoint, filed with no invariant impact and no fund-loss path.\n- **Expected outcome:** marked `Out-of-scope` per [`PROGRAM_BRIEF.md`](./PROGRAM_BRIEF.md) §3.4; not eligible for payout; counted under §4 of [`QUARTERLY_REPORT_TEMPLATE.md`](./QUARTERLY_REPORT_TEMPLATE.md) \"Out-of-scope\".\n- **Validates:** out-of-scope rejection template, researcher-facing tone (no penalty for filing in good faith), counter reconciliation.\n\n### 4.5 Optional Scenario S5 — Researcher-team severity disagreement\n\nIf time and people allow, run a fifth scenario where the synthetic researcher proposes 🔴 Critical for a finding the team rates 🟠 High. This exercises the `team's decision is final but accompanied by written rationale` clause in [`SEVERITY_RUBRIC.md`](./SEVERITY_RUBRIC.md) §3. Skipping S5 is acceptable; it must then be verified in the first real submission post-launch.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Timeline\n\nThe dry-run is designed to complete in **two business weeks** end-to-end. Day numbering starts when the first synthetic report is filed.\n\n| Day | Activity | Owner | Output |\n|-----|----------|-------|--------|\n| D-3 | Final go/no-go review against §2 preconditions | Triage owner | Row updated in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §3 |\n| D0 morning | Synthetic researcher files S1 | Synthetic researcher | Platform submission ID logged |\n| D0 evening | Triage owner acknowledges S1 | Triage owner | Acknowledge timestamp logged |\n| D1 | Triage owner files S2, S4 in parallel | Synthetic researcher / triage owner | Two more submission IDs logged |\n| D2 | Severity classification for S1 published to platform | Triage owner + reviewer | Severity decision recorded per [`SEVERITY_RUBRIC.md`](./SEVERITY_RUBRIC.md) §3 |\n| D3 | S3 (duplicate) filed | Synthetic researcher | Duplicate detection exercised |\n| D4 | Severity decisions for S2, S3, S4 published | Triage owner + reviewer | All four severity decisions on record |\n| D5–D7 | Internal \"fix\" simulated (the synthetic findings target staging only — no real code change is merged) | Engineering | Fix simulated and recorded |\n| D8 | Payout disbursement for S1 and S2 to security-team-controlled wallet | Treasury | On-chain payout tx hashes recorded |\n| D9 | Coordinated-disclosure timing verified (90-day clock would start; for the dry-run, we explicitly do not publish) | Triage owner | Disclosure clock test recorded |\n| D10 | Dry-run quarterly-report draft produced from [`QUARTERLY_REPORT_TEMPLATE.md`](./QUARTERLY_REPORT_TEMPLATE.md) using S1–S4 data | Report author | Draft committed to `reports/dry-run-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md` |\n| D11–D12 | Post-mortem against §6 exit criteria | All roles | Decision logged in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §3 |\n\nIf the dry-run cannot complete within two weeks because of a blocker found mid-rehearsal, **pause** the dry-run, fix the blocker, and restart from D0. Do not extend the timeline silently — a row must be added to [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §12.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Exit Criteria\n\nThe dry-run is `pass` only when **all** of the following hold:\n\n- All four required scenarios (S1–S4) ran end-to-end with no manual workaround outside the documented process.\n- Every SLA in [`PROGRAM_BRIEF.md`](./PROGRAM_BRIEF.md) §5.3 was met for S1 and S2 (acknowledgement, severity classification, payout).\n- The treasury disbursement for S1 and S2 settled on-chain within the SLA window and was reconciled against the platform's payout log.\n- The quarterly-report draft produced on D10 reconciles row-for-row against [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §6 (findings ledger) and §7 (SLA tracker).\n- No finding against the dry-run **itself** is rated 🔴 Critical or 🟠 High in the post-mortem.\n- The platform program page remained `private` / `unlisted` throughout. No external researcher viewed it.\n\nAny failure on a single criterion blocks the public launch. The remediation is recorded in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §12 (open questions) with a target re-run date.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Cleanup\n\nWithin five business days after exit criteria are met:\n\n- Close all four synthetic platform submissions as `dry-run, no real impact`. Do not delete them — the platform's audit log of the rehearsal is the durable evidence.\n- Return the dry-run payout balances from the security-team-controlled wallet to the program treasury. Record on-chain reversal tx hashes in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §3.\n- Commit the dry-run quarterly-report draft to `reports/dry-run-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md` for historical reference. The first **public** quarterly report (per [`QUARTERLY_REPORT_TEMPLATE.md`](./QUARTERLY_REPORT_TEMPLATE.md)) is produced separately at the end of the first calendar quarter post-launch.\n- File a `docs(security): A5 dry-run report <date>` PR linking: the four platform submission IDs, the post-mortem notes, and the row update in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §3 checklist.\n- Schedule the public launch per [`ENGAGEMENT.md`](./ENGAGEMENT.md) §7 only after this PR is merged.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Post-Launch Re-Run Triggers\n\nA dry-run is repeated (in whole or in part) whenever any of the following occur after the public launch:\n\n- The triage owner of record in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §1 changes.\n- A new component is added to scope per [`PROGRAM_BRIEF.md`](./PROGRAM_BRIEF.md) §3 (run S2 against the new component).\n- The platform vendor changes (full dry-run).\n- A reward band changes by more than 25 % in either direction (run S1 to validate the new Critical disbursement path).\n- An SLA in [`PROGRAM_BRIEF.md`](./PROGRAM_BRIEF.md) §5.3 changes.\n- An audit at A1 or A2 produces a re-issued [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) `Gating Decision`.\n\nEach re-run is recorded in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §13 (change log).\n\n---\n\n## 9. References\n\n- [Engagement plan](./ENGAGEMENT.md) (§7 timeline, §9 acceptance)\n- [Engagement status](./STATUS.md) (§1 parties, §3 launch checklist, §9 artifacts, §11 compliance, §12 open questions, §13 change log)\n- [Program brief](./PROGRAM_BRIEF.md) (§3 scope, §5.3 SLAs, §5.4 disclosure, §5.5 duplicates)\n- [Severity rubric](./SEVERITY_RUBRIC.md)\n- [Quarterly report template](./QUARTERLY_REPORT_TEMPLATE.md)\n- [Remediation workflow](../REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md)\n- [A1 audit status](../A1-core-contracts/STATUS.md)\n- [A2 audit status](../A2-external-adapters/STATUS.md)\n- [Issue #116](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/116)\n"

The PoC is a transaction trace on local sandbox; no testnet deployment.\n- **Expected severity:** 🔴 Critical (smart contract).\n- **Expected payout band:** $10,000 baseline, no uplift.\n- **Validates:** Critical acknowledgement SLA, Critical severity floor in [`SEVERITY_RUBRIC.md`](./SEVERITY_RUBRIC.md) §3.1, treasury disbursement of the largest baseline reward, coordinated-disclosure window calculation.\n\n### 4.2 Scenario S2 — Valid High (off-chain)\n\n- **Synthetic finding:** a fabricated cross-merchant IDOR PoC against a staging copy of `api/` that exposes one merchant's invoice list to another merchant's API key.\n- **Expected severity:** 🟠 High (off-chain).\n- **Expected payout band:** $2,500.\n- **Validates:** off-chain severity classification, post-D4 webhook-replay reasoning if applicable, payout in non-Critical band.\n\n### 4.3 Scenario S3 — Duplicate\n\n- **Synthetic finding:** the same `I5` PoC from S1 filed by the synthetic researcher under a second platform account, after S1 has been triaged but before it is publicly disclosed.\n- **Expected outcome:** marked `Duplicate` per [`PROGRAM_BRIEF.md`](./PROGRAM_BRIEF.md) §5.5; not eligible for payout; counted under §4 of [`QUARTERLY_REPORT_TEMPLATE.md`](./QUARTERLY_REPORT_TEMPLATE.md) \"Duplicate\".\n- **Validates:** duplicate-detection policy, researcher-facing communication template, counter reconciliation in the quarterly report.\n\n### 4.4 Scenario S4 — Out-of-scope\n\n- **Synthetic finding:** a volumetric DoS against the public health endpoint, filed with no invariant impact and no fund-loss path.\n- **Expected outcome:** marked `Out-of-scope` per [`PROGRAM_BRIEF.md`](./PROGRAM_BRIEF.md) §3.4; not eligible for payout; counted under §4 of [`QUARTERLY_REPORT_TEMPLATE.md`](./QUARTERLY_REPORT_TEMPLATE.md) \"Out-of-scope\".\n- **Validates:** out-of-scope rejection template, researcher-facing tone (no penalty for filing in good faith), counter reconciliation.\n\n### 4.5 Optional Scenario S5 — Researcher-team severity disagreement\n\nIf time and people allow, run a fifth scenario where the synthetic researcher proposes 🔴 Critical for a finding the team rates 🟠 High. This exercises the `team's decision is final but accompanied by written rationale` clause in [`SEVERITY_RUBRIC.md`](./SEVERITY_RUBRIC.md) §3. Skipping S5 is acceptable; it must then be verified in the first real submission post-launch.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Timeline\n\nThe dry-run is designed to complete in **two business weeks** end-to-end. Day numbering starts when the first synthetic report is filed.\n\n| Day | Activity | Owner | Output |\n|-----|----------|-------|--------|\n| D-3 | Final go/no-go review against §2 preconditions | Triage owner | Row updated in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §3 |\n| D0 morning | Synthetic researcher files S1 | Synthetic researcher | Platform submission ID logged |\n| D0 evening | Triage owner acknowledges S1 | Triage owner | Acknowledge timestamp logged |\n| D1 | Triage owner files S2, S4 in parallel | Synthetic researcher / triage owner | Two more submission IDs logged |\n| D2 | Severity classification for S1 published to platform | Triage owner + reviewer | Severity decision recorded per [`SEVERITY_RUBRIC.md`](./SEVERITY_RUBRIC.md) §3 |\n| D3 | S3 (duplicate) filed | Synthetic researcher | Duplicate detection exercised |\n| D4 | Severity decisions for S2, S3, S4 published | Triage owner + reviewer | All four severity decisions on record |\n| D5–D7 | Internal \"fix\" simulated (the synthetic findings target staging only — no real code change is merged) | Engineering | Fix simulated and recorded |\n| D8 | Payout disbursement for S1 and S2 to security-team-controlled wallet | Treasury | On-chain payout tx hashes recorded |\n| D9 | Coordinated-disclosure timing verified (90-day clock would start; for the dry-run, we explicitly do not publish) | Triage owner | Disclosure clock test recorded |\n| D10 | Dry-run quarterly-report draft produced from [`QUARTERLY_REPORT_TEMPLATE.md`](./QUARTERLY_REPORT_TEMPLATE.md) using S1–S4 data | Report author | Draft committed to `reports/dry-run-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md` |\n| D11–D12 | Post-mortem against §6 exit criteria | All roles | Decision logged in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §3 |\n\nIf the dry-run cannot complete within two weeks because of a blocker found mid-rehearsal, **pause** the dry-run, fix the blocker, and restart from D0. Do not extend the timeline silently — a row must be added to [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §12.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Exit Criteria\n\nThe dry-run is `pass` only when **all** of the following hold:\n\n- All four required scenarios (S1–S4) ran end-to-end with no manual workaround outside the documented process.\n- Every SLA in [`PROGRAM_BRIEF.md`](./PROGRAM_BRIEF.md) §5.3 was met for S1 and S2 (acknowledgement, severity classification, payout).\n- The treasury disbursement for S1 and S2 settled on-chain within the SLA window and was reconciled against the platform's payout log.\n- The quarterly-report draft produced on D10 reconciles row-for-row against [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §6 (findings ledger) and §7 (SLA tracker).\n- No finding against the dry-run **itself** is rated 🔴 Critical or 🟠 High in the post-mortem.\n- The platform program page remained `private` / `unlisted` throughout. No external researcher viewed it.\n\nAny failure on a single criterion blocks the public launch. The remediation is recorded in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §12 (open questions) with a target re-run date.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Cleanup\n\nWithin five business days after exit criteria are met:\n\n- Close all four synthetic platform submissions as `dry-run, no real impact`. Do not delete them — the platform's audit log of the rehearsal is the durable evidence.\n- Return the dry-run payout balances from the security-team-controlled wallet to the program treasury. Record on-chain reversal tx hashes in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §3.\n- Commit the dry-run quarterly-report draft to `reports/dry-run-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md` for historical reference. The first **public** quarterly report (per [`QUARTERLY_REPORT_TEMPLATE.md`](./QUARTERLY_REPORT_TEMPLATE.md)) is produced separately at the end of the first calendar quarter post-launch.\n- File a `docs(security): A5 dry-run report <date>` PR linking: the four platform submission IDs, the post-mortem notes, and the row update in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §3 checklist.\n- Schedule the public launch per [`ENGAGEMENT.md`](./ENGAGEMENT.md) §7 only after this PR is merged.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Post-Launch Re-Run Triggers\n\nA dry-run is repeated (in whole or in part) whenever any of the following occur after the public launch:\n\n- The triage owner of record in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §1 changes.\n- A new component is added to scope per [`PROGRAM_BRIEF.md`](./PROGRAM_BRIEF.md) §3 (run S2 against the new component).\n- The platform vendor changes (full dry-run).\n- A reward band changes by more than 25 % in either direction (run S1 to validate the new Critical disbursement path).\n- An SLA in [`PROGRAM_BRIEF.md`](./PROGRAM_BRIEF.md) §5.3 changes.\n- An audit at A1 or A2 produces a re-issued [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) `Gating Decision`.\n\nEach re-run is recorded in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §13 (change log).\n\n---\n\n## 9. Disclosure Policy\n\nTONBANKCARD follows a **coordinated disclosure** model:\n\n1. Reporter submits vulnerability via the channel in Section 1\n2. TONBANKCARD acknowledges receipt and opens a private investigation\n3. TONBANKCARD and reporter agree on a disclosure timeline (default: 90 days from acknowledgement)\n4. A patch or mitigation is developed and deployed\n5. Reporter is given a preview of the disclosure and credited (if desired)\n6. A public disclosure is issued after the fix is available\n\n**Early disclosure may occur** if:\n\n- The vulnerability is already being actively exploited\n- A partial fix is available that significantly reduces risk\n\n**Extension of the 90-day timeline** may be requested by either party in writing. Extensions are granted on a case-by-case basis.\n\nIf TONBANKCARD does not respond within the timelines defined in Section 4, reporters may proceed with disclosure at their discretion, having acted in good faith.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Safe Harbor Statement\n\nTONBANKCARD supports responsible security research. If you report a vulnerability in good faith and in accordance with this policy, we will not pursue legal action against you for that research.\n\nGood faith research means:\n\n- You do not access, modify, or exfiltrate data beyond what is necessary to demonstrate the vulnerability\n- You do not disrupt service availability or degrade performance for other users\n- You do not use social engineering techniques against team members or users\n- You report the issue to us before public disclosure\n- You allow reasonable time for a fix before disclosing publicly\n\nThis safe harbor applies to research conducted under these terms. It does not extend to:\n\n- Exploitation of vulnerabilities for personal gain\n- Access to or exfiltration of user data\n- Any activity that violates applicable law\n\nThis statement is not legal advice and does not constitute a legal agreement.    [solve worker-1]     "originalFile": "# TONBANKCARD Protocol — Responsible Disclosure & Vulnerability Reporting Policy\n\n**Document Type:** Security Policy\n**Issue Reference:** [#66 — Issue 10.7 — Responsible Disclosure & Vulnerability Reporting Policy](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/66)\n**Status:** Active\n**Last Updated:** 2026-03-05\n\n---\n\n## Table of Contents\n\n1. [Reporting Channels](#1-reporting-channels)\n2. [Encryption Requirements](#2-encryption-requirements)\n3. [Scope](#3-scope)\n4. [Response Timeline](#4-response-timeline)\n5. [Disclosure Policy](#5-disclosure-policy)\n6. [Safe Harbor Statement](#6-safe-harbor-statement)\n\n---\n\n## Supported Versions\n\n| Version | Status | Security Support |\n|---------|--------|-----------------|\n| v1.0.x | Active | Supported |\n\nEarlier versions and pre-release deployments are not covered by this policy.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Reporting Channels\n\n**DO NOT** disclose security vulnerabilities publicly. Public disclosure before a patch is available puts all users at risk.\n\nThe preferred channel is GitHub's private security advisory feature:\n\n1. Go to the [Security tab](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/security) of this repository\n2. Click **\"Report a vulnerability\"**\n3. Provide a detailed description of the issue\n\nIf you are unable to use GitHub's private advisory feature, report via email:\n\n- **Email:** security@tonbankcard.com\n- **Subject line format:** `[SECURITY] <brief description>`\n- Include a detailed description of the issue, reproduction steps, and potential impact\n\nIf you do not receive an acknowledgement within 72 hours, send a follow-up referencing your original report.\n\n### What to Include\n\nA useful vulnerability report includes:\n\n- Description of the vulnerability and its potential impact\n- Steps to reproduce the issue\n- Affected contract(s) or component(s)\n- Proof of concept or test case, if available\n- Suggested severity (Critical, High, Medium, Low)\n\n---\n\n## 2. Encryption Requirements\n\nFor sensitive vulnerability reports, encrypted submission is strongly preferred.\n\n- **PGP:** Encrypt your report to the TONBANKCARD security team PGP key (key details to be published at `security@tonbankcard.com` upon request)\n- **Plain email** is accepted for low-severity or non-sensitive reports\n- Do not include full exploit code or credential material in unencrypted email\n\nEncryption key details will be provided upon initial contact if not yet published.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Scope\n\n### In Scope\n\nThe following components are in scope for vulnerability reports:\n\n- **Smart contracts:** `PaymentHub`, `MerchantNFT`, and related on-chain contracts in this repository (`contracts/`)\n- **Backend API:** REST endpoints handling invoice creation, settlement verification, and merchant registry (`api/`)\n- **Merchant SDK:** JavaScript/TypeScript SDK published under `@tonbankcard/sdk` (`sdk/`)\n- **Authentication and access control logic:** Key management, role-based access, admin operations\n- **Protocol-level logic:** Settlement finality, reorg handling, invariant violations\n\n### Priority Focus Areas\n\nThe most security-critical areas of this protocol:\n\n- **Fund safety:** any path that could result in unauthorized fund movement\n- **NFT ownership enforcement:** any bypass of the ownership check\n- **Lock bypass:** any path to transfer from a locked account\n- **Admin key misuse:** any undocumented admin capability\n\n### Out of Scope\n\nThe following are not in scope:\n\n- Already-deployed and frozen external contracts (TBC Token Jetton, NFT Collections, TBC Diamonds, TONCO DEX) — these are immutable and separately governed\n- Third-party services (ChangeNOW, NOWPayments, CoinRabbit, TONCO) — report vulnerabilities directly to those providers\n- Vulnerabilities in third-party dependencies unless directly exploitable through TONBANKCARD code\n- TON blockchain infrastructure, validator nodes, or core protocol\n- Reports requiring physical access to infrastructure\n- Social engineering attacks against team members or users\n- Denial-of-service attacks without demonstrated exploit impact\n- Issues in test environments or non-production deployments with no production impact\n- Theoretical vulnerabilities with no demonstrated impact\n\n---\n\n## 4. Response Timeline\n\n| Milestone | Target |\n|-----------|--------|\n| Acknowledgement of receipt | Within 72 hours |\n| Initial severity assessment | Within 7 days |\n| Status update to reporter | Every 14 days until resolved |\n| Patch for critical severity | Within 30 days |\n| Patch for high severity | Within 60 days |\n| Patch for medium/low severity | Within 90 days |\n\n### Fix Timeline by Severity\n\n| Severity | Target Fix Timeline |\n|----------|---------------------|\n| Critical | Within 72 hours for containment; patch within 30 days |\n| High | Within 60 days |\n| Medium | Within 90 days |\n| Low | Next planned release |\n\nThese are target timelines. Complex issues involving on-chain contracts may require additional time due to audit and deployment constraints. Reporters will be kept informed of any delays.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Disclosure Policy\n\nTONBANKCARD follows a **coordinated disclosure** model:\n\n1. Reporter submits vulnerability via the channel in Section 1\n2. TONBANKCARD acknowledges receipt and opens a private investigation\n3. TONBANKCARD and reporter agree on a disclosure timeline (default: 90 days from acknowledgement)\n4. A patch or mitigation is developed and deployed\n5. Reporter is given a preview of the disclosure and credited (if desired)\n6. A public disclosure is issued after the fix is available\n\n**Early disclosure may occur** if:\n\n- The vulnerability is already being actively exploited\n- A partial fix is available that significantly reduces risk\n\n**Extension of the 90-day timeline** may be requested by either party in writing. Extensions are granted on a case-by-case basis.\n\nIf TONBANKCARD does not respond within the timelines defined in Section 4, reporters may proceed with disclosure at their discretion, having acted in good faith.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Safe Harbor Statement\n\nTONBANKCARD supports responsible security research. If you report a vulnerability in good faith and in accordance with this policy, we will not pursue legal action against you for that research.\n\nGood faith research means:\n\n- You do not access, modify, or exfiltrate data beyond what is necessary to demonstrate the vulnerability\n- You do not disrupt service availability or degrade performance for other users\n- You do not use social engineering techniques against team members or users\n- You report the issue to us before public disclosure\n- You allow reasonable time for a fix before disclosing publicly\n\nThis safe harbor applies to research conducted under these terms. It does not extend to:\n\n- Exploitation of vulnerabilities for personal gain\n- Access to or exfiltration of user data\n- Any activity that violates applicable law\n\nThis statement is not legal advice and does not constitute a legal agreement. Researchers are responsible for understanding and complying with all applicable laws.\n\n---\n\n## Non-Custodial Architecture\n\nTONBANKCARD is a **non-custodial protocol**. The architecture enforces that:\n\n- No admin or operator can move user funds\n- No emergency mechanism exists that transfers or seizes funds\n- Account locks restrict outgoing transfers but do not confiscate balances\n\nFor more on the security model, see [docs/security/SECURITY.md](docs/security/SECURITY.md).\n\n---\n\n## Security Documentation\n\nFor the full security framework, see:\n\n- [docs/security/SECURITY.md](docs/security/SECURITY.md) — Security documentation index and unified framework\n- [docs/security/THREAT_MODEL.md](docs/security/THREAT_MODEL.md) — Threat model and security architecture\n- [docs/security/KEY_MANAGEMENT.md](docs/security/KEY_MANAGEMENT.md) — Key management and operational security\n- [docs/security/INCIDENT_RESPONSE.md](docs/security/INCIDENT_RESPONSE.md) — Incident response procedures\n- [docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md](docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md) — Audit readiness status\n\n---\n\n**Security Contact:** security@tonbankcard.com\n",

   [solve worker-1]     "originalFile": "# TONBANKCARD Protocol — Responsible Disclosure & Vulnerability Reporting Policy\n\n**Document Type:** Security Policy\n**Issue Reference:** [#66 — Issue 10.7 — Responsible Disclosure & Vulnerability Reporting Policy](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/66)\n**Status:** Active\n**Last Updated:** 2026-05-16\n\n---\n\n## Table of Contents\n\n1. [Reporting Channels](#1-reporting-channels)\n2. [Encryption Requirements](#2-encryption-requirements)\n3. [Scope](#3-scope)\n4. [Response Timeline](#4-response-timeline)\n5. [Disclosure Policy](#5-disclosure-policy)\n6. [Safe Harbor Statement](#6-safe-harbor-statement)\n\n---\n\n## Supported Versions\n\n| Version | Status | Security Support |\n|---------|--------|-----------------|\n| v1.0.x | Active | Supported |\n\nEarlier versions and pre-release deployments are not covered by this policy.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Reporting Channels\n\n**DO NOT** disclose security vulnerabilities publicly. Public disclosure before a patch is available puts all users at risk.\n\nThe preferred channel is GitHub's private security advisory feature:\n\n1. Go to the [Security tab](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/security) of this repository\n2. Click **\"Report a vulnerability\"**\n3. Provide a detailed description of the issue\n\nIf you are unable to use GitHub's private advisory feature, report via email:\n\n- **Email:** security@tonbankcard.com\n- **Subject line format:** `[SECURITY] <brief description>`\n- Include a detailed description of the issue, reproduction steps, and potential impact\n\nIf you do not receive an acknowledgement within 72 hours, send a follow-up referencing your original report.\n\n### What to Include\n\nA useful vulnerability report includes:\n\n- Description of the vulnerability and its potential impact\n- Steps to reproduce the issue\n- Affected contract(s) or component(s)\n- Proof of concept or test case, if available\n- Suggested severity (Critical, High, Medium, Low)\n\n---\n\n## 2. Encryption Requirements\n\nFor sensitive vulnerability reports, encrypted submission is strongly preferred.\n\n- **PGP:** Encrypt your report to the TONBANKCARD security team PGP key (key details to be published at `security@tonbankcard.com` upon request)\n- **Plain email** is accepted for low-severity or non-sensitive reports\n- Do not include full exploit code or credential material in unencrypted email\n\nEncryption key details will be provided upon initial contact if not yet published.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Scope\n\n### In Scope\n\nThe following components are in scope for vulnerability reports:\n\n- **Smart contracts:** `PaymentHub`, `MerchantNFT`, and related on-chain contracts in this repository (`contracts/`)\n- **Backend API:** REST endpoints handling invoice creation, settlement verification, and merchant registry (`api/`)\n- **Merchant SDK:** JavaScript/TypeScript SDK published under `@tonbankcard/sdk` (`sdk/`)\n- **Authentication and access control logic:** Key management, role-based access, admin operations\n- **Protocol-level logic:** Settlement finality, reorg handling, invariant violations\n\n### Priority Focus Areas\n\nThe most security-critical areas of this protocol:\n\n- **Fund safety:** any path that could result in unauthorized fund movement\n- **NFT ownership enforcement:** any bypass of the ownership check\n- **Lock bypass:** any path to transfer from a locked account\n- **Admin key misuse:** any undocumented admin capability\n\n### Out of Scope\n\nThe following are not in scope:\n\n- Already-deployed and frozen external contracts (TBC Token Jetton, NFT Collections, TBC Diamonds, TONCO DEX) — these are immutable and separately governed\n- Third-party services (ChangeNOW, NOWPayments, CoinRabbit, TONCO) — report vulnerabilities directly to those providers\n- Vulnerabilities in third-party dependencies unless directly exploitable through TONBANKCARD code\n- TON blockchain infrastructure, validator nodes, or core protocol\n- Reports requiring physical access to infrastructure\n- Social engineering attacks against team members or users\n- Denial-of-service attacks without demonstrated exploit impact\n- Issues in test environments or non-production deployments with no production impact\n- Theoretical vulnerabilities with no demonstrated impact\n\n---\n\n## 4. Response Timeline\n\n| Milestone | Target |\n|-----------|--------|\n| Acknowledgement of receipt | Within 72 hours |\n| Initial severity assessment | Within 7 days |\n| Status update to reporter | Every 14 days until resolved |\n| Patch for critical severity | Within 30 days |\n| Patch for high severity | Within 60 days |\n| Patch for medium/low severity | Within 90 days |\n\n### Fix Timeline by Severity\n\n| Severity | Target Fix Timeline |\n|----------|---------------------|\n| Critical | Within 72 hours for containment; patch within 30 days |\n| High | Within 60 days |\n| Medium | Within 90 days |\n| Low | Next planned release |\n\nThese are target timelines. Complex issues involving on-chain contracts may require additional time due to audit and deployment constraints. Reporters will be kept informed of any delays.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Disclosure Policy\n\nTONBANKCARD follows a **coordinated disclosure** model:\n\n1. Reporter submits vulnerability via the channel in Section 1\n2. TONBANKCARD acknowledges receipt and opens a private investigation\n3. TONBANKCARD and reporter agree on a disclosure timeline (default: 90 days from acknowledgement)\n4. A patch or mitigation is developed and deployed\n5. Reporter is given a preview of the disclosure and credited (if desired)\n6. A public disclosure is issued after the fix is available\n\n**Early disclosure may occur** if:\n\n- The vulnerability is already being actively exploited\n- A partial fix is available that significantly reduces risk\n\n**Extension of the 90-day timeline** may be requested by either party in writing. Extensions are granted on a case-by-case basis.\n\nIf TONBANKCARD does not respond within the timelines defined in Section 4, reporters may proceed with disclosure at their discretion, having acted in good faith.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Safe Harbor Statement\n\nTONBANKCARD supports responsible security research. If you report a vulnerability in good faith and in accordance with this policy, we will not pursue legal action against you for that research.\n\nGood faith research means:\n\n- You do not access, modify, or exfiltrate data beyond what is necessary to demonstrate the vulnerability\n- You do not disrupt service availability or degrade performance for other users\n- You do not use social engineering techniques against team members or users\n- You report the issue to us before public disclosure\n- You allow reasonable time for a fix before disclosing publicly\n\nThis safe harbor applies to research conducted under these terms. It does not extend to:\n\n- Exploitation of vulnerabilities for personal gain\n- Access to or exfiltration of user data\n- Any activity that violates applicable law\n\nThis statement is not legal advice and does not constitute a legal agreement. Researchers are responsible for understanding and complying with all applicable laws.\n\n---\n\n## Non-Custodial Architecture\n\nTONBANKCARD is a **non-custodial protocol**. The architecture enforces that:\n\n- No admin or operator can move user funds\n- No emergency mechanism exists that transfers or seizes funds\n- Account locks restrict outgoing transfers but do not confiscate balances\n\nFor more on the security model, see [docs/security/SECURITY.md](docs/security/SECURITY.md).\n\n---\n\n## Security Documentation\n\nFor the full security framework, see:\n\n- [docs/security/SECURITY.md](docs/security/SECURITY.md) — Security documentation index and unified framework\n- [docs/security/THREAT_MODEL.md](docs/security/THREAT_MODEL.md) — Threat model and security architecture\n- [docs/security/KEY_MANAGEMENT.md](docs/security/KEY_MANAGEMENT.md) — Key management and operational security\n- [docs/security/INCIDENT_RESPONSE.md](docs/security/INCIDENT_RESPONSE.md) — Incident response procedures\n- [docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md](docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md) — Audit readiness status\n\n---\n\n**Security Contact:** security@tonbankcard.com\n",

   [solve worker-1]     "originalFile": "# TONBANKCARD Protocol — Responsible Disclosure & Vulnerability Reporting Policy\n\n**Document Type:** Security Policy\n**Issue Reference:** [#66 — Issue 10.7 — Responsible Disclosure & Vulnerability Reporting Policy](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/66)\n**Status:** Active\n**Last Updated:** 2026-05-16\n\n---\n\n## Table of Contents\n\n1. [Reporting Channels](#1-reporting-channels)\n2. [Encryption Requirements](#2-encryption-requirements)\n3. [Scope](#3-scope)\n4. [Response Timeline](#4-response-timeline)\n5. [Disclosure Policy](#5-disclosure-policy)\n6. [Safe Harbor Statement](#6-safe-harbor-statement)\n7. [Bug Bounty Program](#7-bug-bounty-program)\n\n---\n\n## Supported Versions\n\n| Version | Status | Security Support |\n|---------|--------|-----------------|\n| v1.0.x | Active | Supported |\n\nEarlier versions and pre-release deployments are not covered by this policy.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Reporting Channels\n\n**DO NOT** disclose security vulnerabilities publicly. Public disclosure before a patch is available puts all users at risk.\n\nThe preferred channel is GitHub's private security advisory feature:\n\n1. Go to the [Security tab](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/security) of this repository\n2. Click **\"Report a vulnerability\"**\n3. Provide a detailed description of the issue\n\nIf you are unable to use GitHub's private advisory feature, report via email:\n\n- **Email:** security@tonbankcard.com\n- **Subject line format:** `[SECURITY] <brief description>`\n- Include a detailed description of the issue, reproduction steps, and potential impact\n\nIf you do not receive an acknowledgement within 72 hours, send a follow-up referencing your original report.\n\n### What to Include\n\nA useful vulnerability report includes:\n\n- Description of the vulnerability and its potential impact\n- Steps to reproduce the issue\n- Affected contract(s) or component(s)\n- Proof of concept or test case, if available\n- Suggested severity (Critical, High, Medium, Low)\n\n---\n\n## 2. Encryption Requirements\n\nFor sensitive vulnerability reports, encrypted submission is strongly preferred.\n\n- **PGP:** Encrypt your report to the TONBANKCARD security team PGP key (key details to be published at `security@tonbankcard.com` upon request)\n- **Plain email** is accepted for low-severity or non-sensitive reports\n- Do not include full exploit code or credential material in unencrypted email\n\nEncryption key details will be provided upon initial contact if not yet published.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Scope\n\n### In Scope\n\nThe following components are in scope for vulnerability reports:\n\n- **Smart contracts:** `PaymentHub`, `MerchantNFT`, and related on-chain contracts in this repository (`contracts/`)\n- **Backend API:** REST endpoints handling invoice creation, settlement verification, and merchant registry (`api/`)\n- **Merchant SDK:** JavaScript/TypeScript SDK published under `@tonbankcard/sdk` (`sdk/`)\n- **Authentication and access control logic:** Key management, role-based access, admin operations\n- **Protocol-level logic:** Settlement finality, reorg handling, invariant violations\n\n### Priority Focus Areas\n\nThe most security-critical areas of this protocol:\n\n- **Fund safety:** any path that could result in unauthorized fund movement\n- **NFT ownership enforcement:** any bypass of the ownership check\n- **Lock bypass:** any path to transfer from a locked account\n- **Admin key misuse:** any undocumented admin capability\n\n### Out of Scope\n\nThe following are not in scope:\n\n- Already-deployed and frozen external contracts (TBC Token Jetton, NFT Collections, TBC Diamonds, TONCO DEX) — these are immutable and separately governed\n- Third-party services (ChangeNOW, NOWPayments, CoinRabbit, TONCO) — report vulnerabilities directly to those providers\n- Vulnerabilities in third-party dependencies unless directly exploitable through TONBANKCARD code\n- TON blockchain infrastructure, validator nodes, or core protocol\n- Reports requiring physical access to infrastructure\n- Social engineering attacks against team members or users\n- Denial-of-service attacks without demonstrated exploit impact\n- Issues in test environments or non-production deployments with no production impact\n- Theoretical vulnerabilities with no demonstrated impact\n\n---\n\n## 4. Response Timeline\n\n| Milestone | Target |\n|-----------|--------|\n| Acknowledgement of receipt | Within 72 hours |\n| Initial severity assessment | Within 7 days |\n| Status update to reporter | Every 14 days until resolved |\n| Patch for critical severity | Within 30 days |\n| Patch for high severity | Within 60 days |\n| Patch for medium/low severity | Within 90 days |\n\n### Fix Timeline by Severity\n\n| Severity | Target Fix Timeline |\n|----------|---------------------|\n| Critical | Within 72 hours for containment; patch within 30 days |\n| High | Within 60 days |\n| Medium | Within 90 days |\n| Low | Next planned release |\n\nThese are target timelines. Complex issues involving on-chain contracts may require additional time due to audit and deployment constraints. Reporters will be kept informed of any delays.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Disclosure Policy\n\nTONBANKCARD follows a **coordinated disclosure** model:\n\n1. Reporter submits vulnerability via the channel in Section 1\n2. TONBANKCARD acknowledges receipt and opens a private investigation\n3. TONBANKCARD and reporter agree on a disclosure timeline (default: 90 days from acknowledgement)\n4. A patch or mitigation is developed and deployed\n5. Reporter is given a preview of the disclosure and credited (if desired)\n6. A public disclosure is issued after the fix is available\n\n**Early disclosure may occur** if:\n\n- The vulnerability is already being actively exploited\n- A partial fix is available that significantly reduces risk\n\n**Extension of the 90-day timeline** may be requested by either party in writing. Extensions are granted on a case-by-case basis.\n\nIf TONBANKCARD does not respond within the timelines defined in Section 4, reporters may proceed with disclosure at their discretion, having acted in good faith.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Safe Harbor Statement\n\nTONBANKCARD supports responsible security research. If you report a vulnerability in good faith and in accordance with this policy, we will not pursue legal action against you for that research.\n\nGood faith research means:\n\n- You do not access, modify, or exfiltrate data beyond what is necessary to demonstrate the vulnerability\n- You do not disrupt service availability or degrade performance for other users\n- You do not use social engineering techniques against team members or users\n- You report the issue to us before public disclosure\n- You allow reasonable time for a fix before disclosing publicly\n\nThis safe harbor applies to research conducted under these terms. It does not extend to:\n\n- Exploitation of vulnerabilities for personal gain\n- Access to or exfiltration of user data\n- Any activity that violates applicable law\n\nThis statement is not legal advice and does not constitute a legal agreement. Researchers are responsible for understanding and complying with all applicable laws.\n\n---\n\n## Non-Custodial Architecture\n\nTONBANKCARD is a **non-custodial protocol**. The architecture enforces that:\n\n- No admin or operator can move user funds\n- No emergency mechanism exists that transfers or seizes funds\n- Account locks restrict outgoing transfers but do not confiscate balances\n\nFor more on the security model, see [docs/security/SECURITY.md](docs/security/SECURITY.md).\n\n---\n\n## Security Documentation\n\nFor the full security framework, see:\n\n- [docs/security/SECURITY.md](docs/security/SECURITY.md) — Security documentation index and unified framework\n- [docs/security/THREAT_MODEL.md](docs/security/THREAT_MODEL.md) — Threat model and security architecture\n- [docs/security/KEY_MANAGEMENT.md](docs/security/KEY_MANAGEMENT.md) — Key management and operational security\n- [docs/security/INCIDENT_RESPONSE.md](docs/security/INCIDENT_RESPONSE.md) — Incident response procedures\n- [docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md](docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md) — Audit readiness status\n\n---\n\n**Security Contact:** security@tonbankcard.com\n",

[Reporting Channels](#1-reporting-channels)\n2. [Encryption Requirements](#2-encryption-requirements)\n3. [Scope](#3-scope)\n4. [Response Timeline](#4-response-timeline)\n5. [Disclosure Policy](#5-disclosure-policy)\n6. [Safe Harbor Statement](#6-safe-harbor-statement)\n7. [Bug Bounty Program](#7-bug-bounty-program)\n\n---\n\n## Supported Versions\n\n| Version | Status | Security Support |\n|---------|--------|-----------------|\n| v1.0.x | Active | Supported |\n\nEarlier versions and pre-release deployments are not covered by this policy.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Reporting Channels\n\n**DO NOT** disclose security vulnerabilities publicly. Public disclosure before a patch is available puts all users at risk.\n\n> **Once the A5 bug bounty program is launched**, the bounty platform is the preferred channel for in-scope components and is the **only** channel eligible for monetary rewards. See [Section 7 — Bug Bounty Program](#7-bug-bounty-program). The channels below remain available for out-of-scope reports and as a fallback if the platform is unavailable.\n\nThe preferred channel is GitHub's private security advisory feature:\n\n1. Go to the [Security tab](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/security) of this repository\n2. Click **\"Report a vulnerability\"**\n3. Provide a detailed description of the issue\n\nIf you are unable to use GitHub's private advisory feature, report via email:\n\n- **Email:** security@tonbankcard.com\n- **Subject line format:** `[SECURITY] <brief description>`\n- Include a detailed description of the issue, reproduction steps, and potential impact\n\nIf you do not receive an acknowledgement within 72 hours, send a follow-up referencing your original report.\n\n### What to Include\n\nA useful vulnerability report includes:\n\n- Description of the vulnerability and its potential impact\n- Steps to reproduce the issue\n- Affected contract(s) or component(s)\n- Proof of concept or test case, if available\n- Suggested severity (Critical, High, Medium, Low)\n\n---\n\n## 2. Encryption Requirements\n\nFor sensitive vulnerability reports, encrypted submission is strongly preferred.\n\n- **PGP:** Encrypt your report to the TONBANKCARD security team PGP key (key details to be published at `security@tonbankcard.com` upon request)\n- **Plain email** is accepted for low-severity or non-sensitive reports\n- Do not include full exploit code or credential material in unencrypted email\n\nEncryption key details will be provided upon initial contact if not yet published.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Scope\n\n### In Scope\n\nThe following components are in scope for vulnerability reports:\n\n- **Smart contracts:** `PaymentHub`, `MerchantNFT`, and related on-chain contracts in this repository (`contracts/`)\n- **Backend API:** REST endpoints handling invoice creation, settlement verification, and merchant registry (`api/`)\n- **Merchant SDK:** JavaScript/TypeScript SDK published under `@tonbankcard/sdk` (`sdk/`)\n- **Authentication and access control logic:** Key management, role-based access, admin operations\n- **Protocol-level logic:** Settlement finality, reorg handling, invariant violations\n\n### Priority Focus Areas\n\nThe most security-critical areas of this protocol:\n\n- **Fund safety:** any path that could result in unauthorized fund movement\n- **NFT ownership enforcement:** any bypass of the ownership check\n- **Lock bypass:** any path to transfer from a locked account\n- **Admin key misuse:** any undocumented admin capability\n\n### Out of Scope\n\nThe following are not in scope:\n\n- Already-deployed and frozen external contracts (TBC Token Jetton, NFT Collections, TBC Diamonds, TONCO DEX) — these are immutable and separately governed\n- Third-party services (ChangeNOW, NOWPayments, CoinRabbit, TONCO) — report vulnerabilities directly to those providers\n- Vulnerabilities in third-party dependencies unless directly exploitable through TONBANKCARD code\n- TON blockchain infrastructure, validator nodes, or core protocol\n- Reports requiring physical access to infrastructure\n- Social engineering attacks against team members or users\n- Denial-of-service attacks without demonstrated exploit impact\n- Issues in test environments or non-production deployments with no production impact\n- Theoretical vulnerabilities with no demonstrated impact\n\n---\n\n## 4. Response Timeline\n\n| Milestone | Target |\n|-----------|--------|\n| Acknowledgement of receipt | Within 72 hours |\n| Initial severity assessment | Within 7 days |\n| Status update to reporter | Every 14 days until resolved |\n| Patch for critical severity | Within 30 days |\n| Patch for high severity | Within 60 days |\n| Patch for medium/low severity | Within 90 days |\n\n### Fix Timeline by Severity\n\n| Severity | Target Fix Timeline |\n|----------|---------------------|\n| Critical | Within 72 hours for containment; patch within 30 days |\n| High | Within 60 days |\n| Medium | Within 90 days |\n| Low | Next planned release |\n\nThese are target timelines. Complex issues involving on-chain contracts may require additional time due to audit and deployment constraints. Reporters will be kept informed of any delays.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Disclosure Policy\n\nTONBANKCARD follows a **coordinated disclosure** model:\n\n1. Reporter submits vulnerability via the channel in Section 1\n2. TONBANKCARD acknowledges receipt and opens a private investigation\n3. TONBANKCARD and reporter agree on a disclosure timeline (default: 90 days from acknowledgement)\n4. A patch or mitigation is developed and deployed\n5. Reporter is given a preview of the disclosure and credited (if desired)\n6. A public disclosure is issued after the fix is available\n\n**Early disclosure may occur** if:\n\n- The vulnerability is already being actively exploited\n- A partial fix is available that significantly reduces risk\n\n**Extension of the 90-day timeline** may be requested by either party in writing. Extensions are granted on a case-by-case basis.\n\nIf TONBANKCARD does not respond within the timelines defined in Section 4, reporters may proceed with disclosure at their discretion, having acted in good faith.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Safe Harbor Statement\n\nTONBANKCARD supports responsible security research. If you report a vulnerability in good faith and in accordance with this policy, we will not pursue legal action against you for that research.\n\nGood faith research means:\n\n- You do not access, modify, or exfiltrate data beyond what is necessary to demonstrate the vulnerability\n- You do not disrupt service availability or degrade performance for other users\n- You do not use social engineering techniques against team members or users\n- You report the issue to us before public disclosure\n- You allow reasonable time for a fix before disclosing publicly\n\nThis safe harbor applies to research conducted under these terms. It does not extend to:\n\n- Exploitation of vulnerabilities for personal gain\n- Access to or exfiltration of user data\n- Any activity that violates applicable law\n\nThis statement is not legal advice and does not constitute a legal agreement. Researchers are responsible for understanding and complying with all applicable laws.\n\n---\n\n## Non-Custodial Architecture\n\nTONBANKCARD is a **non-custodial protocol**. The architecture enforces that:\n\n- No admin or operator can move user funds\n- No emergency mechanism exists that transfers or seizes funds\n- Account locks restrict outgoing transfers but do not confiscate balances\n\nFor more on the security model, see [docs/security/SECURITY.md](docs/security/SECURITY.md).\n\n---\n\n## Security Documentation\n\nFor the full security framework, see:\n\n- [docs/security/SECURITY.md](docs/security/SECURITY.md) — Security documentation index and unified framework\n- [docs/security/THREAT_MODEL.md](docs/security/THREAT_MODEL.md) — Threat model and security architecture\n- [docs/security/KEY_MANAGEMENT.md](docs/security/KEY_MANAGEMENT.md) — Key management and operational security\n- [docs/security/INCIDENT_RESPONSE.md](docs/security/INCIDENT_RESPONSE.md) — Incident response procedures\n- [docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md](docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md) — Audit readiness status\n\n---\n\n**Security Contact:** security@tonbankcard.com\n",

Directory Layout\n30\t\n31\t```\n32\tdocs/security/audits/\n33\t├── README.md                       — This index\n34\t├── REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md         — How findings are triaged, fixed, and verified\n35\t├── REPORT_TEMPLATE.md              — Canonical layout for incoming audit reports\n36\t├── A1-core-contracts/              — Issue #112 engagement\n37\t│   ├── ENGAGEMENT.md               — Scope, deliverables, candidate firms, evaluation matrix\n38\t│   └── STATUS.md                   — Live state of the engagement (firm, dates, findings)\n39\t├── A2-phase4-contracts/            — Issue #113 engagement (gated by A1 completion)\n40\t│   ├── ENGAGEMENT.md               — Phase 4 scope with dedicated cross-chain bridge review\n41\t│   └── STATUS.md                   — Live state, A1 upstream-gate tracker, threat-ID ledger\n42\t└── A4-offchain-services/           — Issue #115 engagement (off-chain pentest)\n43\t    ├── ENGAGEMENT.md               — api/ + backend/indexer/ + sdk/ pentest scope, OWASP-driven\n44\t    ├── STATUS.md                   — Live state, D4/D5 upstream-gate tracker, OWASP coverage\n45\t    ├── OWASP_CHECKLIST.md          — OWASP Top 10:2021 category-by-category required tests\n46\t    └── PENTEST_PLAN.md             — Detailed per-component test cases, PoC expectations\n47\t```\n48\t\n49\tFuture engagements (A5 bug bounty, etc.) are added as sibling folders named after the roadmap ID.\n50\t\n51\t---\n52\t\n53\t## 3. Gating Rules\n67\t\n68\tThe following rules are **non-negotiable** and apply to every engagement listed in §3:\n69\t\n70\t1. **No mainnet deployment** of any in-scope contract before the corresponding audit report is published and remediation is verified by the auditor.\n71\t2. **Critical findings:** zero tolerance — every Critical must be remediated and re-verified before sign-off.\n72\t3. **High findings:** remediated, or formally accepted with rationale signed off by the maintainers in `STATUS.md`.\n73\t4. **Medium findings:** remediated or documented as accepted risk in `docs/audit-notes.md`.\n74\t5. **Audit report is public** — published in this directory and linked from `docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md`.\n75\t6. **Frozen scope** — once an engagement is signed, the contract set under audit is frozen at a specific commit (see [`audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md`](../../../audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md)).\n76\t\n77\t---\n78\t\n79\t## 5.    [solve worker-1]       "content": "# TONBANKCARD — External Security Audits\n\n**Document Type:** Index — External Security Audits\n**Issue References:**\n- [#112 — A1 Formal Security Audit — Core Contracts](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/112)\n- [#113 — A2 Formal Security Audit — Phase 4 Contracts](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/113)\n- [#115 — A4 Penetration Testing — Off-Chain Services](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/115)\n**Track:** A — Security & Audit ([DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md](../../../TEMP/DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md))\n**Status:** Active\n**Last Updated:** 2026-05-16\n\n---\n\n## 1. Purpose\n\nThis directory tracks every **external security engagement** performed on the TONBANKCARD protocol. It is the canonical location for:\n\n- Audit engagement plans (RFP-style)\n- Auditor selection records\n- Frozen audit packages handed over to auditors\n- Audit reports as delivered by external firms\n- Remediation pull requests and re-audit attestations\n- Public disclosure artifacts\n\nInternal pre-audit reviews (such as [`audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md`](../../../audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md)) and the system-level audit ([`docs/audit/FULL_SYSTEM_AUDIT.md`](../../audit/FULL_SYSTEM_AUDIT.md)) live elsewhere — this directory is reserved for **third-party** engagements that gate mainnet deployment.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Directory Layout\n\n```\ndocs/security/audits/\n├── README.md                       — This index\n├── REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md         — How findings are triaged, fixed, and verified\n├── REPORT_TEMPLATE.md              — Canonical layout for incoming audit reports\n├── A1-core-contracts/              — Issue #112 engagement\n│   ├── ENGAGEMENT.md               — Scope, deliverables, candidate firms, evaluation matrix\n│   └── STATUS.md                   — Live state of the engagement (firm, dates, findings)\n├── A2-phase4-contracts/            — Issue #113 engagement (gated by A1 completion)\n│   ├── ENGAGEMENT.md               — Phase 4 scope with dedicated cross-chain bridge review\n│   └── STATUS.md                   — Live state, A1 upstream-gate tracker, threat-ID ledger\n└── A4-offchain-services/           — Issue #115 engagement (off-chain pentest)\n    ├── ENGAGEMENT.md               — api/ + backend/indexer/ + sdk/ pentest scope, OWASP-driven\n    ├── STATUS.md                   — Live state, D4/D5 upstream-gate tracker, OWASP coverage\n    ├── OWASP_CHECKLIST.md          — OWASP Top 10:2021 category-by-category required tests\n    └── PENTEST_PLAN.md             — Detailed per-component test cases, PoC expectations\n```\n\nFuture engagements (A5 bug bounty, etc.) are added as sibling folders named after the roadmap ID.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Engagement Index\n\n| ID | Scope | Roadmap | Issue | Status | Firm | Report |\n|----|-------|---------|-------|--------|------|--------|\n| **A1** | Core contracts (PaymentHub, MerchantPaymentHub, account-locks, nft-resolver, collateral signal) | [A1](../../../TEMP/DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md) | [#112](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/112) | Engagement preparation complete — awaiting firm selection | — | — |\n| **A2** | Phase 4 contracts (CrossChainBridge, MultiSigCard, RecurringPayments, LendingProtocolCoordinator) | [A2](../../../TEMP/DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md) | [#113](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/113) | Engagement preparation complete — awaiting A1 completion and firm selection | — | — |\n| **A4** | Off-chain services (`api/`, `backend/indexer/`, `sdk/`) | [A4](../../../TEMP/DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md) | [#115](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/115) | Engagement preparation complete — awaiting D4 hardening and firm selection | — | — |\n| A5 | Bug bounty program | A5 | TBD | Not started | — | — |\n\nWhen a new external engagement begins, copy `A1-core-contracts/` as a starting template, update its `ENGAGEMENT.md` for the new scope, and add a row to this table.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Gating Rules\n\nThe following rules are **non-negotiable** and apply to every engagement listed in §3:\n\n1. **No mainnet deployment** of any in-scope contract before the corresponding audit report is published and remediation is verified by the auditor.\n2. **Critical findings:** zero tolerance — every Critical must be remediated and re-verified before sign-off.\n3. **High findings:** remediated, or formally accepted with rationale signed off by the maintainers in `STATUS.md`.\n4. **Medium findings:** remediated or documented as accepted risk in `docs/audit-notes.md`.\n5. **Audit report is public** — published in this directory and linked from `docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md`.\n6. **Frozen scope** — once an engagement is signed, the contract set under audit is frozen at a specific commit (see [`audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md`](../../../audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md)).\n\n---\n\n## 5. Where Auditors Should Start\n\nExternal auditors engaging with TONBANKCARD should read, in order:\n\n1. [`docs/audit/external-audit-intro.md`](../../audit/external-audit-intro.md) — protocol intent and constraints\n2. [`audit/SCOPE.md`](../../../audit/SCOPE.md) — contracts in scope, focus areas\n3. [`audit/INVARIANTS.md`](../../../audit/INVARIANTS.md) — formal invariants I1–I7\n4. [`audit/THREAT_MODEL.md`](../../../audit/THREAT_MODEL.md) — attack vectors and mitigations\n5. [`audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md`](../../../audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md) — frozen commit, compiler versions\n6. [`audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md`](../../../audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md) — reproducible build\n7. [`audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md`](../../../audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md) — known findings from internal pre-audit\n8. Engagement-specific `ENGAGEMENT.md` in the relevant subdirectory\n\nThe [`docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md`](../AUDIT_READINESS.md) document is the navigation hub for all of the above.\n\n---\n\n## 6.
