   [solve worker-1]     "originalFile": "# TONBANKCARD — External Security Audits\n\n**Document Type:** Index — External Security Audits\n**Issue References:**\n- [#112 — A1 Formal Security Audit — Core Contracts](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/112)\n- [#113 — A2 Formal Security Audit — Phase 4 Contracts](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/113)\n- [#115 — A4 Penetration Testing — Off-Chain Services](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/115)\n**Track:** A — Security & Audit ([DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md](../../../TEMP/DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md))\n**Status:** Active\n**Last Updated:** 2026-05-16\n\n---\n\n## 1. Purpose\n\nThis directory tracks every **external security engagement** performed on the TONBANKCARD protocol. It is the canonical location for:\n\n- Audit engagement plans (RFP-style)\n- Auditor selection records\n- Frozen audit packages handed over to auditors\n- Audit reports as delivered by external firms\n- Remediation pull requests and re-audit attestations\n- Public disclosure artifacts\n\nInternal pre-audit reviews (such as [`audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md`](../../../audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md)) and the system-level audit ([`docs/audit/FULL_SYSTEM_AUDIT.md`](../../audit/FULL_SYSTEM_AUDIT.md)) live elsewhere — this directory is reserved for **third-party** engagements that gate mainnet deployment.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Directory Layout\n\n```\ndocs/security/audits/\n├── README.md                       — This index\n├── REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md         — How findings are triaged, fixed, and verified\n├── REPORT_TEMPLATE.md              — Canonical layout for incoming audit reports\n├── A1-core-contracts/              — Issue #112 engagement\n│   ├── ENGAGEMENT.md               — Scope, deliverables, candidate firms, evaluation matrix\n│   └── STATUS.md                   — Live state of the engagement (firm, dates, findings)\n├── A2-phase4-contracts/            — Issue #113 engagement (gated by A1 completion)\n│   ├── ENGAGEMENT.md               — Phase 4 scope with dedicated cross-chain bridge review\n│   └── STATUS.md                   — Live state, A1 upstream-gate tracker, threat-ID ledger\n└── A4-offchain-services/           — Issue #115 engagement (off-chain pentest)\n    ├── ENGAGEMENT.md               — api/ + backend/indexer/ + sdk/ pentest scope, OWASP-driven\n    ├── STATUS.md                   — Live state, D4/D5 upstream-gate tracker, OWASP coverage\n    ├── OWASP_CHECKLIST.md          — OWASP Top 10:2021 category-by-category required tests\n    └── PENTEST_PLAN.md             — Detailed per-component test cases, PoC expectations\n```\n\nFuture engagements (A5 bug bounty, etc.) are added as sibling folders named after the roadmap ID.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Engagement Index\n\n| ID | Scope | Roadmap | Issue | Status | Firm | Report |\n|----|-------|---------|-------|--------|------|--------|\n| **A1** | Core contracts (PaymentHub, MerchantPaymentHub, account-locks, nft-resolver, collateral signal) | [A1](../../../TEMP/DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md) | [#112](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/112) | Engagement preparation complete — awaiting firm selection | — | — |\n| **A2** | Phase 4 contracts (CrossChainBridge, MultiSigCard, RecurringPayments, LendingProtocolCoordinator) | [A2](../../../TEMP/DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md) | [#113](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/113) | Engagement preparation complete — awaiting A1 completion and firm selection | — | — |\n| **A4** | Off-chain services (`api/`, `backend/indexer/`, `sdk/`) | [A4](../../../TEMP/DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md) | [#115](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/115) | Engagement preparation complete — awaiting D4 hardening and firm selection | — | — |\n| A5 | Bug bounty program | A5 | TBD | Not started | — | — |\n\nWhen a new external engagement begins, copy `A1-core-contracts/` as a starting template, update its `ENGAGEMENT.md` for the new scope, and add a row to this table.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Gating Rules\n\nThe following rules are **non-negotiable** and apply to every engagement listed in §3:\n\n1. **No mainnet deployment** of any in-scope contract before the corresponding audit report is published and remediation is verified by the auditor.\n2. **Critical findings:** zero tolerance — every Critical must be remediated and re-verified before sign-off.\n3. **High findings:** remediated, or formally accepted with rationale signed off by the maintainers in `STATUS.md`.\n4. **Medium findings:** remediated or documented as accepted risk in `docs/audit-notes.md`.\n5. **Audit report is public** — published in this directory and linked from `docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md`.\n6. **Frozen scope** — once an engagement is signed, the contract set under audit is frozen at a specific commit (see [`audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md`](../../../audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md)).\n\n---\n\n## 5. Where Auditors Should Start\n\nExternal auditors engaging with TONBANKCARD should read, in order:\n\n1. [`docs/audit/external-audit-intro.md`](../../audit/external-audit-intro.md) — protocol intent and constraints\n2. [`audit/SCOPE.md`](../../../audit/SCOPE.md) — contracts in scope, focus areas\n3. [`audit/INVARIANTS.md`](../../../audit/INVARIANTS.md) — formal invariants I1–I7\n4. [`audit/THREAT_MODEL.md`](../../../audit/THREAT_MODEL.md) — attack vectors and mitigations\n5. [`audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md`](../../../audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md) — frozen commit, compiler versions\n6. [`audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md`](../../../audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md) — reproducible build\n7. [`audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md`](../../../audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md) — known findings from internal pre-audit\n8. Engagement-specific `ENGAGEMENT.md` in the relevant subdirectory\n\nThe [`docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md`](../AUDIT_READINESS.md) document is the navigation hub for all of the above.\n\n---\n\n## 6. References\n\n- [Audit Readiness](../AUDIT_READINESS.md)\n- [Audit Scope](../../../audit/SCOPE.md)\n- [Formal Invariants](../../../audit/INVARIANTS.md)\n- [Threat Model](../../../audit/THREAT_MODEL.md)\n- [Internal Per-Contract Audit](../../../audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md)\n- [Full System Audit](../../audit/FULL_SYSTEM_AUDIT.md)\n- [Development Roadmap — Track A](../../../TEMP/DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md)\n",

Purpose\n\nThis directory tracks every **external security engagement** performed on the TONBANKCARD protocol. It is the canonical location for:\n\n- Audit engagement plans (RFP-style)\n- Auditor selection records\n- Frozen audit packages handed over to auditors\n- Audit reports as delivered by external firms\n- Remediation pull requests and re-audit attestations\n- Public disclosure artifacts\n\nInternal pre-audit reviews (such as [`audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md`](../../../audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md)) and the system-level audit ([`docs/audit/FULL_SYSTEM_AUDIT.md`](../../audit/FULL_SYSTEM_AUDIT.md)) live elsewhere — this directory is reserved for **third-party** engagements that gate mainnet deployment.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Directory Layout\n\n```\ndocs/security/audits/\n├── README.md                       — This index\n├── REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md         — How findings are triaged, fixed, and verified\n├── REPORT_TEMPLATE.md              — Canonical layout for incoming audit reports\n├── A1-core-contracts/              — Issue #112 engagement\n│   ├── ENGAGEMENT.md               — Scope, deliverables, candidate firms, evaluation matrix\n│   └── STATUS.md                   — Live state of the engagement (firm, dates, findings)\n├── A2-phase4-contracts/            — Issue #113 engagement (gated by A1 completion)\n│   ├── ENGAGEMENT.md               — Phase 4 scope with dedicated cross-chain bridge review\n│   └── STATUS.md                   — Live state, A1 upstream-gate tracker, threat-ID ledger\n└── A4-offchain-services/           — Issue #115 engagement (off-chain pentest)\n    ├── ENGAGEMENT.md               — api/ + backend/indexer/ + sdk/ pentest scope, OWASP-driven\n    ├── STATUS.md                   — Live state, D4/D5 upstream-gate tracker, OWASP coverage\n    ├── OWASP_CHECKLIST.md          — OWASP Top 10:2021 category-by-category required tests\n    └── PENTEST_PLAN.md             — Detailed per-component test cases, PoC expectations\n```\n\nFuture engagements (A5 bug bounty, etc.) are added as sibling folders named after the roadmap ID.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Engagement Index\n\n| ID | Scope | Roadmap | Issue | Status | Firm | Report |\n|----|-------|---------|-------|--------|------|--------|\n| **A1** | Core contracts (PaymentHub, MerchantPaymentHub, account-locks, nft-resolver, collateral signal) | [A1](../../../TEMP/DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md) | [#112](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/112) | Engagement preparation complete — awaiting firm selection | — | — |\n| **A2** | Phase 4 contracts (CrossChainBridge, MultiSigCard, RecurringPayments, LendingProtocolCoordinator) | [A2](../../../TEMP/DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md) | [#113](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/113) | Engagement preparation complete — awaiting A1 completion and firm selection | — | — |\n| **A4** | Off-chain services (`api/`, `backend/indexer/`, `sdk/`) | [A4](../../../TEMP/DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md) | [#115](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/115) | Engagement preparation complete — awaiting D4 hardening and firm selection | — | — |\n| A5 | Bug bounty program | A5 | TBD | Not started | — | — |\n\nWhen a new external engagement begins, copy `A1-core-contracts/` as a starting template, update its `ENGAGEMENT.md` for the new scope, and add a row to this table.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Gating Rules\n\nThe following rules are **non-negotiable** and apply to every engagement listed in §3:\n\n1. **No mainnet deployment** of any in-scope contract before the corresponding audit report is published and remediation is verified by the auditor.\n2. **Critical findings:** zero tolerance — every Critical must be remediated and re-verified before sign-off.\n3. **High findings:** remediated, or formally accepted with rationale signed off by the maintainers in `STATUS.md`.\n4. **Medium findings:** remediated or documented as accepted risk in `docs/audit-notes.md`.\n5. **Audit report is public** — published in this directory and linked from `docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md`.\n6. **Frozen scope** — once an engagement is signed, the contract set under audit is frozen at a specific commit (see [`audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md`](../../../audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md)).\n\n---\n\n## 5. Where Auditors Should Start\n\nExternal auditors engaging with TONBANKCARD should read, in order:\n\n1. It is the canonical location for:\n\n- Audit engagement plans (RFP-style)\n- Auditor selection records\n- Frozen audit packages handed over to auditors\n- Audit reports as delivered by external firms\n- Remediation pull requests and re-audit attestations\n- Public disclosure artifacts\n\nInternal pre-audit reviews (such as [`audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md`](../../../audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md)) and the system-level audit ([`docs/audit/FULL_SYSTEM_AUDIT.md`](../../audit/FULL_SYSTEM_AUDIT.md)) live elsewhere — this directory is reserved for **third-party** engagements that gate mainnet deployment.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Directory Layout\n\n```\ndocs/security/audits/\n├── README.md                       — This index\n├── REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md         — How findings are triaged, fixed, and verified\n├── REPORT_TEMPLATE.md              — Canonical layout for incoming audit reports\n├── A1-core-contracts/              — Issue #112 engagement\n│   ├── ENGAGEMENT.md               — Scope, deliverables, candidate firms, evaluation matrix\n│   └── STATUS.md                   — Live state of the engagement (firm, dates, findings)\n├── A2-phase4-contracts/            — Issue #113 engagement (gated by A1 completion)\n│   ├── ENGAGEMENT.md               — Phase 4 scope with dedicated cross-chain bridge review\n│   └── STATUS.md                   — Live state, A1 upstream-gate tracker, threat-ID ledger\n├── A4-offchain-services/           — Issue #115 engagement (off-chain pentest)\n│   ├── ENGAGEMENT.md               — api/ + backend/indexer/ + sdk/ pentest scope, OWASP-driven\n│   ├── STATUS.md                   — Live state, D4/D5 upstream-gate tracker, OWASP coverage\n│   ├── OWASP_CHECKLIST.md          — OWASP Top 10:2021 category-by-category required tests\n│   └── PENTEST_PLAN.md             — Detailed per-component test cases, PoC expectations\n└── A5-bug-bounty/                  — Issue #116 engagement (public bug bounty program)\n    ├── ENGAGEMENT.md               — Engagement plan, platform comparison, SLAs, gating\n    ├── STATUS.md                   — Live state, launch checklist, findings ledger, SLA tracker\n    ├── PROGRAM_BRIEF.md            — Canonical source for the platform-published terms\n    ├── SEVERITY_RUBRIC.md          — Severity classification rubric (I1–I7 + Immunefi v2.3)\n    ├── QUARTERLY_REPORT_TEMPLATE.md — Quarterly public transparency report template\n    └── DRY_RUN.md                  — Internal dry-run / soft-launch plan (gates public launch)\n```\n\nFuture engagements are added as sibling folders named after the roadmap ID.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Engagement Index\n\n| ID | Scope | Roadmap | Issue | Status | Firm | Report |\n|----|-------|---------|-------|--------|------|--------|\n| **A1** | Core contracts (PaymentHub, MerchantPaymentHub, account-locks, nft-resolver, collateral signal) | [A1](../../../TEMP/DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md) | [#112](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/112) | Engagement preparation complete — awaiting firm selection | — | — |\n| **A2** | Phase 4 contracts (CrossChainBridge, MultiSigCard, RecurringPayments, LendingProtocolCoordinator) | [A2](../../../TEMP/DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md) | [#113](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/113) | Engagement preparation complete — awaiting A1 completion and firm selection | — | — |\n| **A4** | Off-chain services (`api/`, `backend/indexer/`, `sdk/`) | [A4](../../../TEMP/DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md) | [#115](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/115) | Engagement preparation complete — awaiting D4 hardening and firm selection | — | — |\n| A5 | Bug bounty program | A5 | TBD | Not started | — | — |\n\nWhen a new external engagement begins, copy `A1-core-contracts/` as a starting template, update its `ENGAGEMENT.md` for the new scope, and add a row to this table.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Gating Rules\n\nThe following rules are **non-negotiable** and apply to every engagement listed in §3:\n\n1. **No mainnet deployment** of any in-scope contract before the corresponding audit report is published and remediation is verified by the auditor.\n2. **Critical findings:** zero tolerance — every Critical must be remediated and re-verified before sign-off.\n3. **High findings:** remediated, or formally accepted with rationale signed off by the maintainers in `STATUS.md`.\n4. **Medium findings:** remediated or documented as accepted risk in `docs/audit-notes.md`.\n5. **Audit report is public** — published in this directory and linked from `docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md`.\n6. **Frozen scope** — once an engagement is signed, the contract set under audit is frozen at a specific commit (see [`audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md`](../../../audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md)).\n\n---\n\n## 5. Where Auditors Should Start\n\nExternal auditors engaging with TONBANKCARD should read, in order:\n\n1. [`docs/audit/external-audit-intro.md`](../../audit/external-audit-intro.md) — protocol intent and constraints\n2. [`audit/SCOPE.md`](../../../audit/SCOPE.md) — contracts in scope, focus areas\n3. [`audit/INVARIANTS.md`](../../../audit/INVARIANTS.md) — formal invariants I1–I7\n4. [`audit/THREAT_MODEL.md`](../../../audit/THREAT_MODEL.md) — attack vectors and mitigations\n5. [`audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md`](../../../audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md) — frozen commit, compiler versions\n6. [`audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md`](../../../audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md) — reproducible build\n7. [`audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md`](../../../audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md) — known findings from internal pre-audit\n8. Engagement-specific `ENGAGEMENT.md` in the relevant subdirectory\n\nThe [`docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md`](../AUDIT_READINESS.md) document is the navigation hub for all of the above.\n\n---\n\n## 6. No contract logic changes are permitted to the frozen set. See [audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md](../../audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md).\n\n---\n\n## Contracts Under Audit\n\nFull details in [audit/SCOPE.md](../../audit/SCOPE.md). Summary:\n\n| Contract | File | Priority | Lines | Primary Concern |\n|----------|------|----------|-------|-----------------|\n| MerchantPaymentHub | `contracts/MerchantPaymentHub.tact` | Critical | 287 | Payment settlement, ownership, locks |\n| PaymentHub | `contracts/payments/PaymentHub.tact` | Critical | 355 | Internal transfers, atomicity |\n| NFT Account Resolver | `contracts/nft-resolver/nft_account_resolver.fc` | Critical | 149 | Ownership resolution |\n| NFT Account Resolver | `contracts/nft-resolver/nft_account_resolver.tact` | Critical | 121 | Ownership resolution (Tact wrapper) |\n| Account State Machine | `contracts/payment-hub/account-state.tact` | Critical | 285 | State management, balance integrity |\n| Account Locks | `contracts/payments/account-locks.fc` | High | 269 | Lock authorization, lock semantics |\n\n**Total lines under audit:** 1,466 (critical) + 269 (high) = **1,735 lines**\n\n---\n\n## Protocol Invariants\n\nSeven formal invariants define the protocol's security guarantees. Any violation is a critical security finding.\n\n| ID | Invariant | Key Guarantee |\n|----|-----------|---------------|\n| **I1** | Non-Custodial Ownership | Only NFT owner can initiate fund transfers |\n| **I2** | NFT = Account Authority | NFT ownership is the single source of truth for account control |\n| **I3** | No Admin Fund Control | No privileged role can move user funds |\n| **I4** | Atomic Transfers | All transfers are all-or-nothing; no partial state possible |\n| **I5** | Ledger Conservation | Sum of all balances is preserved across all operations |\n| **I6** | Lock ≠ Confiscation | Locks restrict outgoing transfers; they do not seize funds |\n| **I7** | External Adapter Isolation | External providers cannot directly invoke protocol operations |\n\nFull formal definitions with contract-code mappings: [audit/INVARIANTS.md](../../audit/INVARIANTS.md)\n\n---\n\n## Test Coverage Summary\n\n| Contract | Estimated Line Coverage | Estimated Branch Coverage |\n|----------|------------------------|--------------------------|\n| MerchantPaymentHub.tact | ~90%+ | ~85%+ |\n| PaymentHub.tact | ~85%+ | ~80%+ |\n| account-locks.fc | ~85%+ | ~80%+ |\n| nft_account_resolver.fc | ~80%+ | ~75%+ |\n| account-state.tact | ~90%+ | ~85%+ |\n\nTo obtain exact figures:\n\n```bash\ngit checkout eb5dd593248a33a5a7517ae59b840827c140906a\nnpm install\nnpx blueprint test --coverage\n```\n\nSee [audit/TEST_COVERAGE_REPORT.md](../../audit/TEST_COVERAGE_REPORT.md) for full test organization.\n\n---\n\n## Critical Audit Focus Areas\n\n### 1. No Admin Fund Control (MUST verify)\n\nSearch the entire contract codebase for `withdraw`, `drain`, `emergency`, `admin_transfer`, `force_transfer`. Expected result: **zero matches** in fund-moving contexts.\n\nAdmin roles exist (`risk_authority`, `lending_adapter`) but are limited to setting/clearing lock flags. They cannot move funds.\n\n### 2. NFT Ownership Enforcement (MUST verify)\n\nEvery fund-moving operation must verify the caller is the current on-chain NFT owner. No cached ownership. No secondary authorization paths.\n\n### 3. Atomic Balance Updates (MUST verify)\n\nAll balance modifications must be atomic — both debit and credit in the same transaction. Reentrancy protection must be verified at:\n- `PaymentHub.tact` lines 149–150 (reentrancy guard)\n- `PaymentHub.tact` lines 196–202 (`executeTransfer`)\n\n### 4. Lock Enforcement (MUST verify)\n\nLocks prevent sending but must never seize funds. Verify:\n- `account-locks.fc` `can_receive()` always returns 1\n- Lock operations do not modify balances\n- FRAUD_LOCK and COLLATERAL_LOCK both correctly gate `can_send()`\n\n### 5. No Upgrade Paths (MUST verify)\n\nContracts are immutable. No upgradeable proxy patterns. No `setAdmin()` paths that could change invariants.\n\n---\n\n## Known Limitations (Auditor Notice)\n\n| Limitation | Severity | Description |\n|------------|----------|-------------|\n| Invoice replay (off-chain only) | MEDIUM | Contract does not enforce invoice uniqueness on-chain; handled off-chain |\n| DAO unlock not implemented | LOW | FROZEN → ACTIVE transition requires future DAO governance |\n| Lending unlock not implemented | LOW | COLLATERAL_LOCKED → ACTIVE requires Lending Adapter (not yet deployed) |\n| NFT ownership integration (partial) | MEDIUM | Some contracts rely on calling contract for ownership check |\n| Single admin key (temporary) | HIGH | Admin key is single-key pending multi-sig migration (Q1 2026) |\n\nThese are documented accepted risks. Full details in [docs/audit-notes.md](../audit-notes.md).\n\n---\n\n## Auditor Engagement Process\n\n### Access\n\n- Repository: `https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol`\n- Audit freeze commit: `eb5dd593248a33a5a7517ae59b840827c140906a`\n- Build instructions: [audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md](../../audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md)\n- Contact for questions: via GitHub issues tagged `audit`\n\n### Scope Confirmation\n\nBefore beginning, auditors must confirm:\n- Which contracts are in scope (see [audit/SCOPE.md](../../audit/SCOPE.md))\n- Which compiler versions to use (see [audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md](../../audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md))\n- Which invariants to verify (see [audit/INVARIANTS.md](../../audit/INVARIANTS.md))\n\n### Expected Deliverables\n\n| Deliverable | Description |\n|-------------|-------------|\n| Audit Report | Findings categorized by severity (Critical, High, Medium, Low, Informational) |\n| Finding References | Each finding references specific invariant(s) and contract line(s) |\n| Reproduction Steps | Each finding includes steps to reproduce |\n| Suggested Fixes | Where applicable |\n| Invariant Attestation | Statement on whether each of I1–I7 holds |\n\nThe end-to-end engagement workflow (intake → triage → remediation → re-verification → disclosure) is canonicalised in [docs/security/audits/REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md](./audits/REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md). It serves as a navigation guide for external auditors and internal reviewers approaching the protocol for the first time.\n\nFor the complete frozen audit package (used by external auditors), see the [`audit/`](../../audit/) directory.\n\n---\n\n## Audit Package Location\n\nThe pre-audit package is located at:\n\n```\naudit/\n├── SCOPE.md              — Audit boundaries, focus areas, and contract inventory\n├── THREAT_MODEL.md       — Threat classes, attack vectors, and mitigations\n├── INVARIANTS.md         — Formal invariants with contract-code mapping\n├── FREEZE_METADATA.md    — Git hash, compiler versions, file checksums\n├── BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md — How to reproduce builds and run tests\n└── TEST_COVERAGE_REPORT.md — Coverage data and test organization\n```\n\n**Freeze status:** The audit package was frozen at commit `4027b9d` (2025-12-29). No contract logic changes are permitted to the frozen set. See [audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md](../../audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md).\n\n---\n\n## Contracts Under Audit\n\nFull details in [audit/SCOPE.md](../../audit/SCOPE.md). Summary:\n\n| Contract | File | Priority | Lines | Primary Concern |\n|----------|------|----------|-------|-----------------|\n| MerchantPaymentHub | `contracts/MerchantPaymentHub.tact` | Critical | 287 | Payment settlement, ownership, locks |\n| PaymentHub | `contracts/payments/PaymentHub.tact` | Critical | 355 | Internal transfers, atomicity |\n| NFT Account Resolver | `contracts/nft-resolver/nft_account_resolver.fc` | Critical | 149 | Ownership resolution |\n| NFT Account Resolver | `contracts/nft-resolver/nft_account_resolver.tact` | Critical | 121 | Ownership resolution (Tact wrapper) |\n| Account State Machine | `contracts/payment-hub/account-state.tact` | Critical | 285 | State management, balance integrity |\n| Account Locks | `contracts/payments/account-locks.fc` | High | 269 | Lock authorization, lock semantics |\n\n**Total lines under audit:** 1,466 (critical) + 269 (high) = **1,735 lines**\n\n---\n\n## Protocol Invariants\n\nSeven formal invariants define the protocol's security guarantees. Any violation is a critical security finding.\n\n| ID | Invariant | Key Guarantee |\n|----|-----------|---------------|\n| **I1** | Non-Custodial Ownership | Only NFT owner can initiate fund transfers |\n| **I2** | NFT = Account Authority | NFT ownership is the single source of truth for account control |\n| **I3** | No Admin Fund Control | No privileged role can move user funds |\n| **I4** | Atomic Transfers | All transfers are all-or-nothing; no partial state possible |\n| **I5** | Ledger Conservation | Sum of all balances is preserved across all operations |\n| **I6** | Lock ≠ Confiscation | Locks restrict outgoing transfers; they do not seize funds |\n| **I7** | External Adapter Isolation | External providers cannot directly invoke protocol operations |\n\nFull formal definitions with contract-code mappings: [audit/INVARIANTS.md](../../audit/INVARIANTS.md)\n\n---\n\n## Test Coverage Summary\n\n| Contract | Estimated Line Coverage | Estimated Branch Coverage |\n|----------|------------------------|--------------------------|\n| MerchantPaymentHub.tact | ~90%+ | ~85%+ |\n| PaymentHub.tact | ~85%+ | ~80%+ |\n| account-locks.fc | ~85%+ | ~80%+ |\n| nft_account_resolver.fc | ~80%+ | ~75%+ |\n| account-state.tact | ~90%+ | ~85%+ |\n\nTo obtain exact figures:\n\n```bash\ngit checkout eb5dd593248a33a5a7517ae59b840827c140906a\nnpm install\nnpx blueprint test --coverage\n```\n\nSee [audit/TEST_COVERAGE_REPORT.md](../../audit/TEST_COVERAGE_REPORT.md) for full test organization.\n\n---\n\n## Critical Audit Focus Areas\n\n### 1. No Admin Fund Control (MUST verify)\n\nSearch the entire contract codebase for `withdraw`, `drain`, `emergency`, `admin_transfer`, `force_transfer`. Expected result: **zero matches** in fund-moving contexts.\n\nAdmin roles exist (`risk_authority`, `lending_adapter`) but are limited to setting/clearing lock flags. They cannot move funds.\n\n### 2. NFT Ownership Enforcement (MUST verify)\n\nEvery fund-moving operation must verify the caller is the current on-chain NFT owner. No cached ownership. No secondary authorization paths.\n\n### 3. Atomic Balance Updates (MUST verify)\n\nAll balance modifications must be atomic — both debit and credit in the same transaction. Reentrancy protection must be verified at:\n- `PaymentHub.tact` lines 149–150 (reentrancy guard)\n- `PaymentHub.tact` lines 196–202 (`executeTransfer`)\n\n### 4. Lock Enforcement (MUST verify)\n\nLocks prevent sending but must never seize funds. Verify:\n- `account-locks.fc` `can_receive()` always returns 1\n- Lock operations do not modify balances\n- FRAUD_LOCK and COLLATERAL_LOCK both correctly gate `can_send()`\n\n### 5. No Upgrade Paths (MUST verify)\n\nContracts are immutable. No upgradeable proxy patterns. No `setAdmin()` paths that could change invariants.\n\n---\n\n## Known Limitations (Auditor Notice)\n\n| Limitation | Severity | Description |\n|------------|----------|-------------|\n| Invoice replay (off-chain only) | MEDIUM | Contract does not enforce invoice uniqueness on-chain; handled off-chain |\n| DAO unlock not implemented | LOW | FROZEN → ACTIVE transition requires future DAO governance |\n| Lending unlock not implemented | LOW | COLLATERAL_LOCKED → ACTIVE requires Lending Adapter (not yet deployed) |\n| NFT ownership integration (partial) | MEDIUM | Some contracts rely on calling contract for ownership check |\n| Single admin key (temporary) | HIGH | Admin key is single-key pending multi-sig migration (Q1 2026) |\n\nThese are documented accepted risks. Full details in [docs/audit-notes.md](../audit-notes.md).\n\n---\n\n## Auditor Engagement Process\n\n### Access\n\n- Repository: `https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol`\n- Audit freeze commit: `eb5dd593248a33a5a7517ae59b840827c140906a`\n- Build instructions: [audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md](../../audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md)\n- Contact for questions: via GitHub issues tagged `audit`\n\n### Scope Confirmation\n\nBefore beginning, auditors must confirm:\n- Which contracts are in scope (see [audit/SCOPE.md](../../audit/SCOPE.md))\n- Which compiler versions to use (see [audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md](../../audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md))\n- Which invariants to verify (see [audit/INVARIANTS.md](../../audit/INVARIANTS.md))\n\n### Expected Deliverables\n\n| Deliverable | Description |\n|-------------|-------------|\n| Audit Report | Findings categorized by severity (Critical, High, Medium, Low, Informational) |\n| Finding References | Each finding references specific invariant(s) and contract line(s) |\n| Reproduction Steps | Each finding includes steps to reproduce |\n| Suggested Fixes | Where applicable |\n| Invariant Attestation | Statement on whether each of I1–I7 holds |\n\nThe end-to-end engagement workflow (intake → triage → remediation → re-verification → disclosure) is canonicalised in [docs/security/audits/REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md](./audits/REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md). NFTAccountResolver (no dependencies)\n3. AccountStateMachine (depends on AccountLocks)\n4. PaymentHub        (depends on AccountLocks, NFTAccountResolver, AccountStateMachine)\n5. MerchantPaymentHub (depends on PaymentHub)\n6. CollateralSignal  (no dependencies)\n7. PublicCollateralLookup (depends on CollateralSignal)\n```\n\n---\n\n## Verification (verify.ts)\n\n### Usage\n\n```bash\n# Verify against a deployment manifest\nnpx ts-node scripts/deploy/verify.ts --manifest deployments/mainnet/2026-03-19T12-00-00Z.json\n\n# Verify a specific contract address\nnpx ts-node scripts/deploy/verify.ts --address EQAjH... --contract PaymentHub\n```\n\n### What It Verifies\n\n1. Contract code hash matches compiled source\n2. Contract state is initialized correctly\n3. Admin addresses match deployment configuration\n4. Invariants I1–I7 are structurally satisfied (code inspection)\n\n---\n\n## Deployment Manifest Format\n\nEach deployment creates a manifest in `deployments/{network}/{timestamp}.json`:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"version\": \"1.0.0\",\n  \"network\": \"mainnet\",\n  \"timestamp\": \"2026-03-19T12:00:00Z\",\n  \"commit\": \"abc1234\",\n  \"deployer\": \"EQA...\",\n  \"contracts\": {\n    \"PaymentHub\": {\n      \"address\": \"EQA...\",\n      \"codeHash\": \"abc123...\",\n      \"deployTx\": \"tx_hash...\",\n      \"deployBlock\": 123456\n    }\n  },\n  \"configuration\": {\n    \"adminAddress\": \"EQA...\",\n    \"riskAuthority\": \"EQA...\",\n    \"lendingAdapter\": null\n  }\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## Security Checklist Before Deployment\n\n- [ ] All pre-production fixes applied (see `docs/audit/FULL_SYSTEM_AUDIT.md` F-CRIT-1 to F-CRIT-5)\n- [ ] Admin key stored in hardware wallet (Ledger/Trezor)\n- [ ] risk_authority key stored in hardware wallet\n- [ ] Deployment key is cold storage (air-gapped)\n- [ ] Test deployment on testnet successful\n- [ ] Verification script passes on testnet deployment\n- [ ] Security audit completed\n- [ ] Deployment manifest reviewed by second person\n\n---\n\n## References\n\n- **Deployment Matrix:** [`docs/deployments/network-matrix.md`](../../docs/deployments/network-matrix.md)\n- **Key Management:** [`docs/security/KEY_MANAGEMENT.md`](../../docs/security/KEY_MANAGEMENT.md)\n- **Audit Freeze Metadata:** [`audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md`](../../audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md)\n- **Full System Audit:** [`docs/audit/FULL_SYSTEM_AUDIT.md`](../../docs/audit/FULL_SYSTEM_AUDIT.md)",

Objective\n\nProcure a **formal external security audit** of the Phase 2 core smart contracts by a TON-specialist firm. Successfully completing this engagement is a mandatory gate before any TONBANKCARD mainnet deployment touching the in-scope contracts.\n\nSuccess criteria (mirror of issue #112 acceptance criteria):\n\n- [ ] Audit firm engaged and scope signed\n- [ ] Frozen audit package delivered (see §5)\n- [ ] All Critical findings remediated and re-verified\n- [ ] All High findings remediated, or formally accepted with rationale in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md)\n- [ ] All Medium findings addressed (remediated or documented as accepted risk in `docs/audit-notes.md`)\n- [ ] Audit report published in this directory\n- [ ] Remediation PR(s) merged and re-verified by auditor\n- [ ] `docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md` updated with completion status\n\n---\n\n## 2. In-Scope Contracts\n\nThe audit covers exactly the contracts listed in issue #112 §3:\n\n| # | Contract | File | Language | Reason |\n|---|----------|------|----------|--------|\n| 1 | PaymentHub | `contracts/payments/PaymentHub.tact` | Tact | Core payment routing, NFT account abstraction |\n| 2 | MerchantPaymentHub | `contracts/MerchantPaymentHub.tact` | Tact | Merchant-facing payment processing |\n| 3 | Account Locks | `contracts/payments/account-locks.fc` | FunC | FRAUD_LOCK and COLLATERAL_LOCK flag logic |\n| 4 | NFT Account Resolver (FunC) | `contracts/nft-resolver/nft_account_resolver.fc` | FunC | On-chain NFT ownership resolver |\n| 5 | NFT Account Resolver (Tact) | `contracts/nft-resolver/nft_account_resolver.tact` | Tact | Tact wrapper for the resolver |\n| 6 | Public Collateral Lookup | `contracts/collateral-lookup/PublicCollateralLookup.tact` | Tact | Collateral signal read interface |\n| 7 | Collateral Signal | `contracts/CollateralSignal.tact` | Tact | Collateral signal emission |\n\nSupporting types and interfaces (`contracts/types/`, `contracts/interfaces/`) are in scope **for context only** — they are reviewed insofar as they affect the contracts above. They have already been covered by the internal per-contract audit in [`audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md`](../../../../audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md).\n\n---\n\n## 3. Out of Scope\n\nExplicitly **not** part of this engagement (per issue #112 §4):\n\n- Phase 4 contracts (`CrossChainBridge.tact`, `MultiSigCard.tact`, `RecurringPayments.tact`, `LendingProtocolCoordinator.tact`) — covered by engagement **A2**\n- Off-chain services (`api/`, `backend/`, `sdk/`) — covered by engagement **A4**\n- Governance contracts (`contracts/governance/*`) — covered in **Track E**\n- Frontend, dashboard, wallet UI\n\nExternal pre-deployed contracts (TBC jetton, NFT collections, TONCO DEX pool) are treated as trust assumptions; their audits are referenced via [`audit/SCOPE.md`](../../../../audit/SCOPE.md) §\"Out-of-Scope Components\".\n\n---\n\n## 4. Threat Model — Required Coverage\n\nThe audit must explicitly evaluate every attack class enumerated in issue #112 §5, mapped to the protocol-level threat model in [`audit/THREAT_MODEL.md`](../../../../audit/THREAT_MODEL.md):\n\n| # | Class | Where to look |\n|---|-------|---------------|\n| T1 | Re-entrancy / message ordering | `PaymentHub.tact` reentrancy guard (lines 149–150), all `receive(...)` handlers |\n| T2 | NFT ownership spoofing | `nft-resolver/*`, `MerchantPaymentHub.checkOwnership` (lines 90–96) |\n| T3 | Lock bypass | `account-locks.fc` `get_can_send` / `get_can_receive`, all fund-moving paths |\n| T4 | Admin key abuse | search for `deployer`, `admin`, `risk_authority`, `lending_adapter` — verify invariant I3 |\n| T5 | Atomicity failure | `PaymentHub.executeTransfer` (lines 196–202), debit/credit pairing |\n| T6 | Integer overflow / underflow | All `Int as uintN` casts, balance arithmetic |\n| T7 | Replay attacks | Message uniqueness, on-chain vs. off-chain replay protection |\n| T8 | Gas griefing | `receive` handler gas costs, refund paths, message storage |\n\nInvariant attestation in the final report must cover **I1–I7** as defined in [`audit/INVARIANTS.md`](../../../../audit/INVARIANTS.md).\n\n---\n\n## 5. Audit Package (Frozen Hand-off)\n\nThe protocol team will deliver the following package to the selected firm at engagement kickoff. The audited commit is frozen at the kickoff and recorded in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §\"Audited commit\".\n\n| Artifact | Location | Notes |\n|----------|----------|-------|\n| Audit intro pack | [`docs/audit/external-audit-intro.md`](../../../audit/external-audit-intro.md) | Protocol intent, trust model, intentional design constraints |\n| Scope | [`audit/SCOPE.md`](../../../../audit/SCOPE.md) | Contracts, focus areas, out-of-scope list |\n| Threat model | [`audit/THREAT_MODEL.md`](../../../../audit/THREAT_MODEL.md) | T1–T8 attack classes with mitigations |\n| Formal invariants | [`audit/INVARIANTS.md`](../../../../audit/INVARIANTS.md) | I1–I7 with contract-line mapping |\n| Freeze metadata | [`audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md`](../../../../audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md) | Compiler versions, file hashes, frozen commit |\n| Build instructions | [`audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md`](../../../../audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md) | Reproducible build & test commands |\n| Test coverage | [`audit/TEST_COVERAGE_REPORT.md`](../../../../audit/TEST_COVERAGE_REPORT.md) | Coverage breakdown per contract |\n| Internal pre-audit | [`audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md`](../../../../audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md) | Internal findings already mitigated or known |\n| Full system audit | [`docs/audit/FULL_SYSTEM_AUDIT.md`](../../../audit/FULL_SYSTEM_AUDIT.md) | System-wide context |\n| Audit readiness | [`docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md`](../../AUDIT_READINESS.md) | Entry-point navigation document |\n| Audit notes | [`docs/audit-notes.md`](../../../audit-notes.md) | Known accepted limitations |\n\nThe auditor receives **read access** to the public GitHub repository at the frozen commit, plus a direct contact channel agreed at kickoff.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Candidate Firms\n\nThree firm classes are acceptable per the roadmap and issue #112:\n\n1. **Top-tier general smart-contract auditors with TON experience**, e.g., Trail of Bits, OtterSec, Halborn.\n2. **Layer-1-agnostic auditors with proven non-EVM track record**, e.g., CertiK, Quantstamp.\n3. **TON-ecosystem specialists**, e.g., CertiK TON desk, TonGuard, scalebit (TON), Veridise TON desk.\n\nA non-exhaustive long list is maintained in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §\"Firm long list\".\n\n### 6.1 Evaluation Matrix\n\nEach shortlisted firm is scored on the following criteria. Numeric scores 1–5 (5 = excellent). Final score = weighted sum.\n\n| Criterion | Weight | Notes |\n|-----------|--------|-------|\n| TON / Tact / FunC depth | 25% | Prior TON engagements, in-house TON expertise, Tact language coverage |\n| Methodology rigor | 20% | Manual review hours per LOC, fuzzing/property testing, formal methods readiness |\n| Reputation & references | 15% | Publicly available audit reports, ecosystem feedback |\n| Re-audit / remediation policy | 15% | Verified re-test included, follow-up support |\n| Cost & timeline fit | 15% | Total cost, calendar window, latest available start |\n| Communication & transparency | 10% | Daily-stand-up cadence, willingness to publish, NDA flexibility |\n\n### 6.2 Conflict-of-interest screen\n\nFirms must disclose any prior engagement with TONBANKCARD operators, TON Foundation grant overlap, holding of TBC token / TBC Diamonds / Series 7777/8888 NFTs, or other potential conflicts. Disqualifying conditions are recorded in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md).\n\n---\n\n## 7. Engagement Process\n\n```\nT-0   Issue published                                       ✅\nT+0   Firm long list assembled                              ⏳\nT+1w  Shortlist (3 firms) + RFP sent\nT+3w  Proposals received, evaluation matrix populated\nT+4w  Firm selected, contract signed\nT+4w  Audit kickoff:  freeze commit + package handover\nT+8w  Mid-audit checkpoint (preliminary findings)\nT+10w Draft report delivered\nT+11w Remediation PRs opened (per REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md)\nT+13w Remediation merged\nT+14w Re-verification by auditor\nT+14w Final report published in this directory\nT+14w STATUS.md flipped to COMPLETED\nT+15w Disclosure summary in CHANGELOG.md + public channels\n```\n\nAll dates are anchored to the kickoff and tracked in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md). The remediation phase follows [`REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md`](../REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md) verbatim.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Deliverables From Auditor\n\nThe signed engagement must require the following deliverables (mirrored in the report template):\n\n1. **Audit report**, structured per [`REPORT_TEMPLATE.md`](../REPORT_TEMPLATE.md):\n   - Findings categorised by severity\n   - Each finding references file:line, invariant(s), and threat-model class\n   - Reproduction steps for every Critical and High\n   - Suggested fixes where applicable\n   - Explicit attestation per invariant I1–I7\n2. **Reproducible PoCs** for every Critical and High finding.\n3. **Re-verification letter** signed after remediation against a specific commit hash.\n4. **Right to publish** the report in this repository.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Acceptance / Gating Decision\n\nThe engagement is closed when:\n\n- All eight checkboxes in §1 are ticked.\n- [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) records the gating verdict as `READY` or `READY WITH ACCEPTED RISKS`.\n- [`docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md`](../../AUDIT_READINESS.md) §\"Audit completion status\" is updated.\n- `CHANGELOG.md` carries a disclosure entry referencing the report.\n\nA verdict of `BLOCKED` keeps mainnet deployment paused per [`README.md`](../README.md) §4.\n\n---\n\n## 10. The audited commit is frozen at the kickoff and recorded in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §\"Audited commit\".\n\n| Artifact | Location | Notes |\n|----------|----------|-------|\n| Audit intro pack | [`docs/audit/external-audit-intro.md`](../../../audit/external-audit-intro.md) | Protocol intent, trust model, intentional design constraints |\n| Scope | [`audit/SCOPE.md`](../../../../audit/SCOPE.md) | Contracts, focus areas, out-of-scope list |\n| Threat model | [`audit/THREAT_MODEL.md`](../../../../audit/THREAT_MODEL.md) | T1–T8 attack classes with mitigations |\n| Formal invariants | [`audit/INVARIANTS.md`](../../../../audit/INVARIANTS.md) | I1–I7 with contract-line mapping |\n| Freeze metadata | [`audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md`](../../../../audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md) | Compiler versions, file hashes, frozen commit |\n| Build instructions | [`audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md`](../../../../audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md) | Reproducible build & test commands |\n| Test coverage | [`audit/TEST_COVERAGE_REPORT.md`](../../../../audit/TEST_COVERAGE_REPORT.md) | Coverage breakdown per contract |\n| Internal pre-audit | [`audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md`](../../../../audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md) | Internal findings already mitigated or known |\n| Full system audit | [`docs/audit/FULL_SYSTEM_AUDIT.md`](../../../audit/FULL_SYSTEM_AUDIT.md) | System-wide context |\n| Audit readiness | [`docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md`](../../AUDIT_READINESS.md) | Entry-point navigation document |\n| Audit notes | [`docs/audit-notes.md`](../../../audit-notes.md) | Known accepted limitations |\n\nThe auditor receives **read access** to the public GitHub repository at the frozen commit, plus a direct contact channel agreed at kickoff.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Candidate Firms\n\nThree firm classes are acceptable per the roadmap and issue #112:\n\n1. **Top-tier general smart-contract auditors with TON experience**, e.g., Trail of Bits, OtterSec, Halborn.\n2. **Layer-1-agnostic auditors with proven non-EVM track record**, e.g., CertiK, Quantstamp.\n3. **TON-ecosystem specialists**, e.g., CertiK TON desk, TonGuard, scalebit (TON), Veridise TON desk.\n\nA non-exhaustive long list is maintained in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) §\"Firm long list\".\n\n### 6.1 Evaluation Matrix\n\nEach shortlisted firm is scored on the following criteria. Numeric scores 1–5 (5 = excellent). Final score = weighted sum.\n\n| Criterion | Weight | Notes |\n|-----------|--------|-------|\n| TON / Tact / FunC depth | 25% | Prior TON engagements, in-house TON expertise, Tact language coverage |\n| Methodology rigor | 20% | Manual review hours per LOC, fuzzing/property testing, formal methods readiness |\n| Reputation & references | 15% | Publicly available audit reports, ecosystem feedback |\n| Re-audit / remediation policy | 15% | Verified re-test included, follow-up support |\n| Cost & timeline fit | 15% | Total cost, calendar window, latest available start |\n| Communication & transparency | 10% | Daily-stand-up cadence, willingness to publish, NDA flexibility |\n\n### 6.2 Conflict-of-interest screen\n\nFirms must disclose any prior engagement with TONBANKCARD operators, TON Foundation grant overlap, holding of TBC token / TBC Diamonds / Series 7777/8888 NFTs, or other potential conflicts. Disqualifying conditions are recorded in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md).\n\n---\n\n## 7. Engagement Process\n\n```\nT-0   Issue published                                       ✅\nT+0   Firm long list assembled                              ⏳\nT+1w  Shortlist (3 firms) + RFP sent\nT+3w  Proposals received, evaluation matrix populated\nT+4w  Firm selected, contract signed\nT+4w  Audit kickoff:  freeze commit + package handover\nT+8w  Mid-audit checkpoint (preliminary findings)\nT+10w Draft report delivered\nT+11w Remediation PRs opened (per REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md)\nT+13w Remediation merged\nT+14w Re-verification by auditor\nT+14w Final report published in this directory\nT+14w STATUS.md flipped to COMPLETED\nT+15w Disclosure summary in CHANGELOG.md + public channels\n```\n\nAll dates are anchored to the kickoff and tracked in [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md). The remediation phase follows [`REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md`](../REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md) verbatim.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Deliverables From Auditor\n\nThe signed engagement must require the following deliverables (mirrored in the report template):\n\n1. **Audit report**, structured per [`REPORT_TEMPLATE.md`](../REPORT_TEMPLATE.md):\n   - Findings categorised by severity\n   - Each finding references file:line, invariant(s), and threat-model class\n   - Reproduction steps for every Critical and High\n   - Suggested fixes where applicable\n   - Explicit attestation per invariant I1–I7\n2. **Reproducible PoCs** for every Critical and High finding.\n3. **Re-verification letter** signed after remediation against a specific commit hash.\n4. **Right to publish** the report in this repository.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Acceptance / Gating Decision\n\nThe engagement is closed when:\n\n- All eight checkboxes in §1 are ticked.\n- [`STATUS.md`](./STATUS.md) records the gating verdict as `READY` or `READY WITH ACCEPTED RISKS`.\n- [`docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md`](../../AUDIT_READINESS.md) §\"Audit completion status\" is updated.\n- `CHANGELOG.md` carries a disclosure entry referencing the report.\n\nA verdict of `BLOCKED` keeps mainnet deployment paused per [`README.md`](../README.md) §4.\n\n---\n\n## 10. Compare the two hashes\n */\nfunction verifyCodeHash(\n  address: string,\n  expectedHash: string,\n  contractName: string\n): { passed: boolean; actual: string } {\n  // Placeholder: real implementation would query TON blockchain\n  // const client = new TonClient({ endpoint: rpcEndpoint });\n  // const codeCell = await client.getContractState(Address.parse(address));\n  // const actualHash = codeCell.code?.hash().toString('hex') ?? expectedHash.startsWith('[DRY RUN]') ? true : false,\n    actual: '[Requires blockchain query - run after real deployment]',\n  };\n}\n\n/**\n * Verify contract invariants are structurally enforced.\n *\n * This performs a static analysis of the contract source to confirm:\n * - No admin fund access functions exist\n * - NFT ownership checks are present in transfer paths\n * - Lock checks are present in transfer paths\n */\nfunction verifyInvariants(contractName: string): { passed: boolean; details: string[] } {\n  const details: string[] = [];\n\n  // Check that no admin withdrawal functions exist in contract source\n  const contractFiles: Record<string, string> = {\n    PaymentHub: 'contracts/payments/PaymentHub.tact',\n    MerchantPaymentHub: 'contracts/MerchantPaymentHub.tact',\n    AccountLocks: 'contracts/payments/account-locks.fc',\n    NFTAccountResolver: 'contracts/nft-resolver/nft_account_resolver.fc',\n  };\n\n  const file = contractFiles[contractName];\n  if (!file || !fs.existsSync(file)) {\n    details.push(`Source file not found for ${contractName}`);\n    return { passed: false, details };\n  }\n\n  const source = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8');\n\n  // Check absence of dangerous patterns\n  const forbiddenPatterns = [\n    { pattern: /adminWithdraw/i, description: 'Admin withdrawal function' },\n    { pattern: /emergencyDrain/i, description: 'Emergency drain function' },\n    { pattern: /forcedTransfer/i, description: 'Forced transfer function' },\n    { pattern: /set_code\\s*\\(/i, description: 'Code upgrade function' },\n  ];\n\n  let passed = true;\n  for (const { pattern, description } of forbiddenPatterns) {\n    if (pattern.test(source)) {\n      details.push(`FAIL: Found forbidden pattern: ${description}`);\n      passed = false;\n    }\n  }\n\n  if (passed) {\n    details.push('No forbidden admin fund patterns found');\n  }\n\n  return { passed, details };\n}\n\n// ─── Main Verification ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\nfunction verifyFromManifest(manifestPath: string): VerificationReport {\n  if (!fs.existsSync(manifestPath)) {\n deployment manifest: ${manifestPath}`);\n  console.log(`   Network:    ${manifest.network}`);\n  console.log(`   Timestamp:  ${manifest.timestamp}`);\n  console.log(`   Commit:     ${manifest.commit}`);\n\n  const report: VerificationReport = {\n    timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),\n    network: manifest.network,\n    manifestFile: manifestPath,\n    allPassed: true,\n    results: [],\n  };\n\n  for (const [contractName, deployment] of Object.entries(manifest.contracts)) {\n    const dep = deployment as { address: string; codeHash: string };\n    console.log(`\\n  Contract: ${contractName}`);\n    console.log(`  Address:  ${dep.address}`);\n\n    const errors: string[] = [];\n\n    // 1. Verify code hash\n    const { passed: hashPassed, actual } = verifyCodeHash(\n      dep.address,\n      dep.codeHash,\n      contractName\n    );\n\n    // 2. Verify invariants via source analysis\n    const { passed: invariantsPassed, details } = verifyInvariants(contractName);\n\n    details.forEach(d => console.log(`    ${d.startsWith('FAIL') ? '❌' : '✅'} ${d}`));\n\n    if (!invariantsPassed) {\n      errors.push(...details.filter(d => d.startsWith('FAIL')));\n    }\n\n    const result: VerificationResult = {\n      contract: contractName,\n      address: dep.address,\n      codeHashMatch: hashPassed,\n      stateValid: true, // Would be checked against blockchain\n      adminAddressMatch: true, // Would be checked against blockchain\n      errors,\n    };\n\n    report.results.push(result);\n\n    if (errors.length > 0 || !invariantsPassed) {\n      report.allPassed = false;\n    }\n  }\n\n  return report;\n}\n\nfunction printReport(report: VerificationReport): void {\n  console.log('\\n\\n═══════════════════════════════════════');\n  console.log('  VERIFICATION REPORT');\n  console.log('═══════════════════════════════════════');\n  console.log(`  Network:    ${report.network}`);\n  console.log(`  Manifest:   ${report.manifestFile}`);\n  console.log(`  Verified:   ${report.timestamp}`);\n  console.log('───────────────────────────────────────');\n\n  for (const result of report.results) {\n    const icon = result.errors.length === 0 ? Directory Layout\n\n```\ndocs/security/audits/\n├── README.md                       — This index\n├── REMEDIATION_WORKFLOW.md         — How findings are triaged, fixed, and verified\n├── REPORT_TEMPLATE.md              — Canonical layout for incoming audit reports\n├── A1-core-contracts/              — Issue #112 engagement\n│   ├── ENGAGEMENT.md               — Scope, deliverables, candidate firms, evaluation matrix\n│   └── STATUS.md                   — Live state of the engagement (firm, dates, findings)\n├── A2-phase4-contracts/            — Issue #113 engagement (gated by A1 completion)\n│   ├── ENGAGEMENT.md               — Phase 4 scope with dedicated cross-chain bridge review\n│   └── STATUS.md                   — Live state, A1 upstream-gate tracker, threat-ID ledger\n├── A4-offchain-services/           — Issue #115 engagement (off-chain pentest)\n│   ├── ENGAGEMENT.md               — api/ + backend/indexer/ + sdk/ pentest scope, OWASP-driven\n│   ├── STATUS.md                   — Live state, D4/D5 upstream-gate tracker, OWASP coverage\n│   ├── OWASP_CHECKLIST.md          — OWASP Top 10:2021 category-by-category required tests\n│   └── PENTEST_PLAN.md             — Detailed per-component test cases, PoC expectations\n└── A5-bug-bounty/                  — Issue #116 engagement (public bug bounty program)\n    ├── ENGAGEMENT.md               — Engagement plan, platform comparison, SLAs, gating\n    ├── STATUS.md                   — Live state, launch checklist, findings ledger, SLA tracker\n    ├── PROGRAM_BRIEF.md            — Canonical source for the platform-published terms\n    ├── SEVERITY_RUBRIC.md          — Severity classification rubric (I1–I7 + Immunefi v2.3)\n    ├── QUARTERLY_REPORT_TEMPLATE.md — Quarterly public transparency report template\n    └── DRY_RUN.md                  — Internal dry-run / soft-launch plan (gates public launch)\n```\n\nFuture engagements are added as sibling folders named after the roadmap ID.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Engagement Index\n\n| ID | Scope | Roadmap | Issue | Status | Firm | Report |\n|----|-------|---------|-------|--------|------|--------|\n| **A1** | Core contracts (PaymentHub, MerchantPaymentHub, account-locks, nft-resolver, collateral signal) | [A1](../../../TEMP/DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md) | [#112](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/112) | Engagement preparation complete — awaiting firm selection | — | — |\n| **A2** | Phase 4 contracts (CrossChainBridge, MultiSigCard, RecurringPayments, LendingProtocolCoordinator) | [A2](../../../TEMP/DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md) | [#113](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/113) | Engagement preparation complete — awaiting A1 completion and firm selection | — | — |\n| **A4** | Off-chain services (`api/`, `backend/indexer/`, `sdk/`) | [A4](../../../TEMP/DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md) | [#115](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/115) | Engagement preparation complete — awaiting D4 hardening and firm selection | — | — |\n| **A5** | Bug bounty program (public, Immunefi or HackenProof) | [A5](../../../TEMP/DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md) | [#116](https://github.com/xlabtg/tonbankcard-protocol/issues/116) | Engagement preparation complete — awaiting A1 + A2 completion, platform selection, and dry-run | — | — |\n\nWhen a new external engagement begins, copy `A1-core-contracts/` as a starting template, update its `ENGAGEMENT.md` for the new scope, and add a row to this table.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Gating Rules\n\nThe following rules are **non-negotiable** and apply to every engagement listed in §3:\n\n1. **No mainnet deployment** of any in-scope contract before the corresponding audit report is published and remediation is verified by the auditor.\n2. **Critical findings:** zero tolerance — every Critical must be remediated and re-verified before sign-off.\n3. **High findings:** remediated, or formally accepted with rationale signed off by the maintainers in `STATUS.md`.\n4. **Medium findings:** remediated or documented as accepted risk in `docs/audit-notes.md`.\n5. **Audit report is public** — published in this directory and linked from `docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md`.\n6. **Frozen scope** — once an engagement is signed, the contract set under audit is frozen at a specific commit (see [`audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md`](../../../audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md)).\n\n---\n\n## 5. Where Auditors Should Start\n\nExternal auditors engaging with TONBANKCARD should read, in order:\n\n1. [`docs/audit/external-audit-intro.md`](../../audit/external-audit-intro.md) — protocol intent and constraints\n2. [`audit/SCOPE.md`](../../../audit/SCOPE.md) — contracts in scope, focus areas\n3. [`audit/INVARIANTS.md`](../../../audit/INVARIANTS.md) — formal invariants I1–I7\n4. [`audit/THREAT_MODEL.md`](../../../audit/THREAT_MODEL.md) — attack vectors and mitigations\n5. [`audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md`](../../../audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md) — frozen commit, compiler versions\n6. [`audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md`](../../../audit/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md) — reproducible build\n7. [`audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md`](../../../audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md) — known findings from internal pre-audit\n8. Engagement-specific `ENGAGEMENT.md` in the relevant subdirectory\n\nThe [`docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md`](../AUDIT_READINESS.md) document is the navigation hub for all of the above.\n\n---\n\n## 6.    [solve worker-1]         "content": "# Tonbankcard Protocol — Development Roadmap\n\n**Date**: 2026-03-22\n**Based on**: Repository analysis at commit `0c54950`\n**Related to**: Issue #86\n\n---\n\n## Executive Summary\n\nThe Tonbankcard Protocol has successfully completed all four planned development phases. The codebase is feature-complete at the implementation level. The next logical development steps focus on **production readiness, ecosystem maturity, and long-term sustainability** — moving the protocol from a well-built codebase to a production-grade, battle-tested, and adopted financial infrastructure.\n\nThe roadmap is organized into six tracks:\n\n1. **Track A — Security & Audit** (highest priority)\n2. **Track B — Production Deployment & Operations**\n3. **Track C — Ecosystem & Developer Experience**\n4. **Track D — Protocol Maturity & Hardening**\n5. **Track E — Governance & Decentralization**\n6. **Track F — Advanced Features & Expansion**\n\n---\n\n## Track A — Security & Audit ⚠️ Critical Priority\n\nAll Phase 4 contracts and the core Phase 2 contracts require formal security review before production use. This track must be completed before any mainnet deployments.\n\n### A1. Formal Security Audit — Core Contracts\n**Scope**: `contracts/payments/PaymentHub.tact`, `contracts/MerchantPaymentHub.tact`, `contracts/payments/account-locks.fc`, `contracts/nft-resolver/`\n\n**Actions**:\n- Engage a TON-specialist audit firm (e.g., Trail of Bits, CertiK, or TON-ecosystem-specific auditors)\n- Prepare audit package: contracts + documentation + `docs/security/AUDIT_READINESS.md`\n- Address all findings (Critical/High mandatory, Medium recommended)\n- Publish audit reports publicly\n\n**Deliverables**: Audit report, remediation PR, public disclosure\n\n---\n\n### A2. Formal Security Audit — Phase 4 Contracts\n**Scope**: `CrossChainBridge.tact`, `MultiSigCard.tact`, `RecurringPayments.tact`, `LendingProtocolCoordinator.tact`\n\n**Actions**:\n- Phase 4 contracts are higher risk (cross-chain bridge, multi-sig flows)\n- Separate audit engagement from core contracts\n- Cross-chain bridge requires special attention to message replay and bridge validator compromise scenarios\n\n**Deliverables**: Separate audit report for Phase 4, remediation PRs\n\n---\n\n### A3. Formal Verification of Protocol Invariants\n**Scope**: Critical invariants I1–I7 defined in `docs/invariants.md`\n\n**Actions**:\n- Explore TLA+ or Lean 4 formal proofs for key invariants\n- At minimum, machine-verified property tests for I4 (atomicity) and I7 (lock enforcement)\n- Integrate formal verification tooling into CI (e.g., `@ton/blueprint` property-based tests)\n\n**Deliverables**: Formal verification report or property test suite\n\n---\n\n### A4. Penetration Testing — Off-Chain Services\n**Scope**: `api/`, `backend/indexer/`, `sdk/`\n\n**Actions**:\n- API security review: OWASP Top 10, rate limiting, CORS, authentication\n- Indexer: replay attack prevention, data integrity validation\n- SDK: supply chain security (npm audit), dependency pinning\n\n**Deliverables**: Pentest report, remediation PRs\n\n---\n\n### A5. Bug Bounty Program\n**Actions**:\n- Set up Immunefi or HackenProof bug bounty program\n- Define scope (smart contracts as highest severity, APIs as medium)\n- Set reward tiers aligned with severity (Critical: $10K+, High: $5K, Medium: $1K)\n- Reference `SECURITY.md` for initial framework\n\n**Deliverables**: Live bug bounty program, updated `SECURITY.md`\n\n---\n\n## Track B — Production Deployment & Operations\n\n### B1. Testnet Deployment & Validation\n**Actions**:\n- Deploy all Phase 2 and Phase 4 contracts to TON testnet\n- Run end-to-end integration tests against deployed testnet contracts\n- Validate all adapters (`backend/adapters/`) against testnet gateway sandboxes\n- Update `docs/existing-contracts.md` with testnet addresses\n\n**Deliverables**: Deployed testnet contracts, updated contract address registry\n\n---\n\n### B2. Mainnet Deployment Plan\n**Actions**:\n- Define deployment order (dependencies: NFT resolver → Payment Hub → Merchant Hub)\n- Create deployment runbook (`scripts/deploy/`)\n- Multi-sig deployment: deployer keys should be multi-sig wallet, not a single key\n- Deployment verification: on-chain state checks post-deployment\n- Immutability verification: confirm no upgrade paths were introduced\n\n**Deliverables**: Deployment runbook, multi-sig setup guide\n\n---\n\n### B3. Production Monitoring & Alerting\n**Scope**: `docs/production/`\n\n**Actions**:\n- Implement blockchain event monitoring (block time, transaction failures, unusual volume)\n- Set up alerting for: large outgoing transfers, account lock activity, bridge contract events\n- Dashboard: Grafana or Datadog for indexer service metrics\n- On-call rotation and incident response drill (using `docs/security/INCIDENT_RESPONSE.md`)\n\n**Deliverables**: Monitoring setup, alerting runbook, on-call schedule\n\n---\n\n### B4. Infrastructure as Code\n**Actions**:\n- Containerize backend services (`api/`, `backend/indexer/`) with Docker\n- Create `docker-compose.yml` for local development environment\n- Helm charts or Terraform configs for production deployment\n- Environment variable management (`schemas/` can define config schemas)\n\n**Deliverables**: Dockerfile per service, docker-compose, IaC configs\n\n---\n\n### B5. Database Migration Strategy\n**Actions**:\n- `backend/indexer` uses both SQLite and PostgreSQL — formalize the migration strategy\n- Create database schema documentation\n- Add schema versioning and migration tooling (`npm run db:migrate` exists but needs docs)\n- Backup and recovery procedures\n\n**Deliverables**: DB migration guide, schema docs, backup runbook\n\n---\n\n## Track C — Ecosystem & Developer Experience\n\n### C1. Public Documentation Site\n**Actions**:\n- Convert `docs/` markdown files into a hosted documentation site (e.g., Docusaurus, GitBook)\n- Publish at `docs.tonbankcard.com` or equivalent\n- Include: architecture guide, merchant integration guide, SDK reference, API reference\n- Auto-generate API docs from TypeScript types in `sdk/src/types.ts`\n\n**Deliverables**: Hosted documentation site, auto-generated SDK/API docs\n\n---\n\n### C2. SDK Developer Experience Improvements\n**Scope**: `sdk/`\n\n**Actions**:\n- Publish `@tonbankcard/merchant-sdk` to npm registry (currently v1.0.0 but requires actual publishing)\n- Add interactive examples in `examples/` directory (currently exists but may be sparse)\n- Add SDK changelog (`sdk/CHANGELOG.md` referenced but may need updates)\n- Provide React, Vue, and plain HTML integration examples\n- Add Postman collection for the Merchant API\n\n**Deliverables**: npm publish workflow, example integrations, Postman collection\n\n---\n\n### C3. Purpose\n\nThis document defines a single, repeatable workflow for processing findings from any external audit listed in [`README.md`](./README.md). It exists so that:\n\n- Every finding has a tracked GitHub issue\n- Every fix has a reviewable pull request\n- Auditors can re-verify fixes against a stable artifact\n- Public disclosure follows a predictable timeline\n\nIt applies to engagements A1, A2, A4, future re-audits, and any out-of-band advisories.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Severity Classification\n\nThe protocol uses the severity scale already established in [`audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md`](../../../audit/SMART_CONTRACTS_SECURITY_AUDIT.md) and issue #110:\n\n| Severity | Definition | Response Time | Mandatory Action |\n|----------|------------|---------------|------------------|\n| 🔴 **CRITICAL** | Threat to user funds or non-custodial guarantee | 24h triage / 7-day fix target | **Must be remediated**. Mainnet deployment blocked until re-verified. |\n| 🟠 **HIGH** | Serious logic error that can lead to loss of funds or privilege escalation under plausible conditions | 72h triage / 14-day fix target | Remediated **or** formally accepted in `STATUS.md` with rationale and compensating control |\n| 🟡 **MEDIUM** | Bug or deviation that produces incorrect behaviour without direct fund loss | 1-week triage / 30-day fix target | Remediated or documented as accepted risk in `docs/audit-notes.md` |\n| 🟢 **LOW** | Style, documentation, or hardening issue | Best-effort | Addressed in batches; tracked but non-blocking |\n| ℹ️ **INFORMATIONAL** | Notes, suggestions, design observations | Optional | Logged in `STATUS.md` if not actioned |\n\nMainnet deployment is gated on the rules in [`README.md`](./README.md) §4.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Workflow\n\n```\nAuditor delivers report\n        │\n        ▼\n1. Intake          ─►  Hash + commit report to audits/<ID>/report-vN.pdf\n        │\n        ▼\n2. Triage          ─►  Open one GitHub issue per finding (label: audit:<ID>, severity:<level>)\n        │\n        ▼\n3. Remediation     ─►  Branch issue-<n>-<slug>, PR linked back to the finding issue\n        │\n        ▼\n4. Re-verification ─►  Auditor confirms fix on remediation commit hash\n        │\n        ▼\n5. Disclosure      ─►  STATUS.md flipped to COMPLETED; AUDIT_READINESS.md updated; public note\n```\n\nEach step is described below in detail.\n\n### 3.1 Intake\n\nWhen an audit report is received:\n\n1. Save the report as `docs/security/audits/<ID>/report-v<N>.pdf` (or `.md`) — keep the original filename in `STATUS.md`.\n2. Record SHA-256 of the file in `STATUS.md` for tamper evidence.\n3. Confirm the audited commit hash matches the freeze recorded in `audit/FREEZE_METADATA.md`. If it does not, raise this with the auditor before triage.\n4. Commit the report on a branch named `audit/<ID>-report-intake`. **Do not modify the report after this commit.**\n\n### 3.2 Triage\n\nFor every finding:\n\n1. Open a GitHub issue titled `[audit-<ID>] <finding-id>: <short title>`.\n2. Apply labels:\n   - `audit:<ID>` (e.g., `audit:A1`)\n   - `severity:critical` / `severity:high` / `severity:medium` / `severity:low` / `severity:informational`\n   - `type:security`\n3. Copy the auditor's description, evidence, and recommendation verbatim into the issue body.\n4. Cross-link the issue from the corresponding row in `audits/<ID>/STATUS.md` §\"Findings ledger\".\n\nThe triage owner is the maintainer named in `audits/<ID>/STATUS.md` §\"Engagement parties\". Triage SLAs:\n\n- Critical: triage within 24 hours of intake\n- High: 72 hours\n- Medium / Low / Informational: 7 days\n\n### 3.3 Remediation\n\nFor every finding that will be remediated:\n\n1. Create a branch named `issue-<n>-<slug>` per the contributing guidelines.\n2. Reproduce the finding in a test case before applying the fix. The test must fail on the audited commit.\n3. Implement the fix and run the full test suite (`npx blueprint test`).\n4. Open a pull request with the description fields below:\n\n```markdown\n## Audit Finding\nEngagement: <A1 / A2 / …>",
